bettencourtschueller.arts: Since 1999 it has backed French crafts through the Liliane Bettencourt Prize pour l'intelligence de la main, and it funds choral singing, including the Chants libres festival.

bezirksamtfriedrichshainkreuzberg.what: The administration of Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg, the second of Berlin’s twelve districts, formed by a merger in 2001 and led by district mayor Clara Herrmann with five councillors.
bezirksamtfriedrichshainkreuzberg.money: The district’s public budget; a Berlin Bezirksamt is an authority subordinate to the city government, the Senate.
bezirksamtfriedrichshainkreuzberg.arts: Culture sits in the district mayor’s own department, with finance, personnel and economy.

bezos.money: Jeff Bezos's money comes from Amazon, which he founded: online retail, cloud computing and advertising.

facts.t: Amazon's revenue was $716,924 million in 2025.
In September 2025 Amazon agreed to pay $2.5 billion, including $1.5 billion in refunds, to settle US Federal Trade Commission claims that it enrolled customers in Prime through deceptive practices.
Amazon.com Services LLC reported $17,780,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025 in its Lobbying Disclosure Act reports.
Amazon Europe Core SARL declared EU lobbying costs of €9,000,000 to €9,999,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

bgeraldcantor.what: An American investment banker (1916 to 1996) from the Bronx who founded B.G. Cantor and Company, which became the New York securities firm Cantor Fitzgerald.
bgeraldcantor.money: His fortune from Cantor Fitzgerald, among the biggest institutional brokers of US government securities.
bgeraldcantor.arts: With his wife Iris he built the world's largest private collection of Rodin's works and gave Rodins to more than 70 institutions, including the Brooklyn Museum and LACMA.

bhp.what: An Australian mining company founded in Broken Hill in 1885 as the Broken Hill Proprietary Company, headquartered in Melbourne and listed only in Australia since 2022.
bhp.money: Mining and selling iron ore, copper and coal; revenue was US$51.26 billion in the 2025 financial year.

facts.t: BHP reported revenue of US$51.3 billion and underlying attributable profit of US$10.2 billion for the year to 30 June 2025.
In November 2025 London’s High Court ruled BHP liable for the 2015 collapse of Samarco’s Fundão dam in Mariana, Brazil, in a lawsuit the claimants’ lawyers valued at up to £36 billion.

bigantstudios.what: An Australian video game developer in Southbank, Melbourne, founded in 2000 by its chief executive Ross Symons and owned since 2021 by Nacon.
bigantstudios.money: Sales of its sports video games, including the Cricket, AFL and Rugby League series.

bikubenfonden.what: A Danish philanthropic foundation in Copenhagen, formed in 2010 from Bikuben Fonden of 1989 and BG Fonden, with roots in the savings bank Sparekassen Bikuben, founded 1857.
bikubenfonden.money: An endowment from its ownership share in Sparekassen Bikuben and later BG Bank; it granted DKK 151.8 million in 2025.

bilgiliholding.what: An Istanbul real estate group founded by Abdülhakim Bilgili, based in Akaretler, Beşiktaş; its projects include the Akaretler Row Houses, W Istanbul and Galataport.
bilgiliholding.money: Real estate development and investment, tourism and asset management, financed through funds with outside investors and partnerships with hotel and brand groups.
bilgiliholding.arts: It runs an arts arm, Bilgili Art.

biocon.money: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw's money comes from Biocon, the Bengaluru biopharmaceutical company she founded.

facts.t: Biocon's revenue from operations for FY25 grew 9 per cent to ₹11,537.8 crore, and net profit declined 0.9 per cent to ₹1,013.3 crore.

In June 2022 the CBI arrested a joint drugs controller in an alleged Rs 9 lakh bribery case to favour Biocon Biologics' insulin aspart injection, and booked the company's associate vice president L Praveen Kumar; the company denied the allegations.

birminghamcityuniversity|UK.what: A public university in Birmingham, a higher education corporation under the Education Reform Act 1988 with university status since 1992, rooted in the Birmingham College of Art.
birminghamcityuniversity|UK.money: Mostly student tuition fees: GBP 289.8 million in the year to July 2024, against GBP 23.0 million in funding body grants.

bisisilva.what: A Nigerian contemporary art curator (1962 to 2019) who founded the Centre for Contemporary Art, Lagos, opened in December 2007, and the Asiko Art School.
bisisilva.arts: She co-curated the second Thessaloniki Biennale in 2009 and was a curator of the 2006 Dakar Biennale.

blackmagicdesign.what: A privately held Australian maker of digital film cameras and video production equipment, founded in 2001 by its chief executive Grant Petty and based in South Melbourne.
blackmagicdesign.money: Sales of its cameras, broadcast hardware and software, including the DaVinci Resolve editing and colour grading application.

blackmonfamily.what: A family that the Montgomery Museum of Fine Arts names among the patrons whose gifts paid for the galleries of its 1988 building, which has a Blackmon Gallery.

blavatnikfamily.money: Len Blavatnik’s fortune began with Russian oil and aluminium assets after the Soviet collapse and is held through Access Industries, including Warner Music and LyondellBasell stakes.

facts.t: Access Industries’ stake in the oil company TNK was sold to Rosneft in 2013, and Blavatnik made $7 billion.
Blavatnik donated $1 million directly to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee in 2017.
Access Industries made a £1.25 million donation to the UK Conservative Party, revealed in May 2024.

Len Blavatnik gave $347,200 in personal contributions to federal candidates, parties and PACs in the 2023 to 2024 cycle; the largest went to Grow the Majority ($150,000), Emmer Majority Builders ($50,000) and Jacky Rosen Victory Fund ($21,600), in contributions reported to the Federal Election Commission.

blkbcantonalbank.what: The cantonal bank of Basel-Landschaft, founded in 1864 as a public-law institution with its seat in Liestal, whose liabilities the canton guarantees by law.
blkbcantonalbank.money: Retail banking, mortgages, private banking and lending to small and medium-sized firms, with an annual profit of CHF 130.2 million in 2022.
blkbcantonalbank.arts: Its sponsorship has two themes, art and culture and nature and leisure, and it has a foundation for culture and education.

bloomberg.money: Bloomberg’s money comes from Bloomberg L.P., Michael Bloomberg’s financial data and media company; Bloomberg Philanthropies gives it away.

facts.t: Bloomberg L.P. declared EU lobbying costs of €600,000 to €699,999 for 2025, with 3.7 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.
Bloomberg L.P. reported $400,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.
One outside firm reported $460,000 in 2025 fees from Bloomberg Philanthropies for US federal lobbying, under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

Michael Bloomberg gave $50,421,147 in personal contributions to federal candidates, parties and PACs in the 2023 to 2024 cycle; the largest went to FF PAC ($19,000,000), HMP ($13,000,000) and Everytown-Demand a Seat PAC ($7,000,000), in contributions reported to the Federal Election Commission.

blount.what: A Portland saw chain maker founded by Joseph Buford Cox in 1947, bought by Winton M. Blount's Blount Industries in 1985 and called Blount, Inc. until 2021.
blount.money: Sales of saw chain and other equipment for the forestry, agriculture and construction industries.

bmo.money: BMO’s money comes from banking, wealth management and capital markets in Canada and the United States.

facts.t: InfluenceMap gives BMO a C grade for its climate finance policy engagement.
BMO reported $1,200,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.
BMO’s federal PAC (Good Governance Fund) gave $187,000 to federal candidates in the 2023 to 2024 cycle, 40% to Republicans and 60% to Democrats, in its reports to the Federal Election Commission.

bmofinancial.what: Canada's oldest bank, founded in Montreal in 1817, with its operating headquarters in Toronto, listed in Toronto and New York.
bmofinancial.money: Banking, wealth management and capital markets, with revenue of CA$36.27 billion and net income of CA$8.73 billion in 2025.

bmoharris.what: A US national bank headquartered in Chicago, founded in 1882 as N.W. Harris & Co., owned by the Bank of Montreal since 1984 and called BMO Harris Bank until 2023.
bmoharris.money: Consumer, corporate, private and investment banking, mortgages, cards and wealth management in the United States.

bmw.money: BMW’s money comes from making and financing cars and motorcycles.

facts.t: BMW declared EU lobbying costs of €2,000,000 to €2,249,999 for 2025, with 9.25 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.
InfluenceMap gives BMW a C- grade for its climate policy engagement.
BMW of North America reported $1,270,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

bmwculturalpartnerships.what: A German maker of cars and motorcycles under the BMW, Mini and Rolls-Royce brands, founded in 1916 and headquartered in Munich.
bmwculturalpartnerships.money: Vehicle sales and financing, with revenue of €133.5 billion in 2025, in a group where Stefan Quandt holds 27.7% and Susanne Klatten 22.5%.
bmwculturalpartnerships.arts: It has run cultural programmes for over half a century, including the BMW Art Cars since 1975, in contemporary art, music, film and design.

bmwpartneredopencall.what: A German maker of cars and motorcycles under the BMW, Mini and Rolls-Royce brands, founded in 1916 and headquartered in Munich.
bmwpartneredopencall.money: Vehicle sales and financing, with revenue of €133.5 billion in 2025, in a group where Stefan Quandt holds 27.7% and Susanne Klatten 22.5%.
bmwpartneredopencall.arts: It has run cultural programmes for over half a century, including the BMW Art Cars since 1975, in contemporary art, music, film and design.

bndes.what: Brazil's national development bank, a federal public company created by law in 1952 and owned by the Brazilian government, with its seat in Rio de Janeiro.
bndes.money: Returns on its loans, Fundo de Amparo ao Trabalhador money and equity income: R$ 122.2 billion, R$ 23.3 billion and R$ 8.8 billion in 2023.

bnkbusanbank.what: A South Korean regional bank founded in 1967 and based in Busan, part of BNK Financial Group, launched in 2011 as BS Financial Group.
bnkbusanbank.money: Retail banking and foreign exchange through about 229 branches in Korea.

bnkkyongnambank.what: A South Korean regional bank serving South Gyeongsang and Ulsan, opened in 1970, wholly owned by BNK Financial Group since 2015, with its head office in Changwon.
bnkkyongnambank.money: Interest and fees from regional banking, with net profit of ₩210.5 billion and total assets of ₩34.6 trillion in 2015.

bnpparibas.money: BNP Paribas's money comes from banking: retail banking in France, Belgium and Italy, corporate and investment banking, and insurance and asset management.

facts.t: BNP Paribas reported 2025 net income, group share, of €12,225 million.

In July 2014 BNP Paribas pleaded guilty in US federal court to conspiring to violate US sanctions, a week after agreeing to forfeit about $8.9 billion, for processing billions of dollars for clients in Sudan, Cuba and Iran.
Banking on Climate Chaos 2026 reports that BNP Paribas cut its fossil fuel financing by 27.8% in 2025 compared with 2024.
BNP Paribas declared EU lobbying costs of €1,500,000 to €1,749,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.
BNP Paribas RCC, Inc. reported $340,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

bnpparibasfortis.what: A Belgian bank created in May 2009, when the French group BNP Paribas bought 75% of Fortis Bank from the Belgian Federal Participation and Investment Company.
bnpparibasfortis.money: Banking in Belgium and abroad as a subsidiary of BNP Paribas.

bnz.money: Bank of New Zealand, a retail and business bank owned by National Australia Bank.

facts.t: BNZ reported a statutory net profit of $1,499 million for the year to 30 September 2025.
BNZ pleaded guilty to not properly disclosing overseas currency fees on its cards and was fined $550,000 in the Auckland District Court, agreeing to pay $5 million in compensation.
The Commerce Commission warned BNZ that it had likely breached responsible lending and disclosure duties under the credit contracts law; BNZ had refunded about $3.8 million in interest and fees.

boardchairclaredavis.what: Chairman of the board of the Frank Lloyd Wright House in Ebsworth Park, the non-profit that preserves the Wright house in Kirkwood, Missouri, as a museum and public park.

bodenmann.what: A private foundation in Basel, set up in 1999 by Maja Oeri and her husband Hans U. Bodenmann in memory of their son Laurenz Jakob; it built and manages Schaulager.
bodenmann.money: The private fortune of Maja Oeri, granddaughter of Emanuel Hoffmann, whose father Fritz Hoffmann-La Roche founded the Roche pharmaceutical group in 1896.
bodenmann.arts: It gave CHF 50 million, half the cost, for the Kunstmuseum Basel extension opened in 2016, and funds two art history professorships at the University of Basel.

boeing.what: A US aerospace manufacturer founded in Seattle in 1916 by William E. Boeing, making airliners, military aircraft, rockets, satellites and missiles, with headquarters in Arlington, Virginia.
boeing.money: Sales of commercial airplanes and of defence, space and security products and services: revenue of USD 89.5 billion in 2025.

facts.t: Boeing's revenue was $89,463 million in 2025.

In January 2021 Boeing agreed to pay more than $2.5 billion to settle a US Justice Department fraud conspiracy charge over the 737 MAX, whose two crashes killed 346 people: a $243.6 million fine, $1.77 billion to airlines and a $500 million crash-victim fund.
The Boeing Company reported $11,340,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025 in its Lobbying Disclosure Act reports.
Boeing Belgium SRL declared EU lobbying costs of €800,000 to €899,999 for 2024 to the EU Transparency Register.

boghossian.what: A foundation created in 1992 by the jeweller Robert Boghossian and his sons Jean and Albert, of Armenian origin, based at the Villa Empain in Brussels.
boghossian.money: The Boghossian family of jewellers who created it.
boghossian.arts: In its first fifteen years it worked mainly on the living conditions of young people in Armenia and Lebanon.

bohemiasekt.what: A Czech sparkling wine maker in Starý Plzenec near Plzeň, producing sekt there since 1945; Germany's Henkell group took a qualified majority in the company in 1999.
bohemiasekt.money: Sales of its own sparkling wines and of Henkell Freixenet brands such as Freixenet cava and Mionetto prosecco on the Czech market.

bolognafiere.what: A trade fair company in Bologna, listed on Euronext Growth Milan; in 2022 public shareholders held 52.24%, led by the Comune di Bologna and the city's Chamber of Commerce.
bolognafiere.money: Its exhibition business, about 90 events in 2024, which brought record revenue of €274.1 million and a profit of €3.9 million.

bombardier.money: The Beaudoin-Bombardier family’s money comes from Bombardier and BRP, the companies founded by Joseph-Armand Bombardier that it controls, given through the Fondation J. Armand Bombardier.

bonfils.what: A Denver foundation, tax-exempt since 1967, named for Helen Bonfils (1889 to 1972), who managed The Denver Post and left her estate to the Denver Center for the Performing Arts.
bonfils.money: Investment income: US$907,797 of its US$1,400,833 revenue in the year to June 2025, when it held total assets of US$39,657,792.
bonfils.arts: In 2021 it pledged a US$500,000 matching gift toward the US$36 million renovation of the Bonfils Theatre Complex.

bonnierfamilyfoundermoney.what: A privately held Swedish group founded in 1804 by Gerhard Bonnier and controlled by the Bonnier family, with 175 companies in 15 countries.
bonnierfamilyfoundermoney.money: Media, real estate through Bonnier Fastigheter and investments through Bonnier Capital: EBITA of SEK 2,402 million in 2025.

borismints.what: A Russian businessman, born in 1958, who founded the O1 Group investment company in 2004 and chaired Otkritie Financial Corporation from 2004 to 2013.
borismints.money: His stakes in Otkritie, sold in 2013, and in O1 Properties and the Future Financial Group, sold in 2018.

borusan.money: Borusan’s money comes from Borusan Holding, the Kocabıyık family’s Turkish industrial group, from steel pipe to machinery, logistics, cars and energy.

facts.t: The Borusan Group reported consolidated revenue of ₺257 billion for 2024, 39% growth.

bosch.money: Bosch's money comes from making car parts, industrial technology, power tools and home appliances; the Robert Bosch Stiftung, a foundation, holds most of the company's shares and lives on its dividends.

facts.t: The Bosch Group reported preliminary 2025 sales revenue of 91 billion euros (2024: 90.3 billion euros), with an EBIT margin from operations of around 2 percent.
In May 2019 prosecutors in Stuttgart fined Robert Bosch GmbH 90 million euros for a negligent violation of supervisory obligations over its role in the diesel emissions scandal; Bosch did not appeal.
Robert Bosch GmbH declared EU lobbying costs of €2,250,000 to €2,499,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register, with 12 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.
Robert Bosch Stiftung GmbH declared EU lobbying costs of €100,000 to €199,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register, with 2 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.
Robert Bosch LLC reported $860,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

bouygues.money: Bouygues' money comes from construction (Bouygues Construction, Colas, property), energy and services (Equans), television (TF1) and telecoms (Bouygues Telecom).

facts.t: Bouygues reported 2025 sales of 56.88 billion euros and net profit attributable to the group of 1.14 billion euros.
Bouygues Europe declared EU lobbying costs of €800,000 to €899,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

bp.money: BP’s money comes from producing, refining and trading oil and gas.

facts.t: BP’s underlying replacement cost profit for 2024 was $8.9 billion, down from $13.8 billion in 2023.
BP declared EU lobbying costs of €2,000,000 to €2,249,999 for 2025, with 5.6 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.
InfluenceMap gives BP a C- grade for its climate policy engagement.
In 2015 the US Justice Department announced a civil settlement with BP over the Deepwater Horizon spill worth $20.8 billion.
In December 2023 the British Museum signed a partnership with BP worth £50 million over ten years, funding refurbishment of its buildings.
BP America reported $4,560,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.
BP Corporation North America’s PAC gave $41,500 to federal candidates in the 2023 to 2024 cycle, 75% to Republicans and 25% to Democrats, in its reports to the Federal Election Commission.

bpd.what: A Dutch and German area developer founded in 1946 as Bouwspaarkas Drentsche Gemeenten, headquartered in Amsterdam and wholly owned by Rabobank.
bpd.money: Developing and selling homes and residential areas in the Netherlands and Germany, about 395,000 homes so far.
bpd.arts: Its BPD Cultuurfonds has funded art and culture projects tied to architecture and the built environment for over 35 years, and BPD owns over 1,000 contemporary artworks.

bradesco.what: A Brazilian bank founded by Amador Aguiar in Marília in 1943, headquartered at Cidade de Deus in Osasco, São Paulo state; Brazil's third largest bank by assets.
bradesco.money: Its commercial banking, insurance, pension, annuity and credit card business; revenue was US$35.3 billion in 2025.

facts.t: Bradesco’s recurring net profit rose 20% to R$19.554 billion in 2024.

bramall.what: A grant-making charity (England and Wales number 1121670) set up by Terry Bramall, former chairman of the housebuilder Keepmoat, with a £100 million endowment in 2008.
bramall.money: Terry Bramall's fortune from Keepmoat, sold in 2007 for £783 million; the charity's investments earned £2.43 million in the year to 5 April 2025.
bramall.arts: Promoting the arts is one of its charitable purposes; it spent £7.76 million on charitable activities in the year to 5 April 2025.

brazilianforeignministry|Brazil.what: Brazil's foreign ministry, called Itamaraty after the palace that houses it in Brasília, which advises the president on foreign relations; Mauro Vieira has been minister since January 2023.
brazilianforeignministry|Brazil.arts: Its remit includes the cultural side of Brazil's foreign relations.

brazilsministryofculture|Brazil.what: Brazil's federal culture ministry, created in March 1985 under President José Sarney, abolished three times, most recently in 2019, and re-created on 1 January 2023 under Margareth Menezes.
brazilsministryofculture|Brazil.arts: Its main instrument is the Lei Rouanet of 1991, which lets companies and individuals sponsor culture against up to 4% and 6% of their income tax.

brdgroupesocitgnrale.what: A Romanian bank based in Bucharest, formerly the state Banca Română pentru Dezvoltare, bought by France's Société Générale in 1999, which holds 60.17%.
brdgroupesocitgnrale.money: Commercial, investment and private banking in Romania, with revenue of RON 4.3 billion and net income of RON 1.5 billion in 2025.

brickworks.what: Australia's largest brick manufacturer and building products company, combined with the Sydney investment house Washington H. Soul Pattinson in September 2025.
brickworks.money: Sales of bricks and other building products in Australia and North America, plus industrial property and investments.

britishcolumbiaartscouncil|Canada.what: An agency of the Province of British Columbia, created in 1995 under the Arts Council Act and based in Victoria.
britishcolumbiaartscouncil|Canada.money: The provincial budget, through the Ministry of Tourism, Arts, Culture and Sport.

britishcouncil|Ghana.what: The UK's cultural relations organisation under royal charter, a public corporation and charity sponsored by the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office.
britishcouncil|Ghana.money: Commercial income, 69 per cent of it from English teaching and exams in 2024-25, plus FCDO grant-in-aid of about 15 per cent.

britishcouncil|Pakistan.what: The UK's cultural relations organisation under royal charter, a public corporation and charity sponsored by the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office.
britishcouncil|Pakistan.money: Commercial income, 69 per cent of it from English teaching and exams in 2024-25, plus FCDO grant-in-aid of about 15 per cent.

britishcouncil|UK.what: The UK's cultural relations organisation under royal charter, a public corporation and charity sponsored by the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office.
britishcouncil|UK.money: Commercial income, 69 per cent of it from English teaching and exams in 2024-25, plus FCDO grant-in-aid of about 15 per cent.

britishcouncil|Ukraine.what: The UK's cultural relations organisation under royal charter, a public corporation and charity sponsored by the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office.
britishcouncil|Ukraine.money: Commercial income, 69 per cent of it from English teaching and exams in 2024-25, plus FCDO grant-in-aid of about 15 per cent.

britishfriendsofballetnacionaldecuba.what: A London charity registered on 7 October 2008, under a constitution adopted that February, to support the Ballet Nacional de Cuba.
britishfriendsofballetnacionaldecuba.money: Total income was £8,150 in the year to 31 December 2025.

broad.money: Eli Broad's fortune came from insurance and home construction (KB Home and SunAmerica).

bronfman.money: These ties are the Charles Bronfman branch of the Seagram fortune: the Claudine and Stephen Bronfman family foundation (Stephen is Charles Bronfman’s son, of Claridge) and the Samuel and Saidye Bronfman Family Foundation of Seagram’s founder; not Edgar Bronfman Jr. or Phyllis Lambert.

brotfrdiwelt.what: The worldwide aid agency of Germany's Protestant regional and free churches, part of the Evangelisches Werk für Diakonie und Entwicklung in Berlin.
brotfrdiwelt.money: Federal and church development funds plus donations; of EUR 341.7 million available in 2025, donations and collections gave EUR 72.6 million.

brown.what: A Houston family foundation set up in 1951 by the brothers Herman and George R. Brown and their wives, Margarett Root Brown and Alice Pratt Brown.
brown.money: The Brown brothers' fortune from Brown & Root, the construction firm merged with Halliburton in 1962.
brown.arts: It has distributed more than US$2 billion since 1951, with arts and education among its five areas.

brownforman.what: A family-controlled, publicly traded US spirits and wine company, maker of Jack Daniel's and Woodford Reserve, founded in Louisville, Kentucky, in 1870 by George Garvin Brown.
brownforman.money: Sales of its spirits and wines: revenue of USD 5.37 billion and net income of USD 783 million in the year to April 2025.

brusselscapital.what: One of the three federal regions of Belgium, formed on 18 June 1989; its government is a minister-president and four ministers elected by the regional parliament.
brusselscapital.money: The regional budget, voted by the Brussels Parliament; the government's 2026 budget closes with a deficit of 957 million euros.

buditek.money: Budi Tek was a Chinese-Indonesian entrepreneur and collector; the sources read do not name the business his money came from.

bukharaoil.what: An oil refinery in the Karaulbazar district of Bukhara region, Uzbekistan, opened on 22 August 1997, with capacity for 2.5 million tonnes of crude oil and condensate a year.
bukharaoil.money: Sales of motor gasoline, diesel and aviation kerosene; it made a net profit of 2.2 trillion soums, about US$183.4 million, in January to September 2026.

bukhman.what: A London charity (no. 1205571) set up in 2023 by Igor and Anastasia Bukhman; Igor co-founded the mobile games company Playrix with his brother Dmitry in 2004.
bukhman.money: Donations, £2.55 million of £2.57 million income in the year to March 2025; Igor Bukhman's fortune comes from Playrix.

bulgari.what: An Italian luxury house founded in Rome in 1884 by the silversmith Sotirios Voulgaris, owned by the French group LVMH since 2011.
bulgari.money: Sales of jewellery, watches, fragrances, accessories and leather goods, as part of LVMH.

bulgarianstate|Austria.what: The national government of Bulgaria, whose executive is the Council of Ministers in Sofia, led by Prime Minister Rumen Radev since 8 May 2026.

bundesministeriumfrkunstundkultur.what: The Austrian federal ministry for housing, arts, culture, media and sport in Vienna, led by Vice-Chancellor Andreas Babler; it holds the federal arts and culture brief.
bundesministeriumfrkunstundkultur.arts: Its culture spending was €623.193 million in 2025, 1.47 percent less than in 2024, according to the Kunst- und Kulturbericht 2025.

burdockbrewery.what: A craft brewery in downtown Toronto, brewing since 2015, with a restaurant and music hall on Bloor Street and a tavern in Kensington.
burdockbrewery.money: Sales of its beer online, wholesale and at its own restaurant, tavern and music hall.

burkhardvarnholt.what: A Swiss banker who was chief investment officer of Credit Suisse (Switzerland) and before that of Bank Julius Bär and Bank J. Safra Sarasin.
burkhardvarnholt.arts: He has served on Tate's Africa Acquisitions Committee.

burkinafasoscultureministry|Burkina Faso.what: Burkina Faso's ministry for communication, culture, arts and tourism (MCCAT), headed by Minister Pingdwendé Gilbert Ouédraogo in December 2025.
burkinafasoscultureministry|Burkina Faso.money: The state budget of Burkina Faso.
burkinafasoscultureministry|Burkina Faso.arts: Its events in 2025 included FESPACO, the Nuit des Galian and the Ouagadougou international tourism and hotel fair.

busanmetropolitancity|South Korea.what: The city government of Busan, South Korea's second most populous city, led by Mayor Jeon Jae-soo.
busanmetropolitancity|South Korea.money: Local taxes (5.38 trillion won), national subsidies (7.79 trillion won) and allocation tax in its 19.35 trillion won budget proposed for 2027.

byd.money: BYD makes electric and hybrid cars, among them the Denza brand, as well as batteries and phone components.

facts.t: BYD reported total revenue of 777.102 billion yuan for 2024 and net profit attributable to shareholders of 40.254 billion yuan, up 34%.

In May 2025 Brazilian labour prosecutors sued BYD and two contractors over 220 Chinese workers found in conditions analogous to slavery at its Camaçari plant site, demanding 257 million reais from the three companies.
BYD Motors and its US subsidiaries reported $300,000 of their own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.
BYD European B.V. declared EU lobbying costs of €200,000 to €299,999 a year, with 0.75 full-time-equivalent lobbyists (register as of 12 November 2026).

cabildodetenerife.what: The governing council of the island of Tenerife, set up on 16 March 1913 in Santa Cruz de Tenerife; Rosa Dávila is its president.
cabildodetenerife.money: The Cabildo's budget, €1,278 million consolidated for 2026.

cafesjian.what: A US family foundation in Shoreview, Minnesota, founded by Gerard L. Cafesjian, a former executive vice president of the legal publisher West Publishing, who died in 2013.
cafesjian.money: An endowment from its founder; assets were USD 55.4 million in 2023, when it paid USD 1.67 million in grants.
cafesjian.arts: Its founder also set up the Cafesjian Center for the Arts in Yerevan.

cairnsartgallery.what: The fundraising foundation of Cairns Art Gallery, set up in 2000, registered as a charity with the ACNC and run by a volunteer board of local professionals.
cairnsartgallery.money: Donations it raises, all spent on buying artworks for the gallery's permanent collection.
cairnsartgallery.arts: It has given more than AUD 840,000 toward the purchase of 79 works by 28 artists.

caissedepargnecepac.what: A cooperative savings bank in Groupe BPCE, formed in 1991 and based in Marseille, serving Provence, Corsica and French overseas territories in 13 départements.
caissedepargnecepac.money: Retail and business banking, notably housing, healthcare and energy transition loans, under a cooperative model with about 320,000 member shareholders.
caissedepargnecepac.arts: It spends nearly EUR 6 million a year on average on sponsorship, CSR and microloans, and supports the CEPAC Silo performance hall in Marseille.

californiaartscouncil|United States.what: A California state agency in Sacramento, founded in 1976 under Governor Jerry Brown; the governor and the state legislature appoint its eight council members.
californiaartscouncil|United States.money: State budget funds, plus proceeds of the California Arts License Plate and voluntary contributions.
californiaartscouncil|United States.arts: On 14 August 2026 the council allocated nearly $24.6 million for 1,200 grants to nonprofit organisations and units of government.

californiainstituteofarts.what: A private art school in Santa Clarita, California, formed in 1961 by Walt and Roy Disney through the merger of Chouinard Art Institute and the Los Angeles Conservatory of Music.
californiainstituteofarts.money: Program services brought in $82,980,132 of its $122,015,803 revenue in 2024 to 2025, and contributions $10,472,635.
californiainstituteofarts.arts: With the Herb Alpert Foundation it set up the Alpert Award in the Arts in 1994, a yearly $75,000 fellowship for each of five artists.

caloustegulbenkian.what: A Portuguese foundation set up in Lisbon in 1956 under the will of Calouste Gulbenkian, an Armenian oil magnate; it runs the Gulbenkian Museum and Orchestra.
caloustegulbenkian.money: An endowment from Calouste Gulbenkian's oil fortune; it fully owned the oil company Partex until selling it to a Thai company in 2019.

calq.what: A public agency set up by the Government of Quebec in 1994 to fund professional artists, writers and arts organisations.
calq.money: The Government of Quebec; its 2024-2025 budget for grants and administration was C$191.8 million.
calq.arts: In 2024-2025 it granted more than C$178.6 million, including 2,011 individual grants and support for 900 organisations.

cambridgecitycouncil|UK.what: The district council for the city of Cambridge in Cambridgeshire, England, which meets at Cambridge Guildhall; no party has held overall control since 2026.
cambridgecitycouncil|UK.money: The municipal budget of Cambridge City Council.

camper.what: A Spanish shoe company founded in 1975 in Inca, Mallorca, by Lorenzo Fluxà, grandson of a Mallorcan cobbler, and led by the fourth generation of the Fluxà family.
camper.money: Sales of its shoes, around 4 million pairs a year, through more than 400 stores in 40 countries.

camposfamilyfirmsnutriasia.what: A Philippine food company founded on 1 October 1990 by Joselito D. Campos Jr., son of Unilab founder Jose Yao Campos; based at JY Campos Centre, Taguig.
camposfamilyfirmsnutriasia.money: Sales of sauces, seasonings and cooking oils under brands such as Datu Puti, Mang Tomas, UFC and Silver Swan; it holds Del Monte Pacific.

canada.what: The federal executive of Canada, made up of the Cabinet under Prime Minister Mark Carney and over 103 departments and agencies.

canadacouncilforarts|Canada.what: Canada's public arts funder, a federal Crown corporation set up in 1957 that reports to Parliament through the Minister of Canadian Heritage; based in Ottawa.
canadacouncilforarts|Canada.money: Annual appropriations from the Parliament of Canada, plus income from its endowment, donations and bequests.
canadacouncilforarts|Canada.arts: It also runs the Canada Council Art Bank, which rents out its collection of contemporary Canadian art.

canadalife.what: A Canadian insurer founded in 1847 in Hamilton, combined in 2020 with Great-West Life and London Life, with its head office in Winnipeg.
canadalife.money: Its insurance and wealth business; it is wholly owned by Great-West Lifeco, about 72% owned by Power Financial Corporation.

canadianheritage.what: The Government of Canada's department for arts, culture, broadcasting, official languages and sport, created in 1993 and headquartered in the Jules Léger Building, Gatineau, Quebec.
canadianheritage.money: The federal budget of the Government of Canada: CA$3.89 billion for the department in 2020.

canica.what: The Hagen family's investment company in Oslo, set up in 1985 by Stein Erik Hagen, who died in 2026; Caroline Marie Hagen Kjos has controlled it since May 2026.
canica.money: Returns on its financial, industrial and real estate investments, including 196,351,000 shares in Orkla, of which it is the largest shareholder.
canica.arts: It owns a collection of mainly Nordic 19th and 20th century art, including Asger Jorn and Edvard Munch, and lends works to exhibitions.

canon.what: A Japanese maker of cameras, printers, medical and semiconductor equipment, set up in 1937 as Precision Optical Instruments and headquartered in Shimomaruko, Ōta, Tokyo.
canon.money: Sales of optical, imaging, medical and industrial products worldwide; revenue was ¥4.03 trillion in 2022.

cantonofgeneva.what: One of the 26 cantons of Switzerland, a Swiss canton since 19 May 1815, governed by a Conseil d'État of seven members and a Grand Conseil of 100.
cantonofgeneva.arts: Its Service cantonal de la culture committed 47,805,598 francs in 2025, 14 percent more than in 2024; a culture promotion law has applied since January 2024.

cantonofneuchtel.what: A Swiss canton, a republic since the revolution of 1 March 1848, with a five-member Conseil d'État, a 100-seat Grand Conseil and 180,365 residents at the end of 2025.
cantonofneuchtel.money: The cantonal budget, with operating revenue of CHF 2,444,590,150 for 2026, adopted by the Grand Conseil on 2 December 2025.

cantonofsarajevo.what: The government of Sarajevo Canton, a canton of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina established in 1995, led by a prime minister and a cabinet.

cantonofzurich.what: A Swiss canton that joined the Swiss Confederacy in 1351, governed by a seven-member Regierungsrat and a 180-seat Cantonal Council.
cantonofzurich.money: The cantonal budget, in which the Cantonal Council raised the culture funding budget from 2026.
cantonofzurich.arts: Its Fachstelle Kultur, under the Direktion der Justiz und des Innern, pays operating grants to cultural institutions, as a rule for four years.

canva.money: Canva is a Sydney online design platform sold by subscription.

facts.t: Canva said its annual recurring revenue reached $4 billion by the end of 2025.

caomei.what: Co-founder with her husband, the collector Yan Shijie, of Beijing's Red Brick Art Museum, which opened on 23 May 2014.

capexcellence.what: An intercommunal authority created on 30 December 2008 that joins Pointe-à-Pitre, Les Abymes and Baie-Mahault in Guadeloupe, with 97,888 residents; its president is Eric Jalton.

capital.what: A US private foundation of Capital Group, the privately owned investment manager founded in 1931 by Jonathan Bell Lovelace; its last return on file covers the year to June 2019.
capital.money: Capital Group, which had more than US$3.6 trillion under management on 30 June 2026.
capital.arts: Over 25 years it bought American photographs, including works by Ansel Adams, Edward Curtis, Gordon Parks and Edward Weston, with advice from Stanford's Cantor Arts Center.

carlosslim.money: Carlos Slim’s money comes from telecoms and from Grupo Carso, his industrial, construction and retail group.

facts.t: Grupo Carso had revenues of 202,983 million pesos in 2024, 2.3% above the year before.

The elevated section of Mexico City’s Metro Line 12 that Carso’s builder CICSA built and delivered in 2013 collapsed on 3 May 2021, killing 26 people; in October 2021 CICSA agreed to rehabilitate it while saying it was not responsible.
Carso’s October 2021 agreement with Mexico City over Line 12 includes a fund for the families of the 26 dead and the injured, its amount still under analysis at the time.

carlowcountycouncil|Ireland.what: The local authority of County Carlow, Ireland, governed by the Local Government Act 2001, with 18 elected members and a chief executive, Coilín O'Reilly.
carlowcountycouncil|Ireland.money: Its draft 2026 budget set EUR 83.3 million of spending; the Department of Housing allocated it EUR 9.214 million of local property tax.

carlowleo.what: The County Carlow office in Ireland’s network of 31 Local Enterprise Offices, which advise small businesses and give them grants; it sits in Carlow town.
carlowleo.money: Irish state money through Enterprise Ireland, the agency of the Department of Enterprise, Tourism and Employment that operates the 31 offices.

carlsberg.money: The Carlsberg Foundation, set up by the brewer J.C. Jacobsen in 1876 with shares in his brewery, controls the Carlsberg brewing group; its money, and that of the New Carlsberg Foundation it oversees, comes from the brewery's dividends.

facts.t: Carlsberg Breweries A/S declared EU lobbying costs of €50,000 to €99,999 for its financial year March 2024 to February 2025 to the EU Transparency Register, with 1.3 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.

carolynclarkpowers.what: A Los Angeles philanthropist raised in Tulsa, Oklahoma, who joined the MOCA board in 2009, was its president for seven years and now chairs it.
carolynclarkpowers.arts: She co-chaired the Los Angeles Philharmonic's opening night gala from 2007 to 2012 and co-chairs the Dockery Farms Foundation in Mississippi.

carter.what: A Texas private foundation incorporated in 1945 by Amon G. Carter, publisher of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram, and his wife Nenetta Burton Carter, based in Fort Worth.
carter.money: An endowment seeded in 1947 with $8,511,712 from the sale of the Carters' Wasson Field oil interests; net assets were $553,053,361 in 2024.
carter.arts: Its grants cover art and culture among other fields, and its charitable gifts passed $900 million by 31 December 2025.

cartier.money: Cartier's money comes from selling jewellery and watches; it is the largest house of Compagnie Financière Richemont, which also owns Van Cleef & Arpels.

facts.t: Richemont, Cartier's owner, reported group sales of €21.4 billion for the year to 31 March 2025 and an overall profit for the year of €2.8 billion.
Richemont International SA declared EU lobbying costs of €200,000 to €299,999 for its financial year April 2025 to March 2026 to the EU Transparency Register, with 0.1 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.

casinosaustria.what: An Austrian casino company founded in 1967 and based in Vienna; the Czech group Allwyn is its main shareholder and the state holding ÖBAG holds 33.24%.
casinosaustria.money: Gambling: its casinos and Austrian lotteries business brought gross gaming revenue of €1.56 billion in 2025.

cassaruralealtogarda.what: A cooperative credit bank in Trentino, formed on 1 July 2021 from rural banks dating back to 1892, with over 15,600 members and offices in Arco and Rovereto.
cassaruralealtogarda.money: Its banking business with members and customers.

caterpillar.money: Caterpillar's money comes from making construction and mining machinery, engines and turbines.

facts.t: Caterpillar's revenue was $67,589 million in 2025.
Caterpillar Inc. reported $5,446,800 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025 in its Lobbying Disclosure Act reports.
Caterpillar Distribution Services Europe bv declared EU lobbying costs of €300,000 to €399,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

caterpillarannounced.what: The philanthropic arm of Caterpillar Inc., the construction and mining equipment maker based in Irving, Texas; it has given to more than 11,000 organisations in 110 countries since 1952.
caterpillarannounced.money: Gifts of USD 60.2 million in 2023, according to its IRS return, plus income on assets of USD 194 million.

cattolicaassicurazioni.what: An Italian insurer founded as a cooperative in Verona in 1896, controlled by Generali since 2021 and a division and brand of Generali Italia since July 2023.
cattolicaassicurazioni.money: Insurance premiums, within the Generali group, which held 95.1 percent of the company by July 2022 and delisted it that August.

cavendishfarms.what: A frozen potato processor owned by J.D. Irving, Limited, the New Brunswick group founded in 1882; it is North America's fourth largest processor of frozen potato products.
cavendishfarms.money: Sales of frozen fries, potato products and appetizers from its plants in Canada and the United States.

cbkrotterdam.what: Rotterdam’s centre for visual art, a municipal service until 1 January 2006, when it became an independent foundation with a supervisory board; it runs SIR, BKOR, Art Office and TENT.
cbkrotterdam.money: Subsidies, mainly the City of Rotterdam’s culture plan grant: government subsidies were €4.02 million of its €4.47 million income in 2025.
cbkrotterdam.arts: It gave €969,760 in subsidies and grants in 2025.

ccpar.what: A Rio de Janeiro municipal company for concessions and public-private partnerships, created in June 2022 by Law 251/22, that took over Cdurp, which ran Porto Maravilha.
ccpar.money: The municipality of Rio de Janeiro, its owner.

cemex.what: A Mexican building materials company that began in 1920 as Cementos Portland Monterrey, seated in San Pedro Garza García, Nuevo León.
cemex.money: Sales of cement, ready-mix concrete and aggregates: about USD 13 billion revenue in 2020.
cemex.arts: It gives the Premio CEMEX, an annual award for works in sustainability, accessibility, construction and architecture.

cenovus.money: Cenovus’s money comes from oil sands and conventional oil and gas production and refining; it took over Husky Energy in 2021.

facts.t: Cenovus reported net earnings of $3,930 million for 2025, against $3,142 million in 2024.
Husky Oil Operations Limited, now Cenovus, was sentenced in April 2024 to a total of $2.5 million after pleading guilty over a November 2018 oil spill in the White Rose field off Newfoundland.
InfluenceMap gives Cenovus an E+ grade for its climate policy engagement.
Cenovus US Corporation reported $770,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act (the second quarter as amended).

centurybank.what: A locally owned, state-chartered community bank in Santa Fe, New Mexico, founded in 1887 as the Mutual Building and Loan Association.
centurybank.money: Lending, deposits and wealth management in New Mexico; total assets were USD 1.36 billion on 30 June 2026, according to the FDIC.

cesine.what: A private university centre for business, communication and design in Santander, set up in 1993 and part of the French school group EDH (Écoles Denis-Huisman).
cesine.money: Student fees for its official degrees and for top-up degrees certified by London Metropolitan University.

cfao.what: A French distribution group in Africa for nearly 175 years, now a subsidiary of Japan's Toyota Tsusho Corporation, with headquarters in Boulogne-Billancourt.
cfao.money: Sales of vehicles, medicines, consumer goods and renewable power in 40 African countries; revenue EUR 9.1 billion, 91 percent of it in Africa.
cfao.arts: With Toyota Tsusho it runs the Toyota Tsusho CFAO African Art Award; works by the first edition's five laureates went on show in Japan in 2026.

chadwickloher.what: A private foundation in Minneapolis, Minnesota, tax-exempt since 2003, with John W. Dayton as president and Chadwick L. Dayton as secretary.
chadwickloher.money: Returns on its investments, chiefly asset sales, on net assets of USD 3.85 million at the end of 2024; it gave USD 950,237 that year.

chairedbymiucciaprada.what: An Italian luxury fashion group founded in Milan in 1913 by Mario Prada, listed in Hong Kong, with Miuccia Prada as executive director and Patrizio Bertelli as chairman.
chairedbymiucciaprada.money: Sales of luxury goods under the Prada, Miu Miu, Church's and Versace brands, with net revenues of €5.7 billion in 2025.
chairedbymiucciaprada.arts: The group lists Fondazione Prada, the Milan contemporary art institution active since 1993, among its sponsorships.

chanel.what: A luxury fashion house founded by Coco Chanel in Paris in 1910, privately owned by Alain and Gérard Wertheimer through Chanel Limited of London; its French arm sits in Neuilly-sur-Seine.
chanel.money: Sales of fashion, fragrance and beauty products; revenue was USD 19.3 billion in 2025 and net profit USD 2.9 billion.

facts.t: Chanel declared EU lobbying costs of €900,000 to €999,999 for 2024, its latest closed year on the register, with 1.75 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.
Chanel reported $190,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

chanelforworthexhibition.what: A luxury fashion house founded by Coco Chanel in Paris in 1910, privately owned by Alain and Gérard Wertheimer through Chanel Limited of London; its French arm sits in Neuilly-sur-Seine.
chanelforworthexhibition.money: Sales of fashion, fragrance and beauty products; revenue was USD 19.3 billion in 2025 and net profit USD 2.9 billion.

changwoncity|South Korea.what: The city government of Changwon, capital of South Gyeongsang Province, South Korea, formed when Changwon, Masan and Jinhae merged on 1 July 2010.
changwoncity|South Korea.money: The municipal budget of Changwon, a city of about 1.0 million people.
changwoncity|South Korea.arts: It holds the Changwon Sculpture Biennale in honour of the sculptor Moon Shin.

chariloto.what: A Tokyo company founded in 2006 that sells keirin and auto race betting tickets online and runs velodromes; a wholly owned subsidiary of MIXI since March 2019.
chariloto.money: Betting ticket sales on keirin cycle races and auto races through its Chari-Loto site, plus velodromes it owns or runs, including Toyama and Ito Onsen.

charitiesaid.what: A registered charity that handles giving for donors and companies and owns CAF Bank; it began in 1924 inside the National Council of Social Service and became independent in 1974.
charitiesaid.money: Money that individuals, companies and foundations give through CAF for onward donation: £1.4 billion went to charities through it in 2025/26.

chartwelltrust.money: A charitable trust set up in the early 1970s by Robert Gardiner, then a Hamilton businessman and accountant, to collect contemporary art for public galleries and support the visual arts.

chase.what: A Jamaican company incorporated on 25 November 2002 under the Companies Act, based in Kingston, that funds culture, health, arts, sports and education.
chase.money: Monetary contributions from the lottery companies, which it receives, administers and distributes.
chase.arts: Its culture grants go to libraries, archives, historic sites, monuments, documentary film and cultural activities.

cherylsaban.what: A private grantmaking foundation in Los Angeles, tax exempt since January 2000, with Cheryl Saban as president and Haim Saban as senior vice president.
cherylsaban.money: Contributions received each year, $8,361,756 in 2024, and Haim Saban made his money in children's television and the 2001 sale of Fox Family Worldwide.

chevron.money: Chevron’s money comes from producing, refining and selling oil and gas.

facts.t: Chevron reported net income attributable to the company of $17,661 million for 2024, down from $21,369 million in 2023.
Chevron USA and affiliated companies spent $14,226,941 lobbying California officials in 2024.
InfluenceMap gives Chevron a D- grade for its climate policy engagement.
Chevron Belgium declared EU lobbying costs of €800,000 to €899,999 for 2025, with 1.75 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.
Chevron U.S.A. reported $7,960,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.
The Chevron Employees PAC gave $1,049,500 to federal candidates in the 2023 to 2024 cycle, 89% to Republicans and 9% to Democrats, in its reports to the Federal Election Commission.

chewsculture.money: The foundation's money is Chiu Tsai-hsing's own, made in electronics companies he founded in the 1970s and early 1980s, as the record gives it from Money Weekly (2012).

chinaminshengbank.what: A Chinese commercial bank founded on 12 January 1996 by Jing Shuping as the first bank set up with private-sector shareholders, listed in Shanghai and Hong Kong.
chinaminshengbank.money: Its banking business: operating income of CNY 137.4 billion and total assets of CNY 7.64 trillion in 2023.

christchurchartgalleryraisesacquisition.what: A charitable trust registered in 2008 as the CAG Artworks Trust to support Christchurch Art Gallery Te Puna o Waiwhetū, renamed in 2014 and again in 2024.
christchurchartgalleryraisesacquisition.money: Donations, partner gifts, gala dinners and auctions; its income was NZ$541,789 in the year to March 2026.
christchurchartgalleryraisesacquisition.arts: It funded Martin Creed's Work No. 2314 and helped buy Bill Hammond's Bone Yard Open Home for the gallery collection.

christensveaas.what: A private investment company set up in 1998 and owned by the Norwegian investor Christen Sveaas, managed from Oslo.
christensveaas.money: Returns on its stakes in offshore, shipping, financial services, technology and real estate companies, mainly in Europe.

christensveaasart.what: A Norwegian foundation set up in October 2019 by Christen Sveaas, owner of the investment company Kistefos AS, to manage, protect and lend his art collection.
christensveaasart.money: Gifts from Christen Sveaas: about 800 works from his private collection in 2020, with later donations taking the total past 850.

christianboros.what: A German media entrepreneur and art collector, born in 1964 in Zabrze, who founded the Boros Agentur für Kommunikation in 1990 and co-founded the publisher Distanz Verlag in 2010.
christianboros.arts: He and Karen Boros won the 2024 Art Cologne Prize.

chubb.what: An insurer incorporated and headquartered in Zurich and listed on the New York Stock Exchange, founded as ACE Limited in Bermuda in 1985.
chubb.money: Premiums and investment income from property, casualty, accident, health, reinsurance and life insurance; revenue was US$59.4 billion in 2025.

chugokubank.what: A regional bank founded in Okayama on 21 December 1930, a subsidiary since October 2022 of the holding company Chugin Financial Group.
chugokubank.money: Banking; Chugin Financial Group reported total assets of ¥10.76 trillion and deposits of ¥8.31 trillion for 2024.

churchilldownsincorporated.what: A US racing, casino and online wagering company based in Louisville, Kentucky, which grew from the Churchill Downs racetrack, opened in 1875 as home of the Kentucky Derby.
churchilldownsincorporated.money: Its racetracks, casinos and the online wagering service TwinSpires: revenue of USD 2.93 billion in 2025.

cibc.money: CIBC’s money comes from personal, commercial and wealth banking in Canada and the United States, and capital markets.

facts.t: CIBC reported net income of $8.5 billion for the year ended 31 October 2025.

cincinnatimuseumassociation.what: A nonprofit corporation incorporated in Cincinnati in 1881, after the work of the Women's Art Museum Association, to run the Cincinnati Art Museum in Eden Park.
cincinnatimuseumassociation.money: Contributions of $15.6 million and investment income of $8.8 million made up most of its $29.5 million revenue in the year to August 2025.

citi.money: Citi's money comes from Citigroup's banking: consumer and corporate banking, markets and wealth management.

facts.t: Citigroup's revenue was $75,716 million in 2025.

In July 2024 the Federal Reserve Board fined Citigroup $60.6 million for violating its 2020 enforcement action, citing insufficient progress on data quality management; with the Comptroller of the Currency the penalties totalled about $135.6 million.
Citigroup Washington, Inc. reported $5,360,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025 in its Lobbying Disclosure Act reports.
Citigroup Inc. declared EU lobbying costs of €800,000 to €899,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

citibank.what: An American bank holding company in New York, formed in 1998 by merging Citicorp, parent of Citibank (chartered 1812), with Travelers.
citibank.money: Banking and financial services; it is the third-largest US banking institution by assets.

citifm.what: A private radio station in Accra that began broadcasting on 5 November 2004, founded by Nik Amarteifio and led by managing director Samuel Attah-Mensah.
citifm.money: It is owned and run by Omni Media Ltd, which also operates the news site Citinewsroom.com.

cittmetropolitana.what: The metropolitan city of Florence, a local authority of 41 municipalities in Tuscany that replaced the Province of Florence on 1 January 2015 under Law 56/2014.
cittmetropolitana.money: The budget of the Città metropolitana di Firenze.

cittmetropolitanadibari.what: A local authority of 41 comuni in Apulia that replaced the Province of Bari on 1 January 2015; its metropolitan mayor is Vito Leccese, mayor of Bari.
cittmetropolitanadibari.money: The budget of the Città Metropolitana di Bari.

citybridge|UK.what: The working name of Bridge House Estates, a London charity established by royal charter in 1282 to maintain London Bridge; its sole trustee is the City of London Corporation.
citybridge|UK.money: Income from its property and investment endowment: £31.2 million of £42.6 million income in the year to March 2025.

citygovernment|aros.what: The municipality of Aarhus in the Central Denmark Region, run by a city council of 31 members under a magistrate system; Anders Winnerskjold is mayor.
citygovernment|aros.money: The municipal budget of Aarhus, set by the city council.

citygovernment|dundee-contemporary-arts.what: The local authority for Dundee City, one of the 32 council areas of Scotland, created in its modern form in 1996.
citygovernment|dundee-contemporary-arts.money: A revenue budget of £502 million for 2026 to 2027; council tax funds 18 percent of the budget.

citygovernment|kamloops-art-gallery.what: The municipal government of Kamloops, British Columbia, a city incorporated in 1893 and amalgamated in 1973, run by an elected city council.
citygovernment|kamloops-art-gallery.money: Property taxes collected from homeowners each July, set through a yearly budget and five-year financial plan, with utilities on separate budgets.

citygovernment|kunsthalle-mannheim.what: The city government of Mannheim, an urban district of 319,536 inhabitants (31 December 2025) in Baden-Württemberg and the state's second most populous city.
citygovernment|kunsthalle-mannheim.money: The municipal budget, with ordinary revenue of 1,646,343,951 euros planned for 2026 after a second supplementary budget cut it by 82 million euros.
citygovernment|kunsthalle-mannheim.arts: The Kunsthalle Mannheim, founded for the city's 300th anniversary in 1907, is one of its municipal enterprises (Eigenbetriebe).

citygovernment|spike-island-bristol.what: The local authority for Bristol, a unitary authority since 1996, based at City Hall on College Green; the Green Party has been its largest party since the 2024 election.
citygovernment|spike-island-bristol.money: Council tax, business rates, government grants and fees: council tax gives £316.54 million of the £634.1 million net revenue budget for 2026 to 2027.

cityofamsterdam|Netherlands.what: The municipality of Amsterdam, the Dutch capital, governed by an elected city council and an executive of mayor and aldermen from the city hall at Amstel 1.
cityofamsterdam|Netherlands.money: Its municipal budget: income forecast at €7.75 billion for 2026, down from €8.1 billion, partly because the national government gives municipalities less.
cityofamsterdam|Netherlands.arts: Its 2026 budget set aside €28.5 million for the Amsterdam Museum's renovation and €3.2 million for H'ART Museum.

cityofatlanta|USA.what: An office of the Mayor of Atlanta, established in 1974 to support the city's cultural resources.
cityofatlanta|USA.money: The City of Atlanta's municipal budget.
cityofatlanta|USA.arts: It runs the Municipal Support for the Arts grants, the Public Art Program, the Atlanta Jazz Festival and the Chastain Arts Center.

cityofavignon|France.what: The commune of Avignon, prefecture of the Vaucluse department in Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, with 92,188 residents in 2023.

cityofballarat|Australia.what: The local council for Ballarat in western Victoria, formed on 6 May 1994 by merging the City of Ballaarat, the Shire of Ballarat and the Borough of Sebastopol.
cityofballarat|Australia.money: Property rates and charges, calculated from property valuations and limited by the Victorian Government's rate cap.
cityofballarat|Australia.arts: It has owned the Art Gallery of Ballarat since 1977 and pays its operating costs.

cityofbergamo|Italy.what: The municipal government of Bergamo, the fourth largest city in Lombardy, led by Mayor Elena Carnevali.
cityofbergamo|Italy.money: The Comune di Bergamo's municipal budget.
cityofbergamo|Italy.arts: With TenarisDalmine it is a founding member of GAMeC, the public-private gallery of modern and contemporary art that opened in 1991.

cityofbielefeld|Germany.what: The city of Bielefeld, a public-law corporation in North Rhine-Westphalia and the largest city of Ostwestfalen-Lippe, with 331,419 residents at the end of 2025.
cityofbielefeld|Germany.money: The municipal budget of the city of Bielefeld.

cityofbilbao|Spain.what: The city council of Bilbao, made up of the mayor, a governing board and a municipal plenary, with its seat at Bilbao City Hall on Plaza Ernesto Erkoreka.
cityofbilbao|Spain.money: The municipal budget: 751 million euros for 2026, 32 million more than in 2025, approved without new debt.
cityofbilbao|Spain.arts: Its 2026 budget plan gives the culture directorate 49,817,713 euros; Teatro Arriaga receives 8.1 million euros and Bilbaoarte 1,068,356 euros.

cityofbrno|Czechia.what: The statutory city of Brno, the Czech Republic's second-largest city with 404,296 inhabitants on 1 January 2026, run from the Magistrát města Brna in the South Moravian Region.

cityofbrussels|Belgium.what: The municipal government of the City of Brussels, capital of Belgium and the largest municipality of the Brussels-Capital Region, with 196,828 inhabitants in January 2024.
cityofbrussels|Belgium.money: The city budget: more than EUR 1.1 billion of ordinary spending in 2025, with tax revenue of EUR 455.9 million as its largest source.

cityofcologne|Germany.what: The city of Cologne, represented by Lord Mayor Torsten Burmester, with its seat at the Historisches Rathaus.

cityofcopenhagen|Denmark.what: Denmark's most populous municipality, covering central Copenhagen, with 673,575 residents in March 2026.
cityofcopenhagen|Denmark.money: The municipal budget, which the parties at City Hall agree each year.
cityofcopenhagen|Denmark.arts: The 2027 budget agreement sets aside DKK 19.3 million over three years for a partnership programme for the city's cultural life.

cityofdallas|USA.what: The municipal government of Dallas, Texas, run under a council-manager system with a 14-member city council.
cityofdallas|USA.money: Property taxes and other city revenue: a FY 2025-26 budget of US$5.20 billion, of which the General Fund is US$1.9 billion.

cityofdarebin|Australia.what: The local council for Darebin in Melbourne's northern suburbs, formed in 1994 by merging most of the former Cities of Northcote and Preston.
cityofdarebin|Australia.money: Rates and charges, which made up 65% of its A$243.01 million revenue in 2024-25.

cityofdenver|USA.what: The consolidated city and county government of Denver, Colorado, with an elected mayor and a 13-member city council.
cityofdenver|USA.money: Its General Fund, led by sales tax revenue, projected at US$1.68 billion for 2027.

cityofdetroit|USA.what: The city government of Detroit, Michigan's most populous city and the county seat of Wayne County, with 639,111 residents at the 2020 census.

cityofdornbirn|Austria.what: The municipal government of Dornbirn, the most populous town in the Austrian state of Vorarlberg.
cityofdornbirn|Austria.money: The municipal budget of Dornbirn, which plans income of EUR 256.94 million for 2026.
cityofdornbirn|Austria.arts: It gives culture grants within the funds set aside in its annual budget.

cityofdortmund|Germany.what: The city government of Dortmund, an independent city of 600,880 inhabitants (31 December 2025) in North Rhine-Westphalia and the largest city of the Ruhr.
cityofdortmund|Germany.money: The municipal budget, which the city council set as a two-year plan for 2025 and 2026 on 12 December 2024.
cityofdortmund|Germany.arts: Its municipal enterprise Kulturbetriebe Dortmund has run the city's museums, libraries and culture office since 1995; its 2027 plan foresees a city subsidy of 86.6 million euros.

cityofdresden|Germany.what: The city of Dresden, capital of Saxony, with 562,764 residents at the end of 2025; Dirk Hilbert has been its mayor since 2015.

cityofdsseldorf|Germany.what: The municipal government of Düsseldorf, capital of the German state of North Rhine-Westphalia.
cityofdsseldorf|Germany.arts: Its Kulturamt gives grants for visual art, literature, music, performing arts and cultural education, and awards the city's Förderpreise.

cityofedinburghcouncil|UK.what: The unitary local authority for the City of Edinburgh, in its current form since 1996, with administrative headquarters at Waverley Court since 2007.
cityofedinburghcouncil|UK.money: Government grants (45.6%), non-domestic rates (27.6%) and council tax (26.8%) fund its £1,454.3 million budget for 2025/26.

cityofespoo|Finland.what: The municipal government of Espoo, Finland's second most populous municipality, west of Helsinki in Uusimaa; EMMA Espoo Museum of Modern Art is one of its units.
cityofespoo|Finland.money: Municipal income tax, set at 5.3% for 2026, and real estate tax; tax funding is estimated at about EUR 1,365 million for 2026.

cityofessen|Germany.what: Essen, a city in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany, with 573,618 residents at the end of 2025, led by Lord Mayor Thomas Kufen since 21 October 2015.
cityofessen|Germany.money: The municipal budget of the city of Essen.
cityofessen|Germany.arts: In 1922 the city and Essen citizens jointly bought the Folkwang collection, the founding collection of the Museum Folkwang.

cityoffortworth|USA.what: The city government of Fort Worth, Texas, the county seat of Tarrant County, founded as an army outpost in 1849, with an estimated 1,028,117 residents in 2025.
cityoffortworth|USA.money: The municipal budget of Fort Worth.

cityoffrankfurtcultureoffice|Germany.what: The culture office of the City of Frankfurt am Main, which takes applications for the city's arts grants, under the city's culture and science department.
cityoffrankfurtcultureoffice|Germany.money: The municipal budget of the City of Frankfurt am Main.

cityoffribourg|Switzerland.what: The communal government of Fribourg, Switzerland, led by a five-member full-time Conseil communal under a syndic, with an 80-member Conseil général as its assembly.
cityoffribourg|Switzerland.money: The communal budget, fed by taxes on residents and companies; the Conseil général approved the 2026 budget on 9 and 10 December 2025.

cityofgeneva|Switzerland.what: The municipal government of Geneva, Switzerland, with a five-member Conseil administratif as executive and an elected Conseil municipal as assembly.
cityofgeneva|Switzerland.money: The city budget voted by the Conseil municipal: CHF 1.4 billion of spending and a CHF 69.9 million deficit for 2026.

cityofghent|Belgium.what: The municipal government of Ghent, capital of East Flanders and Belgium's second-largest municipality, with 270,473 inhabitants at the end of 2024; Mathias De Clercq is mayor.
cityofghent|Belgium.money: The Flemish Municipal Fund and the city's surcharges on personal income tax and property tax, which it names as its main income.

cityofgranada|Nicaragua.what: The municipal government of Granada, capital of Nicaragua's Granada Department, a city founded on 21 April 1524 by Francisco Hernández de Córdoba; the municipality had 134,104 people in 2022.

cityofgraz|Austria.what: The city government of Graz, capital of the Austrian state of Styria and Austria's second largest city.
cityofgraz|Austria.arts: It spent EUR 59,336,360 on culture in 2024, which was 3.7% of all city spending.

cityofgreatergeelong|Australia.what: The local council for Geelong and the Bellarine in Victoria, formed in 1993 by amalgamating the City of Geelong with neighbouring cities and shires.
cityofgreatergeelong|Australia.money: Rates and charges, 46.9% of its budgeted A$728.0 million revenue for 2025-26, with operating grants supplying 10.7%.

cityofhague|Netherlands.what: The municipality of The Hague, seat of the Dutch government and capital of South Holland, run by an elected council and a college of mayor and aldermen.
cityofhague|Netherlands.money: The municipal budget, funded mainly by Dutch state payments from the Gemeentefonds and specific grants, plus local taxes.
cityofhague|Netherlands.arts: Its Meerjarenbeleidsplan Kunst en Cultuur for 2025 to 2028 has a total budget of €71.7 million; the college of mayor and aldermen adopted it in September 2024.

cityofhamilton|Canada.what: The municipal government of Hamilton, Ontario, a port city on Lake Ontario whose current boundaries date from an amalgamation on 1 January 2001.
cityofhamilton|Canada.money: Property taxes; its adopted 2025 tax-supported budget of $2.4 billion raised the average residential tax bill by 5.61%.

cityofhelsinki|Finland.what: The municipal government of Helsinki, Finland's capital, led by an 85-seat City Council; it is the only Finnish municipality that runs social, health and rescue services.
cityofhelsinki|Finland.money: Municipal income and property taxes; central government funds its social, health and rescue division. Municipal operating revenue was €1,383 million in 2025.

cityofhiroshima|Japan.what: The municipal government of Hiroshima, capital of Hiroshima Prefecture, led by Mayor Kazumi Matsui since April 2011.
cityofhiroshima|Japan.money: City taxes of ¥262.8 billion and national local allocation tax of ¥78.0 billion help fund its fiscal 2025 general account of ¥722.9 billion.

cityofjohannesburg|South Africa.what: The metropolitan municipality that governs Johannesburg, South Africa's largest city.
cityofjohannesburg|South Africa.money: The municipal budget of the City of Johannesburg.

cityofjrvenp|Finland.what: The town of Järvenpää in Uusimaa, about 37 km north of Helsinki, a full town since 1967, with 46,944 residents at the end of 2025.

cityofkarlsruhedepartmentofculturalaffai.what: The culture office of the City of Karlsruhe, the third largest city in Baden-Württemberg, whose Kulturbüro department handles culture grants.
cityofkarlsruhedepartmentofculturalaffai.money: The municipal budget of Karlsruhe, set by the city council.
cityofkarlsruhedepartmentofculturalaffai.arts: Its Kulturbüro gives project grants on application to artists from every art form.

cityoflausanne|Switzerland.what: The city of Lausanne, capital of the canton of Vaud on Lake Geneva, with 145,596 residents at the end of 2025.

cityoflehavre|France.what: The commune of Le Havre, a port city and subprefecture of the Seine-Maritime department in Normandy, on the Seine estuary, with France's largest container port.
cityoflehavre|France.money: The municipal budget of Le Havre.

cityofleipzig|Germany.what: The city of Leipzig, a public-law corporation headed by its Oberbürgermeister and the most populous city in Saxony, with 633,592 residents at the end of 2025.

cityoflille|France.what: The city of Lille, capital of the Hauts-de-France region and prefecture of the Nord department, with 238,246 residents in 2023.

cityoflinz|Austria.what: The statutory city of Linz, capital of Upper Austria and Austria's third-largest city, with 214,272 residents on 1 January 2026.

cityofljubljana|Slovenia.what: The City Municipality of Ljubljana, the local government of Slovenia's capital, led by Mayor Zoran Janković.

cityoflondonfunding|United Kingdom.what: The municipal governing body of the City of London, based at Guildhall, with a Lord Mayor, a Court of Aldermen and a Court of Common Council.
cityoflondonfunding|United Kingdom.money: Three funds: the City Fund of grants, business rates and council tax, the City's Estate endowment of property income, and the City Bridge Foundation charity.
cityoflondonfunding|United Kingdom.arts: City's Estate pays for the Guildhall School of Music & Drama, and City Bridge Foundation has made grants from its investment portfolio since 1995.

cityoflondon|United Kingdom.what: The municipal governing body of the City of London, based at Guildhall, with a Lord Mayor, a Court of Aldermen and a Court of Common Council.
cityoflondon|United Kingdom.money: Three funds: the City Fund of grants, business rates and council tax, the City's Estate endowment of property income, and the City Bridge Foundation charity.
cityoflondon|United Kingdom.arts: City's Estate pays for the Guildhall School of Music & Drama, and City Bridge Foundation has made grants from its investment portfolio since 1995.

cityofmainz|Germany.what: The city government of Mainz, capital of the German state of Rhineland-Palatinate and its largest city.
cityofmainz|Germany.arts: It gave institutions and cultural initiatives EUR 17,055,265 in institutional funding in 2025.

cityofmalm|Sweden.what: The municipality of Malmö, Sweden's third-largest city and seat of Skåne County, with 365,644 residents in 2024.

cityofmechelen|Belgium.what: The city government of Mechelen in the Belgian province of Antwerp, a city of 90,355 inhabitants on 1 January 2026 and the sixth largest in Flanders.
cityofmechelen|Belgium.money: Local taxes and fees, which brought in 1,211 euros per inhabitant from residents and businesses at the end of 2024.

cityofmelbourne|Australia.what: The local government area for inner Melbourne, Victoria, governed by Melbourne City Council from Melbourne Town Hall, with Nicholas Reece as Lord Mayor since July 2024.
cityofmelbourne|Australia.money: The municipal budget of the City of Melbourne.

cityofmnchengladbach|Germany.what: Mönchengladbach's city government: an independent city (kreisfreie Stadt) in North Rhine-Westphalia with 267,176 inhabitants at the end of 2025, led by Lord Mayor Felix Heinrichs.

cityofmontbliard|France.what: The municipal government of Montbéliard, a sub-prefecture of the Doubs with 24,672 inhabitants in 2023 and the seat of Pays de Montbéliard Agglomération.
cityofmontbliard|France.money: The municipal budget: €56,035,290 of revenue in 2018, of which local taxes brought €14,270,000 (33%).

cityofnancy|France.what: The commune of Nancy, prefecture of the Meurthe-et-Moselle department in the Grand Est region, with 104,387 residents in 2022.

cityofnice|France.what: The city of Nice on the French Riviera, prefecture of the Alpes-Maritimes department in the Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur region.

cityofnorfolk|USA.what: The government of Norfolk, an independent city in Virginia that belongs to no county, with 238,005 residents at the 2020 census; Kenny Alexander is its mayor.

cityofoaklandsubsidy|USA.what: The municipal government of Oakland, a charter city incorporated on 4 May 1852 and the seat of Alameda County, California.
cityofoaklandsubsidy|USA.money: The City of Oakland's municipal budget.
cityofoaklandsubsidy|USA.arts: It owns the Oakland Museum of California's buildings and collection, and planned to cut yearly museum operating spending from $6.5 million to $3 million after a nonprofit took over management.

cityofoslo|Norway.what: The municipality of Oslo, Norway's capital, which carries both municipal and county functions and is run on a parliamentary model with a city government (byråd).
cityofoslo|Norway.money: The city budget, adopted for 2026 by the city council on 11 December 2025 and later adjusted for higher tax revenue.
cityofoslo|Norway.arts: Its culture agency Kulturetaten gives grants and stipends for art and culture and runs the Vigeland Museum and the city's art collection.

cityofparis|France.what: The municipal government of Paris, run by the Council of Paris and its Mayor, with the powers of both a commune and a département.
cityofparis|France.money: The City of Paris budget voted by the Council of Paris, which pays for culture mainly from operating spending.

cityofperth|Australia.what: The local government for central Perth, the capital of Western Australia; it took in part of the City of Subiaco on 1 July 2016.
cityofperth|Australia.money: Rates, fees and charges, interest, reserves, loans and government grants fund its A$303 million budget for 2025-26.

cityofphiladelphia|USA.what: The city government of Philadelphia, founded by William Penn in 1682 and the most populous city in Pennsylvania, with 1.60 million residents at the 2020 census.

cityofpoitiers|France.what: Poitiers's city government; the city is the prefecture of the Vienne department in Nouvelle-Aquitaine and a university city of 90,899 inhabitants in 2025.

cityofreykjavk|Iceland.what: The municipal government of Reykjavík, Iceland's capital, run by a 23-member City Council elected for four-year terms.
cityofreykjavk|Iceland.money: The city budget set by the City Council; the 2025 budget, approved on 3 December 2024, planned a surplus of nearly ISK 1.3 billion.

cityofsanfrancisco|USA.what: The only consolidated city-county in California, governed by a strong mayor and the Board of Supervisors.
cityofsanfrancisco|USA.money: The city and county budget, about US$15.9 billion in fiscal 2024-25.

cityofsarajevo|Bosnia and Herzegovina.what: The city government of Sarajevo, capital of Bosnia and Herzegovina, covering the municipalities of Centar, Novi Grad, Novo Sarajevo and Stari Grad, with a City Council and mayor.
cityofsarajevo|Bosnia and Herzegovina.money: The City of Sarajevo's annual budget, adopted by the City Council.
cityofsarajevo|Bosnia and Herzegovina.arts: Its policy for the current council term makes completing the Ars Aevi museum a special focus of its museum infrastructure work.

cityofstockholm|Sweden.what: The municipal government of Stockholm, Sweden's most populous municipality, run by a 101-member municipal assembly elected every four years.
cityofstockholm|Sweden.money: The city budget adopted by the municipal assembly.

cityofstuttgart|Germany.what: The city government of Stuttgart, capital of the German state of Baden-Württemberg, with its council and administration seated at the Rathaus on Marktplatz.
cityofstuttgart|Germany.money: The city budget: EUR 10.6 billion for 2026 and 2027 together, an austerity budget financed by taxes, fees and new loans.
cityofstuttgart|Germany.arts: On 12 November 2026 the city council adopted, for the first time, overall goals and criteria for its institutional culture funding.

cityofsydney|Australia.what: The local government for Sydney's central business district and inner suburbs, set up by an Act of Parliament in 1842 and governed under the City of Sydney Act 1988.
cityofsydney|Australia.money: Rates and annual charges of A$442.8 million, within budgeted operating income of A$748.5 million for 2025-26.
cityofsydney|Australia.arts: Its 2025-26 budget gives A$10.9 million to community accommodation grants and in-kind support such as venue hire.

cityoftoronto|Canada.what: The city government of Toronto, Canada's most populous city and capital of Ontario, with 2,794,356 residents in the 2021 census.
cityoftoronto|Canada.money: The municipal budget of the City of Toronto.

cityofturinculturaldepartment|Italy.what: The municipality of Turin, capital of Piedmont, with its seat at Piazza Palazzo di Città; Stefano Lo Russo has been mayor since 27 October 2021.
cityofturinculturaldepartment|Italy.money: The municipal budget; its 2025 to 2027 plan repays a deficit of 577,654,134 euros at 66,980,863 euros a year.
cityofturinculturaldepartment|Italy.arts: The 2025 to 2027 budget sets current spending on culture, events, sport, tourism and commerce at 36,406,769 euros for 2025.

cityofutrecht|Netherlands.what: The municipality of Utrecht, capital of Utrecht province and the fourth-largest city in the Netherlands, with 378,140 inhabitants in January 2026.
cityofutrecht|Netherlands.money: The municipal budget, funded mainly by Dutch state payments from the Gemeentefonds and specific grants, plus local taxes.
cityofutrecht|Netherlands.arts: Its Cultuurnota 2025 to 2028 makes €50,162,678 a year available at 2023 prices, including €17,224,048 for four-year grants.

cityofvancouver|Canada.what: The municipal government of Vancouver, British Columbia, run by an elected mayor and ten councillors who serve four-year terms.
cityofvancouver|Canada.money: The City of Vancouver's municipal budget, which its elected council controls.
