expertisefrance.money: Revenue from the cooperation projects it carries out, put at €120 million a year by the economy ministry at its 2015 launch.

exxonmobil.money: ExxonMobil produces and refines oil and gas and makes chemicals; Mobil merged into it in 1999.

facts.t: ExxonMobil reported 2025 earnings of $28.8 billion and cash flow from operations of $52.0 billion.
In May 2022 Massachusetts' Supreme Judicial Court rejected ExxonMobil's bid to dismiss the state's 2019 lawsuit accusing it of misleading the public about climate change, so the case can go forward.
Exxon Mobil Corp reported $8,500,000 in US federal lobbying for 2025 in its own Lobbying Disclosure Act reports.
ExxonMobil Petroleum & Chemical declared EU lobbying costs of €4,000,000 to €4,499,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

exxonmobilqatar.what: The Qatar affiliate of the US oil company Exxon Mobil, a partner of QatarEnergy in gas and LNG joint ventures since the 1980s.
exxonmobilqatar.money: Its shares in nine LNG trains and 27 LNG ships run with QatarEnergy.

fairfieldcountybank|USA.what: A community bank founded in 1871 in Ridgefield, Connecticut, where Ridgefield Savings Bank opened in the Old Hundred building, now the Aldrich Museum.
fairfieldcountybank|USA.money: Deposits, loans and wealth services for Fairfield County clients; the bank gives its size as $1.9 billion.

farrow.what: A British paint and wallpaper maker started in 1946 by the chemists John Farrow and Richard Ball in Wimborne Minster, Dorset; the Danish coatings group Hempel bought it in 2021.
farrow.money: Sales of its paints and wallpapers through its own showrooms and stockists; net income £16.03 million in 2019/2020.

fastretailing.money: Fast Retailing’s money comes from clothing retail, above all Uniqlo, and GU.

facts.t: Fast Retailing reported revenue of 3.4005 trillion yen for the year to August 2025, and operating profit of 564.2 billion yen.

US Customs and Border Protection blocked a January 2021 shipment of Uniqlo shirts under its order on cotton from the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps, over forced-labour concerns, and rejected the company’s protest in May 2021.

fcccommunities.what: A not-for-profit company set up in 1997 as Waste Recycling Environmental and renamed in 2019; it hands out Landfill Communities Fund grants across the UK.
fcccommunities.money: Money from the landfill activities of the waste company FCC Environment and its Severn Waste Services, paid under the Landfill Communities Fund.
fcccommunities.arts: It has granted over £295.5 million to more than 8,680 projects since 1997, including landscaping at the Stourbridge Glass Museum.

fdrationwalloniebruxelles.what: The government of the French Community of Belgium, one of the country's three language communities, established in 1980 and using the name Wallonia-Brussels Federation since 2011.
fdrationwalloniebruxelles.money: Federal transfers: shares of VAT (€9.21 billion) and personal income tax (€3.46 billion), together 94% of its 2025 revenue.

federalgovernmentcommissionerforculture|.what: The German federal government's office for culture and media policy, headed by a Minister of State, currently Wolfram Weimer, with staff in Bonn and Berlin.
federalgovernmentcommissionerforculture|.money: The federal budget: the cabinet set about €2.5 billion for culture and media in 2026.

federalgovernment|smithsonian-air-and-sp.what: The national government of the United States, with legislative, executive and judicial branches under the Constitution in force since 1789, seated in Washington, D.C.
federalgovernment|smithsonian-air-and-sp.money: Federal taxes: individual income taxes gave 51 percent and payroll taxes 35 percent of federal receipts in fiscal 2018.
federalgovernment|smithsonian-air-and-sp.arts: Yearly federal appropriations from Congress pay about two-thirds of the Smithsonian Institution’s budget of about USD 1.25 billion.

federalinbal|Mexico.what: A Mexican federal agency for the arts and arts education, created in 1946 and part of the Secretaría de Cultura since 2015; it sits in the Palacio de Bellas Artes.
federalinbal|Mexico.money: The Mexican federal government, as a deconcentrated body of the Secretaría de Cultura.
federalinbal|Mexico.arts: It runs 29 art schools and, with INAH, protects buildings declared artistic heritage.

federalministryforarts|Austria.what: The Austrian federal ministry for housing, arts, culture, media and sport in Vienna, led by Vice-Chancellor Andreas Babler; it holds the federal arts and culture brief.
federalministryforarts|Austria.arts: Its culture spending was €623.193 million in 2025, 1.47 percent less than in 2024, according to the Kunst- und Kulturbericht 2025.

federalofficeofculture|Switzerland.what: The Swiss federal office for culture policy, cultural funding and heritage, part of the Federal Department of Home Affairs in Bern, led by Carine Bachmann since 2022.
federalofficeofculture|Switzerland.money: The Swiss federal budget, through the Federal Department of Home Affairs.
federalofficeofculture|Switzerland.arts: Its total budget was close to CHF 170 million in 2014.

fentonartstrust.what: A London charitable trust founded in 1986 by Shu-Yao Fenton in memory of her husband Colin, a collector of antiques and pictures.
fentonartstrust.money: An endowment from the founder's estate, the substantial part of which passed to the trust after her death in 2000.
fentonartstrust.arts: It supports thirty to forty beneficiaries a year, all artists at the start of their careers in the creative arts.

ferozegujral.what: A non-profit trust in New Delhi set up in 2008 by Feroze Gujral, a founding patron and trustee of the Kochi-Muziris Biennale, and her husband.
ferozegujral.money: The founders' wealth; the husband, Mohit Gujral, son of the painter Satish Gujral, is an architect and real estate developer.
ferozegujral.arts: It has supported more than 150 artists and 50 exhibitions in India and abroad.

ferragamo.what: An Italian luxury fashion company founded in Florence in 1927 by Salvatore Ferragamo, listed on the Italian stock exchange since 2011 and about 65% owned by the Ferragamo family.
ferragamo.money: Sales of footwear, leather goods, clothing, accessories and perfumes, with revenue of 1,035 million euros in 2024.

ferrerangel.money: The Ferré-Rangel family’s money comes from El Nuevo Día, the Puerto Rican newspaper it owns.

ferroviedellostato.what: Italy's state-owned railway holding company, based in Rome, whose units include Trenitalia, the network manager Rete Ferroviaria Italiana and the road operator ANAS.
ferroviedellostato.money: Its transport, infrastructure and logistics businesses; operating revenue €17.3 billion in 2025, including €9.2 billion from transport services.

fidelity.money: The Johnson family's money comes from Fidelity Investments, the Boston fund manager Edward C. Johnson II founded in 1946; the Fidelity Foundation is its US foundation and the Fidelity UK Foundation that of Fidelity International.

facts.t: Forbes says Fidelity Investments managed discretionary assets of $7.1 trillion as of December 2025, and that Abigail Johnson owns an estimated 29% of the firm.
FMR LLC, Fidelity's parent, reported $2,970,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

fidelityuk.what: An independent grant-making charity for UK non-profit organisations, established by trust deed on 13 July 1988, with its office at Tadworth, Surrey.
fidelityuk.money: Support from Fidelity International since it was established, and income from its own investments.

finlandsministryofeducation|Finland.what: One of Finland's twelve ministries, in charge of education, science, culture, sport and youth; it began as the Ecclesiastical Department in 1809.
finlandsministryofeducation|Finland.money: The Finnish state budget; appropriations for its administrative branch are about €9 billion in 2026.

finnishheritageagency|Finland.what: A Finnish government agency under the Ministry of Education and Culture that preserves the country's material cultural heritage and protects archaeological sites and built heritage.
finnishheritageagency|Finland.arts: In spring 2023 it paid EUR 668,000 in grants toward the exhibition fees of 440 visual artists in 167 exhibitions.

finnishministryofeducation|Finland.what: One of Finland's twelve ministries, in charge of education, science, culture, sport and youth; it began as the Ecclesiastical Department in 1809.
finnishministryofeducation|Finland.money: The Finnish state budget; appropriations for its administrative branch are about €9 billion in 2026.

finnmarkcounty|Norway.what: The regional government of Finnmark county in northern Norway, re-established on 1 January 2024 after four years merged into Troms og Finnmark, with its administration in Vadsø.
finnmarkcounty|Norway.money: The county budget set by its elected county council.
finnmarkcounty|Norway.arts: It runs a culture and cultural heritage service and gives grants to festivals in the county.

firsthorizonbank.what: A regional bank chartered in Memphis in 1864 as First National Bank of Memphis, now the banking unit of NYSE-listed First Horizon Corporation; it merged with IberiaBank in 2020.
firsthorizonbank.money: Banking across 12 southeastern US states; the group reported assets of US$88.7 billion in 2022.

firstpeoplesstaterelations|Australia.what: A group in the Victorian Department of Premier and Cabinet, in Melbourne, that took over the former Aboriginal Victoria; it works on cultural rights, self-determination, treaty and truth.
firstpeoplesstaterelations|Australia.money: The budget of the State of Victoria, through the Department of Premier and Cabinet.

flagart.what: A nonprofit exhibition space in New York, set up as a private operating foundation by the collector Glenn Fuhrman and open to the public since 2008.
flagart.money: Returns on net assets of $24.5 million (2024), mostly asset sales and dividends; Glenn Fuhrman is president and treasurer.
flagart.arts: It runs the Serpentine x FLAG Art Foundation Prize and lends contemporary works from the Fuhrman Family Foundation collection to museums.

flemishcommunity.what: One of Belgium's three language communities, responsible for culture and education in the Dutch-language area and Brussels; the Flemish Government under Matthias Diependaele is its executive.
flemishcommunity.money: The budget of the Flemish Government; its Department of Culture, Youth and Media pays arts subsidies under the Arts Decree.

flemishgovernment|Belgium.what: The executive of the Flemish Community and Flemish Region of Belgium, led by a Minister-President and answerable to the Flemish Parliament.
flemishgovernment|Belgium.money: The Flemish public budget, which its Department of Culture, Youth and Media spends on arts subsidies under the Arts Decree (Kunstendecreet).

fletcher.money: Fletcher Building, a New Zealand building materials and construction group, came out of the Fletcher Challenge conglomerate that the Dunedin listing names.

facts.t: For the year to 30 June 2025 Fletcher Building reported revenue of $7 billion and a net loss of $419 million.
Fletcher Building set aside A$155 million (NZ$168 million) for a settlement over leaking pipes made by its Iplex subsidiary in Western Australian homes, without admitting liability.

florahewlett.what: A US private foundation in Menlo Park, California, set up in 1966 by Hewlett-Packard co-founder Bill Hewlett and his wife Flora.
florahewlett.money: An endowment of about US$13.9 billion at the end of 2024, from the Hewletts' personal gifts; it is independent of HP.
florahewlett.arts: Its Performing Arts programme awarded US$40.5 million in 94 grants in the San Francisco Bay Area in 2024.

florim.what: A ceramic tile maker in Fiorano Modenese, founded by Giovanni Lucchese in 1962 as Floor Gres, run by his son Claudio Lucchese, and a Società Benefit since 2020.
florim.money: Sales of porcelain surfaces for architecture and design: EUR 416 million revenue in 2024.
florim.arts: Its Fondazione Ing. Giovanni Lucchese, set up in 2013, promotes social and cultural projects around Modena.

fnbfirstrand.money: FirstRand’s money comes from banking, through FNB, RMB and WesBank; the Thapong tie is its Botswana arm’s FNB Foundation.

facts.t: FirstRand’s normalised earnings rose 10% to R41.8 billion in the year to June 2025.
In the same year it took a further R2.7 billion pre-tax provision tied to the UK investigation into the vehicle finance market, after R3 billion the year before.

fokal.what: Fondation Connaissance et Liberté, a Haitian national foundation created in 1995 and recognised as of public utility in 2000, working in education, development, arts and civil society.
fokal.money: Mainly the Open Society Foundations, with grants from the Kellogg and Ford foundations, the European Union and the Agence Française de Développement.
fokal.arts: It has run a cultural centre in central Port-au-Prince since 2003.

fonalledas.money: The Fonalledas family’s money comes from Empresas Fonalledas, owner of the Plaza Las Américas shopping centre in San Juan.

fondart.what: A competitive public arts fund of the Chilean government, created in 1992 and administered by the Undersecretariat of Cultures and Arts.
fondart.money: The Chilean state budget through the Ministry of Cultures, Arts and Heritage.

fondazionebancadelmontedilombardia.what: An Italian banking foundation in Pavia, formed in July 1992 under the Amato law when its banking business passed to Banca del Monte di Lombardia S.p.A.
fondazionebancadelmontedilombardia.money: Returns on its endowment and shareholdings; the bank it spun off merged with Cassa di Risparmio di Cuneo into Banca Regionale Europea in 1995.

fondazionecariplo.what: A foundation of banking origin created in Milan in December 1991, when the Amato law split the Cariplo savings bank into this foundation and a commercial bank.
fondazionecariplo.money: Returns on an endowment of 8,207,623,005 euros (2023) built on its stake in the Cariplo bank, which later merged into Intesa Sanpaolo.

fondazionecrfirenze.what: A Florence foundation of banking origin, created in April 1992 when the Cassa di Risparmio di Firenze, a savings bank founded by 100 citizens in 1829, became a company.
fondazionecrfirenze.money: Returns on an endowment of about 2 billion euros inherited from the savings bank, including a holding in Intesa Sanpaolo.
fondazionecrfirenze.arts: Culture is one of its four missions, and its endowment includes an art collection.

fondazionecrt.what: A banking foundation formed in Turin in 1991, when the Cassa di Risparmio di Torino moved its banking business into a separate company; Italy's third-largest by assets.
fondazionecrt.money: Returns on its endowment, inherited from the Cassa di Risparmio di Torino and long including a large UniCredit shareholding.
fondazionecrt.arts: It has given more than 2 billion euros to over 50,000 projects in art, research, training, welfare, environment and innovation.

fondazionedivenezia.what: An Italian banking foundation formed in 1992 when the Cassa di Risparmio di Venezia, founded in 1822, was split into a bank and a foundation.
fondazionedivenezia.money: An endowment from its former ownership of the Cassa di Risparmio di Venezia, now part of Intesa Sanpaolo, in which it held 0.33% in 2013.

fondazionedonnaregina.what: The foundation that runs Madre, the museum of contemporary art in Naples; Angela Tecce is president and Eugenio Viola became director in August 2026.
fondazionedonnaregina.money: Contributions mainly from the Campania Region: €3.4 million in 2021, with €4.7 million expected for 2022, according to Il Sole 24 Ore.

fondazionepasquinelli.what: A private foundation set up in Milan at the end of 2011 by Giuseppina Antognini, its president, in memory of her partner, the Milanese entrepreneur Francesco Pasquinelli.
fondazionepasquinelli.money: The private means of Giuseppina Antognini and the late Francesco Pasquinelli, whose art collection its exhibitions show.
fondazionepasquinelli.arts: It runs the exhibition series L'arte in una stanza at its Milan seat and launched a national network of youth orchestras and choirs.

forartsiniciative.what: A New York grant-making foundation that began in 1931 as the American Center for Students and Artists in Paris and took its present name in 2008.
forartsiniciative.money: An endowment created from the 1996 sale of the American Center's Paris building to the French Ministry of Culture, now about $30 million.
forartsiniciative.arts: It has made more than 800 grants totalling nearly $20 million to artists, curators and independent art spaces in many countries.

forartsinitiatives.what: A New York grant-making foundation that began in 1931 as the American Center for Students and Artists in Paris and took its present name in 2008.
forartsinitiatives.money: An endowment created from the 1996 sale of the American Center's Paris building to the French Ministry of Culture, now about $30 million.
forartsinitiatives.arts: It has made more than 800 grants totalling nearly $20 million to artists, curators and independent art spaces in many countries.

ford.what: A private foundation set up in Michigan on 15 January 1936 by Edsel Ford and Henry Ford of the Ford Motor Company; based in New York since 1953.
ford.money: An endowment built on Ford Motor Company shares, sold between 1955 and 1974; about $16 billion in 2025.
ford.arts: Its Ford Foundation Symphony Program gave $80.2 million to 61 American orchestras from 1966 to 1976.

facts.t: The Ford Foundation reported total assets of $16,791,366,964 at the end of 2023 and $607,405,678 in grants paid that year, in its Form 990-PF.

fordgrantstomuseum.what: A private foundation set up in Michigan on 15 January 1936 by Edsel Ford and Henry Ford of the Ford Motor Company; based in New York since 1953.
fordgrantstomuseum.money: An endowment built on Ford Motor Company shares, sold between 1955 and 1974; about $16 billion in 2025.
fordgrantstomuseum.arts: Its Ford Foundation Symphony Program gave $80.2 million to 61 American orchestras from 1966 to 1976.

fortabat.money: The Fortabat fortune came from the cement maker Loma Negra, which Amalia Lacroze de Fortabat sold in 2005.

facts.t: The sale of Loma Negra brought Amalia Lacroze de Fortabat US$1,025 million, from which US$440 million of debt had to be paid.

A 2014 study by Argentina’s Procuración General set out how Loma Negra gained from the 1976 coup and the 1977 murder of Carlos Alberto Moreno, a labour lawyer who had won occupational illness cases for its miners; Página/12 reported the inquiry moving to the board Amalia Fortabat chaired.

foster.what: A British architecture and engineering firm founded in London in 1967 by Norman Foster, who keeps a controlling interest; Hennick & Company became its largest shareholder in 2021.
foster.money: Fees for architecture, engineering and design commissions worldwide; revenue £571.2 million in 2024/25.

foundationnorth.money: An endowment that began with the ASB Bank shares settled on it under the Trustee Banks Restructuring Act 1988 (it was the ASB Community Trust); its grants are paid from the returns on its investment fund.

facts.t: In the year to 31 March 2026 Foundation North committed $72,018 thousand in grants and other funding, and held total assets of $1,951,081 thousand.

foundingsponsoreczacba.what: A Turkish industrial group founded in 1942 by Dr. Nejat F. Eczacıbaşı, with headquarters in Levent, Istanbul, and over 9,000 employees.
foundingsponsoreczacba.money: Sales of building products, healthcare products and natural resources in more than 90 markets, plus technology, finance, real estate and investment businesses.
foundingsponsoreczacba.arts: Its arts commitments include the Istanbul Foundation for Culture and Arts, the İzmir Foundation for Culture, Arts and Education and the Dr. Nejat F. Eczacıbaşı Foundation (1978).

fourpillarsgin.what: A gin distillery founded in Healesville, Victoria, in 2013 by Cameron Mackenzie, Stuart Gregor and Matt Jones; wholly owned by the drinks group Lion since July 2023.
fourpillarsgin.money: Sales of its gin; Lion bought half in 2019 and the rest in 2023, placing it in its Four Corners Global Spirits division.

foyle.what: A UK grant-making charity formed in 2000 to carry out the will of bookseller Christina Foyle; it closed in December 2025 and entered voluntary liquidation in June 2026.
foyle.money: The estate of Christina Foyle, daughter of a founder of Foyles bookshop on Charing Cross Road, London.
foyle.arts: From 2000 to 2025 it gave over £185M to almost 7,500 charities and state schools, mainly for arts and learning.

francesgibsonmcglothlin.what: Jim McGlothlin, founder and chairman of The United Company of Bristol, Virginia, who died in August 2025 aged 85, and his wife Frances.
francesgibsonmcglothlin.money: The coal business he started in 1970, when he bought a coal company at auction, and The United Company's energy, hospitality and casino interests.

francisbaconmbart.what: A Monaco non-profit opened on 28 October 2014 to study Francis Bacon; it houses the MB Art Collection of over 3,500 items.
francisbaconmbart.money: Its founder and director, the collector Majid Boustany, who owns that collection and adds to it through regular acquisitions.
francisbaconmbart.arts: It funds scholarships and prizes with the École du Louvre, the University of Oxford and the Musée du Louvre, and is the main funder of books and documentaries on Bacon.

frankenthaler.what: A New York non-profit formed by the painter Helen Frankenthaler in 1984; it became active in 2013, when her estate closed.
frankenthaler.money: Endowed by the artist; net assets were $173,182,625 in 2024, when sales of assets brought 86.3% of revenue.
frankenthaler.arts: Its Frankenthaler Climate Initiative made its first grants, totalling $5.1 million, in July 2021.

frderstiftungderhamburgerkunsthalle.what: A private-law foundation in Hamburg, set up on private initiative to support the Hamburger Kunsthalle; the Hans Brökel Stiftung provided its founding capital.
frderstiftungderhamburgerkunsthalle.money: Donations, endowment gifts and bequests that build its capital; it spends the interest on the museum.

freelands.what: A London art education charity set up in 2015 by the media executive Elisabeth Murdoch, who chairs its board.
freelands.money: Investment income on a large 2019 donation, plus services donated by Freelands Group, owned by a trust of which Elisabeth Murdoch is a beneficiary.
freelands.arts: In 2025 it paid grants totalling £1,475,492 to 28 organisations.

freelandsfdn.what: A London charity that champions art education, set up in 2015 by its chair Elisabeth Murdoch, founder of the television producer Shine.
freelandsfdn.money: Charitable donations from its founder since 2015, including a substantial one in 2019, and income from the foundation's investments.
freelandsfdn.arts: It funds art education through grants, awards, fellowships and residencies, and spent £4,479,195 in 2024.

freestateofbavaria|Germany.what: The German federal state of Bavaria, governed by the Bavarian State Government under Minister-President Markus Söder from the State Chancellery in Munich.

freestateofsaxony|Germany.what: The German state of Saxony, represented by the Saxon State Chancellery in Dresden under Minister-President Michael Kretschmer.
freestateofsaxony|Germany.money: The state budget of Saxony: a double budget of about 50 billion euros for 2025 and 2026.

frenchembassy|Paraguay.what: France's diplomatic mission in Asunción, sharing a building with the European Union delegation; Jean-Philippe Gavois is ambassador.
frenchembassy|Paraguay.money: The French state; the embassy calls the budget for its cultural cooperation in Paraguay modest.
frenchembassy|Paraguay.arts: With the artists' association Gente de Arte it has run Paraguay's main visual arts prize, the Prix Matisse, for 25 years, and added photography and documentary prizes in 2018.

frenchministryofculturesubventions|Franc.what: The culture ministry of the French state, set up in 1959 with André Malraux as minister; its regional directorates of cultural affairs (DRAC) fund institutions across France.
frenchministryofculturesubventions|Franc.money: The French state budget: the 2026 finance bill requested €3.747 billion in payment credits for the Culture mission.

frenchministryofculture|France.what: The culture ministry of the French state, set up in 1959 with André Malraux as minister; its regional directorates of cultural affairs (DRAC) fund institutions across France.
frenchministryofculture|France.money: The French state budget: the 2026 finance bill requested €3.747 billion in payment credits for the Culture mission.

frenchstate|France.what: The culture ministry of the French state, set up in 1959 with André Malraux as minister; its regional directorates of cultural affairs (DRAC) fund institutions across France.
frenchstate|France.money: The French state budget: the 2026 finance bill requested €3.747 billion in payment credits for the Culture mission.

friendsofbdt.what: A foundation set up in 2015 to support the Tovstonogov Bolshoi Drama Theatre (BDT) in St Petersburg; Nikolai Dobrinov chairs its board.
friendsofbdt.money: Donations, contributions and subsidies; the theatre names Goznak, Promsvyazbank and Polymetal as regular partners of the theatre and the fund.
friendsofbdt.arts: It pays for new productions, tours, and publishing, exhibition and festival projects at the BDT.

friendsofcentrepompidou.what: A French association recognised as of public utility, founded in 1903 as the Société des Amis du Musée du Luxembourg and renamed Amis du Centre Pompidou in 2017.
friendsofcentrepompidou.money: Members' subscriptions, donations, bequests and dedicated funds, plus its annual Dîner des Amis.
friendsofcentrepompidou.arts: Its twelve acquisition committees take part, with the curators, in choosing new works for the Musée national d'art moderne.

friendsofweissenhofestate.what: A nonprofit association registered in Stuttgart on 17 November 1979 to restore the 1927 Weissenhof Estate; Bodo Rasch, Mia Seeger and Frei Otto formed its first board.
friendsofweissenhofestate.money: Members' dues of €50 a year; since 2006 it runs the Weissenhof Museum in the Le Corbusier House for the City of Stuttgart.

fristartmuseum.what: A Nashville 501(c)(3) foundation for the Frist Art Museum, tax exempt since July 1998; William R. Frist is its chairman and president.
fristartmuseum.money: Investment income and asset sales on a portfolio of $73,137,463 in total assets at the end of 2024.

frittord.money: Fritt Ord was founded in 1974 by the Narvesen chain of convenience stores.

frittordprojects.what: A Norwegian private foundation for free expression, set up in Oslo on 7 June 1974 by Narvesen kiosk executives Jens Henrik Nordlie and Finn Skedsmo and lawyer Jens Christian Hauge.
frittordprojects.money: An endowment that began as the shares of the Narvesen kiosk company, which it sold in stages until November 2001.

fujisankei.what: A Japanese media group formed in 1967 by Fuji Television, the Sankei Shimbun newspaper and the radio stations Nippon Broadcasting System and Nippon Cultural Broadcasting; Nobutaka Shikanai founded it.
fujisankei.money: The television, newspaper, radio, film, music and property businesses of its member companies, many of them owned by Fuji Media Holdings.
fujisankei.arts: Its art and culture group includes the Utsukushi-ga-hara Open-Air Museum and the Japan Art Association, which runs the Ueno Royal Museum and the Praemium Imperiale prize.

fukutake.what: A Japanese foundation that runs Benesse Art Site Naoshima with Benesse Corporation, grown from a foundation Soichiro Fukutake set up in 2004.
fukutake.money: A personal endowment from Soichiro Fukutake, former head of Benesse, the Okayama correspondence education and publishing company.
fukutake.arts: It has been a founding patron of CIMAM, the international committee for modern art museums, since 2000.

fultoncounty|USA.what: The county government of Fulton County, Georgia, led by a seven-member Board of Commissioners and based at the Fulton County Government Center in Atlanta.
fultoncounty|USA.money: The county budget, funded in part by property tax, which the FY2026 budget kept at 8.87 mills.
fultoncounty|USA.arts: Its Department of Arts & Culture runs the Contracts for Services programme: $2,857,643 in initial FY2026 awards to 200 organisations.

funarte.what: A public foundation of the Brazilian federal government, linked to the Ministry of Culture, created in 1975 and based in Rio de Janeiro.
funarte.arts: It gives grants and prizes and runs programmes for visual arts, music, dance, theatre and circus across Brazil.

fundacibarcelonacultura.what: A private foundation set up by Barcelona City Council on 27 December 2004 to support the city's Institut de Cultura; the mayor Jaume Collboni chairs its board.
fundacibarcelonacultura.money: Sponsorship and patronage agreements it signs with companies for the Institut de Cultura's programmes.
fundacibarcelonacultura.arts: It promotes circles of companies that back the city's museums.

fundacicatalunyalapedrera.what: A private Catalan special foundation founded in 2013 from the transformation of the savings bank Caixa d'Estalvis de Catalunya, Tarragona i Manresa; it runs La Pedrera in Barcelona.
fundacicatalunyalapedrera.money: Visitor income from La Pedrera above all, plus its nature sites, programmes and group companies; group income was €66.6 million in 2025.

fundacilacaixa.what: A Spanish banking foundation that grew out of the la Caixa savings bank, headquartered in Barcelona since March 2025.
fundacilacaixa.money: Dividends from its holding company CriteriaCaixa, which holds 31 per cent of CaixaBank and 9.99 per cent of Telefónica.
fundacilacaixa.arts: Its social work budget, which covers cultural as well as social and scientific projects, is €710 million for 2026.

fundacinamador.what: A Panamanian non-profit foundation established in 2000 that operates and cares for the Biomuseo, Frank Gehry's museum of biodiversity in Panama City.
fundacinamador.money: Tickets, school and tourist visits, events, service contracts and donations; in 2016 Panama's state agreed $18 million for the museum's second phase.

fundacinamalialacrozedefortabat.what: A private Argentine foundation set up by Amalia Lacroze de Fortabat, owner of the cement maker Loma Negra; it was first named Fundación Alfredo Fortabat y Amalia Lacroze de Fortabat.
fundacinamalialacrozedefortabat.money: The fortune of Amalia Lacroze de Fortabat from Loma Negra, Argentina's largest cement maker, whose 80% stake she sold to Camargo Correa in 2005.
fundacinamalialacrozedefortabat.arts: It has given more than $40 million to Argentine charities since 1976.

fundacinamparo.what: A Mexican private foundation set up in 1979 by the banker Manuel Espinosa Yglesias in honour of his wife; it sponsors the Museo Amparo in Puebla, opened in 1991.
fundacinamparo.money: The fortune of Manuel Espinosa Yglesias, general director and major shareholder of the bank Bancomer from 1959 until the 1982 bank expropriation.

fundacinbancariabbk.what: A Basque banking foundation formed in 2014 when the Bilbao Bizkaia Kutxa savings bank converted into a foundation; it is the majority shareholder of Kutxabank.
fundacinbancariabbk.money: Its Kutxabank stake: 1,140,000 shares, 57% of the bank's capital, which made up its €2,774 million net worth at the 2014 conversion.

fundacinbancosantander.what: The corporate foundation of the Santander banking group, based in Madrid; it shows the bank's art collection at the Sala de Arte Santander in Boadilla del Monte.
fundacinbancosantander.money: Mostly dividends on its Banco Santander shares, held since April 1992; its income was €31,328,998 in 2025.

fundacinbat.what: A foundation in Bogotá whose privacy notice lets it pass personal data to companies of the British American Tobacco group.
fundacinbat.money: BAT, the London-based cigarette and nicotine maker: a 2025 article BAT paid for calls the foundation key to BAT Group's sustainability strategy.
fundacinbat.arts: With support from Colombia's Ministry of Culture it runs the Gran Salón BAT de Arte Popular, a folk art competition with prizes.

fundacinbbva.what: The foundation of the Spanish banking group BBVA, with headquarters in Bilbao and an office in Madrid.
fundacinbbva.money: The BBVA Group, whose corporate social responsibility the foundation carries out.

fundacinbotn.what: A family foundation set up in Santander on 18 April 1964 by Marcelino Botín Sanz de Sautuola, vice-chairman of Banco de Santander, and his wife Carmen Yllera.
fundacinbotn.money: An endowment that began with Marcelino Botín's bequest of 500 million pesetas, which his widow then increased.
fundacinbotn.arts: In 2024 Jaime Botín gave it portraits from his collection for a room at Centro Botín, with an annual financial endowment.

fundacincarlosslim.what: The philanthropic body of Carlos Slim Helú and his family, created in Mexico City in 1986 as Asociación Carso A.C. by Slim and his wife Soumaya Domit.
fundacincarlosslim.money: The fortune of Carlos Slim Helú, drawn from his holdings in Mexican companies through his conglomerate Grupo Carso.

fundacincostantini.money: Eduardo Costantini’s money comes from Consultatio, his listed real estate company, known for the Nordelta gated communities.

facts.t: Costantini’s 72 percent stake in Consultatio was worth about US$580 million at the April 2024 share price.

fundacinculturaldelbancocentraldebolivia.what: A state public-law body created by Law 1670 of 31 October 1995 under the oversight of the Banco Central de Bolivia; it runs six national museums, archives and cultural centres.
fundacinculturaldelbancocentraldebolivia.money: A yearly allocation in the central bank's budget: Bs 108,290,618.62 of its Bs 113,004,689.62 budget in force at May 2024, plus ticket and sales income.

fundacinjumexgrants.money: The López family’s money comes from Grupo Jumex, the Mexican juice and food company; Eugenio López Alonso is its heir.

facts.t: Expansión gave Jumex’s sales as between US$1,000 million and US$1,100 million, an analyst’s estimate, in 2013.

fundacinmontemadrid.what: A private non-profit foundation in Madrid, entered in the state register of foundations in July 2022, that runs educational, social, cultural and environmental centres and programmes.
fundacinmontemadrid.money: Mainly the proceeds of El Monte, its financial-inclusion business of more than 300 years; group companies include Monteoro, a gold and jewellery dealer.
fundacinmontemadrid.arts: It owns an art collection and gives the Carmen Alborch short story prize and, with RNE, a young poetry prize.

fundacinmutuamadrilea.what: The foundation of the Spanish insurer Mutua Madrileña, set up in 2003 for medical research and widened to social, road safety and cultural work in 2009.
fundacinmutuamadrilea.money: Funds from Mutua Madrileña, the Madrid insurer founded in 1930 that sells car, health and life insurance.
fundacinmutuamadrilea.arts: Cultural work takes about a quarter of the foundation's resources (2024).

fundacinpaiz.what: A Guatemalan family foundation that grew from scholarships Graciela Andrade de Paiz began giving in the early 1970s; it has held the Bienal de Arte Paiz since 1978.
fundacinpaiz.money: The Paiz family and public donations; its marimba festival began in 1980 in the family's Paiz stores.
fundacinpaiz.arts: It runs the Bienal de Arte Paiz, the Festival de Marimba, the Premio Monteforte Toledo literary prize and a collection of about 300 Guatemalan works.

fundacinprosegur.what: The corporate foundation of Prosegur, the Madrid security company Herberto Gut founded in 1976; it turned its focus to social action and education in 2005.
fundacinprosegur.money: Support from Prosegur, whose guarding, cash-in-transit and security technology businesses had €4,291 million revenue in 2017.
fundacinprosegur.arts: It has worked with the Fundación Amigos del Museo del Prado since 2006 and runs a programme called El Arte como Motor de Cambio.

fundacionalfredoharphelu.what: A Mexican foundation funded by the banker Alfredo Harp Helú, former owner of Banamex, giving to education, culture, sport, health and the environment.
fundacionalfredoharphelu.money: Harp Helú's fortune, from Citigroup's 2001 purchase of Banamex; the foundation's assets stood at MXN 14.532 billion in 2018.
fundacionalfredoharphelu.arts: Of MXN 6.83 billion it had given to projects by 2018, MXN 1.58 billion, 23 percent, went to culture.

fundacionaxamexico.what: The foundation of AXA México, working on health, emergency aid, road safety, art and climate change; it has given over MXN 60 million to newborn care since 2018.
fundacionaxamexico.arts: Since 2008 it has made grants in art and culture, among them to the art school SOMA, the Patronato de Arte Contemporáneo and MUAC's Arkheia archive.

fundaciontelevisa.what: The philanthropic arm of the Mexican broadcaster Grupo Televisa, known earlier as Fundación Cultural Televisa.
fundaciontelevisa.arts: Its photographic collection and archive, begun in 1974, holds hundreds of thousands of images; it organised the Gabriel Figueroa exhibition shown at LACMA.

fundaodeserralvesendowment.what: A foundation in Porto created by Decree-Law 240-A/89 of 27 July 1989 as a partnership between the Portuguese State and about 51 public and private bodies.
fundaodeserralvesendowment.money: Contributions from its 181 founders, which include companies and private individuals, alongside cooperation with the State.

fundaoedp.what: The corporate foundation of the Portuguese electricity company EDP, S.A., which set it up in December 2004; it is seated at the Central Tejo in Lisbon.
fundaoedp.money: EDP, S.A., the electricity company that owns it.
fundaoedp.arts: It keeps an art collection, gives the New Artists Award and the Art Grand Prize, and publishes Electra magazine.

fundaomanuelantniodamota.what: A corporate foundation of the Portuguese construction group Mota-Engil, set up by public deed in Porto on 18 December 2009 and declared of public utility in 2014.
fundaomanuelantniodamota.money: Funds from the Mota-Engil construction and engineering group, which calls the foundation an instrument of its social responsibility policy.

fundaomillenniumbcp.what: The foundation of the Portuguese bank Banco Comercial Português, set up by the bank in 1991, working in culture, education and social development.
fundaomillenniumbcp.money: Funds from the bank, Portugal's largest private bank, which made €856.0 million net income in 2023.

fundaorobertomarinho.what: A private non-profit foundation for education and heritage, set up in November 1977 in Rio de Janeiro by the journalist Roberto Marinho.
fundaorobertomarinho.money: It belongs to Grupo Globo, the Brazilian media group.

fundos.what: A private foundation created in 2015 from the social fund of the Caja España-Duero savings bank; based at Casa Botines in León, it works across Castilla y León.
fundos.money: The buildings, art and archives of the former Caja España-Duero social fund, plus revenue from the Casa Botines museum and its MonteCredit pawn loans.
fundos.arts: Its collection and historical archive came from the savings bank, whose social fund held more than 10,500 artworks in 2014.

furla.what: An Italian leather goods company founded in Bologna in 1927 by Aldo and Margherita Furlanetto, based in San Lazzaro di Savena and controlled by two branches of the Furlanetto family.
furla.money: Sales of handbags and accessories: revenue of EUR 513 million in 2018.
furla.arts: Giovanna Furlanetto set up the Fondazione Furla in Bologna in 2008 to help young talent in creative work from art to fashion.

futurescreensni.what: A Northern Ireland creative industries research partnership set up in 2018, led by Ulster University with Queen's University Belfast, one of nine AHRC Creative Industries Clusters.
futurescreensni.money: A UK Research and Innovation grant through the AHRC; the Department for Communities and the Arts Council of Northern Ireland now support its network.

gador.what: An Argentine pharmaceutical company founded in 1940 by Dr. Nicolás Gador, joined in 1948 by Américo and Jorge Balla, whose descendants still sit on its board.
gador.money: Sales of its medicines; it makes more than 2 billion tablets a year and holds over 800 product registrations worldwide.

galaxyentertainment.what: A Hong Kong listed company, formerly K. Wah Construction Materials, that runs casinos and hotels in Macau through Galaxy Casino S.A.; the Lui family controls 50.3%.
galaxyentertainment.money: Casino gaming, hotels and construction materials: group net revenue of HK$49.2 billion in 2025, of which HK$39.6 billion came from gaming.

galerialuisastrina.what: A commercial art gallery in São Paulo opened in 1974 by the collector Luisa Strina; it was the first Latin American gallery invited to Art Basel.
galerialuisastrina.money: Sales of work by the artists it shows.

galeriemaxhetzler.what: A commercial contemporary art gallery founded by Max Hetzler in Stuttgart in September 1974; it has spaces in Berlin, Paris and London and a venue in Marfa, Texas.
galeriemaxhetzler.money: Sales of work by the more than sixty artists it represents.

galleriessuchasgagosian.what: A commercial art gallery owned and directed by the dealer Larry Gagosian, who opened his first gallery in Los Angeles in 1980; it had 19 exhibition spaces in 2024.
galleriessuchasgagosian.money: Sales of artworks; a 2011 Wall Street Journal survey estimated its annual sales at about $1 billion.

galpenergia.what: A Portuguese energy company formed in 1999 by merging Petrogal, Gás de Portugal and Transgás, seated in Lisbon; Amorim Energia holds 35.8 percent.
galpenergia.money: Oil and gas exploration and production, refining, fuel marketing, and gas and power sales: EUR 961 million profit in 2024.

gamingforfiveyears.what: A Philippine government-owned corporation created in 1977 under Ferdinand Marcos Sr; it regulates gambling and runs the Casino Filipino chain under the Office of the President.
gamingforfiveyears.money: Gaming revenue from its own and licensed casinos and e-games, plus interest and service fees: total revenues of P106.04 billion in 2025.

gandel.money: The Gandel family’s money comes from shopping centres: John Gandel bought Melbourne’s Chadstone Shopping Centre in 1983, after growing his parents’ Sussan clothing chain with Marc Besen.

facts.t: In its 2024-25 donor return to the Australian Electoral Commission, The Gandel Group Pty Ltd, the family company, disclosed $385,000 in political donations: $10,000 to Labor branches and $375,000 to Liberal and National branches.

garantibbvainternational.what: A Dutch bank set up in Amsterdam in 1990 as a subsidiary of Istanbul's Türkiye Garanti Bankası, now Garanti BBVA, of which Spain's BBVA owns 85.97%.
garantibbvainternational.money: Its banking business within the Garanti BBVA group, which had US$15.53 billion revenue in 2024.

garfieldweston.money: The Garfield Weston Foundation is a UK charity endowed by the Weston family; its income comes from Wittington Investments, of which it owns 79.2%, and through it a 46.0% holding in Associated British Foods (Primark, Twinings, British Sugar), whose controlling shareholder Wittington is. It is not the Canadian Weston branch (George Weston Ltd, Loblaw).

facts.t: Associated British Foods reported group revenue of £19,459m and adjusted operating profit of £1,734m for the 52 weeks to 13 September 2025.
At 5 April 2025 the Foundation owned 79.2% of Wittington Investments, the ultimate holding company of Associated British Foods, and through it 46.0% of ABF.

gasterra.what: A Dutch natural gas wholesaler created in Groningen in 2005 from the split of Gasunie, owned by Shell (25%), ExxonMobil (25%) and the Dutch state (50%).
gasterra.money: Sales of natural gas, revenue €9.6 billion in 2017; after the end of Groningen field production it is winding down by 31 December 2026.

gates.money: Bill Gates's money comes from Microsoft, which he co-founded; the Gates Foundation is endowed from his fortune, and Microsoft's own gifts are named apart in these entries.

facts.t: The Gates Foundation reported total assets of $76,951,451,400 at the end of 2023 and paid $7,200,556,970 in contributions and grants that year (Form 990-PF).
Microsoft's revenue was $281,724 million in its fiscal year to June 2025.
Microsoft Corporation reported $9,360,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025 in its Lobbying Disclosure Act reports.
Microsoft Corporation declared EU lobbying costs of €7,000,000 to €7,999,999 for its year from July 2025 to June 2026 to the EU Transparency Register.

gateshead.what: The local authority for the Metropolitan Borough of Gateshead in Tyne and Wear, created in 1974 under the Local Government Act 1972 and based at Gateshead Civic Centre.
gateshead.money: Council Tax supplied 39% of its income, according to its 2024-25 budget page, alongside government funding.

gazprom.money: Gazprom’s money comes from natural gas: the state-controlled company is, in the US Treasury’s words, the world’s largest natural gas company, and it co-owns Belgazprombank in Belarus with Gazprombank.

facts.t: On 24 February 2022 the US Treasury listed Gazprom, which it called the world’s largest natural gas company, among 11 entities owned or controlled by the Russian government that are subject to prohibitions on new debt and equity.

gazprombank.money: Gazprombank’s money comes from banking: Russia’s third-largest financial institution, closely tied to the energy sector, it co-owns Belgazprombank in Belarus with Gazprom.

facts.t: On 24 February 2022 the US Treasury listed Gazprombank among 11 entities owned or controlled by the Russian government that are subject to prohibitions on new debt and equity.

On 21 November 2024 the US Treasury designated Gazprombank and six foreign subsidiaries, saying it is a conduit for Russia to buy military materiel and that the government uses it to pay soldiers, including combat bonuses.

gazpromfinancedparks.what: Russia's state-owned energy company, founded on 8 August 1989; the Russian government holds 50.23% and it is headquartered in the Lakhta Center, Saint Petersburg.
gazpromfinancedparks.money: Sales of natural gas, oil and petrochemicals and gas pipeline transport; revenue US$115 billion in 2025.

gazpromneft.what: Russia's third largest oil producer, founded in 1995 as Sibneft and seated in St Petersburg, under EU sanctions since March 2022; Gazprom holds 95.68 percent.
gazpromneft.money: Oil and gas production and refining: RUB 3.61 trillion revenue in 2025.

gbengaoyebode.what: A lawyer, co-founder of the Nigerian law firm Aluko & Oyebode; he is married to Aisha Muhammed-Oyebode, founder of the Murtala Muhammed Foundation.

geffen.money: David Geffen's money comes from the record labels he founded, Asylum, Geffen and DGC, and the film studio DreamWorks.

facts.t: Forbes put David Geffen's net worth at $9.7 billion on 17 November 2026.

gemeenteleiden|Netherlands.what: The municipality of Leiden in South Holland, with 127,046 inhabitants in January 2023, run by a council and a college of mayor and aldermen.
gemeenteleiden|Netherlands.money: The municipal budget, funded mainly by Dutch state payments from the Gemeentefonds and specific grants, plus local taxes.
gemeenteleiden|Netherlands.arts: It has owned Museum De Lakenhal, its municipal museum of fine art and history, since the museum opened in 1874.

gemeenterotterdam|Netherlands.what: The municipality of Rotterdam, governed by a directly elected council of 45 members and a college of mayor and aldermen.
gemeenterotterdam|Netherlands.money: The municipal budget, about two thirds of it from the national government and other authorities in the 2026 budget.

genelec.what: A Finnish maker of active loudspeakers for studios, broadcasting and film, founded in 1978 by Ilpo Martikainen and Topi Partanen, with its factory and headquarters in Iisalmi.
genelec.money: Sales of its loudspeakers and studio monitors: revenue of €43,614,000 in 2025, with 203 employees.

generali.money: Generali's money comes from insurance and asset management; it is Italy's largest insurer.

facts.t: Generali reported a net result of €4,172 million for 2025, up 12.0% from €3,724 million in 2024.
Assicurazioni Generali S.p.A declared EU lobbying costs of €1,250,000 to €1,499,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register, with 3.95 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.

generalitatdecatalunyadepartmentofcultur.what: The culture department of the Generalitat de Catalunya, the Catalan government, seated at the Palau Marc on the Rambla in Barcelona; Sònia Hernández has been minister since 12 August 2024.
generalitatdecatalunyadepartmentofcultur.money: The budget of the Generalitat: 574 million euros for 2026, 1.8 percent of the Catalan government's accounts.
generalitatdecatalunyadepartmentofcultur.arts: It manages cultural heritage, archives and museums, the cultural industries and Catalan traditional and popular culture.

generalpartnerkomernbanka.what: A Czech bank founded in 1990 from the commercial arm of the State Bank of Czechoslovakia, based in Prague; Société Générale bought the state's 60% stake in 2001.
generalpartnerkomernbanka.money: Banking for individuals, businesses and municipalities in Czechia; net income was CZK 17.4 billion in 2024.

generalpoliticaldepartment|China.what: The People's Liberation Army's chief political organ under the Central Military Commission until January 2016, when it was disbanded and the Commission's Political Work Department replaced it.

genesis.what: A UK charity registered on 5 January 2001 by its founder and chairman John Studzinski, an investment banker at PIMCO, which backs emerging artists in theatre and music.
genesis.arts: During the pandemic it launched the £1 million Genesis Kickstart Fund, which paid for 95 projects with 1,000 freelance creative professionals from 2021 to March 2023.

genevahisheirs.what: A Swiss foundation registered in Geneva in December 1958 to help Bolivian students and professors and to support cultural, social and ecological work in Bolivia.
genevahisheirs.money: A fund of US$10 million set up when the Bolivian Patiño foundation ran short of money; the Patiño wealth came from Bolivian tin mining.
genevahisheirs.arts: Its statutes include topping up the resources of the Fundación Universitaria Simón I. Patiño, created in Bolivia in 1931, and supporting literary and music prizes.

georgiapower.what: An investor-owned electric utility in Atlanta, the largest of the four utilities owned by Southern Company; it began in 1902 as the Georgia Railway and Power Company.
georgiapower.money: Electricity sales to more than 2.8 million customers in Georgia, generated at coal, gas and nuclear plants including Plant Scherer and Plant Vogtle.

gerardcafesjian.what: An American businessman and philanthropist (1925 to 2013) who rose to executive vice president of West Publishing and founded the Cafesjian Family Foundation and the Cafesjian Museum Foundation.
gerardcafesjian.money: His career at West Publishing in St. Paul, Minnesota, from which he retired when the company was sold in 1996.
gerardcafesjian.arts: Through the Cafesjian Family Foundation he put more than $128 million into projects in Armenia.

gerdahenkel.what: A private foundation in Düsseldorf set up in June 1976 by Lisa Maskell in memory of her mother Gerda Henkel; it funds historical humanities research and heritage work.
gerdahenkel.money: An endowment set up by Lisa Maskell, granddaughter of Fritz Henkel, who founded the Henkel company in 1876.
gerdahenkel.arts: In its autumn 2026 round it awarded €10.9 million to 115 research projects.

germanfederalforeignoffice|Germany.what: Germany's federal foreign ministry, based in Berlin with a second seat in Bonn; it runs the foreign service and German foreign and European policy.
germanfederalforeignoffice|Germany.money: The German federal budget, as a supreme federal authority.

germanfederalforeignoffice|Poland.what: Germany's federal foreign ministry, based in Berlin with a second seat in Bonn; it runs the foreign service and German foreign and European policy.
germanfederalforeignoffice|Poland.money: The German federal budget, as a supreme federal authority.

germanfederalgovernment|Germany.what: The federal executive of Germany, made up of the Federal Chancellor and the federal ministers under the Basic Law, with its seat in Berlin.

germanykfw.what: Germany's state-owned development bank, a public-law institution formed in 1948 under the Marshall Plan and based in Frankfurt; the federal government owns 80% and the states 20%.
germanykfw.money: It raises over 90% of its funds on capital markets, mainly through bonds guaranteed by the federal government.

germanysforeignoffice.what: Germany's federal foreign ministry, based in Berlin with a second seat in Bonn; it runs the foreign service and German foreign and European policy.
germanysforeignoffice.money: The German federal budget, as a supreme federal authority.

gesellschaftderfreundederakademiederknst.what: A friends' association of the Berlin Akademie der Künste, founded on 5 July 1999 with Klaus Mangold and Rolf-E. Breuer as its first board chairs.
gesellschaftderfreundederakademiederknst.money: Members' dues, from €150 for young friends to €10,000 for large companies a year, and extra donations.

gesellschaftfrmodernekunstsupportit.what: A registered non-profit association in Cologne, founded in 1985 by collectors from the Rhineland to support the Museum Ludwig through acquisitions, exhibitions and projects.
gesellschaftfrmodernekunstsupportit.money: Dues from more than 650 members: €660 a year for an individual and €2,500 for a company.
gesellschaftfrmodernekunstsupportit.arts: Its annual Wolfgang Hahn Prize puts up to €100,000 toward buying the winner's work for the Museum Ludwig; Lee Ufan won in 2026.

getty.money: The J. Paul Getty Trust is endowed by the oilman J. Paul Getty's bequest of Getty Oil stock; the J. Paul Getty Jr. Charitable Trust is the separate trust of his son, Sir Paul Getty.

facts.t: The J. Paul Getty Trust reported assets with a fair market value of $16,341,567,063 at the end of its tax year to June 2023, in its Form 990-PF.

ghanatourismauthority.what: Ghana's state tourism agency under the Ministry of Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts; founded in 1960 as the Ghana Tourist Board and renamed by Act 817 of 2011.
ghanatourismauthority.money: The Tourism Development Fund, fed by a 1% levy patrons pay at tourism businesses since October 2012, plus government money.

gibbs.money: Alan Gibbs's fortune came from investment banking and deals such as the Freightways buyout, Telecom's privatisation and the founding of Sky TV, and later from Auckland's Viaduct Harbour land; Dame Jenny Gibbs is his former wife.

facts.t: Alan Gibbs gave $100,000 to the ACT Party in April 2008.
Alan Gibbs gave ACT another $100,000 the day before the 2008 election, disclosed under the Electoral Finance Act.

The Electoral Commission referred ACT to the police for disclosing late a series of donations, adding up to more than $30,000, from Alan Gibbs and Dame Jenny Gibbs, its biggest backers, made before the 2014 election.

gijncity|Spain.what: The city council of Gijón in Asturias, seated on the Plaza Mayor and led since 2023 by mayor Carmen Moriyón of Foro Asturias.
gijncity|Spain.money: The municipal budget, voted by the council plenary, the 2025 budget taking effect after publication in the BOPA on 20 December 2024.

gilbertfamily.what: The family foundation of Dan Gilbert, co-founder, majority owner and chairman of Rocket Mortgage, and his wife Jennifer Gilbert; based in Detroit and US tax-exempt since October 2021.
gilbertfamily.money: Contributions of $130,606,908 in 2024, 99.1% of its revenue; the Gilberts' fortune comes from Rocket Mortgage.

gilberts.what: The family foundation of Dan Gilbert, co-founder, majority owner and chairman of Rocket Mortgage, and his wife Jennifer Gilbert; based in Detroit and US tax-exempt since October 2021.
gilberts.money: Contributions of $130,606,908 in 2024, 99.1% of its revenue; the Gilberts' fortune comes from Rocket Mortgage.

glasgowcitycouncil|United Kingdom.what: The local authority for the Glasgow City council area, the most populous of Scotland's 32, a unitary authority since 1 April 1996 with 85 councillors.
glasgowcitycouncil|United Kingdom.money: The council's annual budget, set by a vote of its councillors.

glasgowliferun.what: A charity and company formed in December 2006 and controlled by Glasgow City Council, for which it runs arts, music, sport, events, festivals and libraries.
glasgowliferun.money: A service fee from Glasgow City Council, about 60 percent of income, plus what its culture and sport programmes earn.

glasshousetrusthesettled.what: A grant-making charity incorporated on 30 November 2011, funded by its trustee Alex Sainsbury; one of the Sainsbury Family Charitable Trusts, which share an administration in London.
glasshousetrusthesettled.money: An expendable endowment from its funder Alex Sainsbury, held in an investment portfolio: net assets of £6,671,700 on 5 April 2025.
glasshousetrusthesettled.arts: It gives long-term support to a few projects in the built environment, child development, social policy and art, and takes no applications.

glennfuhrman.what: A New York collector couple; Glenn Fuhrman founded the FLAG Art Foundation, which opened in 2008, and with Amanda co-founded the Fuhrman Family Foundation.
glennfuhrman.money: Glenn Fuhrman's career in finance; in 2008 he was co-head of MSD Capital, the firm formed to manage Michael Dell's money.
glennfuhrman.arts: He is a trustee of the Museum of Modern Art and the Tate Americas Foundation and a board member of the Institute of Contemporary Art, Philadelphia.

globalradio.what: A British media company founded in 2007 by Ashley Tabor-King with backing from his father Michael Tabor; it owns Heart, Capital, Classic FM, LBC and other radio stations.
globalradio.money: Advertising sold on its radio stations and on its outdoor billboards, a business it built by buying Primesight and Outdoor Plus in 2018.

godrej.money: The Godrej money comes from the Godrej companies; since the family's 2024 split, Jamshyd Godrej's side holds the unlisted Godrej & Boyce and its affiliates and a Mumbai land bank, and Adi and Nadir Godrej keep the listed Godrej Industries firms.

goethe.what: Germany's cultural institute, a registered association headquartered in Munich with more than 150 centres in 99 countries that teach German and run cultural exchange.
goethe.money: Mainly annual grants from the German Federal Foreign Office, plus its own tuition and exam fees and money from sponsors and patrons.

goetheinstitut.what: Germany's cultural institute, a registered association headquartered in Munich with more than 150 centres in 99 countries that teach German and run cultural exchange.
goetheinstitut.money: Mainly annual grants from the German Federal Foreign Office, plus its own tuition and exam fees and money from sponsors and patrons.

goetheinstitute.what: Germany's cultural institute, a registered association headquartered in Munich with more than 150 centres in 99 countries that teach German and run cultural exchange.
goetheinstitute.money: Mainly annual grants from the German Federal Foreign Office, plus its own tuition and exam fees and money from sponsors and patrons.

goldenharvestssponsorshipofsummit.what: A Bangladeshi conglomerate based in Dhaka that started as a commodity brokerage and now runs food, dairy, IT, logistics, property and insurance companies; Rajeeb Samdani is managing director.
goldenharvestssponsorshipofsummit.money: Its companies, among them frozen food, Bloop ice cream, a Domino's Pizza joint venture, Nippon Express Bangladesh and Sonali Life Insurance.
goldenharvestssponsorshipofsummit.arts: It lists the Samdani Art Foundation, set up in 2011 by Nadia and Rajeeb Samdani and producer of the Dhaka Art Summit, as its CSR work.

goldmansachs.money: Goldman Sachs is a US investment bank, trader and asset manager.

facts.t: Goldman Sachs reported 2025 net revenues of $58.28 billion and net earnings of $17.18 billion.

In October 2020 Goldman Sachs agreed to pay more than $2.9 billion to resolve US and other investigations into its role in the 1MDB scandal; the DOJ said it had conspired to use more than $1.6 billion in bribes to officials.
The Goldman Sachs Group reported $3,960,000 in US federal lobbying for 2025 in its own Lobbying Disclosure Act reports.
The Goldman Sachs Group declared EU lobbying costs of €1,500,000 to €1,749,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

goldreefcity|South Africa.what: A casino, hotel and theme park complex opened in 1987 on a gold mine closed in 1971, south of central Johannesburg; Tsogo Sun owns it.
goldreefcity|South Africa.money: Casino gaming, hotels and the theme park, through Tsogo Sun, half owned by Hosken Consolidated Investments; Tsogo Sun merged with Gold Reef Resorts in 2011.

goldshoman.what: A non-profit foundation that Arab Bank set up in Amman in 1978 to support science, the humanities and culture in the Arab world.
goldshoman.money: Arab Bank's profits: in 2011 the bank gave it over 8 million Jordanian dinars, about 87% of its community investment budget.
goldshoman.arts: It runs a cultural forum, film screenings and musical evenings in Amman, and gives cultural grants and an award for creativity.

goldsmith.what: A New York private foundation created in 1955 by Horace Ward Goldsmith, who bought a New York Stock Exchange seat in 1927.
goldsmith.money: Investment returns, chiefly gains on asset sales and dividends, on assets of $826 million in 2024.

goodstorage.what: A Brazilian urban storage company in São Paulo, founded by its chief executive Thiago Cordeiro, which marked ten years in 2023.
goodstorage.money: Rent from self storage units and city warehouses in São Paulo: more than BRL 300 million revenue in 2025, 40 percent above 2024.

google.money: Google's money comes from Alphabet, its parent, mainly from search and other advertising, with cloud services and YouTube.

facts.t: Alphabet's revenue was $402,836 million in 2025.
In September 2025 the European Commission fined Google €2.95 billion for abusing its dominance in online advertising technology.
Google Client Services LLC reported $13,100,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025 in its Lobbying Disclosure Act reports.
Google Ireland Limited and its affiliates declared EU lobbying costs of €5,500,000 to €5,999,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

gordondarling.money: The Gordon Darling Foundation was set up in June 1991 by the businessman Gordon Darling to support the visual arts through public institutions.

governmentagencyofkoreasministryofcultur.what: The South Korean central government ministry for culture, art, religion, sports and tourism, formed on 29 February 2008 and based in the Sejong Government Complex.
governmentagencyofkoreasministryofcultur.money: The South Korean national budget: ₩7.067 trillion (US$4.9 billion) for the ministry in fiscal 2025.
governmentagencyofkoreasministryofcultur.arts: It funds support for the Korean wave (Hallyu).

governmentofabudhabi|UAE.what: Abu Dhabi's emirate government in the UAE: a hereditary monarchy under Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan since 14 May 2022, with the Executive Council as its cabinet.
governmentofabudhabi|UAE.money: Oil, the primary source of government funding; the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, Mubadala and Abu Dhabi Holding Company invest surplus reserves.
governmentofabudhabi|UAE.arts: A 2017 French Senate report put its payments under the Louvre Abu Dhabi agreement at EUR 974.5 million for 2007 to 2037, with EUR 477 million paid by 2017.

governmentofbangladesh|Bangladesh.what: The central government of Bangladesh, set up under the constitution adopted on 4 November 1972, with executive, legislative and judicial branches.

governmentofindia|India.what: The Union government of India, in its present form since the Constitution took effect on 26 January 1950, seated in New Delhi and led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
governmentofindia|India.money: The Union budget of India: total expenditure is estimated at Rs 50,65,345 crore for 2025-26.

governmentofitalianrepublic|Bosnia and H.what: The national government of Italy, made up of the prime minister, Giorgia Meloni since October 2022, and the ministers, seated in Palazzo Chigi, Rome.

governmentofjapan|Japan.what: The central government of Japan under the Constitution of Japan; the Cabinet, led by the prime minister whom the National Diet nominates, holds executive power.

governmentofkerala|India.what: The government of the Indian state of Kerala, led by Chief Minister V. D. Satheesan since 18 May 2026, with its headquarters at the Secretariat in Thiruvananthapuram.
governmentofkerala|India.money: Its own taxes and other revenue plus transfers from the Government of India: ₹1,24,861.06 crore in 2024-25, ₹31,732.25 crore of it from the centre.
governmentofkerala|India.arts: The state allocated ₹7.5 crore to the Kochi-Muziris Biennale, whose sixth edition then Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan opened on 12 December 2025.

governmentofnorthkorea|North Korea.what: The state government of North Korea, whose Cabinet was formed in 1948 in Pyongyang and which the Workers' Party of Korea rules.
governmentofnorthkorea|North Korea.money: The North Korean state budget, which the Supreme People's Assembly sets; the Cabinet prepares it.
governmentofnorthkorea|North Korea.arts: The state Mansudae Art Studio, founded in 1959, is the only body sanctioned to portray the Kim family; its Overseas Project Group has built monuments in Africa and Asia.

governmentofontario|Canada.what: The provincial government of Ontario, Canada, led by Premier Doug Ford since June 2018, with its legislature at Queen's Park in Toronto.
governmentofontario|Canada.money: The Ontario provincial budget: total expense is projected at C$232.5 billion for 2025-26.

governmentofpunjab|Pakistan.what: The provincial government of Punjab, Pakistan, based in Lahore; the Punjab Assembly elects the chief minister, who heads it with a cabinet.

governmentofsindhownspalace|Pakistan.what: The provincial government of Sindh, Pakistan, seated in Karachi and headed by a Chief Minister, with powers set out in the 1973 Constitution.
governmentofsindhownspalace|Pakistan.money: The provincial budget, which the Sindh Assembly passed for 2026-27 with a total outlay of Rs3.652 trillion.
governmentofsindhownspalace|Pakistan.arts: Its Culture, Tourism & Antiquities Department is one of its secretariat departments.

governorateofvaticancitystate|Vatican Ci.what: The government of Vatican City State; its president, Sister Raffaella Petrini since March 2025, also heads the Pontifical Commission, whose members the Pope appoints for five years.
governorateofvaticancitystate|Vatican Ci.money: Vatican City's own income from stamps, coins, medals, souvenirs, museum admission and publications: revenues of €770 million in 2021.

gracejuddlanders.what: A New Britain, Connecticut widow who in 1934 gave her house to the New Britain Institute; the art museum opened there in 1937.
gracejuddlanders.money: Her own estate, much of which she lost in the 1929 stock market crash.

gracekennedy.money: GraceKennedy’s money comes from food manufacturing and distribution and from financial services, in Jamaica and abroad.

facts.t: GraceKennedy’s revenue rose 6.4% to J$177.8 billion in 2025, while net profit fell 18% to J$7.25 billion after Hurricane Melissa.

grandcasinodelyonlepharaonaspartenairehi.what: A casino with slot machines and gaming tables at the Cité Internationale in Lyon's 6th arrondissement, run by Groupe Partouche, the casino group Isidore Partouche founded in 1973.
grandcasinodelyonlepharaonaspartenairehi.money: Gaming revenue; its parent Groupe Partouche reported €460.2 million of revenue for the year to 31 October 2025, €415 million from casinos.

greaterlondonauthoritypublicfunding.what: The devolved regional government of Greater London, established in 2000 and made up of the Mayor of London and the 25-member London Assembly.
greaterlondonauthoritypublicfunding.money: Government grants and retained business rates of £8,466.8 million and £1,667.0 million from council tax payers in its 2026 to 2027 budget.

greatersheppartoncouncil|Australia.what: The local council for the City of Greater Shepparton, a local government area in the Hume region of Victoria, Australia, established in 1994.

greekministryofculture|Greece.what: The Greek government ministry for cultural heritage and the arts, set up on 26 August 1971 as the Ministry of Culture and Sciences; Lina Mendoni is minister.
greekministryofculture|Greece.money: The Greek state budget, which allotted it €189,293,000 for 2025.
greekministryofculture|Greece.arts: Its agencies include the Acropolis Museum, the National Gallery in Athens, the National Theatre of Greece and the Athens Epidaurus Festival.

greenbergfamily.what: The Ottawa family behind the Minto Group, a real estate company founded in Ottawa in 1955 by four Greenberg brothers; Roger Greenberg is its executive chairman.
greenbergfamily.money: Profits of the Minto Group, a privately held real estate company active across North America.
greenbergfamily.arts: The family gives to health, sports, arts and education causes.

grnlandsbanken.what: One of Greenland's two commercial banks, founded by Danish banks on 26 May 1967, listed on the Copenhagen stock exchange and headquartered in Nuuk.
grnlandsbanken.money: Lending, deposits and services for about 50,000 customers in Greenland: profit before tax of DKK 181.4 million in 2025.

groupedassault.what: The Dassault family's holding company, which traces its start to the aircraft maker Marcel Dassault set up in 1929; Éric Trappier has led it since 2025.
groupedassault.money: Its holdings: 62% of Dassault Aviation, which owns 26% of the defence group Thales, 45.1% of Dassault Systèmes, Groupe Figaro and Immobilière Dassault.
groupedassault.arts: It owns the Paris auction house Artcurial and runs a group patronage programme.

groupegalerieslafayette.what: A French retail group owned by the Moulin family, grown from a Paris shop Théophile Bader and Alphonse Kahn opened in 1894; it runs Galeries Lafayette stores and La Redoute.
groupegalerieslafayette.money: Retail sales in its stores and brands, €4.5 billion a year, and property held through its real estate arm Citynove.

groupewendel.what: A French listed investment company in Paris, controlled by the Wendel family, whose business began when Jean-Martin Wendel bought the Hayange forges in 1704.
groupewendel.money: Returns on the companies it owns stakes in, with consolidated revenue of 7.1 billion euros in 2023.
groupewendel.arts: It was awarded the title Grand Mécène de la Culture in 2012, and the chairman of its supervisory board sits on the Centre Pompidou-Metz board.

grupograda.what: A Panamanian communications and technology group in Panama City that owns the IT supplier Data Serve and radio stations including Estereo Azul, Antena 8 and Crush 89.7.
grupograda.money: Sales of IT equipment, audio and video systems and services through Data Serve, in business since 1989, and advertising on its radio stations.

grupohabita.money: Grupo Habita’s money comes from running boutique hotels in Mexico.

grupopromerica.what: A regional banking group that grew from Banpro, the Nicaraguan bank Ramiro Ortiz Mayorga founded in Managua in November 1991 with 133 partners; it now operates in nine countries.
grupopromerica.money: Interest and fees from its banks: Banpro in Nicaragua, Banco Promerica in five countries, Produbanco in Ecuador and St. Georges Bank.

grupoultra.what: A Brazilian holding company founded in 1937 by Ernesto Igel as a home gas distributor, seated in São Paulo.
grupoultra.money: Fuel distribution through Ipiranga, LPG sales through Ultragaz and liquid bulk storage through Ultracargo: net revenue of BRL 147 billion in 2022.

facts.t: Ultrapar reported net profit of R$2.542 billion for 2025, up 1%, on net revenue of R$142.478 billion.

gstaserlachiusfinearts.what: A private fine arts foundation in Mänttä, Finland, set up in 1933 by the industrialist Gösta Serlachius to keep his art collection and build a museum.
gstaserlachiusfinearts.money: An endowment from Gösta Serlachius: nearly 3,000 shares in G.A. Serlachius, his family's paper company, plus property.
gstaserlachiusfinearts.arts: Its collections hold more than 10,000 works, known for Finnish Golden Age art and old European masters.

guangdongprovincialauthorities|China.what: The provincial government of Guangdong, China's most populous province and largest provincial economy, seated in the capital Guangzhou.

gucci.what: An Italian luxury fashion house founded in Florence in 1921 by Guccio Gucci and owned since 1999 by the French luxury group Kering.
gucci.money: Sales of clothing, leather goods, shoes and accessories: 7.65 billion euros in 2024.

guineanstate|Guinea.what: The national government of Guinea, led by Mamady Doumbouya, who took power in a 2021 coup and won the presidential election of 28 December 2025.

gulbenkian.what: A Portuguese foundation set up in Lisbon in 1956 under the will of Calouste Gulbenkian, an Armenian oil magnate; it runs the Gulbenkian Museum and Orchestra.
gulbenkian.money: An endowment from Calouste Gulbenkian's oil fortune; it fully owned the oil company Partex until selling it to a Thai company in 2019.

gulfstream.what: An American maker of business jets, a subsidiary of the defence contractor General Dynamics since 1999, headquartered in Savannah, Georgia, where it set up in 1967.
gulfstream.money: Sales and servicing of its business jets, such as the G650, G700 and G800; General Dynamics' aerospace division brought 23% of group revenue in 2024.

gyeongnam.what: The government of South Gyeongsang Province in southeastern South Korea, seated in Changwon since 1983; Park Wan-su is governor.
gyeongnam.money: Provincial taxes and national government money: a 2026 budget of KRW 14.2845 trillion, as proposed in November 2025.

habasit.what: A Swiss maker of conveyor and power transmission belts, founded in 1946 by Fernand and Alice Habegger, with its head office and a main plant in Reinach, Basel-Landschaft.
habasit.money: Sales of its belts and conveyor components to food, packaging, printing and other industries in more than 70 countries.

habibbank.what: A Pakistani commercial bank founded in 1941 in Bombay by the Habib family, headquartered at Habib Bank Plaza in Karachi and controlled by the Aga Khan Fund for Economic Development.
habibbank.money: Consumer, business and Islamic banking: revenue of Rs. 361.10 billion and net income of Rs. 66.76 billion in 2025.

haim.what: An Israeli-American media investor born in 1944, founder of Saban Entertainment and chairman and chief executive of Saban Capital Group, a private investment firm in Los Angeles.
haim.money: Children's television, including Power Rangers, and the 2001 sale of Fox Family Worldwide to Disney for $5.3 billion, from which he profited about $1.6 billion.

halabja.what: An Iraqi business group based in Sulaymaniyah and chaired by Aso Bamoki, which grew from the Halabja Group for Trading set up in the late 1980s.
halabja.money: Construction, petroleum, trading, real estate, telecommunications and education businesses in Iraq, China, the United Arab Emirates and Turkey, with over 1,750 employees.

halifaxni.what: An independent grant-making charity in Belfast, incorporated on 17 December 1985, one of four sister foundations covering England and Wales, Scotland, Northern Ireland and the Channel Islands.
halifaxni.money: Lloyds Banking Group's profits: the four foundations together receive 0.5 percent of the group's pre-tax profits.

hamber.what: A private foundation in Vancouver set up in 1964 by Aldyen Irene Hamber in memory of her husband Eric Hamber, Lieutenant-Governor of British Columbia from 1937 to 1941.
hamber.money: An endowment from Aldyen Hamber: a C$1 million gift in 1964 and the residue of her estate after her death in 1988.
hamber.arts: It makes grants for cultural, educational and charitable projects in British Columbia.

hamburgischekulturstiftung.what: A private-law foundation in Hamburg founded in 1988 on the initiative of Ingo von Münch, then the city’s culture senator, to fund young artists and youth culture.
hamburgischekulturstiftung.money: Founding capital of 2.5 million DM from the City of Hamburg, plus gifts from private donors, foundations and companies.
hamburgischekulturstiftung.arts: It supported more than 1,900 projects with 15 million euros in all from 1988 to the end of 2019.

hamburgministryofculture|Germany.what: One of eleven departments of the Senate of the Free and Hanseatic City of Hamburg, responsible for culture and media policy; Carsten Brosda has headed it since February 2017.
hamburgministryofculture|Germany.money: The Hamburg state budget: 461 million euros for culture and media in 2025 and 474 million euros in 2026.
hamburgministryofculture|Germany.arts: Its culture office covers theatre, music, the Elbphilharmonie, art, museums, libraries and remembrance culture.

hanafinancial.what: A South Korean financial holding company in Seoul, formed in 2005 around Hana Bank; it bought control of Korea Exchange Bank in 2012.
hanafinancial.money: Interest and fees from its bank, card, securities, insurance and capital companies: net profit of 4.0 trillion won (KRW) in 2025.

hannoverrck.what: A German reinsurance company founded on 6 June 1966 and based in Hannover, one of the world's three largest reinsurers; Talanx holds 50.2% of its voting rights.
hannoverrck.money: Reinsurance premiums paid by insurers worldwide for property, casualty, life and health risks, about €33 billion gross a year.

hansrasmusastrup.what: A Norwegian foundation in Oslo set up in 2013 by the shipbroker and art collector Hans Rasmus Astrup to support the Astrup Fearnley Collection.
hansrasmusastrup.money: The capital and assets of Hans Rasmus Astrup, head of the family shipbroking firm Fearnleys, who gave them all to the foundation.
hansrasmusastrup.arts: Its statutes let it acquire Norwegian and international modern art for the collection shown at Astrup Fearnley Museet.

hansu.what: A private foundation in Basel, set up in 1999 by Maja Oeri and her husband Hans U. Bodenmann in memory of their son Laurenz Jakob; it built and manages Schaulager.
hansu.money: The private fortune of Maja Oeri, granddaughter of Emanuel Hoffmann, whose father Fritz Hoffmann-La Roche founded the Roche pharmaceutical group in 1896.
hansu.arts: It gave CHF 50 million, half the cost, for the Kunstmuseum Basel extension opened in 2016, and funds two art history professorships at the University of Basel.

hanswerner.what: A private foundation in Weinheim set up in 1995 by Josephine Hector and Hans-Werner Hector, a co-founder of SAP; the couple added Hector Stiftung II in 2008.
hanswerner.money: The fortune of Hans-Werner Hector, who sold most of his SAP shares in 1996.
hanswerner.arts: It funds the Hector Kunstpreis, awarded yearly by the Kunsthalle Mannheim, and supports the Sammlung Prinzhorn in Heidelberg.
