kunsthallebern.arts: It buys works by artists shown at the Kunsthalle and lends them mainly to the Kunstmuseum Bern, and held about 400 works in 2016.

kunststiftungnrw.what: A public-law foundation set up on 12 September 1989 by the North Rhine-Westphalia state government under Johannes Rau, based in the Haus der Stiftungen in Düsseldorf.
kunststiftungnrw.money: The proceeds of the lottery operator WestLotto.
kunststiftungnrw.arts: It has funded about 12,000 projects in literature, music, performing arts and visual art with a link to North Rhine-Westphalia since 1989.

kunststiftungvolkswagen.what: A charitable foundation under civil law in Wolfsburg that operates the Kunstmuseum Wolfsburg.
kunststiftungvolkswagen.money: Most of its money comes from the Holler-Stiftung, set up in 1990 from the estate of Asta and Christian Holler, former owners of Volkswagen Versicherungsdienst.

kurabo.what: A Japanese textile and chemicals group founded on 9 March 1888 as Kurashiki Spinning Works in Kurashiki, now headquartered in Osaka.
kurabo.money: Sales of textiles, chemical products, advanced technology equipment, food services and real estate.

kuraray.what: A Japanese chemicals and fibre maker founded in Kurashiki in 1926 by Magosaburō Ōhara and Torajiro Kojima, with head offices in Tokyo and Osaka.
kuraray.money: Sales of chemicals, resins, synthetic fibres, high performance materials and dental materials; its main plants are in Kurashiki.

kuwaitpetroleum.what: Kuwait's state-owned oil company, founded on 27 January 1980 as the umbrella for KOC, KNPC, KOTC and PIC, headquartered in Kuwait City.
kuwaitpetroleum.money: Sales of Kuwait's crude oil, refined products and petrochemicals; revenue was KWD 30.06 billion in fiscal 2024/25.

kyocera.what: A Japanese ceramics and electronics manufacturer founded in Kyoto in 1959 by Kazuo Inamori as Kyoto Ceramic Company, renamed in 1982.
kyocera.money: Sales of industrial ceramics, semiconductor packages, electronic components, solar power systems and office printers; revenue was ¥1.58 trillion in 2018.
kyocera.arts: It runs the Kyocera Museum of Fine Ceramics and the Kyocera Gallery.

lacaixa.money: The "la Caixa" Foundation's budget comes from the dividends its holding CriteriaCaixa receives from its stakes in companies, CaixaBank first among them, with Naturgy, Telefónica and others.

facts.t: CaixaBank reported a net profit of 5,891 million euros for 2025, up 1.8%.
Banking on Climate Chaos 2026 reports that CaixaBank diluted its coal commitments in the past year, backtracking on metallurgical coal used for steelmaking.
CaixaBank declared EU lobbying costs of €600,000 to €699,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

lacity|USA.what: A department of the City of Los Angeles that makes grants to arts and cultural organisations and artists and manages the city's cultural programmes.
lacity|USA.money: By city code, an amount equal to 1% of expected hotel Transient Occupancy Tax revenue, plus Arts Development Fees paid on non-residential building projects.

lambent.what: A New York grantmaker for art, culture and social justice founded by the artist Anne Delaney, grown out of her Starry Night Fund of 2002.
lambent.money: Anne Delaney's philanthropy, held as a fiscally sponsored project of the Tides Center, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit.
lambent.arts: It funds contemporary art and culture tied to social justice in New York City, New Orleans and Nairobi.

lanacin.what: The national government of Colombia, a unitary presidential republic with its capital in Bogotá.

landberlin|Germany.what: The state government of Berlin: the Senate, led by the Governing Mayor (Der Regierende Bürgermeister) through the Senatskanzlei.
landberlin|Germany.money: The Berlin state budget passed by the Abgeordnetenhaus, about EUR 45.5 billion for 2026 and EUR 46.5 billion for 2027.
landberlin|Germany.arts: Its Senate Department for Culture and Social Cohesion has EUR 957.3 million in non-staff funds for 2026, down from EUR 1.026 billion in 2025.

landcareaustralia.what: An independent national not-for-profit for environmental conservation and sustainable land management, set up in 1989, when landcare became a national movement championed by Prime Minister Bob Hawke.
landcareaustralia.money: Grants from government partners, sponsorship from corporate partners and public donations.

landobersterreich|Austria.what: The government of Upper Austria, one of Austria's nine states, run from the Amt der Oö. Landesregierung in Linz.
landobersterreich|Austria.money: The Upper Austrian state budget, about EUR 9.9 billion for 2026, planned with a deficit of about EUR 255 million.

landofsalzburg|Austria.what: A federal state (Land) of Austria with 561,714 inhabitants (2021 census), governed from the city of Salzburg; Governor Karoline Edtstadler heads its government.
landofsalzburg|Austria.money: The state budget: about EUR 4.5 billion for 2026, approved in the Salzburg Landtag on 26 November 2025.
landofsalzburg|Austria.arts: The 2026 budget gives EUR 105 million to art, culture and religious affairs (Kunst, Kultur und Kultus).

landvorarlberg|Austria.what: The administration of the government of the Austrian state of Vorarlberg, population 401,674, led by Landeshauptmann Markus Wallner (ÖVP) and seated in the Landhaus in Bregenz.
landvorarlberg|Austria.money: The state budget of Vorarlberg, which plans €2.8 billion in spending for 2026, including about €200 million in new borrowing.

langhamhotels.money: Langham's money comes from hotels, run by Langham Hospitality Group, part of Hong Kong's Great Eagle Holdings.

langlois.what: A private charitable foundation set up in Montreal in 1997 by Daniel Langlois (1957 to 2023), the founder of the 3D animation software company Softimage.
langlois.money: Daniel Langlois's fortune from Softimage, the company he founded in 1986, which Microsoft bought for 130 million dollars in 1994.
langlois.arts: It supports artistic, scientific and technological research and keeps a documentation collection on electronic and media arts from the 1960s onward.

laskinfamily.what: A private family foundation in Milwaukee, tax-exempt since March 1968; James P. Laskin is its president and William A. Laskin its vice president and treasurer.
laskinfamily.money: Contributions it receives: $10.5 million of its $10.9 million revenue in 2025 and $592,080 of $1.18 million in 2024.

lassonde.money: Pierre Lassonde’s money comes from gold mining finance: he co-founded the royalty company Franco-Nevada and led Newmont.

latam.what: A Chilean airline holding company formed in 2012 when LAN Airlines took over Brazil's TAM Linhas Aéreas, headquartered in Santiago and listed in Santiago and New York.
latam.money: Passenger and cargo flights, with US$13.034 billion revenue in 2024; Sixth Street Partners, Delta Air Lines and Qatar Airways are its largest shareholders.

latrobeuniversity.what: A public research university in Victoria, Australia, established on 9 December 1964, with its main campus in Bundoora, Melbourne, and regional campuses.
latrobeuniversity.money: Government funding and student fees; its budget was A$863.7 million in 2023.

latvianministryofculture|Latvia.what: The Latvian state institution that organises and coordinates culture, social integration and media policy, based in Riga.

lauder.money: The Lauder fortune comes from the Estée Lauder Companies, which sell cosmetics, skincare and fragrance.

facts.t: The Estée Lauder Companies reported net sales of $14,326 million for the fiscal year to June 2025, down from $15,608 million.

Leonard Lauder gave $248,100 in personal contributions to federal candidates, parties and PACs in the 2023 to 2024 cycle; the largest went to Senate Impact Project ($23,100), New York State Democratic Committee ($10,000) and Arizona Democratic Party ($10,000), in contributions reported to the Federal Election Commission.

lavazza.money: Lavazza's money comes from roasting and selling coffee; the Lavazza family owns the group.

facts.t: Luigi Lavazza S.p.A. declared EU lobbying costs of €50,000 to €99,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register, with 1.75 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.

lazardfreresgestion.what: A foundation created in 2020 with the Institut de France by Lazard Frères Gestion, which is owned 99.99% by Compagnie Financière Lazard Frères.
lazardfreresgestion.money: Lazard Frères Gestion's asset management business in Paris; the firm has sponsored heritage projects since 2007.
lazardfreresgestion.arts: It paid for restoring Pierre Dulin's painting of the Hôtel Royal des Invalides, finished in March 2021, and supports four Institut National du Patrimoine students each year.

lazraq.money: The Lazraq family’s money comes from Groupe Alliances, the listed Moroccan property developer Alami Lazraq founded in 1994.

facts.t: Alliances reported consolidated revenue of 2.363 billion dirhams for 2024, up 17%, and consolidated net income of 305 million dirhams.

lazraqfamily.what: A Moroccan property developer listed in Casablanca, founded by Alami Lazraq, who chairs it and controls 51.7 percent of its shares.
lazraqfamily.money: Sales of residential, commercial and tourism property developments across North Africa.
lazraqfamily.arts: Its cultural patronage covers the Fondation MACAAL, built on the art collection of Alami and Farida Lazraq, and a sculpture park.

lecorbusier.what: A French foundation recognised as of public utility by decree on 24 July 1968, universal legatee of the architect Le Corbusier; its seat is the Maison Jeanneret, Paris.
lecorbusier.money: Le Corbusier left it everything he owned, including his archives and the moral and economic rights to all his works, which ADAGP manages.

leechin.money: Michael Lee-Chin’s money comes from AIC mutual funds and Portland Holdings, his investment company.

leedscitycouncil|UK.what: The local authority for the City of Leeds in West Yorkshire, a metropolitan borough council since 1974, which meets at Leeds Civic Hall.
leedscitycouncil|UK.money: Council tax and UK government funding; for 2026/27 its government resources rose by £71.1m and council tax by 4.99 per cent.

leica.what: A German maker of cameras, lenses and optics in Wetzlar, with roots in Carl Kellner's Optical Institute of 1849; Andreas Kaufmann's ACM holds 55% and Blackstone 45%.
leica.money: Sales of cameras, lenses and other optical products; turnover was €596 million in 2024/25.
leica.arts: It runs about 30 Leica galleries and gives the Leica Oskar Barnack Award and the Leica Hall of Fame Award to photographers.

lekoilnigeria.money: Lekoil’s money comes from oil exploration and production in Nigeria.

lendlease.what: An Australian property and construction group founded in Sydney in 1958 by Dick Dusseldorp, with its head office in the International Towers at Barangaroo.
lendlease.money: Property investment, development, construction and asset management: AUD 8.82 billion revenue in 2022.

leonblack.what: An American private equity investor who co-founded Apollo Global Management in 1990 and was its CEO; he chaired the Museum of Modern Art from 2018 to 2021.
leonblack.money: His retained stake in Apollo Global Management; Bloomberg put his net worth at about US$13.8 billion in 2026.

leonidmikhelsonvac.money: Leonid Mikhelson’s money comes from Novatek, the gas producer of which he is chairman and major shareholder.

leonjimenes.money: The León Jimenes family’s money comes from tobacco, through the La Aurora cigar company its founder set up in 1903, and from beer.

facts.t: In 2012 E. León Jimenes sold 41.76% of the Cervecería Nacional Dominicana to AmBev for US$1 billion in cash, keeping a minority stake.

lesamisdesmusesdartetdhistoireluxembourg.what: A Luxembourg non-profit association of friends of six museums, under the patronage of the Grand Duchess, tracing its history to the Société des Amis des Musées founded in 1926.
lesamisdesmusesdartetdhistoireluxembourg.money: Members' subscriptions and donations; gifts and bequests can also go to its public-utility foundation, the Fondation des Amis des Musées.
lesamisdesmusesdartetdhistoireluxembourg.arts: It helps the museums acquire works, among them Jacques Monory's La terrasse no. 5 for the Musée national.

leventis.what: A private foundation set up in May 1979 under provisions made by Anastasios G. Leventis, a Greek Cypriot trader in West Africa, with its executive office in Zurich.
leventis.money: The fortune Anastasios G. Leventis made with A. G. Leventis & Company, his West African trading group founded in 1936.
leventis.arts: Its own initiatives are the A. G. Leventis Gallery and the Leventis Municipal Museum, and it gives grants for heritage conservation, museums and libraries.

leverhulme.what: A UK grant-making charity in London, established in 1925 under the will of the 1st Viscount Leverhulme to fund scholarships for research and education.
leverhulme.money: Its shareholding in Unilever plc, which began as shares in Lever Brothers; it gives out over £100 million a year.

levistrauss.money: Levi Strauss & Co.'s money comes from selling jeans and other clothing.

facts.t: Levi Strauss & Co.'s revenue was $6,282 million in its fiscal year to November 2025.
Outside firms reported $230,000 in 2025 fees from Levi Strauss & Company for US federal lobbying, under the Lobbying Disclosure Act; it filed no in-house report.
Levi Strauss & Co declared EU lobbying costs of €100,000 to €199,999 for its year from December 2024 to November 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

lexus.what: The luxury car division of the Japanese carmaker Toyota Motor Corporation, launched in 1989 and headquartered in Toyota City, Aichi.
lexus.money: Sales of Lexus cars within Toyota Motor Corporation, whose revenue was ¥48.04 trillion in 2025.

lg.money: LG’s money here comes from LG Electronics, which makes televisions, home appliances, vehicle parts and air conditioning.

facts.t: LG Electronics reported 2025 consolidated revenue of KRW 89.2 trillion and operating profit of KRW 2.48 trillion.
In December 2012 the European Commission fined LG Electronics €295.6 million for its part in two cathode ray tube cartels, and LG and Philips a further €392 million jointly.

libbeys.what: Edward Drummond Libbey, owner of the Libbey Glass Company in Toledo, founded the Toledo Museum of Art in 1901 and led it until 1925; Florence Scott Libbey was his wife.
libbeys.money: Edward Libbey's fortune from Libbey Glass, the Owens Bottle Machine Company and Libbey-Owens Sheet Glass, given to the museum as the Libbey Endowment.
libbeys.arts: The Toledo Museum of Art still buys art from the Libbey Endowment, for example a Sasanian silver plate in 2022.

libertyinnorthkorea.what: A US nonprofit that rescues North Korean refugees hiding in China and resettles them, founded at Yale University on 27 March 2004 and registered in Long Beach, California.
libertyinnorthkorea.money: Donations, including money raised by school, college and church Rescue Teams: USD 4,214,232 in 2025.

liljestrand.what: A Honolulu nonprofit, tax-exempt since 2008 and led by members of the Liljestrand family, that preserves the 1952 house Vladimir Ossipoff designed for Howard and Betty Liljestrand.
liljestrand.money: Gifts from the Friends of the Liljestrand Foundation and guided tour income, with revenue of $496,717 in 2023.

lilly.what: A private foundation in Indianapolis, created in 1937 by J.K. Lilly Sr. and his sons Eli and J.K. Jr. through gifts of Eli Lilly and Company stock.
lilly.money: Its endowment, mostly Eli Lilly and Company stock; total assets were US$106 billion in 2025.

linbury.what: A UK grant-making trust, one of the Sainsbury Family Charitable Trusts, set up by Lord Sainsbury of Preston Candover and the ballerina Anya Linden, first granting in 1973.
linbury.money: Investment income and donations; it held funds of £135.0 million at 5 April 2025.
linbury.arts: In the year to April 2025 it paid £3.7 million to culture, including £2.25 million to the National Gallery's Sainsbury Wing.

lincolnfinancial.what: A US insurance and asset management company trading as Lincoln Financial Group, organised in Indiana in 1968 with roots in 1905, headquartered in Radnor, Pennsylvania.
lincolnfinancial.money: Premiums and fees from insurance and asset management, including group life, disability and dental cover; revenue was US$19.230 billion in 2021.

lindapaceendowment.what: A private foundation in San Antonio, founded in 2003 as owner and steward of the art collection of Linda Pace (1945 to 2007), founder of Artpace.
lindapaceendowment.money: The fortune of Linda Pace, whose parents owned Pace Foods, with total assets of $95,476,515 in 2024.
lindapaceendowment.arts: It runs the exhibition spaces Ruby City and Studio in San Antonio and lends works from its collection to museums.

linklaters.what: The corporate foundation of the Paris office of the law firm Linklaters, created in 2015 and chaired by the competition partner Anne Wachsmann-Guigon.
linklaters.money: The law firm Linklaters LLP, headquartered in London, which reported revenues of £2.32 billion in the 2024-25 financial year.
linklaters.arts: It funds image-education programmes for young people at LE BAL in Paris; the Paris office has collected photography since 2010, beginning with Raymond Depardon.

linzagascorepartners.what: A utility holding company formed in October 2000 from the merger of ESG and Stadtbetriebe Linz, wholly owned by the City of Linz through its holding company.
linzagascorepartners.money: Energy supply, municipal services and public transport in Linz and 115 other municipalities: revenue of 1,182.8 million euros in the year to 30 September 2025.

lionfoundation.money: A gaming trust: its money is what players lose on the pokie machines it runs in pubs and hotels, which such trusts are required to give out, 40 percent of revenue by its own account, to community groups.

facts.t: The Department of Internal Affairs laid five charges of breaching the Gambling Act against the Lion Foundation over how much it knew of a person's use of pokie grants to benefit Southland Rugby and an Invercargill restaurant.
Its former chief executive David Conroy was found guilty of false accounting over journal entries made in 2002 to 2004 in the Lion Foundation accounts, in a case brought by the Serious Fraud Office.
Conroy was sentenced to 12 months' home detention and 300 hours of community work.

littlegreene.what: A British paint and wallpaper maker in Manchester, incorporated on 22 May 1996, founded by the chemist David Mottershead and run by him and his family.
littlegreene.money: Sales of house paint and wallpaper, with a factory in Wales.
littlegreene.arts: It has a partnership with the National Trust to develop designs from the Trust's collections.

littlesun.what: A Berlin nonprofit founded in 2012 by the artist Olafur Eliasson and the engineer Frederik Ottesen to bring solar energy to off-grid communities in Africa.
littlesun.money: Donations, funder grants and sales of its solar products; Bloomberg Philanthropies made a US$5 million impact investment in 2014.

liuna.what: A trade union of construction and energy workers in the United States and Canada, founded in 1903 and headquartered in Washington, DC, with about half a million members.
liuna.money: Its 2024 US tax return reports US$111.0 million in revenue, 89.7% of it program service revenue and 6.4% investment income.

liuyiqian.what: A Chinese investor and art collector born in Shanghai in 1963, chairman of the Shanghai investment company Sunline Group and co-founder of the Long Museum with his wife Wang Wei.
liuyiqian.money: Investments since the mid-1980s in listed shares, real estate and pharmaceuticals, giving a net worth Forbes put at USD 1.37 billion in July 2015.

facts.t: Guohua Life Insurance, which Liu Yiqian chairs and cofounded, announced losses of between $23.3m and $28.7m for the first half of 2023.

liverpoolcitycouncil|UK.what: The local authority for the city of Liverpool, a metropolitan borough council since 1974, under Labour control since 2010, with main offices in the Cunard Building.
liverpoolcitycouncil|UK.money: Business rates (£295.1m), council tax (£277.0m) and general government grants (£245.5m) in its 2026-27 budget, £1.8bn gross.

lkab.money: LKAB’s money comes from iron ore mined at Kiruna and Malmberget; the Swedish state has owned all of it since 1976.

facts.t: Mining destabilised the ground under Kiruna and put the town at risk of collapse; LKAB proposed moving the town 3 km east and had allocated about SEK 12 billion to it.

llbean.what: A privately held American retailer of clothing and outdoor equipment, founded in 1912 by Leon Leonwood Bean in Freeport, Maine, where it is still headquartered.
llbean.money: Sales of clothing, footwear and outdoor recreation equipment; revenue was US$1.7 billion in 2023.

localfirmssilson.what: A private company in Southam, Warwickshire, established in 1994 to make thin membranes for X-ray microscopy.
localfirmssilson.money: Sales of silicon nitride and other thin membranes to more than 900 customers in 50 countries.

lockheedmartin.what: A US defence and aerospace manufacturer based in Bethesda, Maryland, formed on 15 March 1995 by the merger of the Lockheed Corporation with Martin Marietta.
lockheedmartin.money: US government contracts: 73 percent of its 2024 revenue came from the federal government, 65 percent from the Department of Defense.

facts.t: Lockheed Martin reported 2025 sales of $75.0 billion and net earnings of $5.0 billion.

Bellingcat recorded 79 geolocated incidents in Gaza where remnants of US-made munitions, among them the Hellfire missile Lockheed Martin makes, were found after strikes, many of which caused death and damage to schools, homes and healthcare buildings.
Lockheed Martin reported $15,550,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act (an amended second-quarter report counted once).

lombardodier.what: A Geneva private bank founded on 11 January 1796, organised as a partnership limited by shares under six managing partners, with headquarters at 1Roof in Bellevue, Geneva.
lombardodier.money: Fees from wealth management, asset management and banking IT services; assets under management were CHF 349 billion in 2023.

lonablottery|Burkina Faso.what: Burkina Faso's national lottery, created on 10 May 1967 by ordinance and a state-owned company (société d'État) since November 1994, based in Ouagadougou.
lonablottery|Burkina Faso.money: Sales of lottery tickets, PMU'B horse-race bets and other games; turnover grew from 30 million FCFA in 1967 to 110 billion FCFA in 2016.

lookgalapresentedbymawer.what: An independent, privately owned investment firm founded in Calgary in 1974 by Charles Mawer as Mawer & Associates.
lookgalapresentedbymawer.money: Fees for managing about C$64.0 billion for individual and institutional investors.
lookgalapresentedbymawer.arts: It pledges at least 1% of pre-tax profits to community causes, which include the arts, and reports more than C$2.5 million donated.

losangelescounty|USA.what: A California county formed on 18 February 1850 and governed by an elected five-member Board of Supervisors, with an estimated 9,694,934 residents in 2025.
losangelescounty|USA.money: The county budget: USD 52.5 billion for 2025-26, as adopted by the Board of Supervisors on 30 September 2025.

loterieromande.what: A public-benefit lottery and sports betting company created in 1937 under an agreement between the governments of the French-speaking Swiss cantons, based in Lausanne; Jura joined in 1979.
loterieromande.money: Lottery and sports betting: gross gaming revenue was CHF 429.8 million in 2025, and its whole profit, CHF 252 million, went to associations.
loterieromande.arts: Its profit goes to associations in culture, social welfare, health, research, education, the environment, tourism, heritage and sport.

lotterywest.what: Western Australia's state lottery operator, set up in 1932 as the Lotteries Commission of Western Australia and headquartered in Subiaco, Perth.
lotterywest.money: Profits from its lottery games, shared under the Lotteries Commission Act 1990 among health, sport, the arts and direct community grants.
lotterywest.arts: The Act sends 5% of profits to the Arts Lottery Account (as of 2013), and Lotterywest is a major supporter of the Perth Festival.

lottothringen|Germany.what: The state lottery of Thuringia, a public-law institution (Anstalt des öffentlichen Rechts) of the Free State of Thuringia, seated in Suhl.
lottothringen|Germany.money: Players' stakes in the lotteries it runs in Thuringia under the 2021 State Treaty on Gambling.

louisartmuseum.what: A nonprofit in St. Louis, tax exempt since September 1985, that supports a single organisation, the Saint Louis Art Museum, and has the museum's director as its president.
louisartmuseum.money: Contributions ($9,188,525), investment income ($8,962,571) and asset sales ($6,707,045) in 2025, on net assets of $356,767,694.

louishansen.what: A Danish commercial foundation in Copenhagen, set up in 1969 by Johanne Louis-Hansen in memory of her husband Aage Louis-Hansen, founder of the ostomy products company Coloplast.
louishansen.money: Dividends on Coloplast shares: its subsidiary Aage og Johanne Louis-Hansen A/S holds 11 percent of the capital and 15 percent of the votes.
louishansen.arts: It gave an average of over 240 million kroner a year in 2019 to 2023, with art and culture the largest field by grants and amount.

louisroederer.what: A champagne house in Reims, founded in 1776 as Dubois Père & Fils, renamed by Louis Roederer in 1833 and still owned by his descendants, the Rouzaud family.
louisroederer.money: Sales of its champagnes, including Cristal, with over 3.5 million bottles shipped a year, and of wines from estates such as Château de Pez.
louisroederer.arts: Its Fondation Louis Roederer gives the Discovery Award at the Rencontres d'Arles photography festival.

louisvuitton.what: A Paris fashion house founded in 1854 by Louis Vuitton, now a subsidiary of the luxury group LVMH.
louisvuitton.money: Sales of leather goods, shoes, watches, jewellery and other luxury products; revenue was €14 billion in 2020.
louisvuitton.arts: In 2006 it opened the Espace Louis Vuitton, an exhibition space on the seventh floor of its Champs-Élysées store in Paris.

loukil.what: A Tunisian family business group founded in 1976 by Mohamed Loukil, who died in 2023, and chaired by his son Bassem Loukil; it works through about 30 companies.
loukil.money: Its companies in agriculture, heavy industry and consulting, and its role as Tunisian representative of Mazda, Kubota, Panasonic, Mitsubishi and Samsung.

lucas.money: George Lucas's money comes from Lucasfilm, the Star Wars studio he sold to Disney in 2012; Mellody Hobson is co-CEO of Ariel Investments.

facts.t: Forbes says George Lucas sold Lucasfilm to Disney in 2012 for $4.1 billion in stock and cash, and put his net worth at $5.5 billion on 17 November 2026.

luce.money: The Henry Luce Foundation was set up by Henry R. Luce, co-founder of Time, Fortune and Life, and lives on its endowment.

facts.t: The Henry Luce Foundation reported total assets of $1,090,872,427 at the end of 2023 and $48,012,564 in grants paid that year, in its Form 990-PF.

lucefdn.what: A private foundation formed in New York in 1936 by Henry R. Luce, co-founder of Time magazine and founder of Fortune and Life.
lucefdn.money: An endowment built from Henry R. Luce's stock in his publishing company, Time Inc., and his estate; total assets were US$1.09 billion in 2023.
lucefdn.arts: Its American Art Program, begun in 1980 with a US$4 million allocation as the Luce Fund for Scholarship in American Art, funds museum exhibitions and collection projects.

ludwig.what: A foundation in Aachen set up in 1997 by Irene Ludwig, a year after the death of her husband Peter Ludwig, to place their collection in public museums.
ludwig.money: The fortune of Irene and Peter Ludwig, who ran the Monheim chocolate company until its sale in 1986, then Ludwig Schokolade until 1998.

lukoil.money: Lukoil’s money comes from oil and gas: exploration, production, refining and sales in Russia and abroad.

facts.t: On 22 October 2025 the US Treasury designated Lukoil and Rosneft, Russia’s two largest oil companies, with a number of their Russian subsidiaries.

luma.what: A Zurich non-profit set up in 2004 by Maja Hoffmann to support contemporary artists; it created the LUMA Arles arts campus, launched in 2013.
luma.money: Its founder Maja Hoffmann belongs to the shareholder pool of Roche founder descendants, which controls Roche Holding.

lvmhlouisvuitton.money: LVMH's money comes from selling luxury goods, wines and spirits, fashion, perfume, watches and jewellery (Louis Vuitton, Dior, Moët Hennessy, Bulgari and others); Bernard Arnault and his family control the group.

facts.t: LVMH reported 2025 revenue of €80,807 million and net profit (Group share) of €10,878 million.

In December 2021 a Paris court validated a settlement under which LVMH pays €10 million, ending an inquiry opened in 2011 into claims that it hired the former French domestic intelligence chief Bernard Squarcini to spy on private citizens, in particular the filmmaker François Ruffin.
LVMH Moët Hennessy Louis Vuitton declared EU lobbying costs of €2,000,000 to €2,249,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register, with 5.7 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.

LVMH Moët Hennessy Louis Vuitton Inc. paid the outside firm S-3 Group $240,000 for US federal lobbying in 2025 (four quarterly reports of $60,000 under the Lobbying Disclosure Act); Moët Hennessy USA reported $215,000 of its own in-house spending.

macallan.what: A single malt Scotch whisky distillery at Easter Elchies, Craigellachie, founded in 1824 by Alexander Reid and owned by Edrington, a private spirits company based in Glasgow.
macallan.money: Whisky sales, with all voting shares in its owner Edrington held by The Robertson Trust, a Scottish charity funded by the dividends.

mackelvie.money: The bequest of James Tannock Mackelvie (1824 to 1885), a businessman who kept an interest in Auckland affairs after returning to Britain; the trust still buys works for the collection.

macquarie.money: Macquarie Group is a Sydney investment bank and asset manager.

facts.t: Macquarie Group reported a net profit after tax of $A3,715 million for the year to 31 March 2025.

In its 2024-25 donor return to the Australian Electoral Commission, Macquarie Group Limited disclosed $205,483 in political donations: $103,543 to Labor branches and $101,940 to Liberal and National branches.

maddocks.what: An Australian law firm that began in Melbourne in 1885 as Maddock & Johnson, founded by Joe Maddocks and Arthur Johnson, with offices in Melbourne, Sydney and Canberra.
maddocks.money: Fees for legal work, from local government clients to construction, employment and commercial law; it has over 95 partners and 700 staff.

madepossiblebylaurenz.what: A private foundation in Basel, set up in 1999 by Maja Oeri and her husband Hans U. Bodenmann in memory of their son Laurenz Jakob; it built and manages Schaulager.
madepossiblebylaurenz.money: The private fortune of Maja Oeri, granddaughter of Emanuel Hoffmann, whose father Fritz Hoffmann-La Roche founded the Roche pharmaceutical group in 1896.
madepossiblebylaurenz.arts: It gave CHF 50 million, half the cost, for the Kunstmuseum Basel extension opened in 2016, and funds two art history professorships at the University of Basel.

madridcitycouncil|Spain.what: Madrid's city council, led by Mayor José Luis Martínez-Almeida of the Partido Popular, with its main seat in the Palacio de Cibeles since November 2007.
madridcitycouncil|Spain.money: The city budget: EUR 6,578 million for 2026, approved by the council plenary on 22 December 2025.

madriddestino.what: A municipal public company that manages Madrid's cultural venues, tourism and events, created in 2013 by merging municipal companies and based at the Conde Duque cultural centre.

maes.what: A Belgian brewery formed in 1988 by merging the Maes brewery at Kontich-Waarloos with Cristal-Alken at Alken, headquartered in Mechelen and owned by Heineken.
maes.money: Beer sales, with profits going to its owner, the Dutch brewer Heineken.

mainzerstadtwerke.what: The municipal utility company of the City of Mainz, supplying electricity, gas, water and public transport, with stakes in about 50 companies.
mainzerstadtwerke.money: Sales of electricity, gas, water and public transport in Mainz and nearby towns; revenue was €508 million in 2019.
mainzerstadtwerke.arts: It set up and supports the Stiftung Kunsthalle Mainz and a Mainz foundation for climate protection and energy efficiency.

malaysiasstateoil|Malaysia.what: Malaysia's state oil and gas company, founded on 17 August 1974, owned by the Government of Malaysia and based in the Petronas Towers in Kuala Lumpur.
malaysiasstateoil|Malaysia.money: Oil, natural gas and petrochemicals, with revenue of US$73.01 billion in 2023.

malberln.what: An independent cultural centre in Trnava, Slovakia, opened in March 2018 and run by the civic association Publikum.sk, founded in 2009.
malberln.money: Public and EU project grants, among them the EU-financed Zmina.Rebuilding programme for Ukrainian culture, plus rentals of its spaces.

manchestercitycouncilcorefunding|UK.what: The local authority for the city of Manchester in Greater Manchester, a metropolitan borough council since 1974, which meets at Manchester Town Hall on Albert Square.
manchestercitycouncilcorefunding|UK.money: Its revenue budget, which passed £1 billion for the first time in 2026/27 as national government funding improved.

manchestercitycouncil|United Kingdom.what: The local authority for the city of Manchester in Greater Manchester, a metropolitan borough council since 1974, which meets at Manchester Town Hall on Albert Square.
manchestercitycouncil|United Kingdom.money: Its revenue budget, which passed £1 billion for the first time in 2026/27 as national government funding improved.

mandel.what: A private family foundation in Cleveland, Ohio; the brothers Jack, Joseph and Morton Mandel set up their first charitable foundation in 1953.
mandel.money: The fortune the Mandel brothers made in Premier Industrial Corporation, which merged with Farnell Electronics in 1996 in a $3 billion deal.
mandel.arts: In 2026 it committed US$125 million to Case Western Reserve University, including a Mandel Humanities Building; its Boston institute runs a Cultural Leadership Program.

manitobaartscouncil|Canada.what: An arm's-length agency of the Province of Manitoba, established in 1965, that makes awards to professional artists and arts organisations through peer assessment.
manitobaartscouncil|Canada.money: The Manitoba provincial budget, through the department of Sport, Culture, Heritage and Tourism.
manitobaartscouncil|Canada.arts: Its budget was C$12.7 million in 2023.

manitobaliquor.what: A Crown corporation of the Province of Manitoba, established on 1 April 2014 under the Manitoba Liquor and Lotteries Corporation Act, based in Winnipeg.
manitobaliquor.money: Sales of liquor and gambling products, including casinos, VLTs and lottery tickets; it delivered C$724.1 million in profit to the Province of Manitoba in 2025-26.
manitobaliquor.arts: Its sponsorship and donation programmes totalled C$4.0 million in 2025-26.

mapei.what: A maker of adhesives, sealants and chemical products for building, founded in Milan in 1937 by Rodolfo Squinzi; the Squinzi family holds 93.95 percent through Emme Esse Vi.
mapei.money: Sales of building chemicals: EUR 4.4 billion revenue in 2025.

mapfre.money: Mapfre's money comes from insurance and reinsurance in Spain, Latin America and elsewhere; Fundación MAPFRE controls the listed company and lives on its dividends.

facts.t: Mapfre reported a 2025 net result of €1,078 million, up from €901.6 million, on premiums of €29,144.7 million.
MAPFRE S.A. declared EU lobbying costs of €500,000 to €599,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

mare.what: A Bucharest foundation set up in February 2015 to run MARe, the Museum of Recent Art, Romania's first private museum of local art from the last five decades.
mare.money: The private money of its founder Roger Akoury, a Lebanese-born pharmaceutical entrepreneur, who funded the building and assembled its collection of around 550 works.

mariahofmanntrust.what: A charitable trust created under the will of Renate Hofmann, widow of the painter Hans Hofmann, admitted to probate in New York County in 1996.
mariahofmanntrust.money: Sales of Hans Hofmann works it holds, through Miles McEnery Gallery, and investment dividends, with net assets of US$37,174,956 in June 2025.
mariahofmanntrust.arts: It supports exhibitions, publications and education on Hofmann's art and, under the will, gives to the Association of German Dioceses for people in need.

marinabaysands.what: A casino resort on Marina Bay in Singapore, owned by Las Vegas Sands and opened in 2010, with a casino, a 1,850-room hotel and a convention centre.
marinabaysands.money: Its casino, hotel, convention and retail business.

maritimeelectric.what: An electric utility serving Prince Edward Island, founded in 1918, headquartered in Charlottetown and owned by Fortis Inc.
maritimeelectric.money: Electricity sales to about 92,000 customers, at rates regulated by the Island Regulatory and Appeals Commission.

marriott.what: A US hotel company headquartered in Bethesda, Maryland, formed in 1993 as successor to the hospitality arm of the Marriott Corporation founded by J. Willard and Alice Marriott.
marriott.money: Operating, franchising and licensing hotel, residential and timeshare brands; revenue was US$26.2 billion in 2025.

marwanassaf.what: A board member of the Beirut Art Center and a trustee of the Sursock Museum in Beirut.

massachusettsculturalcouncil|USA.what: The public arts funding body of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, based in Boston, which makes grants to cultural organizations, schools, communities and individual artists.
massachusettsculturalcouncil|USA.money: An annual appropriation from the Massachusetts Legislature, plus funds from the National Endowment for the Arts.

massy.money: Massy’s money comes from a Trinidad and Tobago group of industrial gases, motors and machinery, and retail across the Caribbean.

facts.t: Massy’s third-party revenue rose 3% to TT$15.8 billion in the year to September 2025, and profit before tax from continuing operations rose 4% to TT$1.1 billion.

mastercard.money: Mastercard runs a global card payments network and takes fees on the transactions.

facts.t: In January 2019 the European Commission fined Mastercard €570,566,000 for limiting merchants' access to better conditions offered by banks elsewhere in the Single Market, in breach of EU antitrust rules.
Mastercard Worldwide reported $5,440,000 in US federal lobbying for 2025 in its own Lobbying Disclosure Act reports.
Mastercard Europe declared EU lobbying costs of €800,000 to €899,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

mazda.what: A Japanese carmaker founded on 30 January 1920 as Toyo Cork Kogyo by Jujiro Matsuda, headquartered in Fuchu, Hiroshima Prefecture.
mazda.money: Sales of cars and commercial vehicles: net sales of 4,918.2 billion yen in the year to March 2026.

mbhbank.what: A Hungarian bank formed on 1 May 2023 by merging MKB Bank, Takarékbank and Budapest Bank; Lőrinc Mészáros holds almost half the shares and the state-owned Corvinus 15%.
mbhbank.money: Interest and fees from banking in Hungary; net income was HUF 165.109 billion in 2025.

mcommemutuelle.what: A French mutual health insurer founded in 1870 and built up through mergers of local mutuals, headquartered in Lille with agencies across northern France and Normandy.
mcommemutuelle.money: Contributions from individual members and employer clients for its health and provident (prévoyance) insurance.

meadows.what: A Dallas foundation set up in 1948 by the oilman Algur H. Meadows and his wife Virginia to benefit the people of Texas.
meadows.money: An endowment from Algur Meadows's fortune in General American Oil Company of Texas, sold to Phillips Petroleum in 1983; assets $694 million in 2023.

megacable.money: Megacable’s money comes from cable television, internet and telephone services in Mexico.

facts.t: Megacable’s sales were 35,430 million pesos in 2025 and its net profit 2,840 million pesos (Análisis B×+ annual table).

mellon.money: The Andrew W. Mellon Foundation's endowment comes from the fortune of the Pittsburgh banker and industrialist Andrew W. Mellon, through his children Paul Mellon and Ailsa Mellon Bruce; the Paul Mellon Centre, part of Yale, and the Richard King Mellon Foundation of Pittsburgh are other Mellon family money named in these entries.

facts.t: The Andrew W. Mellon Foundation reported total assets of $8,027,994,221 at the end of 2023 and paid $549,292,394 in contributions and grants that year (Form 990-PF).
The Richard King Mellon Foundation reported total assets of $2,601,768,833 at the end of 2023 and paid $112,236,615 in contributions and grants that year (Form 990-PF).

memoriav.what: A Swiss non-profit association for preserving audiovisual heritage, founded in Bern on 1 December 1995 by institutions including the National Library and the Federal Archives.
memoriav.money: Federal money from the Federal Office of Culture under four-year performance agreements, on the basis of the Kulturförderungsgesetz since 2012.
memoriav.arts: It runs preservation projects with Swiss memory institutions and makes their holdings searchable on its Memobase portal.

mendeswooddm.what: A commercial contemporary art gallery founded in São Paulo in 2010 by Pedro Mendes, Matthew Wood and Felipe Dmab, with further spaces in Brussels, Paris and New York.
mendeswooddm.money: Sales of work by the artists it represents.

mendozafamily.money: The Mendoza family’s money came from the companies of Eugenio Mendoza Goiticoa, a Venezuelan industrialist.

mercator.what: A private foundation in Essen, run as a non-profit company, founded in 1996 by the Schmidt family of Duisburg, founders of the Metro wholesale group.
mercator.money: Donations from the Meridian Stiftung and the Cambiata Stiftung, which hold the Schmidt family's assets.
mercator.arts: It approved about EUR 58.5 million for 108 new projects in 2024.

mercedesbenz.money: Mercedes-Benz's money comes from making and selling cars and vans, and from car finance.

facts.t: Mercedes-Benz reported net profit of 5.3 billion euros for 2025, down almost 49 percent from 2024, AFP reported.
In a US settlement filed in September 2020 over undisclosed defeat devices in about 250,000 diesel vehicles, Daimler AG and Mercedes-Benz USA agreed to a recall and a civil penalty of $875 million.
Mercedes-Benz Group AG declared EU lobbying costs of €1,750,000 to €1,999,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.
Mercedes-Benz USA reported $1,365,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.
InfluenceMap gives Mercedes-Benz a C- grade for its climate policy engagement.

merciervanlanschot.what: The Belgian branch of the Dutch private bank Van Lanschot Kempen NV, trading under this name since January 2024 after Van Lanschot Belgium and Mercier Vanderlinden combined.
merciervanlanschot.money: Wealth management for clients with €10.5 billion of assets under management (third quarter 2023), run for its parent Van Lanschot Kempen.

mercisbv.what: An Amsterdam company set up by the designer Pieter Brattinga for Dick Bruna, which since 1971 has managed the worldwide rights to his illustrations, Miffy (nijntje) among them.
mercisbv.money: Licensing of Dick Bruna's illustrations for products, and his Dutch books through Mercis Publishing bv since 1995.

merian.what: A public-law foundation in Basel created by the 1857 will of Christoph Merian (1800 to 1858), active since 3 May 1886 under the supervision of the Bürgergemeinde der Stadt Basel.
merian.money: Income from CHF 1.8 billion of yield assets in 2025, made up of rental property, building leases and an equity fund.
merian.arts: Its culture department runs the Cartoonmuseum Basel and the Christoph Merian Verlag, and total giving in 2025 was CHF 23 million.

merribekcouncil|Australia.what: The local council for the City of Merri-bek in Melbourne's inner north, created as the City of Moreland in 1994 and renamed in September 2022, with its seat in Coburg.
merribekcouncil|Australia.money: Property rates, capped by the Victorian government; rates were set to raise A$202,778,329 for 2025-26.

methanex.money: Methanex, a Canadian company, makes methanol from natural gas at plants in the United States, Trinidad, New Zealand and elsewhere.

facts.t: Full year 2025 net income attributable to Methanex shareholders was $80 million, with Adjusted EBITDA of $808 million.
Bracewell LLP registered to lobby the US federal government for Methanex in the fourth quarter of 2025 and reported $40,000 in income from it.

methanexalso.what: A methanol producer headquartered in Vancouver, incorporated in 1992 when it split off from Ocelot, with plants in Canada, Chile, Egypt, New Zealand, Trinidad and Tobago and the US.
methanexalso.money: Sales of methanol, plus ammonia and other products; revenue was US$3.6 billion in 2025.

metrobank.what: A Philippine universal bank founded in Binondo, Manila, in 1962, with George Ty as founder, now headquartered at Metrobank Center in Taguig.
metrobank.money: Its banking business; GT Capital Holdings owns 39.8% and the Ty family and related parties 12.3%, with 47.8% public (June 2026).

miamidadecounty|USA.what: A county in southeast Florida with its seat in Miami, led by Mayor Daniella Levine Cava and a 13-member Board of County Commissioners.
miamidadecounty|USA.money: The county budget: the adopted budget for FY 2025-26 is $13.233 billion.

miamidesigndistrict.what: A partnership of Craig Robins's company Dacra and L Catterton Real Estate, a fund set up in 2016 by Catterton, LVMH and Groupe Arnault, that develops Miami's Design District.
miamidesigndistrict.money: The district's retail property, anchored by more than 200 luxury brands including Hermès, Dior and Cartier.
miamidesigndistrict.arts: The district holds a public art collection, including Buckminster Fuller's Fly's Eye Dome and Zaha Hadid's Elastika.

michaelaudain.what: A Canadian home builder and art collector, born in 1937, chairman since 1992 and a major shareholder of Polygon Homes Ltd. in Vancouver.
michaelaudain.money: His stake in Polygon Homes; he gives mainly through the Audain Foundation, which he set up in 1997 with Yoshiko Karasawa.
michaelaudain.arts: The Audain Foundation funds the annual C$100,000 Audain Prize for the Visual Arts and gave C$2 million to Arts Umbrella in 2023.

michaelotto.what: A German businessman born in 1943, son of Otto Group founder Werner Otto, who chaired its executive board from 1981 to 2007 and is honorary chairman of its supervisory board.
michaelotto.money: The family's Otto Group, the Hamburg mail order and online retailer founded in 1949, which had sales of €16.2 billion in 2023.
michaelotto.arts: In April 2015 he announced the transfer of his majority stake in the Otto Group to a charitable foundation whose payouts go to cultural, social and environmental projects.

middlesbroughcouncil|UK.what: The local authority for the Borough of Middlesbrough in England, a unitary authority since 1996, led by a directly elected mayor.
middlesbroughcouncil|UK.money: Council tax plus a £130.96 million government funding allocation for 2026/27 covering grants and retained business rates.

midea.money: The He family's fortune comes from Midea Group, the home appliance maker He Xiangjian founded.

facts.t: Midea Group reported 2024 revenue of RMB 409.1 billion and net profit attributable to shareholders of RMB 38.5 billion.
The Bureau of Investigative Journalism reported in August 2025 that Midea owns factories linked to China's Uyghur labour transfer scheme; Midea did not respond.
One outside firm reported $30,000 in 2025 fees from Midea America for US federal lobbying, under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

mikekelleyforarts.what: A private grantmaking foundation in Los Angeles, established in 2007 by the artist Mike Kelley, which also keeps his art collection and archives.
mikekelleyforarts.money: Its own assets, $87,212,377 at the end of 2025; contributions that year were $13,900.
mikekelleyforarts.arts: Its Artist Project Grants gave $400,000 to ten Los Angeles organisations in 2019; its Infinite Expansion Grants offer up to $50,000 per project.

millhouse.what: A Moscow company formed in 2006 to manage the assets of Roman Abramovich and his partners; in August 2024 it passed to Centrotrust, a Moscow company.
millhouse.money: The capital of Abramovich, under EU and UK sanctions since 2022, and his partners, who held Sibneft, Rusal and Aeroflot stakes through Millhouse Capital.

miltonkeynescouncil|UK.what: The unitary authority for Milton Keynes, England, created on 1 April 1974 as a borough council and renamed after the borough won city status on 15 August 2022.
miltonkeynescouncil|UK.money: A net budget of GBP 705.666 million in 2025/26, including GBP 407.174 million of Dedicated Schools Grant and GBP 188.333 million of council tax.

minalbajaj.what: A philanthropist, trustee and honorary director of the Jamnalal Bajaj Foundation since 2009, who founded the Mumbai NGO Hamaara Sapna in 2012.
minalbajaj.money: Her support for the biennale runs through Bajaj Beyond, an initiative of the Jamnalal Bajaj Foundation.
minalbajaj.arts: She worked on the restoration of the Dr Bhau Daji Lad Museum in Mumbai and sits on the drama committee of the National Centre for Performing Arts.

minderoo.money: Minderoo Foundation is Andrew and Nicola Forrest’s philanthropy, funded from their iron ore company Fortescue; in 2023 they gave it Fortescue shares worth $5 billion.

facts.t: Fortescue reported a net profit after tax of US$3.4 billion and underlying EBITDA of US$7.9 billion for the year to 30 June 2025.

In May 2026 the Federal Court awarded the Yindjibarndi Ngurra Aboriginal Corporation $150.1 million in native title compensation over the mining tenements for Fortescue’s Solomon Hub, $150 million of it for cultural loss, the highest such award to date.

ministerofheritage.what: Oman's government ministry for heritage, antiquities, museums and tourism; Royal Decree 91/2020 of 18 August 2020 gave the Ministry of Heritage and Culture this name.
ministerofheritage.money: The state budget of the Sultanate of Oman.

ministredelaculture|France.what: The culture ministry of the French state, set up in 1959 with André Malraux as minister; its regional directorates of cultural affairs (DRAC) fund institutions across France.
ministredelaculture|France.money: The French state budget: the 2026 finance bill requested €3.747 billion in payment credits for the Culture mission.

ministryforcultureandheritage|Antarctica.what: The New Zealand government department for arts, culture, built heritage, sport and broadcasting, formed on 1 September 1999 and based in Wellington.
ministryforcultureandheritage|Antarctica.money: The New Zealand state budget, from which it funds 17 agencies, among them Creative New Zealand and Te Papa.

ministryofcultureczechrepublic|Czech Rep.what: The Czech government ministry for culture, established in 1969 and seated in the Nostický palác in Prague; Oto Klempíř is minister.
ministryofcultureczechrepublic|Czech Rep.money: The Czech state budget: 17,228,038,390 koruna for 2026, down from 19,656,512,686 koruna in 2025.

ministryofcultures|Colombia.what: Colombia's national culture ministry, created as the Ministerio de Cultura by Law 397 of 1997 and renamed by Law 2319 of 2023, housed in Bogotá's Palacio Echeverry since 2004.
ministryofcultures|Colombia.money: Colombia's national government budget, from which the ministry had COP 1.09 trillion (1,09 billones) in 2025.
ministryofcultures|Colombia.arts: Of the COP 4.27 trillion it received from 2023 to 2025, 18% went to the country's five largest cities.

ministryofculture|North Macedonia.what: The North Macedonian government ministry for culture and tourism, seated in Skopje; Sedat Sulejmani has been minister since 14 July 2026.
ministryofculture|North Macedonia.money: The state budget of North Macedonia.
ministryofculture|North Macedonia.arts: Its 2025 budget for projects of national interest was 814 million denars (13.23 million euros), supporting 1,365 of 2,888 entries.

ministryofculture|bergen-kunsthall-norwa.what: Norway's government ministry for culture, media, sport and equality, set up in 1982 and renamed Ministry of Culture and Equality on 1 January 2022.

ministryofculture|mus-e-mohammed-vi-d-ar.what: Morocco's government department for youth, culture and sport, based in Rabat and headed by Minister Mohamed Mehdi Bensaid.

ministryofculture|sofia-city-art-gallery.what: Bulgaria's government ministry for culture and heritage, first set up as a separate ministry on 6 February 1954 and based in Sofia.

ministryofculture|tainan-art-museum.what: Taiwan's central government ministry for culture, set up on 20 May 2012 from the Council for Cultural Affairs (1981) and based in New Taipei; Li Yuan is minister.

ministryofinterior|Italy.what: Italy's interior ministry, the national authority for public order and security, based at the Viminale in Rome and led by Matteo Piantedosi since 22 October 2022.

ministryofnationalresources|Hungary.what: Hungary's ministry for health, social affairs, education, culture and sport, formed in 2010, renamed Ministry of Human Capacities in 2012 and dissolved in 2022.
ministryofnationalresources|Hungary.arts: Géza Szőcs was its state secretary for culture.

ministryofocw|Netherlands.what: The Dutch national ministry for education, culture and science, created in 1918 and based in The Hague.
ministryofocw|Netherlands.money: The Dutch state budget, with €618 million a year in 2025-2028 for culture paid through the national cultural infrastructure and six national culture funds.

minsheng.money: Ningxia Minsheng Group is a regional property developer in Ningxia.

facts.t: In 2015 Ningxia Minsheng Group planned to invest $5bn over the next decade in Huaxia-Hetu Art Town, the 18.8 sq. km development MoCA Yinchuan anchors.

miran.what: A construction and trading group in Sulaymaniyah, chaired by Ahmed Haji Ali, which began in 1991 as an import and export company.
miran.money: Government construction contracts, trading and investment.

mirvac.money: Mirvac is a Sydney property developer and landlord of offices, shopping centres and housing.

mit.what: A private research university in Cambridge, Massachusetts, chartered in 1861 and founded by William Barton Rogers.
mit.money: USD 5.37 billion operating revenue in FY2025: 45 percent sponsored research, 29 percent investment return, 9 percent gifts, 8 percent net tuition.

mitre.what: An American nonprofit corporation spun out of MIT Lincoln Laboratory in 1958, with headquarters in Bedford, Massachusetts, and McLean, Virginia.
mitre.money: Contracts to run federally funded research and development centres for US government agencies in aviation, defence, healthcare and cybersecurity: USD 2.37 billion revenue in 2023.

mitsubishi.money: The ties name separate Mitsubishi companies, mostly Mitsubishi Electric (electrical and industrial equipment), and also Mitsubishi Motors, Mitsubishi Chemical and Mitsubishi Gas Chemical.

facts.t: An outside committee’s final report in October 2022 found 197 cases of improper quality inspections at Mitsubishi Electric sites in Japan.

mitsui.what: A Japanese general trading company (sogo shosha) of the Mitsui Group, established in its present form in 1947 and headquartered in Ōtemachi, Tokyo.
mitsui.money: Trading and investment in energy, metals, mobility, chemicals and food: profit attributable to owners of 833.97 billion yen in the year to March 2026.

facts.t: In September 2023 ICOMOS issued a Heritage Alert over the Meiji Jingu Gaien redevelopment in Tokyo, of which Mitsui Fudosan is a major developer; the developers planned to cut down 743 trees.

mitsuifudosan.what: A Japanese real estate developer founded on 15 July 1941 and headquartered in Nihonbashi-Muromachi, Tokyo, listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
mitsuifudosan.money: Leasing, property sales and facility operations; revenue from operations was ¥1,215.4 billion in the first half of fiscal 2026.

mittal.money: Lakshmi Mittal's money comes from ArcelorMittal, the steel and mining company his family controls; his son Aditya Mittal is its chief executive.

facts.t: ArcelorMittal reported net income attributable to equity holders of US$3,152 million for 2025, on sales of US$61,352 million.
A fire at the Kostenko coal mine in Kazakhstan, operated by ArcelorMittal Temirtau, killed 45 people on 28 October 2023.
ArcelorMittal declared EU lobbying costs of €1,250,000 to €1,499,999 for its closed financial year, February 2025 to January 2026.
ArcelorMittal North America Holdings reported $880,000 in its own 2025 US federal lobbying reports, under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.
InfluenceMap scores ArcelorMittal D+ for its climate policy engagement.

mittelbrandenburgischesparkasse.what: A public-law savings bank in Potsdam, opened on 1 July 1991 and owned by an association of five Brandenburg districts and the cities of Brandenburg an der Havel and Potsdam.
mittelbrandenburgischesparkasse.money: Its savings bank business; in 2025 it held €14.273 billion of customer deposits and €17.304 billion in total assets.

mizrahitefahotbank.what: Israel's third largest bank by assets, founded in 1923 by the Mizrachi movement, headquartered in Ramat Gan, with the Ofer and Wertheim groups holding about 41.41%.
mizrahitefahotbank.money: Banking in Israel, where it is the largest mortgage lender, with net profit of NIS 5.6 billion in 2025.

mizuho.money: Mizuho’s money comes from banking, securities and trust business.

facts.t: Japan’s Financial Services Agency issued Mizuho a business improvement order in November 2021 over repeated system failures, and its chief executive Tatsufumi Sakai said he would step down.

mllerfonden.what: A commercial foundation set up in Copenhagen in 1953 by the shipowner Arnold Peter Møller, split from a family foundation he had created in 1946.
mllerfonden.money: Its holdings through A.P. Moller Holding, its investment arm since 2013, which owns the majority of the Maersk shipping and logistics group.
mllerfonden.arts: Its purposes include Danish culture and the upkeep of buildings of cultural and historical value; it paid to restore Kastellet in Copenhagen in 1989 and 1999.

mlleroghustruchastinemckinneymllersfond.what: A commercial foundation set up in Copenhagen in 1953 by the shipowner Arnold Peter Møller, split from a family foundation he had created in 1946.
mlleroghustruchastinemckinneymllersfond.money: Its holdings through A.P. Moller Holding, its investment arm since 2013, which owns the majority of the Maersk shipping and logistics group.
mlleroghustruchastinemckinneymllersfond.arts: Its purposes include Danish culture and the upkeep of buildings of cultural and historical value; it paid to restore Kastellet in Copenhagen in 1989 and 1999.

molson.money: The Molson family’s money comes from Molson Coors, the brewer the family controls with the Coors family, given through the Molson Foundation.

mondotv.money: Mondo TV’s money comes from producing and selling animated programmes, much of the animation work outsourced.

facts.t: In June 2024 Mondo TV agreed to pay $538,000 to settle 18 apparent violations of US sanctions on North Korea, for about $537,939 paid between May 2019 and November 2021 for animation work outsourced to a North Korean state-owned studio.

mondriaan.what: The Dutch public fund for visual art and cultural heritage, formed in Amsterdam in 2012 by merging the Mondriaan Stichting (set up 1994) with Fonds BKVB.
mondriaan.money: The Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science.
mondriaan.arts: In 2024 it approved 2,257 of 4,204 applications, awarding 53,438,678 euros in total.

moody.money: The Moody Foundation of Galveston was founded in 1942 by William Lewis Moody Jr. and Libbie Rice Shearn Moody; Wikipedia gives its main revenue as dividends on American National Insurance Company stock.

mordant.money: Simon Mordant’s money comes from investment banking: he founded the corporate advisory firm Caliburn, which merged with Greenhill & Co. in 2010.

mordashov.money: Alexei Mordashov’s money comes from Severstal, the steel and mining company he controls.

morganstanley.money: Morgan Stanley is a US investment bank and wealth manager.

facts.t: Morgan Stanley reported net revenues of $70.6 billion for 2025, against $61.8 billion a year earlier.
Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC reported $4,450,000 in US federal lobbying for 2025 in its own Lobbying Disclosure Act reports.
Morgan Stanley declared EU lobbying costs of €700,000 to €799,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

moribuilding.what: A Tokyo property developer founded on 2 June 1959, grown out of Mori Fudosan, which Taikichiro Mori set up in 1955.
moribuilding.money: Developing, leasing and managing offices, homes, shops and hotels; the Mori family owns 95.94%.
moribuilding.arts: It opened the Mori Arts Center, with an art museum, on the upper floors of Roppongi Hills Mori Tower in 2003.

facts.t: In September 2005 the Tokyo District Court found two former Mori Building officials and a door maker’s former director guilty of professional negligence over a six-year-old boy’s death in a revolving door at Roppongi Hills in March 2004; they avoided prison.

moriprovan.what: An Australian private giving fund run by a trustee in Victoria, registered as a charity and a deductible gift recipient from 26 June 2021.

morrison.what: A London architecture and urban planning practice founded in 1984 by Bob Allies and Graham Morrison, with studios in Cambridge, Manchester, Dublin, Jeddah and Toronto.
morrison.money: Fees from architecture, urban planning and consultancy commissions, much of it repeat work for long-term clients.

moscowdepartmentofculture|Russia.what: The culture department of the Moscow city government, headed since September 2023 by Alexey Fursin, a minister of the Moscow government.
moscowdepartmentofculture|Russia.money: The Moscow city budget, from which it pays subsidies to the city’s theatres and museums and sets their performance targets.

mothennessy.what: The wine and spirits division of the LVMH luxury group, formed in 1971 when Moët & Chandon merged with Hennessy; Diageo holds a 34 percent stake.
mothennessy.money: Sales of champagne, cognac, wines and spirits: LVMH's Wines & Spirits sector had EUR 5,358 million revenue in 2025.

motiva.what: A Brazilian transport infrastructure company running road and rail concessions, which announced in March 2025 that it would change its name from CCR to Motiva.
motiva.money: Its road, rail and airport concessions: adjusted net revenue of R$ 15.3 billion and net income of R$ 3.27 billion in 2025.

facts.t: In November 2018 CCR agreed to pay R$81.5 million to close a São Paulo prosecutors’ inquiry, begun after the Lava Jato informant Adir Assad said the company paid undeclared campaign money (caixa dois) to politicians of the PSDB, PMDB, PSD and PTB.

mott.what: A private foundation set up in 1926 by Charles Stewart Mott, a Flint industrialist, with its headquarters in the Mott Foundation Building in Flint, Michigan.
mott.money: An endowment from Mott's fortune as a General Motors director for six decades and its largest individual shareholder; assets $3.71 billion in 2023.

mountallisonuniversity.what: A public undergraduate liberal arts university in Sackville, New Brunswick, founded in 1839 on an offer by the Sackville merchant Charles Allison.
mountallisonuniversity.money: Student fees (C$46.6 million) and government and other grants (C$31.4 million) out of C$112.4 million revenue in 2025-26.

mozabanco.what: A Mozambican commercial bank that opened in Maputo in June 2008 and was placed under central bank administration in 2016.
mozabanco.money: Its banking business; Kuhanha, the Banco de Moçambique staff pension fund manager, owns 66% and Arise B.V. 30.7%.

mpb.what: A British online marketplace for used photo and video equipment, founded by Matt Barker, headquartered in Brighton and trading in the UK, Europe and the US.
mpb.money: Buying and selling used camera kit: group net revenue of £63.6 million in the year to 31 March 2025.

mphasis.money: Mphasis's money comes from IT services, mostly for banks and financial firms.

facts.t: Mphasis's net profit for the year ended March 2025 grew 9.5 per cent to Rs 1,702.1 crore, on revenue from operations of Rs 14,230 crore.

mtn.money: MTN’s money comes from mobile voice, data and mobile money services across Africa.

facts.t: MTN Group’s service revenue rose 22.9% to R218.5 billion in 2025, on a reported basis.

In June 2016 MTN Nigeria agreed to pay 330 billion naira ($1.671 billion at the official rate) to settle a fine first set at $5.2 billion for failing to disconnect unregistered phone lines by a regulator’s deadline.

In September 2026 a US federal court in New York let two Anti-Terrorism Act suits proceed to discovery; families of more than 200 US soldiers killed and wounded in Afghanistan claim MTN paid protection money to the Taliban, which MTN denies.
Two outside firms reported $590,000 in 2025 fees from MTN (Dubai) Limited for US federal lobbying, under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

mtropoledelyon.what: A French territorial collectivity created on 1 January 2015 with the powers of a department and a metropolis over 58 communes including Lyon, home to 1,436,354 people in 2023.
mtropoledelyon.money: The budget of the Métropole de Lyon.

mtropoleeuropennedelille.what: The intercommunal authority of 95 communes around Lille, Roubaix and Tourcoing, created in 1967 as an urban community and a métropole since 1 January 2015.
mtropoleeuropennedelille.money: Business taxes it levies directly, household waste tax and French state grants; its 2025 budget was €2.446 billion.

mufgbank.what: A Japanese commercial bank established on 15 August 1919, owned by Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group and headquartered in Marunouchi, Tokyo.
mufgbank.money: Banking through 412 branches in Japan and 101 abroad, with 31,691 employees, as of 31 March 2026.

municipalityofbudapest|Hungary.what: The municipal government of Budapest, led by a mayor and a 33-seat General Assembly that meets at City Hall on Városház Street.
municipalityofbudapest|Hungary.money: Local business tax is its largest income, expected at HUF 318.6 billion within a 2026 budget of HUF 532.5 billion.

municipalityofdro|Italy.what: The municipality of Dro, a town of 5,093 inhabitants in the Sarca valley in the autonomous province of Trento, part of the Alto Garda e Ledro valley community.

municipalityofhagueculturalallocation|Ne.what: The municipality of The Hague, seat of the Dutch government and capital of South Holland, run by an elected council and a college of mayor and aldermen.
municipalityofhagueculturalallocation|Ne.money: The municipal budget, funded mainly by Dutch state payments from the Gemeentefonds and specific grants, plus local taxes.
municipalityofhagueculturalallocation|Ne.arts: Its Meerjarenbeleidsplan Kunst en Cultuur for 2025 to 2028 has a total budget of €71.7 million; the college of mayor and aldermen adopted it in September 2024.

municipalityofmiddelburg|Netherlands.what: The municipality of Middelburg, capital of the province of Zeeland, with 50,439 inhabitants in Middelburg, Arnemuiden and Nieuw- en Sint Joosland.
municipalityofmiddelburg|Netherlands.money: The municipal budget, funded by Dutch state payments from the Gemeentefonds, specific grants and local taxes.

municipalityofprishtina|Kosovo.what: The municipal government of Pristina, the capital and largest city of Kosovo.

municipalityoftrshavn|Faroe Islands.what: The largest municipality of the Faroe Islands, covering the capital Tórshavn and the islands of Nólsoy, Hestur and Koltur, with 23,242 residents in January 2024.

municipalmuseumofcityofkrakw|Poland.what: The municipal government of Kraków, a city with county rights, run by an elected 43-member City Council and the city president.
municipalmuseumofcityofkrakw|Poland.money: The Kraków city budget, which pays for the city's own tasks and those delegated by the national government.

munjal.money: Sunil Kant Munjal's money comes from Hero Enterprise, which he chairs, his part of the Hero group, with firms in insurance broking and real estate.

murdoch.money: The tie here is Freelands Foundation, set up by Elisabeth Murdoch, daughter of Rupert Murdoch, whose family controls News Corp and Fox Corporation.

museumsvereinmnchengladbach.what: The supporters’ association of the municipal Museum Abteiberg in Mönchengladbach, founded in 1902 and formerly called Museumsverein Mönchengladbach.
museumsvereinmnchengladbach.money: Members’ dues, from 55 euros a year, and the annual artists’ editions it sells to members.
museumsvereinmnchengladbach.arts: It helps the museum buy works for its collection.

mvm.what: Hungary's largest state-owned energy company, wholly owned by the Hungarian state, which owns the Paks nuclear power plant, its main source of electricity.
mvm.money: Energy sales, chiefly electricity, much of it from Paks; group revenue was HUF 4,534 billion in 2024, with profit of HUF 324 billion.

mwm.what: A foundation named among the sponsors of the 2019 Ghetto Biennale in Port-au-Prince.

myclinic.what: A private family-style clinic in Prague 6 Dejvice, run by MyClinic s.r.o. (company ID 01490575), caring for patients of all ages from newborns to grandparents.
myclinic.money: Its private medical services: general practice, paediatrics, specialist care, day surgery and health programmes for adults, children and companies.

myer.money: The Sidney Myer Fund and the Myer Foundation come from the fortune of Sidney Myer, who founded the Myer department stores and died in 1934.

mykhaylova.money: Liubov Mykhaylova is a businesswoman who owns IZOLYATSIA; the sources do not say what her business is.

nab.money: National Australia Bank is one of Australia’s four major banks.

facts.t: NAB reported statutory net profit of $6,759 million and cash earnings of $7,091 million for the year to 30 September 2025.

In its 2024-25 donor return to the Australian Electoral Commission, National Australia Bank Limited disclosed $142,500 in political donations: $66,000 to Labor branches and $76,500 to Liberal and National branches.

nacsingapore.what: Singapore's statutory board for the arts, set up on 15 October 1991 under the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth; based at Goodman Arts Centre.
nacsingapore.money: Singapore government funding through the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth; it receives about a third of state arts and culture funding (MCCY, 2021).
nacsingapore.arts: It gives grants, scholarships, awards and platforms to arts practitioners and runs arts education programmes.

nadar.money: The Nadar family’s money comes from HCL, the IT services group Shiv Nadar founded, chiefly HCLTech.

facts.t: HCLTech reported revenue of ₹117,055 crore, up 6.5%, and net income of ₹17,390 crore for the year to March 2025.
In March 2025 Shiv Nadar gifted 47% of his stake in HCL Corp and Vama Delhi to his daughter Roshni Nadar Malhotra, making her the majority shareholder of the family’s holding companies.

namibiangovernment|Namibia.what: The national government of Namibia: the Cabinet led by the president, the National Assembly and National Council, and the courts headed by the Supreme Court.

nanfung.money: Nan Fung Group began as a Hong Kong cotton spinner and now makes its money from property development, financial investment, life sciences and shipping.

naomimilgrom.what: An Australian businesswoman and philanthropist whose private company, ARJ Group Holdings, owns the women's clothing retailers Sportsgirl, Sussan and Suzanne Grae.
naomimilgrom.money: Her fortune from the ARJ Group fashion chains, which the Australian Financial Review's 2025 Rich List valued at A$1.72 billion.
naomimilgrom.arts: Her foundation, set up in 2014, commissions a new MPavilion in Melbourne's Queen Victoria Gardens each year; she was Australia's commissioner at the 2017 Venice Biennale.

nasher.money: The Nasher money comes from Raymond Nasher, a Dallas real estate developer who built NorthPark Center in the early 1960s, and the Nasher Foundation.

nataliaopaleva.what: A Russian collector and general director of the AZ Museum of Anatoly Zverev in Moscow, which she created in 2015; she opened the AZ/ART centre in 2024.
nataliaopaleva.money: A fortune from 20.36 percent of the gold miner GV Gold, built with her Lanta-Bank partners; Forbes put it at USD 260 million in 2018.

natashabelaya.what: A private donor listed among the patrons of the Zotov Centre for Constructivism in Moscow.

nationalartscouncil|Singapore.what: Singapore's statutory board for the arts, set up on 15 October 1991 under the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth; based at Goodman Arts Centre.
nationalartscouncil|Singapore.money: Singapore government funding through the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth; it receives about a third of state arts and culture funding (MCCY, 2021).
nationalartscouncil|Singapore.arts: It gives grants, scholarships, awards and platforms to arts practitioners and runs arts education programmes.

nationalbank.what: A Canadian bank formed in 1979 by the merger of Banque Canadienne Nationale and the Provincial Bank of Canada, with roots in an 1859 Quebec City bank; based in Montreal.
nationalbank.money: Banking profits from personal and commercial banking, wealth management and financial markets: revenue CA$13.98 billion and net income CA$4.02 billion in 2025.

nationalbankcanada.money: National Bank of Canada’s money comes from banking, wealth management and capital markets, mostly in Quebec.

facts.t: National Bank reported fourth-quarter 2025 net income of $1.059 billion and full-year adjusted profit of $4.479 billion.

nationalcultural.what: A Hungarian state fund created by Act XXIII of 1993 that awards grants for the arts, events, publishing and heritage; the Nemzeti Kulturális Támogatáskezelő handles its contracts and payments.
nationalcultural.money: Since 1 January 2010, 90 percent of the gaming tax on the Ötöslottó lottery, which replaced an earlier cultural levy.

nationalendowmentforarts.what: An independent agency of the US federal government, created by Congress in 1965 and signed into law by President Lyndon B. Johnson; based in Washington, D.C.
nationalendowmentforarts.money: Annual appropriations from the US Congress: $207,000,000 a year for 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026.

nationalendowmentforhumanities.what: An independent federal agency of the United States, created with the National Endowment for the Arts by an act President Johnson signed on 29 September 1965.
nationalendowmentforhumanities.money: Annual appropriations from the US Congress: US$207 million in 2023.

nationalgeographicsociety.what: A US nonprofit scientific and educational organisation founded on 13 January 1888 and based in Washington, D.C.; it owns 27% of National Geographic Partners, a joint venture with Disney.
nationalgeographicsociety.money: Donations, investment income and royalties: of $340.5 million revenue in 2025, $189.7 million came from contributions and $58.5 million from investments.

nationallotterycommunity.what: A UK executive non-departmental public body, legally named the Big Lottery Fund and sponsored by the Department for Culture, Media and Sport, that funds community projects.
nationallotterycommunity.money: Money raised by National Lottery players for good causes; it plans to distribute at least £4 billion by 2030.

nationallotteryheritage.what: The UK distributor of National Lottery money for heritage, set up in 1994 as the Heritage Lottery Fund and renamed in 2019; head office in London.
nationallotteryheritage.money: A share of National Lottery proceeds raised from players, plus heritage funding it distributes for the UK and devolved governments.
nationallotteryheritage.arts: Since 1994 it has awarded over £9.9 billion of National Lottery and other funding to more than 54,000 projects.

nationallottery|Belgium.what: Belgium's largest lottery operator, founded in 1934 as the Colonial Lottery and a public-law limited company since 2002, under the Federal Public Service Finance.
nationallottery|Belgium.money: Sales of its lottery games and Scooore sports betting; it pays a monopoly fee to the federal treasury.
nationallottery|Belgium.arts: Parliament decides which projects and organisations receive its yearly subsidies.

nationalmuseumsofkenya.what: A Kenyan state corporation under the Museums and Heritage Act 2006 that runs the country's museums, sites and monuments; its headquarters is on Museum Hill, Nairobi.
nationalmuseumsofkenya.money: Kenya's national government, through the National Treasury, pays staff salaries; admission fees and other earned income cover operating costs.

nationaltrustforhistoric.what: A privately funded nonprofit founded in 1949 by congressional charter and based in Washington, D.C.; it runs historic sites and campaigns to save historic places.
nationaltrustforhistoric.money: Contributions, 66.1% of US$104.9 million revenue in the year to June 2025, plus investment income and asset sales.

naturgy.money: Naturgy’s money comes from gas and electricity: supplying and distributing gas and power in Spain and Latin America, Panama among them.

facts.t: Naturgy’s net profit rose 6.4% to 2,023 million euros in 2025.
Naturgy Energy Group declared EU lobbying costs of €100,000 to €199,999 for 2024 to the EU Transparency Register.
Its US subsidiary Naturgy Candela Devco LLC paid SC Partners $80,000 for federal lobbying in 2025, as the firm reported.

ncmm.what: A Nigerian federal agency set up by Decree 77 of 1979 in place of the Federal Antiquities Department, headquartered in Abuja and managing 53 museums.
ncmm.money: Nigeria's federal budget, which gave it ₦15 billion in 2025, the largest allocation among the culture ministry's agencies.
ncmm.arts: Sixty-five national monuments and sites have been declared, and Nigeria has two UNESCO World Heritage Sites, Sukur Cultural Landscape and Osun Osogbo Sacred Grove.

ndr.what: The public broadcaster for Hamburg, Lower Saxony, Schleswig-Holstein and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, a public-law institution operating as NDR since 1 January 1956; based in Hamburg.
ndr.money: The broadcasting fee paid by households, collected by a joint agency of ARD, ZDF and Deutschlandradio, plus limited on-air advertising.

nec.what: A Japanese IT and electronics company, founded in Tokyo in 1899 as Nippon Electric Company, a member of the Sumitomo Group with headquarters in Minato, Tokyo.
nec.money: Sales of IT services, telecom equipment and aerospace and defence systems: revenue ¥3.42 trillion in fiscal 2025.

nechirvanbarzani.what: A Kurdish politician born in Barzan in 1966, President of the Kurdistan Region of Iraq since 10 June 2019 and earlier its prime minister, grandson of KDP founder Mustafa Barzani.

neilson.money: The Neilson Foundation is funded by Kerr Neilson, founder of the fund manager Platinum Asset Management.
