nepalacademyoffinearts.what: Nepal's national academy for the visual arts, set up by the legislative parliament on 13 April 2010 out of the Nepal Academy; it sits in Sita Bhawan, Naxal, Kathmandu.
nepalacademyoffinearts.money: Funds from the Government of Nepal plus revenue the academy generates itself.
nepalacademyoffinearts.arts: It has departments for painting, traditional arts, sculpture, folk art, handicrafts and architecture, and evaluates and awards artists.

nescafe.what: A Swiss food and drink company based in Vevey, formed in 1905 from the Anglo-Swiss Condensed Milk Company and Henri Nestlé's firm; Nescafé is its instant coffee brand.
nescafe.money: Sales of coffee, baby food, dairy, confectionery, bottled water and pet food: revenue CHF 89.49 billion in 2025.

nesr.money: The Nesr family’s money comes from Webcor Group, one of Angola’s largest companies, which imports and distributes food; Wissam Nesr is its chief executive.

netflix.money: Netflix's money comes from streaming subscriptions and advertising.

facts.t: Netflix's revenue was $45,183 million in 2025.
Netflix, Inc. reported $3,080,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025 in its Lobbying Disclosure Act reports.
Netflix International B.V. declared EU lobbying costs of €700,000 to €799,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

netherlandsembassy|Egypt.what: The embassy of the Netherlands in Egypt, at 18 Hassan Sabri Street in Zamalek, Cairo.
netherlandsembassy|Egypt.money: The Dutch government, which the embassy represents in Egypt.

neubauerfamily.what: A private family foundation in Philadelphia founded by Joseph Neubauer, former chief executive of the food services company Aramark, and his wife Jeanette Lerman-Neubauer.
neubauerfamily.money: Money from Joseph and Jeanette Neubauer, invested: dividends and asset sales brought $9.8 million in fiscal 2024, when net assets were $361 million.
neubauerfamily.arts: It supports Jewish museums in Berlin, Warsaw and Israel, and paid $20.1 million in charitable grants in fiscal 2024.

neuflizeobc.what: The corporate foundation of Banque Neuflize OBC, the private bank of the Dutch group ABN AMRO in France, which runs 11 branches in French cities.
neuflizeobc.money: Banque Neuflize OBC, the French private banking arm of ABN AMRO.
neuflizeobc.arts: It has backed the photography workshops of the Beaux-Arts de Paris since 2013; the bank's photo and video collection, begun in 1997, held nearly 800 works in 2015.

newcarlsberg.what: A Danish art foundation set up in 1902 by the brewer Carl Jacobsen and based in Copenhagen.
newcarlsberg.money: Dividends from shares in Carlsberg A/S, passed on by the Carlsberg Foundation under its charter, plus returns on its own investments.

newcastlecitycouncil|United Kingdom.what: The local authority for Newcastle upon Tyne, a metropolitan borough council since 1974 and a member of the North East Combined Authority since 2024, based at the Civic Centre.
newcastlecitycouncil|United Kingdom.money: Council Tax, business rates and government grants, which set a net revenue budget estimated at £328.2 million for 2026-27.
newcastlecitycouncil|United Kingdom.arts: Its Museums, Arts and Culture division has a net budget of £1,801,670 for 2026-27.

newfortress.money: New Fortress Energy’s money comes from importing and selling liquefied natural gas and from power generation, including Puerto Rico’s state power plants, which its subsidiary Genera PR operates.

facts.t: In May 2025 Puerto Rico’s Energy Bureau ordered Genera PR to cease converting the Palo Seco and Mayagüez units to natural gas, citing the risk of a supply monopoly favouring its parent, New Fortress Energy.
New Fortress Energy paid the firm H.A. Cumber & Company $160,000 for federal lobbying in 2025, as the firm reported.
Genera PR paid the firm Alta Crest $216,000 for federal lobbying in 2025, $54,000 a quarter, as the firm reported.

newyorkcitydepartmentofculturalaffairs|U.what: The New York City government department for culture, a separate city agency since 1976, headed by a commissioner the mayor appoints.
newyorkcitydepartmentofculturalaffairs|U.money: The City of New York's budget.
newyorkcitydepartmentofculturalaffairs|U.arts: Its programmes include Materials for the Arts, which collects donated materials and delivers them to its members.

newyorkstatecouncilonarts|USA.what: A New York State agency for the arts, established in 1960 through a bill in the State Legislature backed by Governor Nelson Rockefeller.
newyorkstatecouncilonarts|USA.money: The New York State budget, enacted by the Governor and Legislature.
newyorkstatecouncilonarts|USA.arts: Its grants reached $80.9 million in fiscal year 2026, and over $161 million including capital funding.

newyorkstate|USA.what: The government of the US state of New York, headquartered at the New York State Capitol in Albany, with Governor Kathy Hochul at the head of the executive.

niedersachsen.what: The culture foundation of the German state of Lower Saxony, set up in 1987 on the initiative of state premier Ernst Albrecht, based in Hannover.
niedersachsen.money: Returns on EUR 58.8 million of capital, EUR 2.1 million in 2025, plus EUR 5.9 million from Lower Saxony's gambling levy.
niedersachsen.arts: It paid out EUR 6.2 million in 2025 and has funded over 4,400 projects with more than EUR 141 million since 1987.

nih.what: The medical research agency of the US Department of Health and Human Services, in Bethesda, Maryland, which began in 1887 as the Hygienic Laboratory.
nih.money: The US federal budget: USD 48.86 billion in 2024.

nike.money: Nike designs and sells sports shoes, clothing and equipment, made by contract factories.

facts.t: Nike reported revenues of $46.3 billion for the year to May 2025, down 10%.
Nike, Inc reported $2,560,000 in US federal lobbying for 2025 in its own Lobbying Disclosure Act reports.
Nike, Inc. declared EU lobbying costs of €500,000 to €599,999 for June 2025 to May 2026 to the EU Transparency Register.

nikolaimoroz.what: A patron who founded the Typography centre for contemporary art in Krasnodar with the art group ZIP, opening on 26 July 2012 in the Sovetskaya Kuban printing works.

nilsastrup.what: A Norwegian foundation in Oslo formed in 1995 from the Thomas Fearnley Foundation, set up in 1939 by the shipowner Thomas Fearnley, and the Heddy and Nils Astrup Foundation.
nilsastrup.money: Endowments from descendants of the Fearnley shipping family.
nilsastrup.arts: Its registered purpose covers social, humanitarian and cultural causes and names the running of the Astrup Fearnley Museet.

nipponfoundation.money: The Nippon Foundation’s money comes from a share of the proceeds of betting on motorboat racing in Japan; the Great Britain Sasakawa Foundation bears the name of its founder, Ryoichi Sasakawa.

facts.t: Ryoichi Sasakawa, who built the motorboat racing business behind the foundation, was held in Sugamo Prison as a Class A war criminal suspect and released in 1948 without ever being indicted, according to the biography the foundation publishes.

nishat.what: A Pakistani business group based in Lahore, founded in 1951 when Mian Muhammad Yahya and his three brothers set up Nishat Mills; chaired by Mian Muhammad Mansha.
nishat.money: Profits of its textile, cement, banking (MCB Bank), insurance (Adamjee), power, hotel and car assembly businesses; Nishat Mills is the flagship company.

nn.what: A Dutch insurance and asset management group in The Hague, parent of Nationale-Nederlanden, formed in 2013 from ING's insurance business and listed in 2014.
nn.money: Premiums and fees from life and non-life insurance, asset management and mortgages.

nomura.money: Nomura’s money comes from securities brokerage, investment banking and asset management; the ties are Nomura Securities and the Nomura Foundation.

facts.t: In 2024 Japanese regulators fined Nomura Securities 21.76 million yen for manipulating 10-year Japanese government bond futures in March 2021.

nonprofitserendipityarts.what: A not-for-profit arts foundation in New Delhi that organises the Serendipity Arts Festival, founded in 2016 by Sunil Kant Munjal, chairman of Hero Enterprise.
nonprofitserendipityarts.money: Its patrons are Sunil Kant Munjal and Hero Enterprise, the business group he chairs.
nonprofitserendipityarts.arts: It gives grants and residencies to artists across South Asia.

nordea.what: A Danish commercial foundation set up in 1989 by the savings bank Sparekassen SDS when it became a limited company, named Nordea-fonden since 2008.
nordea.money: Returns on its assets, chiefly a stake of about 4.4 percent in Nordea Bank Abp. It gives over 80 percent of yearly returns to charity.
nordea.arts: Culture is one of its four areas of support, alongside health, exercise and nature, with a grant pool for culture houses (Kulturhuspuljen).

nordeafonden.what: A Danish commercial foundation set up in 1989 by the savings bank Sparekassen SDS when it became a limited company, named Nordea-fonden since 2008.
nordeafonden.money: Returns on its assets, chiefly a stake of about 4.4 percent in Nordea Bank Abp. It gives over 80 percent of yearly returns to charity.
nordeafonden.arts: Culture is one of its four areas of support, alongside health, exercise and nature, with a grant pool for culture houses (Kulturhuspuljen).

nordlb.what: A German Landesbank and public-law institution, trading under that name since 1 July 1970, owned by Lower Saxony, Saxony-Anhalt and the regional savings banks; based in Hanover.
nordlb.money: Banking profits from corporate, real estate and aircraft finance; Lower Saxony (€1.5 billion) and the German savings banks association (€1.2 billion) recapitalised it in 2019.
nordlb.arts: In 2012 it sold Jeff Koons's sculpture Tulips for $33.7 million and said it would use the proceeds for a foundation for contemporary art in northern Germany.

nornickel.what: A Russian mining and metals company founded in 1993, controlled by Vladimir Potanin's Interros, with mines and smelters at Norilsk in Siberia; based in Moscow.
nornickel.money: Sales of nickel, palladium, copper, platinum and other metals: revenue $13.8 billion in 2025.

norrbottenregion|Sweden.what: The regional authority of Norrbotten County in Sweden, a county council that became a region on 1 January 2017, based in Luleå with about 7,400 staff.
norrbottenregion|Sweden.money: The budget of Region Norrbotten, which runs health and dental care and supports culture, public transport and small firms.

norskekunstforeninger.what: The Norwegian umbrella organisation for public art societies, first founded in 1934 and set up again in 1978, with 170 member societies in 2014 and an office in Oslo.
norskekunstforeninger.money: State operating support through Arts Council Norway (Norsk kulturråd).
norskekunstforeninger.arts: It grants member societies money for art transport, projects and equipment, sends out touring exhibitions and gives a debut prize at the Autumn Exhibition.

north.what: A community trust set up in 1988 to hold the Auckland Savings Bank (ASB) for Auckland and Northland; it was named ASB Community Trust until 2015.
north.money: An endowment from the sale of ASB to the Commonwealth Bank of Australia; it stood at over a billion New Zealand dollars in 2015.

northerntrust.money: Northern Trust is a Chicago bank for wealth management and asset servicing.

facts.t: Northern Trust Corporation reported $420,000 in US federal lobbying for 2025 in its own Lobbying Disclosure Act reports.

northropgrumman.what: The charitable foundation of Northrop Grumman, the US aerospace and defence contractor, based in Falls Church, Virginia, and tax-exempt since 1956.
northropgrumman.money: Contributions of USD 15 million in each of 2022 and 2023; Northrop Grumman drew 87 percent of its 2024 revenue from the US government.

northwestel.money: Northwestel’s money comes from telephone and internet service across Yukon, the Northwest Territories and Nunavut; Bell Canada has been its parent since 1988.

northwestelhelp.what: The incumbent phone carrier of Canada's three territories, created by CN in 1979 and owned by BCE since 1988; BCE agreed in 2024 to sell it to Sixty North Unity.
northwestelhelp.money: Telephone, internet and long-distance fees from customers in Yukon, the Northwest Territories, Nunavut and northern British Columbia and Alberta.

nortonsimon.what: The older of two Pasadena foundations of the industrialist Norton Simon, founder of Hunt's Foods; a private foundation, tax-exempt since 1954, that owns part of his art collection.
nortonsimon.money: Investment income, with no new gifts in recent years: revenue $6.4 million and net assets $194.1 million in 2024.
nortonsimon.arts: It lends its works long term to the Norton Simon Museum, which Simon took over in 1974 when it was the Pasadena Art Museum.

nortonsimonart.what: One of two Pasadena foundations of the industrialist Norton Simon, founder of Hunt's Foods; a private foundation, tax-exempt since 1957, that owns part of his art collection.
nortonsimonart.money: Investment income, with no new gifts in recent years: revenue $15.7 million and net assets $425.5 million in the year to November 2024.
nortonsimonart.arts: It lends its works long term to the Norton Simon Museum; in 2014 public filings put the two foundations' art at about $5 billion.

norval.money: Louis Norval’s money comes from property investment in South Africa.

norwegianmfa.what: The foreign ministry of the Kingdom of Norway, established on 7 June 1905, the day the Storting decided to dissolve the union with Sweden.
norwegianmfa.money: The state budget of Norway, as a government ministry.
norwegianmfa.arts: It is responsible for presenting Norwegian arts and culture abroad, including exchange projects with developing countries, and its embassies administer cultural cooperation with other countries.

norwegianministryofculture|Norway.what: Norway's government ministry for culture, media, sport and equality, set up in 1982 and renamed Ministry of Culture and Equality on 1 January 2022.

nottinghamcitycouncil|UK.what: The unitary local authority for the city of Nottingham, under Labour control since 1991, with main offices at Loxley House.
nottinghamcitycouncil|UK.money: UK government grants, including the Revenue Support Grant, and council tax.

nottinghamtrentuniversity.what: A public university in Nottingham with roots in the Nottingham Government School of Design of 1843, a polytechnic from 1970 and a university since 1992.
nottinghamtrentuniversity.money: Mainly tuition fees: of about £434 million income in 2023-24, £378 million came from teaching and £22 million from research.

novartis.money: Novartis's money comes from making and selling prescription medicines.

facts.t: In July 2020 Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corporation agreed to pay $678 million to settle a US fraud lawsuit over sham speaker programs through which it paid over $100 million to doctors to induce them to prescribe its drugs.
Novartis International AG declared EU lobbying costs of €2,500,000 to €2,749,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.
Novartis reported $7,788,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act, amended figures used where filed.

novatek.what: A Russian gas producer founded in 1994, with its head office in Moscow, on the US sectoral sanctions list since 2014; founder Leonid Mikhelson holds 28 percent.
novatek.money: Natural gas and petroleum production, including Yamal LNG and Arctic LNG 2: RUB 1.45 trillion revenue in 2025.

novonordisk.money: Novo Nordisk's money comes from diabetes and obesity drugs (insulin, Ozempic, Wegovy); the Novo Nordisk Foundation, which gives the atlas ties here, controls the company through its holding company and draws on its dividends.

facts.t: Novo Nordisk reported 2025 net sales of DKK 309,064 million and net profit of DKK 102,434 million.

In January 2025 Novo Nordisk settled Minnesota's insulin pricing lawsuit by agreeing to cap the out-of-pocket cost of its insulin at $35 a month for five years and give free insulin to the neediest Minnesotans.
Novo Nordisk A/S declared EU lobbying costs of €2,000,000 to €2,249,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.
Novo Nordisk Inc. reported $7,230,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

novonordiskfonden.what: A Danish enterprise foundation established in 1989, with roots in a 1922 insulin licence, seated in Hellerup and controlling Novo Nordisk and Novonesis through Novo Holdings.
novonordiskfonden.money: Income from its holdings in Novo Nordisk and Novonesis, managed by Novo Holdings, which managed assets of DKK 694 billion at the end of 2025.

nrwcultureministry|Germany.what: The culture and science ministry of the German state of North Rhine-Westphalia in Düsseldorf, led by Minister Ina Brandes.
nrwcultureministry|Germany.arts: In June 2026 it granted about 18 million euros to Kultur Ruhr GmbH for the Ruhrtriennale, Chorwerk Ruhr, Tanzlandschaft Ruhr and Urbane Künste Ruhr.

nsf.what: An independent US federal agency for science and engineering research, set up by the National Science Foundation Act signed by President Truman on 10 May 1950.
nsf.money: The US federal budget: USD 8.75 billion for fiscal 2026.

nswgovernment|Australia.what: The state government of New South Wales, Australia, led since March 2023 by the Labor Premier Chris Minns.
nswgovernment|Australia.money: The New South Wales state budget, which funds the arts through Create NSW and its Arts and Cultural Funding Program.

ntgovernment|Australia.what: The executive government of Australia's Northern Territory, formed in 1978 when the Commonwealth granted the territory self-government; it sits at Parliament House, Darwin.
ntgovernment|Australia.money: Commonwealth grants supply about A$7.7 billion, or 72%, of its A$10.7 billion revenue (2026-27 budget); mining and petroleum royalties are another source.

ntteast.what: A regional telecom operator for eastern Japan, set up on 1 July 1999 as a wholly owned subsidiary of the NTT holding company; based in Shinjuku, Tokyo.
ntteast.money: Fees for fixed-line telephone, optical fibre and other regional telecommunications services in eastern Japan.

nubank.money: Nubank’s money comes from digital banking, credit cards and loans in Brazil, Mexico and Colombia.

facts.t: Nu Holdings posted net income of $2.9 billion in 2025, against $2.0 billion in 2024.

nunavut.what: The executive government of the Canadian territory of Nunavut, created on 1 April 1999 and run as a consensus government from its seat in Iqaluit.
nunavut.money: The territorial budget of Nunavut, about CA$3.1 billion a year.

nycarlsberg.what: A Danish art foundation set up in 1902 by the brewer Carl Jacobsen and based in Copenhagen.
nycarlsberg.money: Dividends from shares in Carlsberg A/S, passed on by the Carlsberg Foundation under its charter, plus returns on its own investments.

nycarlsbergfondet.what: A Danish art foundation set up in 1902 by the brewer Carl Jacobsen and based in Copenhagen.
nycarlsbergfondet.money: Dividends from shares in Carlsberg A/S, passed on by the Carlsberg Foundation under its charter, plus returns on its own investments.

nycculturalaffairs|USA.what: The New York City government department for culture, a separate city agency since 1976, headed by a commissioner the mayor appoints.
nycculturalaffairs|USA.money: The City of New York's budget.
nycculturalaffairs|USA.arts: Its programmes include Materials for the Arts, which collects donated materials and delivers them to its members.

nycdepartmentofculturalaffairs.what: The New York City government department for culture, a separate city agency since 1976, headed by a commissioner the mayor appoints.
nycdepartmentofculturalaffairs.money: The City of New York's budget.
nycdepartmentofculturalaffairs.arts: Its programmes include Materials for the Arts, which collects donated materials and delivers them to its members.

nycdepartmentofculturalaffairs|USA.what: The New York City government department for culture, a separate city agency since 1976, headed by a commissioner the mayor appoints.
nycdepartmentofculturalaffairs|USA.money: The City of New York's budget.
nycdepartmentofculturalaffairs|USA.arts: Its programmes include Materials for the Arts, which collects donated materials and delivers them to its members.

nysca.what: A New York State agency for the arts, established in 1960 through a bill in the State Legislature backed by Governor Nelson Rockefeller.
nysca.money: The New York State budget, enacted by the Governor and Legislature.
nysca.arts: Its grants reached $80.9 million in fiscal year 2026, and over $161 million including capital funding.

nyu.what: A private research university in New York City, chartered in 1831 by the New York State Legislature and founded in 1832 by Albert Gallatin, based in Greenwich Village.
nyu.money: An operating budget of USD 4.3 billion in 2025, excluding NYU Langone, and an endowment of USD 7.28 billion (2025).

nzct.money: A gaming trust: its money comes from pokie machines that hospitality operators run in their hotels and bars, and it says it returns all its net profit, at least 40 percent of gross profit, as grants.

facts.t: In its 2024/25 financial year NZCT generated $36.334 million for communities and distributed $38.244 million through 1,992 grants.

oak.what: A charitable foundation set up in 1983 by Alan M. Parker, co-founder of the duty-free retailer DFS Group, and headquartered in Geneva.
oak.money: Resources from Alan Parker's interest in the Duty Free Shoppers business; it made about 1,000 grants totalling US$383 million in 2025.
oak.arts: Its Special Interest Programme funds the Jette Parker Artists Programme for young opera singers, which is marking 25 years.

oakfoundation.money: The Oak Foundation was founded in 1983 by the billionaire Alan M. Parker, co-founder of the duty-free company DFS Group.

obayashi.money: Obayashi’s money comes from general construction, civil engineering and property development.

facts.t: In October 2018 the Tokyo District Court fined Obayashi Corporation 200 million yen for rigging bids for maglev (Chuo Shinkansen) station works.

occidental.money: Occidental's money comes from oil and gas production, with chemicals through OxyChem.

facts.t: Occidental Petroleum's revenue was $21,593 million in 2025.
In 2013 Occidental reached a confidential settlement with Achuar Indigenous communities in Peru over 30 years of contamination of the Corrientes River basin.
Occidental paid $190 million in 2014 for the contamination of the Passaic River in New Jersey.
Occidental Petroleum Corporation reported $11,330,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025 in its Lobbying Disclosure Act reports.
Occidental Petroleum Corporation declared EU lobbying costs of €100,000 to €199,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

ocm.what: A media group formed in December 2005 from Trinidad's Caribbean Communications Network and Barbados's Nation Corporation, based in Port of Spain; the state National Investment Fund owns 23%.
ocm.money: Advertising and sales of its newspapers, television and radio, including the Trinidad Express and TV6: revenue TT$301.17 million in 2024.
ocm.arts: It has sponsored the OCM Bocas Prize for Caribbean Literature since 2011.

oct.what: A Chinese state-owned enterprise founded in 1985 in Shenzhen, wholly owned by the State Council and supervised by its State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission.
oct.money: Profits of its tourism and culture parks, property development, hotels and Konka electronics: revenue RMB 110.3 billion in 2018.

octgroup.money: OCT Group (Overseas Chinese Town) is a central state-owned enterprise in tourism, theme parks and property.

facts.t: Overseas Chinese Town A, the group's Shenzhen-listed company, had revenue of 102.6 billion yuan in 2021, then a loss in 2022 and a net loss attributable to shareholders of 1.3 billion yuan in the first half of 2023.

ocw.what: The Dutch national ministry for education, culture and science, created in 1918 and based in The Hague.
ocw.money: The Dutch state budget, with €618 million a year in 2025-2028 for culture paid through the national cultural infrastructure and six national culture funds.

ofcaixageraldedepsitos.what: A private foundation set up by Caixa Geral de Depósitos, Portugal's state-owned bank; its venue in the bank's Lisbon head office opened in October 1993.
ofcaixageraldedepsitos.money: An annual allocation from Caixa Geral de Depósitos, which also made its €3.5 million initial endowment and provides its spaces.

officeofcityhistorianofhavana|Cuba.what: A Cuban public body created on 11 June 1938 as an autonomous municipal office, led by Eusebio Leal from 1968 to 2020, that runs museums and heritage conservation in Havana.
officeofcityhistorianofhavana|Cuba.money: Contributions from other state bodies and a 5 percent tax on historic centre activity, kept when its companies passed to the army-run GAE in 2016.

ogasawara.what: A Japanese public-interest foundation set up on 12 September 1986 by Toshiaki Ogasawara, founder of the fastener maker Nifco, as a science foundation; renamed in 2020.
ogasawara.money: Nifco shares from Toshiaki Ogasawara: 2 million at its founding and 5.94 million from his estate in 2020; basic assets ¥47.61 billion (March 2026).
ogasawara.arts: It began arts grants in 2020, for contemporary art research, translation, exchange and travel; its total grants in 2025 were ¥486.52 million.

ohioartscouncil|USA.what: A state agency of Ohio created in 1965 that funds artists and arts organisations and helps preserve Ohio's cultural heritage.
ohioartscouncil|USA.money: Funds from the State of Ohio budget, set by the Ohio General Assembly, and from the National Endowment for the Arts.

ohiostateuniversity|USA.what: A public land-grant research university in Columbus, Ohio, founded on 22 March 1870 as the Ohio Agricultural and Mechanical College, with 65,405 students.
ohiostateuniversity|USA.money: Its USD 10.4 billion FY2025 plan drew 56 percent from its health system; university funds came 30 percent from tuition, 11 percent from government appropriations.

ohra.what: A Dutch insurance brand founded in 1925, now a trade name of NN Group companies and, for health insurance, of the CZ group; its office is in Arnhem.
ohra.money: Premiums on non-life, life and health insurance it sells directly to customers by phone and online.

oif.what: An intergovernmental organisation of French-speaking states and governments, created in Niamey on 20 March 1970 as the Agence de coopération culturelle et technique, with headquarters in Paris.
oif.money: Statutory contributions from member states and governments, set at €45,718,000 for 2024 within a 2024 to 2027 budget of €270,380,000.

okayamacity|Japan.what: The capital of Okayama Prefecture in western Japan, founded on 1 June 1889 and a government-designated city since 1 April 2009.
okayamacity|Japan.money: Its fiscal 2026 general budget of ¥429.9 billion: city taxes ¥143.6 billion, national and prefectural grants ¥113.5 billion, local allocation tax ¥55.8 billion.

okayamagas.what: A city gas company founded in Okayama on 29 January 1910, supplying Okayama, Kurashiki, Akaiwa, Tamano, Soja and Hayashima.
okayamagas.money: Sales of city gas, gas appliances and pipe work; non-consolidated revenue was ¥24.81 billion in 2015.

omk.what: A Moscow steel pipe maker with five plants between Moscow and the Urals, including the Vyksa Steel Works; under UK sanctions since May 2023 and US sanctions since September 2023.
omk.money: Sales of steel pipes, pipeline valves and fittings, railway wheels and automotive springs.

omkuchastie.what: A charitable foundation founded in 2008 on the initiative of Irina and Anatoly Sedykh; Irina Sedykh chairs its board of trustees and its general director works in Moscow.
omkuchastie.money: OMK, a private Moscow steel company fully controlled by Anatoly Sedykh, with revenue of 169.7 billion rubles in 2020.
omkuchastie.arts: It works in five regions, Vyksa among them, on culture, art and education for local communities beside direct aid to families.

omv.money: OMV's money comes from oil and gas production, refining and fuels, and chemicals.

facts.t: OMV reported 2025 sales from continuing operations of EUR 24.3 billion and a clean CCS Operating Result of EUR 4.6 billion.
InfluenceMap gives OMV a D+ grade for its climate policy engagement.
OMV Aktiengesellschaft declared EU lobbying costs of €400,000 to €499,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

omvzukunftspartner.what: Austria's integrated oil and gas company, founded on 3 July 1956 as Österreichische Mineralölverwaltung; the state holding ÖBAG owns 31.5% and Abu Dhabi's ADNOC 24.9%.
omvzukunftspartner.money: Sales of oil, natural gas, fuels and petrochemicals: revenue €24.3 billion and net income €1.52 billion in 2025.

onassis.what: A private foundation set up in Vaduz, Liechtenstein, in 1975 under the will of the shipowner Aristotle Onassis, in memory of his son Alexander.
onassis.money: Profits of the Onassis Business Foundation, its holding for maritime transport and real estate, formed from half of Aristotle Onassis's estate.
onassis.arts: It endows Greek studies chairs at universities and runs Onassis USA, its New York affiliate based in the Olympic Tower on Fifth Avenue.

ontarioartscouncil|Canada.what: An arm's-length agency of the Ontario government, created by provincial law in 1963 under Premier John Robarts; based in Toronto.
ontarioartscouncil|Canada.money: The Government of Ontario, through its culture ministry.
ontarioartscouncil|Canada.arts: It runs more than fifty funding programmes for Ontario artists and arts organisations.

opec.what: An intergovernmental development finance institution set up on 28 January 1976 by the member states of OPEC; based in Vienna.
opec.money: Capital contributions from its member countries, plus bonds issued on capital markets under its Strategic Framework 2030.

opensociety.what: A grantmaking network founded by investor George Soros, begun with a Budapest foundation in 1984; the Open Society Institute was set up in New York in 1993.
opensociety.money: George Soros's personal fortune: he had given over $32 billion by 2017, including an $18 billion transfer announced that year.

oprahwinfreycharitable.what: A private foundation in Los Angeles with the television host Oprah Winfrey as trustee; tax-exempt since August 2010.
oprahwinfreycharitable.money: Gifts in some years ($35.2 million in 2018, $14.3 million in 2020) and investment income; net assets were $171.1 million at the end of 2024.

optus.what: Australia's second-largest telecom company, owned by Singtel of Singapore; it grew from the satellite operator AUSSAT (1981) and gained a carrier licence in 1991.
optus.money: Mobile, home internet and fixed-line fees from over 10.7 million mobile customers: revenue A$8.05 billion in fiscal 2023.

orange.money: Orange's money comes from telecommunications: mobile, broadband and business networks in France, Europe, Africa and the Middle East.

facts.t: Orange reported 2025 revenue of 40,396 million euros and consolidated net income of 1,139 million euros.
Orange declared EU lobbying costs of €1,250,000 to €1,499,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

oregoncommunity.what: A statewide community foundation founded in 1973, with headquarters in Portland and offices in Baker City, Bend, Eugene, Medford and Salem.
oregoncommunity.money: Charitable funds set up by individuals, families, businesses and organisations: an endowment of US$3.02 billion in 2024, when it made $174 million in grants.
oregoncommunity.arts: Its Creative Heights Initiative funds Oregon arts and culture projects, with $1 million invested through its 2023 round.

orf.what: Austria's national public broadcaster, launched on 1 August 1955 and run from the ORF-Zentrum in Vienna.
orf.money: The ORF-Beitrag, a levy set by law on every Austrian address with an adult resident, plus limited on-air advertising.

orfnamedwertinvest.what: A Vienna real estate developer founded and owned by Michael Tojner, which has built projects in Austria, Germany and New York since 1993.
orfnamedwertinvest.money: Real estate development across housing, offices, hotels and industrial sites.

orkneyislandscouncil|UK.what: The local authority for the Orkney Islands, one of Scotland's 32 council areas, established in 1975 under the Local Government (Scotland) Act 1973 and based in Kirkwall.
orkneyislandscouncil|UK.money: A Scottish Government grant of £120,130,000, about 78% of its 2026/27 budget, plus council tax, service charges and its reserves.

orlen.what: A Polish oil refiner and fuel retailer formed in 1999 by merging the state firms CPN and Petrochemia Płock, based in Płock; the State Treasury holds 49.9 percent.
orlen.money: Oil refining, fuel retail and natural gas trading: sales revenue of PLN 267.8 billion in 2025.

ortizgurdian.money: The Ortiz Gurdián family’s money comes from banking: Ramiro Ortiz Mayorga presides over Banpro, a bank of the Grupo Promerica financial group.

osgf.what: A Tbilisi grant-making foundation in the Open Society Foundations network since 1994, registered in Georgia in 1998; from 2024 its work continues as the Civil Society Foundation.
osgf.money: Grants from the Open Society network's Foundation Open Society Institute and Foundation to Promote Open Society, plus other donors.

oslocollectorsvenke.what: Norwegian art collectors who acquired the KaviarFactory building in Henningsvær, Lofoten, after the cannery closed in 2006 and turned it into a contemporary art space.
oslocollectorsvenke.money: Rolf Hoff's business, which makes signage and produces works for artists.
oslocollectorsvenke.arts: They have lent works to Tate Britain, Garage in Moscow and most Norwegian contemporary art museums, and support artist-run galleries in Oslo.

otpbank.what: Hungary's largest commercial bank, established as OTP Bank on 1 March 1949 with roots in the First National Savings Bank of Pest of 1839; chaired by Sándor Csányi.
otpbank.money: Banking profits from retail and corporate clients in Hungary and subsidiaries across Central and Eastern Europe and Central Asia, such as Bulgaria's DSK Bank.

outset.what: A London arts charity established in 2003 and co-founded by Candida Gertler, registered as charity 1101476, one of an international network of independent Outset charities.
outset.money: Donations pooled from its patrons, with income of £327,947 in the year ending 31 December 2025.
outset.arts: The Outset network says it has distributed over £17 million since 2003 to more than 400 public art institutions.

owsleybrowniii.what: A documentary film director and producer from Louisville, Kentucky, founder of Magnanimus Wine Group in 2005 and son of Owsley Brown II, Brown-Forman's chief executive from 1993 to 2005.
owsleybrowniii.money: His wine business and the family wealth of the Browns, who have run the spirits company Brown-Forman since 1870.
owsleybrowniii.arts: His films include Night Waltz, on Paul Bowles, which won an Independent Spirit Award in 2000, and Music Makes a City, on the Louisville Orchestra.

oxfaminternacional.what: The secretariat of a confederation of over 20 independent Oxfam organisations, formed in 1995 as a Dutch foundation, Stichting Oxfam International, with headquarters in Nairobi.
oxfaminternacional.money: Institutional grants and public fundraising across the confederation, which reported total income of €1,009 million in 2023/24.

oyebode.money: Gbenga Oyebode’s money comes from law and business: he co-founded the law firm Aluko & Oyebode and chairs Okomu Oil Palm, in which he holds 4.37 percent.

paiko.what: A botanical boutique in Kaka'ako, Honolulu, founded by Tamara Rigney and owned by Courtney Monahan, which moved from Auahi Street to Halekauwila Street in 2023.
paiko.money: Sales of houseplants, cut flowers and pots from its shop.

paiz.money: The Paiz family’s money came from Almacenes Paiz, its chain of stores in Guatemala.

paizretailfamily.what: A Guatemalan business family; in 1928 Salvador Paiz's grandfather founded what became the Almacenes Paiz chain and later Walmart Centroamérica.
paizretailfamily.money: Retail: the Almacenes Paiz stores, later part of Walmart Centroamérica; Salvador Paiz now chairs the investment company Grupo PDC.
paizretailfamily.arts: The family's Fundación Paiz runs the Bienal de Arte Paiz, held since 1978.

palmacouncil|Spain.what: The municipal government of Palma, Mallorca, a city of 438,234 people in 2024, led by mayor Jaime Martínez Llabrés of the People's Party.
palmacouncil|Spain.money: The city's municipal budget, set at €626.67 million for 2026 and approved by the council in December 2025.

panasonic.what: A Japanese electronics group founded in 1918 by Kōnosuke Matsushita, named Panasonic since 2008 and a holding company since 2022, headquartered in Kadoma, Osaka.
panasonic.money: Sales of consumer electronics, home appliances, batteries and automotive and industrial systems: revenue of about ¥8.05 trillion in 2026.

facts.t: In April 2018 Panasonic and its in-flight entertainment unit Panasonic Avionics agreed to pay about $280 million to settle US charges under the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act.

paribu.what: A crypto asset exchange based in Istanbul, founded in 2017 by Yasin Oral, who owns it outright and runs it as chief executive.
paribu.money: Its crypto trading and custody business, which reported daily trading volume above US$1 billion in February 2021.

partnersincludeafricanculture.what: A pan-African non-profit trust set up in Bamako in February 2018 by African artists and cultural actors, registered in Mali under a headquarters agreement.
partnersincludeafricanculture.money: Contributions from African artists and cultural actors, and grants from DOEN, the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation, the Ford Foundation and Open Society Foundations.
partnersincludeafricanculture.arts: It finances artistic projects across Africa through calls for projects and trains cultural managers through its ACF Academy.

patino.money: The Patiño foundations’ money goes back to Simón I. Patiño’s tin mines in Bolivia, confiscated in the 1952 revolution; his heirs’ Geneva foundation manages the funds.

patio.what: A Swiss foundation registered in Geneva in December 1958 to help Bolivian students and professors and to support cultural, social and ecological work in Bolivia.
patio.money: A fund of US$10 million set up when the Bolivian Patiño foundation ran short of money; the Patiño wealth came from Bolivian tin mining.
patio.arts: Its statutes include topping up the resources of the Fundación Universitaria Simón I. Patiño, created in Bolivia in 1931, and supporting literary and music prizes.

patriciagurdin.what: An art collector from León, Nicaragua, who founded the Fundación Ortiz-Gurdián in 1996 with Ramiro Ortiz Mayorga to promote the country's cultural development.
patriciagurdin.money: Grupo Promerica, the financial group of her co-founder, whose bank Banpro also supports the foundation's Managua art centre.

patronatodeartecontemporneo.what: A non-profit civil association in Mexico City that began in 2000 on the initiative of Magda Carranza, Osvaldo Sánchez and Patricia Sloane to finance contemporary art in Mexico.
patronatodeartecontemporneo.money: Contributions from its group of patrons, who join a patrons’ programme of visits, trips and seminars.
patronatodeartecontemporneo.arts: It finances non-profit contemporary art projects and has held the SIT_AC international theory symposium since 2002.

patronatopageshowsinterceramic.what: A Mexican maker of ceramic and porcelain tiles and bath and kitchen products, founded in Chihuahua in 1978 by Óscar Almeida Chabre.
patronatopageshowsinterceramic.money: Sales of floor and wall tiles from plants in Chihuahua, Guanajuato and Garland, Texas, through showrooms and franchises in Mexico and abroad.

paulgettytrust.what: A trust founded in 1953 by J. Paul Getty, founder of Getty Oil, that runs the Getty Museum, Research Institute, Conservation Institute and Getty Foundation in Los Angeles.
paulgettytrust.money: An endowment of US$9.4 billion (2025) built on Getty's bequest, which included nearly $660 million in Getty Oil stock received in 1982.
paulgettytrust.arts: The Getty Foundation gives grants to museums and cultural institutions worldwide.

paulhamlyn.what: An independent UK grant-making charity started by publisher Paul Hamlyn in 1987 and in its current form since 2004; based in King's Cross, London.
paulhamlyn.money: An endowment from Paul Hamlyn's publishing fortune: a £50m gift in 1987 and about £308 million from his estate in 2001.
paulhamlyn.arts: It funds children and young people, with a focus on the arts.

paulramsay.what: A private philanthropic foundation in Sydney, founded in 2006 by Paul Ramsay, who started the private hospital company Ramsay Health Care in 1964.
paulramsay.money: A bequest of A$3 billion from Paul Ramsay, who died in 2014 and left most of his estate to the foundation.

paulsmith.what: A British fashion company founded in Nottingham in 1970 by the designer Sir Paul Smith, its majority shareholder, with Itochu holding 40%.
paulsmith.money: Sales of clothing, footwear, eyewear and accessories through 130 shops in more than 60 countries and online.

paulsonfamily.what: The private foundation of hedge fund manager John Paulson, its president, who founded the New York investment firm Paulson & Co. in 1994; tax exempt since 2009.
paulsonfamily.money: John Paulson's fortune from Paulson & Co.; the foundation held USD 1.39 billion in assets and paid USD 6.6 million in grants in 2024.

paysdemontbliardagglomration.what: The intercommunal authority of 73 communes around Montbéliard in the Doubs, a communauté d'agglomération since 1999, in its present form since 1 January 2017.
paysdemontbliardagglomration.money: Local taxes on households and businesses within a total 2026 budget of €214 million, voted on 22 January 2026.

pellerestates.what: A Canadian wine producer listed in Toronto and based in Grimsby, Ontario, whose brands include Peller Estates; in June 2026 it agreed to be bought by Fairfax Financial.
pellerestates.money: Sales of wine, ciders and spirits, including through 101 company stores in Ontario; revenue was C$393.0 million in the year to 31 March 2026.

penguin.what: A British publishing house founded in 1935 by Allen Lane with his brothers Richard and John, since 2013 an imprint of Penguin Random House.
penguin.money: Sales of books, with its parent Penguin Random House owned by the German media group Bertelsmann.

pepsico.what: An American food and drinks company formed in 1965 by the merger of the Pepsi-Cola Company and Frito-Lay, with headquarters in Purchase, in Harrison, New York.
pepsico.money: Sales of food and drinks in more than 200 countries, with revenue of US$93.9 billion in fiscal 2025.

perarte.what: A Swiss foundation initiated in 2025 by Marianne and Martin Haefner and entered in the Zurich commercial register in May 2026 to fund major exhibitions at the Kunsthaus Zürich.
perarte.money: A start capital of CHF 30 million from the Haefner family.

perelman.money: Ronald Perelman's money comes from MacAndrews & Forbes, the holding company through which he bought and sold businesses from candy to cosmetics, Revlon among them.

facts.t: Forbes put Ronald Perelman's net worth at $1.5 billion in November 2026, and says he lost his Revlon holdings in its 2023 bankruptcy proceedings after selling billions of dollars of assets to pay debt in late 2020.

pernodricard.money: Pernod Ricard's money comes from making and selling spirits and wine: Absolut, Jameson, Chivas Regal, Martell and Ricard among its brands.

facts.t: Pernod Ricard reported net sales of €10,959m for its financial year to June 2025 and group net profit of €1,626m.
Pernod Ricard declared EU lobbying costs of €800,000 to €899,999 for its financial year July 2025 to June 2026 to the EU Transparency Register.

Pernod Ricard reported $400,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for the first quarter of 2025, in a report that also ended its in-house registration; outside firms reported further fees from Pernod Ricard USA through the year.

petrobras.money: Petrobras’s money comes from producing, refining and selling oil and gas in Brazil.

facts.t: Petrobras ended 2024 with a net profit of R$36.6 billion (US$7.5 billion).

In 2018 Petrobras settled SEC charges that it misled US investors with false financial statements concealing a massive bribery and bid-rigging scheme, and took a non-prosecution agreement with the US Justice Department, agreeing to pay $933 million in disgorgement and interest and an $853 million penalty, subject to offsets.
InfluenceMap gives Petrobras a C- grade for its climate policy engagement.

petronor.what: A Spanish oil refining company established on 30 November 1968, based in Muskiz in the Basque Country and owned by Repsol (85.98%) and Kutxabank (14.02%).
petronor.money: Refining at Muskiz, which the company calls Spain's largest refinery at 12 million tonnes a year, with over a third of output exported.

pewcharitabletrusts.what: A nonprofit based in Philadelphia, formed from seven trusts that the four children of Sun Oil founder Joseph N. Pew created between 1948 and 1979.
pewcharitabletrusts.money: The Sun Oil fortune of the Pew family, with the seven trusts holding assets of $6 billion as of 2020.
pewcharitabletrusts.arts: It supports civic and cultural projects in Philadelphia.

pfizer.money: Pfizer's money comes from prescription medicines and vaccines.

facts.t: Pfizer's revenue was $62,579 million in 2025.

In September 2009 Pfizer agreed to pay $2.3 billion, then the largest health care fraud settlement, to resolve criminal and civil allegations that it illegally promoted four drugs, including the painkiller Bextra.
Pfizer Inc. reported $12,630,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025 in its Lobbying Disclosure Act reports.
Pfizer Inc. declared EU lobbying costs of €1,250,000 to €1,499,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

pge.what: A Polish energy group with its registered office in Warsaw, formed in its present shape by a merger on 9 May 2007; the State Treasury held 58.39 percent in 2014.
pge.money: Electricity generation, distribution and trading, mainly from hard coal and lignite plants such as Bełchatów: revenue of USD 16.2 billion in 2025.

philipmorris.money: Altria makes its money from cigarettes such as Marlboro in the United States, and from cigars, smokeless tobacco and nicotine products.

facts.t: Altria reported net revenues of about $24.0 billion for 2024, down 1.9%.
Philip Morris was among four tobacco companies in the 1998 Master Settlement Agreement, worth $206 billion to US states.
Altria reported $12,370,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.
ALTRIAPAC, Altria’s PAC, gave $810,500 to federal candidates in the 2023 to 2024 cycle, 68% to Republicans and 30% to Democrats, in its reports to the Federal Election Commission.

phillips.what: An auction house founded in London in 1796, with head offices in London and New York and a UK holding company, Phillips Assets Ltd.
phillips.money: Fees on auction and private sales (UK turnover £89m in 2024), under a parent, Mercury Group Trading, controlled by Leonid Fridlyand and Leonid Strunin.

pictet.money: Pictet's money comes from private banking, wealth management and asset management; it is owned by its partners.

pierides.what: A non-profit cultural foundation of the Pierides family, set up in 1974 and based in Larnaca, with a branch in Athens.
pierides.money: The Pierides family of Larnaca, whose businesses included shipping from 1860, banking from 1866 and insurance from 1872.
pierides.arts: It keeps the Pierides Museum in Larnaca under a trust with Bank of Cyprus and lists eight museums and collections in Cyprus and Athens.

pinakothekdermoderne.what: A foundation in Munich established in 1994 to collect private donations for building the Pinakothek der Moderne.
pinakothekdermoderne.money: Private donations, endowment gifts and bequests.
pinakothekdermoderne.arts: It funds education work at the museum and co-financed the Schaustelle, a temporary space for experiments.

pinault.what: The Pinault family's holding company, founded in Paris in 1992 by François Pinault and chaired by his son François-Henri Pinault since 2003.
pinault.money: Its holdings, chiefly 42.3% of the luxury group Kering, plus Christie's, Château Latour and other wine estates, Creative Artists Agency and Ponant cruises.
pinault.arts: It backs the Pinault Collection, which opened the Bourse de Commerce in Paris in 2021.

pinchuk.money: Victor Pinchuk’s money comes from Interpipe, the maker of steel pipes and railway wheels he founded in 1990, and from his investment group EastOne.

facts.t: Hogan Lovells reported $130,000 in 2025 fees from North American Interpipe for US federal lobbying on trade rules and duties, under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

pinchuks.what: The private philanthropic foundation of the Ukrainian businessman Victor Pinchuk, who consolidated his giving under it in 2006.
pinchuks.money: The fortune of Victor Pinchuk, founder of the pipe, railway wheel and steel producer Interpipe and of the investment firm EastOne Group.
pinchuks.arts: Through PinchukArtCentre it awards the Future Generation Art Prize, $100,000 every two years for artists under 35, announced in December 2009.

pingan.money: Ping An is an insurance and financial services group.

facts.t: Ping An Insurance reported 2024 revenue of RMB 1,141,346 million, and said net profit attributable to shareholders rose 47.8%.

pipertrust.what: A private foundation in Phoenix that Virginia Galvin Piper, widow of the Motorola founder Paul V. Galvin, established in 1995 to fund nonprofits in Maricopa County, Arizona.
pipertrust.money: About $600 million received from Virginia Piper's estate in 2000, held as an invested endowment.
pipertrust.arts: Arts and culture is one of its six programme areas, and its AGILE project builds the capacity of mid-sized arts organisations.

pirellionly.what: An Italian tyre maker founded in Milan in 1872 by Giovanni Battista Pirelli, listed on the Borsa Italiana and headquartered in the city's Bicocca district.
pirellionly.money: Sales of tyres for cars, motorcycles and bicycles, with revenues of 6.8 billion euros in 2025.
pirellionly.arts: It established and supports Pirelli HangarBicocca, a non-profit foundation for contemporary art whose exhibitions are free of charge.

platinumbarjeel.what: A non-profit art foundation in Sharjah, set up in 2010 by the Emirati writer and collector Sultan Sooud Al Qassemi to manage and show his collection of modern Arab art.
platinumbarjeel.money: It holds the personal collection of its founder, a member of Sharjah's ruling Al Qasimi family and chairman of the brokerage Barjeel Geojit Securities.
platinumbarjeel.arts: Since 2018 it has shown its collection in a long-term exhibition at the Sharjah Art Museum under a contract with the Sharjah Museums Authority.

plenitude.what: An Italian energy company and Società Benefit controlled by Eni, registered in Milan and active in more than 15 countries.
plenitude.money: Energy sold to over 11 million European customers and power from about 6 GW of renewables; pro forma EBITDA about €1.1 billion in 2025.

plymouthcitycouncil|UK.what: Plymouth's city council in Devon, England, a unitary authority since 1 April 1998, with 57 councillors meeting at the Council House on Armada Way.
plymouthcitycouncil|UK.money: A revenue budget of GBP 253.4 million for 2025/26: other grants 39 percent, council tax 24 percent, core government grants 16 percent.

pnc.what: A US bank holding company in Pittsburgh, tracing to the Pittsburgh Trust and Savings Company of 1845 and formed as PNC by a 1982 merger.
pnc.money: Interest and fees from personal, small business and corporate banking through PNC Bank; revenue was US$21.49 billion in 2023.

poddar.money: Abhishek Poddar's money comes from his family's companies: he is managing director of Matheson Bosanquet, in tea production, trading and export, and a director of Sua Explosives & Accessories, which makes mining explosives.

pola.money: The money came from the Pola cosmetics company and the Suzuki family that founded it; the foundation was set up with Tsuneji Suzuki’s personal assets.

polishcultureministry|UK.what: Poland's government ministry for culture and national heritage, based in the Potocki Palace in Warsaw; Marta Cienkowska has been minister since 24 July 2025.

polishministryofculture|Poland.what: Poland's government ministry for culture and national heritage, based in the Potocki Palace in Warsaw; Marta Cienkowska has been minister since 24 July 2025.

polygonhomes.what: A Metro Vancouver home builder in business since 1980, chaired by its major shareholder Michael Audain.
polygonhomes.money: Sales of the homes it builds and develops, more than 35,000 to date, from masterplanned communities to high-rise towers.

polytechnischegesellschaft.what: A charitable foundation under German civil law, set up in Frankfurt am Main in 2005 by the Polytechnische Gesellschaft e. V.
polytechnischegesellschaft.money: Most of the proceeds of the Polytechnische Gesellschaft's 2005 sale of Frankfurter Sparkasse; its capital stood at 467 million euros on 31 December 2022.
polytechnischegesellschaft.arts: Its culture programmes include a foundation choir and an opera studio.

pon.what: A family-owned Dutch mobility group founded in 1980 by Ben Pon Jr., whose father became the Dutch Volkswagen importer in 1947, with headquarters in Amsterdam.
pon.money: Car importing and bicycle making, with total revenue of €9.9 billion in 2024, €2.1 billion of it from bicycles.

porscheholdingsalzburg.what: A car distributor in Salzburg, grown from the firm Louise Piëch and Ferry Porsche founded in 1947, sold in 2011 to Volkswagen AG, which owns it fully.
porscheholdingsalzburg.money: Wholesale and retail of Volkswagen Group brands, financial services and IT systems, with revenue of €25.8 billion in 2022.

porticus.what: A philanthropic organisation set up in 1995 to coordinate the giving of the Brenninkmeijer family, owners of C&A, and now part of the family's foundation Constanter.
porticus.money: It raises no funds and advises on grants from Brenninkmeijer family foundations, including Clementia Verein, Stichting Benevolentia, Stiftung Auxilium and Good Energies Foundation.

portomunicipality|Portugal.what: The executive body of the municipality of Porto in Portugal, led by its president, Pedro Duarte.
portomunicipality|Portugal.money: The municipal budget, 491.3 million euros for 2026, raised mainly from local taxes such as the IMI property tax and from fees.

portugueseministryofculture|Portugal.what: Portugal's government ministry for culture, youth and sport, created in June 2025 by the XXV Constitutional Government; Margarida Balseiro Lopes is minister.

power.what: A Canadian holding company founded in 1925 and based in Montreal, controlled since 1968 by a group led by Paul Desmarais.
power.money: Its financial services holdings in insurance, retirement, wealth and asset management, which have included Great-West Life, Canada Life, IGM Financial and Mackenzie.

powercorp.money: Power Corporation of Canada, controlled by the Desmarais family, draws its money from life insurance and wealth management (Great-West Lifeco, IGM Financial) and from holdings in Europe through GBL.

facts.t: Power Corporation reported net earnings from continuing operations of $2,572 million for 2025, against $2,792 million in 2024.

prada.money: Prada's money comes from selling luxury fashion and leather goods (Prada, Miu Miu); Miuccia Prada and Patrizio Bertelli control the group.

facts.t: Prada Group reported 2024 net revenues of €5.4 billion, up 17% at constant currency, and Group net income of €839 million.

praguecityhall|Czech Republic.what: The administrative office of the City of Prague, formed on 1 January 1922, which carries out tasks set by the City Assembly and City Council from New City Hall.
praguecityhall|Czech Republic.money: The city budget, planned for 2025 with income of CZK 110.92 billion and spending of CZK 113.49 billion.

prefeituradorio.what: The municipal government of Rio de Janeiro, led by the mayor and a cabinet of 26 secretariats, with its seat at the Palácio da Cidade.
prefeituradorio.money: The municipal budget of Rio de Janeiro: BRL 45.7 billion in 2024.

preservationleague.what: A non-profit historic preservation organisation founded in 1974 and based in Albany, which gives grants and technical help for historic buildings across New York State.
preservationleague.money: Contributions, 90.3% of its US$1,552,430 revenue in the year to June 2025, with support from the New York State Council on the Arts.
preservationleague.arts: Its Preserve NY Arts + Culture grants, a regrant partnership with the state arts council, pay for building studies of up to US$20,000 for arts and cultural organisations.

princeclaus.what: A Dutch fund set up in 1996 and named after Prince Claus of the Netherlands; it gives grants and awards to artists in places where culture is under pressure.
princeclaus.money: An annual subsidy from the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
princeclaus.arts: Its Principal Award is worth €100,000; since 1996 it has supported almost 2,400 projects in 144 countries.

pritzkerfamily.money: The Pritzker family's money comes from family companies, among them Hyatt Hotels, which the family founded; its Hyatt Foundation sponsors the Pritzker Architecture Prize.

facts.t: Hyatt Hotels Corporation's revenue was $7,101 million in 2025.

privateendowedbyoilmancaloustegulbenkian.what: A Portuguese foundation set up in Lisbon in 1956 under the will of Calouste Gulbenkian, an Armenian oil magnate; it runs the Gulbenkian Museum and Orchestra.
privateendowedbyoilmancaloustegulbenkian.money: An endowment from Calouste Gulbenkian's oil fortune; it fully owned the oil company Partex until selling it to a Thai company in 2019.

privateofpatriziasandrettorerebaudengo.what: A private non-profit contemporary art foundation set up in Turin on 6 April 1995 by the collector Patrizia Sandretto Re Rebaudengo, its president.
privateofpatriziasandrettorerebaudengo.money: Mainly public and private contributions: €275,872 public and €1,812,995 private in 2024, of €2,650,394 total revenue.
privateofpatriziasandrettorerebaudengo.arts: It runs venues in Turin and Guarene d'Alba, a sculpture park at Guarene and the Young Curators Residency Programme.

prohelvetia.what: The Swiss Confederation's arts foundation, set up by the Federal Council in 1939 and made a foundation under public law in 1949; based in Zurich.
prohelvetia.money: The Swiss federal budget, set by parliament in four-year Cultural Messages: CHF 186.9 million for 2025 to 2028.
prohelvetia.arts: In 2025 it approved 2,448 of 7,235 applications and put 86.9 percent of its funds directly into art and culture.

prokhorov.money: Mikhail Prokhorov’s money comes from metals, through his former stake in Norilsk Nickel, and from his investment group Onexim.

promatrepaulista.what: A private maternity hospital in São Paulo, owned since January 2000 by Grupo Santa Joana, which also runs the Santa Joana and Santa Maria maternity hospitals there.
promatrepaulista.money: Its maternity hospital business within Grupo Santa Joana.

promsvyazbank.money: PSB’s money comes from banking: a state-owned bank, nationalised in 2018, that the US Treasury calls critical to Russia’s defence sector.

facts.t: On 22 February 2022 the US Treasury sanctioned PSB and its subsidiaries, calling it critical to Russia’s defence sector, and designated its chairman and chief executive Petr Fradkov.

protective.what: A life insurance and annuity holding company in Birmingham, Alabama, whose main subsidiary was founded in 1907, owned since February 2015 by Dai-ichi Life of Tokyo.
protective.money: Sales of life insurance, annuities and asset protection products, with annual revenues of US$7.75 billion.

protesterscitedwilliam.what: A private foundation in Menlo Park, California, established in 1966 by William R. Hewlett, co-founder of Hewlett-Packard, and his wife Flora Lamson Hewlett.
protesterscitedwilliam.money: An endowment given by Bill Hewlett and his wife Flora, with assets of approximately $13.9 billion on 31 December 2024.
protesterscitedwilliam.arts: Its Performing Arts Program funds the arts in the San Francisco Bay Area and awarded $40.5 million through 94 grants in 2024.

provinceofbc|Canada.what: The provincial government of British Columbia, Canada, led by a Premier and Cabinet answerable to the 93-member Legislative Assembly in Victoria.
provinceofbc|Canada.money: Provincial taxes, natural resource royalties and federal transfers; revenue was forecast at C$83.3 billion for 2025-26.

provinceoflimburg|Netherlands.what: The government of the Dutch province of Limburg, with a 47-seat provincial council and its seat at the Gouvernement aan de Maas in Maastricht.
provinceoflimburg|Netherlands.money: In 2025 the national provinciefonds paid €284.6 million, its surcharge on motor vehicle tax raised €129.3 million and dividends €22.3 million.

provinceofmanitoba|Canada.what: The provincial government of Manitoba, Canada: a cabinet led by the premier and drawn from the elected Legislative Assembly, seated in Winnipeg.
provinceofmanitoba|Canada.money: Provincial taxes and federal transfers: Budget 2026 projects C$26,820 million of revenue for 2026/27, including C$9,657 million from the federal government.

provinceofstyriaculturaldepartment|Austr.what: Department 9 (Culture, Europe, Sports) of the administration of the Austrian state of Styria, headed by Patrick Schnabl and based at Landhausgasse 7 in Graz.
provinceofstyriaculturaldepartment|Austr.money: The budget of the State of Styria.
provinceofstyriaculturaldepartment|Austr.arts: It publishes a Kulturförderungsbericht each year that sets out how its culture funds were awarded.

provincialcouncilofbiscay|Spain.what: The governing body of the historical territory of Bizkaia in the Basque Country, headed since 2023 by the diputada general Elixabete Etxanobe.
provincialcouncilofbiscay|Spain.money: The Bizkaia budget: 11,320.3 million euros for 2026, of which 1,716.2 million go to its own departments.
provincialcouncilofbiscay|Spain.arts: Its department of Basque language, culture and sport receives 70.4 million euros in the 2026 budget plan.

provinciezeeland.what: The provincial government of Zeeland in the Netherlands, seated in Middelburg, with 39 members in its Provinciale Staten and 394,514 inhabitants at the end of 2025.
provinciezeeland.money: The national provinciefonds, €169.4 million in its 2026 budget, plus €46.3 million from motor vehicle tax surcharges and a €16.0 million Westerscheldetunnel dividend.

prtourism.what: A government-owned corporation in charge of tourism in Puerto Rico, created under Governor Luis A. Ferré (1969-1973) and headquartered in the former La Princesa jail in San Juan.
prtourism.money: The room occupancy tax on hotel stays, which Act 272 of 2003 moved from the Treasury to the company to levy, collect and distribute.
prtourism.arts: La Princesa also houses a gallery that shows the agency's art collection.

psb.what: A Moscow bank founded in 1995, nationalised in 2018, made the supporting bank for Russia's defence industry by a 2019 law and under US and UK sanctions since February 2022.
psb.money: Lending to the defence industry and retail banking: a net loss of RUB 19.2 billion in 2025.

pubcharity.money: A gaming trust: its money is the revenue from the pokie machines it runs in pubs and bars, given out as grants for charitable purposes.

facts.t: In the year to 30 September 2025 Pub Charity reported revenue from gaming machines of $107,904 thousand, paid $24,818 thousand in gaming machine duty and distributed $45,333 thousand in grants.

publiccentrefundedbygipuzkoacouncil|Spai.what: The government of the historical territory of Gipuzkoa in the Basque Country, based in San Sebastián and headed by a Diputado General elected by the Juntas Generales.
publiccentrefundedbygipuzkoacouncil|Spai.money: The provincial budget, of which its Hacienda y Finanzas department accounts for about €6.03 billion.

pudilfamily.what: A Czech family foundation in Prague set up by Pavlína Pudil, its board chair, and Petr Pudil; its art collection is on long-term loan to Kunsthalle Praha.
pudilfamily.money: Its co-founder's fortune from a stake in the coal group Czech Coal, sold in 2010, and bpd partners, the family office he co-founded in 2008.
pudilfamily.arts: It supports visual art, research and education and sits on boards and acquisition committees at Tate, KW Berlin and Palais de Tokyo.

puig.what: A Spanish fragrance and fashion company founded in Barcelona in 1914 by Antonio Puig Castelló, listed on the Madrid stock exchange and managed by the Puig family.
puig.money: Sales of perfumes, cosmetics and fashion under brands including Carolina Herrera and Charlotte Tilbury, with revenue of €4.3 billion in 2023.

pumaenergy.money: Trafigura’s money comes from trading oil, metals and minerals; Puma Energy, the fuel distributor it controls, sells fuel in Latin America, Africa and Asia.

facts.t: Trafigura was behind the 2006 dumping of toxic waste in Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire, after which over 100,000 people sought medical help (Amnesty International and Greenpeace Netherlands).

Trafigura pleaded guilty in the United States to conspiring to violate the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act in Brazil, with a criminal penalty of about $80.5 million and forfeiture of about $46.5 million.

Switzerland’s Federal Criminal Court found Trafigura guilty of “organizational failure” in relation to corruption in Angola, with a fine of CHF 3 million and a compensation claim of USD 145 million, for close to USD 5 million in bribes paid between 2009 and 2011.
Trafigura’s net profit was USD 2,666 million for the year to 30 September 2025, down three percent.
Trafigura Pte Ltd declared EU lobbying costs of €400,000 to €499,999 for October 2024 to September 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.
Trafigura Pte Ltd paid the firm Ragnar Group $160,000 for federal lobbying in 2025 ($80,000 in each of the third and fourth quarters), as the firm reported.

pwc.what: A professional services network formed in 1998 by merging Price Waterhouse and Coopers & Lybrand, overseen from London by PricewaterhouseCoopers International Limited, with member firms in 149 countries.
pwc.money: Fees for audit, tax, legal and advisory work: network revenue of USD 55.4 billion in fiscal 2024.

pyur.what: A Berlin cable network and internet provider, trading as PŸUR since September 2017 and taken over in 2021 by Kublai GmbH, then majority-held by a Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners subsidiary.
pyur.money: Cable television, internet and telephone subscriptions for about three million connected households, with revenue of €422.7 million.

qantas.money: Qantas is Australia’s largest airline, with Jetstar and the Qantas loyalty business.

facts.t: The Qantas Group reported revenue and other income of $23,823 million and a statutory profit after tax of $1,605 million for the year to 30 June 2025.
In August 2025 the Federal Court ordered Qantas to pay a $90 million penalty for illegally outsourcing more than 1,800 ground staff in 2020, after its appeal to the High Court failed.

qatarmuseums.what: A Qatari government entity founded in 2005 that runs the country's museums, chaired by Sheikha Al Mayassa bint Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani under the Amir's patronage.
qatarmuseums.arts: It oversees the Museum of Islamic Art, Mathaf, the National Museum of Qatar and the 3-2-1 Qatar Olympic and Sports Museum.

qatarshell.what: Shell's group of companies in Qatar, one of the first international companies to begin oil production there; Richard Tallant chaired it in 2022.
qatarshell.money: Shell's gas business in Qatar, including the Pearl GTL plant at Ras Laffan, run under a production sharing agreement with QatarEnergy.
qatarshell.arts: In November 2018 it agreed to sponsor Company House, the oil history house of Msheireb Museums in Doha.

qattan.what: A Palestinian non-profit foundation set up in 1993 by the businessman Abdel Mohsin Al-Qattan and based in Ramallah; it is also a registered UK charity.
qattan.money: Donations of £2.02 million and investment income of £484,080 in 2025, of £2.62 million income reported by its UK charity.
qattan.arts: It opened a US$21 million headquarters and arts centre in Ramallah in June 2018.

qattantodate.what: A Palestinian non-profit foundation set up in 1993 by the businessman Abdel Mohsin Al-Qattan and based in Ramallah; it is also a registered UK charity.
qattantodate.money: Donations of £2.02 million and investment income of £484,080 in 2025, of £2.62 million income reported by its UK charity.
qattantodate.arts: It opened a US$21 million headquarters and arts centre in Ramallah in June 2018.

qiaozhibing.money: Qiao Zhibing's money comes from karaoke clubs in Shanghai.

qualco.what: A non-profit corporate foundation of Qualco Group, an Athens financial technology company, announced in April 2022 and led by the group's executive chairman Orestis Tsakalotos.
qualco.money: Qualco Group, which sells software, platforms and portfolio management services to banks and financial institutions.
qualco.arts: Culture and Sports is one of its stated pillars of work.

quark.what: A polar expedition cruise company with headquarters in Seattle, operating since 1991 in the Arctic and Antarctica, a member of the UK-based Travelopia travel group.
quark.money: Fares for small-ship expedition cruises on ice-class vessels and icebreakers.

quarkexpeditions.money: Polar expedition cruises; Quark is a member of the Travelopia group, which KKR agreed to buy from TUI in 2017.

facts.t: KKR agreed to buy Travelopia, the travel group Quark belongs to, from TUI; Travelopia then had 53 brands and over 800,000 travellers a year.

quebeccultureministry|Canada.what: The Quebec government ministry for culture, heritage, communications and the French language, led by minister Pascal Bérubé; its culture and communications portfolio took its present form in 2012.
quebeccultureministry|Canada.money: The budget of the Government of Quebec.

rabeesecurities.what: An Iraqi securities brokerage established on 7 January 1995, licensed by the Iraqi Securities Commission and headquartered in Baghdad, chaired by Shwan Ibrahim Taha.
rabeesecurities.money: Brokerage on the Iraq Stock Exchange, investment banking, custody and advisory work; its capital is IQD 3 billion.

rabobank.money: Rabobank's money comes from banking, above all lending to farmers and the food and agriculture business; it is a Dutch cooperative bank.

facts.t: In October 2013 the US CFTC ordered Rabobank to pay a $475 million penalty for false reporting and attempted manipulation of LIBOR and Euribor; in related actions it agreed to a $325 million US Justice Department penalty, a £105 million UK FCA penalty and a €70 million payment to Dutch prosecutors.
Banking on Climate Chaos 2026 ranks Rabobank 48th among the world's banks for fossil fuel financing in 2025, a change of -$212 million (-6.9%) from 2024.
Rabobank declared EU lobbying costs of €300,000 to €399,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register, with 2.25 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.

raiffeisen.money: Raiffeisen is not one company: the atlas ties name Swiss Raiffeisen banks (the Raiffeisen Switzerland cooperative group) and Austrian ones (Raiffeisenlandesbank Oberösterreich, Raiffeisen Salzburg), cooperative banks owned by their members.

rajeebsamdani.what: A non-profit art trust in Dhaka, founded in 2011 by the collector couple Nadia and Rajeeb Samdani.
rajeebsamdani.money: Rajeeb Samdani is managing director of Golden Harvest Group, a Dhaka conglomerate that also sponsors the Dhaka Art Summit.
rajeebsamdani.arts: It is building Srihatta, an art centre and sculpture park in Sylhet, and gives the Samdani Art Award.

ralesfamily.what: Mitchell Rales co-founded the Danaher Corporation with his brother Steven in 1984 and founded Glenstone with his wife, Emily Wei Rales, in 2006.
ralesfamily.money: Mitchell Rales's fortune from Danaher, Colfax and Fortive, estimated at 4 billion dollars in 2025.
ralesfamily.arts: Mitchell Rales is a former president of the National Gallery of Art in Washington.

rattispa.what: An Italian textile company founded in Como in 1945 by Antonio Ratti as Tessitura Serica Antonio Ratti, based in Guanzate and part of the Marzotto Group since 2010.
rattispa.money: Sales of fabrics and accessories to fashion houses.

rbc.money: RBC’s money comes from banking, wealth management, insurance and capital markets.

facts.t: RBC’s UK asset manager, RBC Global Asset Management (UK), declared EU lobbying costs of €10,000 to €24,999 for November 2024 to October 2025; the bank itself is not on the register.
RBC USA Holdco’s federal PAC gave $78,500 to federal candidates in the 2023 to 2024 cycle, 55% to Republicans and 45% to Democrats, in its reports to the Federal Election Commission.

realdania.what: A Danish member-based philanthropic association created in 2000, when Realkredit Danmark sold its mortgage business in its merger with Danske Bank, based in Copenhagen.
realdania.money: Returns on investing the capital it kept from that deal; about 195,000 members own it.
realdania.arts: It funds projects in architecture, planning and the built environment.

recordati.what: A private foundation based in Impruneta near Florence, created by the entrepreneur and art collector Andy Bianchedi in memory of his mother.
recordati.arts: A statutory supporter of Fondazione Palazzo Strozzi since 2024, it appoints one board director and co-promotes the Palazzo Strozzi Future Art programme.

regionecampania.what: The regional government of Campania in southern Italy, seated in Naples and led by President Roberto Fico with a 60-member Regional Council.
regionecampania.money: The regional budget, over EUR 38.5 billion for 2026, almost 70% of it for health.
regionecampania.arts: Its 2026 budget raises cinema funding to EUR 6 million and live-performance funding to EUR 17 million.

regionelazio.what: The regional government of Lazio in central Italy, seated in Rome and led by President Francesco Rocca, with a Regional Council as its legislature.
regionelazio.money: The regional budget; its 2025 economic and financial plan set the 2025 to 2027 budget at about EUR 10 billion.

regionelombardia.what: The regional government of Lombardy, Italy, led by president Attilio Fontana since 2018, with its seat in Milan.

regionepiemonte.what: The regional government of Piedmont, an Italian region with ordinary statute created in 1948 and operating since 1970; seat in Turin.
regionepiemonte.money: The regional budget, which draws on its own taxes such as IRAP, regional surcharges and car tax.

regionetoscana.what: An Italian ordinary-statute region, set up in 1948 and working since 1970, with its seat in Florence and Eugenio Giani as president since 8 October 2020.

regions.what: A bank holding company in Birmingham, Alabama, founded in 1971 as First Alabama Bankshares by the merger of three Alabama banks and renamed in 1994.
regions.money: Commercial, retail and mortgage banking, with revenue of US$9.608 billion and assets of US$158.814 billion in 2025.

regionstockholm|Sweden.what: The regional public body for Stockholm County, set up on 1 January 2019 in place of Stockholm County Council, running healthcare, public transport and regional planning.
regionstockholm|Sweden.money: The regional budget, about SEK 133 billion in 2024, when the regional income tax rate was 12.38 percent.

reliance.money: The Ambani family’s money comes from Reliance Industries: oil refining and petrochemicals, retail, Jio telecoms, oil and gas, and media.

facts.t: Reliance Industries reported consolidated revenue of ₹10,71,174 crore (US$125.3 billion) for 2024-25, up 7.1%.
In January 2021 SEBI fined Reliance Industries Rs 25 crore and Mukesh Ambani Rs 15 crore for manipulating trading in Reliance Petroleum shares in November 2007.
In December 2023 the Securities Appellate Tribunal quashed SEBI’s order against Mukesh Ambani and two other entities in the Reliance Petroleum case.
Eversheds Sutherland reported $195,000 in 2025 fees from Reliance Industries for US federal lobbying, under the Lobbying Disclosure Act (fourth quarter as amended).

relianceindustriesunderbillionairemukesh.what: An Indian conglomerate founded in 1958 by Dhirubhai Ambani, based in Mumbai and chaired by Mukesh Ambani, with the Ambani family holding 50%.
relianceindustriesunderbillionairemukesh.money: Petroleum refining, petrochemicals, natural gas, retail and telecoms, with revenue of ₹11.04 lakh crore (US$120 billion) in 2026.

remai.money: Frank and Ellen Remai’s money comes from Frank Remai’s real estate business in Saskatoon, given through the Frank and Ellen Remai Foundation.

repsol.money: Repsol's money comes from producing oil and gas, refining and selling fuels, chemicals, and electricity.

facts.t: Repsol reported a net income of €1.899 billion for 2025, up 8%, and adjusted net income of €2.568 billion, 15% lower than in 2024.
Repsol, S.A. declared EU lobbying costs of €800,000 to €899,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.
Repsol, S.A. reported $980,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.
InfluenceMap gives Repsol a D grade for its climate policy engagement.

republicofaustria|Austria.what: The Austrian federal state, a republic of nine states whose parliament, head of state, federal government and highest courts sit in Vienna, the federal capital.
republicofaustria|Austria.money: The federal budget of the Republic of Austria.

republicofkosovoministries|Kosovo.what: The government ministry of the Republic of Kosovo for culture, youth and sport.
republicofkosovoministries|Kosovo.money: The Kosovo state budget: EUR 86.4 million planned for the ministry in 2025, down from EUR 88.1 million in 2024.

resoluteav.what: An audio visual and IT installation company trading as Resolute AV, incorporated on 18 October 2023, with its registered office in Godmanchester, Huntingdon.
resoluteav.money: Installing and hiring audio visual systems for commercial, education, residential, church and marine clients.

rgionbourgognefranchecomt.what: The regional council of Bourgogne-Franche-Comté, the French region formed on 1 January 2016 from Burgundy and Franche-Comté, seated in Besançon.
rgionbourgognefranchecomt.money: A EUR 1.922 billion budget in 2025, led by EUR 699 million of national VAT revenue assigned by the French state.
rgionbourgognefranchecomt.arts: Its 2025 budget gives EUR 33.7 million to culture and heritage.

rgioncentrevaldeloire.what: The regional government of Centre-Val de Loire in France, run by an elected regional council of 77 members that sits in Orléans.
rgioncentrevaldeloire.money: The region's own budget, 1.913 billion euros for 2026 before debt rescheduling.

rgiongrandest.what: The regional council of Grand Est, the French region formed in 2016 from Alsace, Champagne-Ardenne and Lorraine, seated in Strasbourg.
