rgiongrandest.money: Mostly national VAT shared out by the French state (53% of French regions' operating revenue in 2024); its planned 2026 budget is EUR 4.1 billion.

rgionhautsdefrance.what: The regional government of Hauts-de-France in France, created on 1 January 2016 and run by an elected regional council of 170 members that sits in Lille.
rgionhautsdefrance.money: The region's own budget, 5.2 billion euros for 2026, adopted on 9 April 2026.

rgionledefrance.what: The French region that contains Paris, run by a regional council of 209 councillors elected for six years, headquartered in Saint-Ouen-sur-Seine.

rgionpaysdelaloire.what: The regional government of Pays de la Loire in France, run by an elected regional council of 93 members that sits in Nantes.
rgionpaysdelaloire.money: The region's own budget, 1.95 billion euros for 2026.

rgionsud.what: The regional council of Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, the south-eastern French region also called Région Sud, seated in Marseille.
rgionsud.money: Mainly a share of national VAT assigned by the French state; councillors adopted a EUR 3.2 billion budget for 2024.
rgionsud.arts: The 2024 budget gave EUR 67 million to arts and culture.

rietumubanka.what: A Latvian commercial bank founded on 14 May 1992 with headquarters in Riga, whose largest shareholders are companies of Leonids Esterkins, Dermot Desmond and Arkādijs Suharenko.
rietumubanka.money: Corporate lending and banking services, with assets of €1.5 billion and net profit of €15.9 million in 2023.

rigacity|Latvia.what: The government of Riga, Latvia's capital, with 60 councillors elected every four years, meeting in the Town Hall on Rātslaukums.
rigacity|Latvia.money: The city budget: planned revenue of 1.5 billion euros in 2026, with growth from personal income tax, against 1.7 billion euros of spending.
rigacity|Latvia.arts: Its 2026 cultural programme centres on the 825th anniversary of Riga.

right:cohen.what: An American hedge fund manager, founder of Point72 Asset Management (2014, Stamford, Connecticut) and owner of the New York Mets.
right:cohen.money: His hedge fund fortune: S.A.C. Capital Advisors from 1992, which pleaded guilty to insider trading in 2013, then Point72.
right:cohen.arts: The Steven & Alexandra Cohen Foundation, started in 2001, has granted US$1.5 billion to health, education, arts and culture and New York projects.

right:griffin.money: Ken Griffin’s money comes from Citadel, his hedge fund, and Citadel Securities, a market-making firm.

facts.t: Citadel’s flagship Wellington fund finished 2024 up 15.1%; the firm had $66 billion in assets under management in December.
Ken Griffin gave $100,000,000 in the 2024 election cycle, fifth among top contributors, according to OpenSecrets data cited by CBS News.
Citadel declared EU lobbying costs of €400,000 to €499,999 for 2025, with 2.25 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.
Citadel reported $650,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.
Citadel Securities’ PAC gave $28,500 to federal candidates in the 2023 to 2024 cycle, 47% to Republicans and 53% to Democrats, in its reports to the Federal Election Commission.

Ken Griffin gave $108,360,344 in personal contributions to federal candidates, parties and PACs in the 2023 to 2024 cycle; the largest went to Senate Leadership Fund ($30,000,000), Congressional Leadership Fund ($17,000,000) and Keystone Renewal PAC ($16,000,000), in contributions reported to the Federal Election Commission.

right:koch.money: The Koch fortune comes from Koch Industries, a private conglomerate in oil refining, pipelines, chemicals, fertilisers, paper and other industries.

facts.t: Forbes lists Koch Industries’ annual revenue at $125 billion on its 2026 list of private companies.
AFP Action, the Koch network’s super PAC, spent roughly $138.5 million on independent expenditures in the 2024 cycle, according to OpenSecrets.
In 2000 Koch Industries agreed to pay a $30 million civil penalty over oil spills from its pipelines in several US states.
Koch Government Affairs, the lobbying arm of Koch Industries, reported $9,320,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

KOCHPAC, the PAC of Koch, Inc. (formerly Koch Industries), gave $1,663,500 to federal candidates in the 2023 to 2024 cycle, 98% to Republicans and 0% to Democrats, in its reports to the Federal Election Commission.

Charles Koch gave $10,000 in personal contributions to federal candidates, parties and PACs in the 2023 to 2024 cycle, all of it to KOCHPAC, the PAC of Koch, Inc., in contributions reported to the Federal Election Commission.

rinatmardanov.what: A person the atlas names as a backer of the launch of Smena, a contemporary culture centre at Burkhana Shakhidi 7 in Kazan.

ringier.what: A family-owned Swiss media group dating from the printing press Johann Rudolf Ringier founded in Zofingen in 1833, with offices in Zurich.
ringier.money: Media brands, sports media platforms and digital marketplaces in 18 European and African countries, with revenue of CHF 918.9 million in 2023.
ringier.arts: Over 200 works of contemporary art hang in its offices, an interest of its publisher Michael Ringier.

riodejaneirostate|Brazil.what: The executive branch of the Brazilian state of Rio de Janeiro, led by the governor, with its seat at the Palácio Guanabara in the state capital since 1975.
riodejaneirostate|Brazil.money: The state budget of Rio de Janeiro.
riodejaneirostate|Brazil.arts: Its culture and creative economy secretariat runs the state culture incentive law, under which ICMS-paying companies put about R$ 230 million into 138 projects in 2024.

riotinto.money: Rio Tinto’s money comes from mining, mainly iron ore, plus aluminium, copper and other minerals.

facts.t: Rio Tinto reported net earnings of US$11,552 million and underlying earnings of $10.87 billion for 2024.
InfluenceMap gives Rio Tinto a C- grade for its climate policy engagement.
Rio Tinto blasted 46,000-year-old rock shelters at Juukan Gorge in May 2020; its chief executive resigned that September.
Rio Tinto declared EU lobbying costs of €900,000 to €999,999 for 2025, with 2.35 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.
Rio Tinto Services reported $1,140,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in three quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.
Rio Tinto America’s PAC gave $14,000 to federal candidates in the 2023 to 2024 cycle, 82% to Republicans and 18% to Democrats, in its reports to the Federal Election Commission.

rnne.what: A non-profit foundation in Berlin, founded in 2020 by Burkhard Saar and named after the Rönnestraße in Charlottenburg, which supports democracy and civil society projects abroad.
rnne.money: A founding endowment from the estate of the Berlin artist and craftsman Ulrich Stroß, plus project grants from the German Federal Foreign Office.

robertdavidliongardiner.what: A private foundation established in 1987 and named for Robert David Lion Gardiner, 16th Lord of the Manor of Gardiner's Island until his death in 2004, based in Riverhead.
robertdavidliongardiner.money: Its endowment, with net assets of US$116,984,003 at December 2025 and income from asset sales, dividends and interest.
robertdavidliongardiner.arts: It funds the study of Long Island history, with grants to historical societies for collections, preservation and exhibition.

robertomarinho.money: The Marinho family’s money comes from Grupo Globo, Brazil’s largest media group, with television, newspapers and streaming.

facts.t: Globo’s net profit fell to R$1.45 billion in 2025, despite growth in revenue.
Roberto Marinho, then president of the group, wrote in 1984 that it had supported the 1964 “revolution”; in 2013 Globo said that support for the coup had been an error.

robertsontrust.what: An independent grant-making trust in Glasgow, established in 1961 by the sisters Elspeth, Agnes and Ethel Robertson, who gave it their shares in the family whisky businesses.
robertsontrust.money: Dividends from Edrington, the spirits company behind The Macallan and Highland Park, in which the trust owns all voting shares.
robertsontrust.arts: It has awarded over £300 million across Scotland over 60 years and now directs its funding at poverty and trauma.

robertweilfamily.what: A private foundation in Stockholm established in 2014 by Robert Weil, working in culture, education and democratic engagement.
robertweilfamily.money: Its assets are managed by Proventus AB, the investment company founded in 1969 and owned by Robert Weil and family.
robertweilfamily.arts: It supports fine arts, drama and dance and is a founding patron of Accelerator at Stockholm University, with Magasin III.

roche.money: Roche's money comes from pharmaceuticals and diagnostics; the Hoffmann and Oeri families, descendants of the founder, control it, and their own foundations (LUMA, the Emanuel Hoffmann Foundation, the Laurenz Foundation) draw on that fortune. The facts below are about the company.

facts.t: Roche reported 2025 group sales of CHF 61,516 million and IFRS net income of CHF 13,799 million.
In May 1999 F. Hoffmann-La Roche agreed to plead guilty and pay a $500 million criminal fine in the US for leading a worldwide conspiracy to fix prices and allocate market shares for vitamins.
F. Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd declared EU lobbying costs of €2,000,000 to €2,249,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

F. Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd and its affiliates reported $410,000 of their own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act; Genentech and Roche Diagnostics are not counted.

rocheespaa.what: The Spanish subsidiary of the Swiss healthcare company Roche, constituted in Barcelona on 21 May 1930 and now seated in Madrid.
rocheespaa.money: Sales of medicines and diagnostics in Spain, with net sales of 739.6 million euros in 2024, and Roche Holding owns all its shares.

rockefellerbrothers.money: The Rockefeller money comes from John D. Rockefeller's Standard Oil fortune; the Rockefeller Brothers Fund was founded in 1940 by John D. Rockefeller Jr.'s five sons and endowed by him in 1951.

facts.t: The Rockefeller Brothers Fund's Form 990-PF for 2024 shows revenue of $76,104,004, expenses of $94,125,890 and net assets of $1,373,487,971.

rockwellautomation.what: A US industrial automation company in Milwaukee, Wisconsin; it began in 1903, founded by Stanton Allen and Lynde Bradley, and took the name Allen-Bradley Company in 1909.
rockwellautomation.money: Sales of industrial automation hardware, software and services under brands such as Allen-Bradley and FactoryTalk: USD 8,342 million in fiscal 2025.

rogers.money: The Rogers family’s money comes from Rogers Communications, the wireless, cable and media company it controls; the ties here are gifts in the company’s name.

facts.t: A review commissioned by the CRTC found that Rogers’ July 2022 outage, which caused a catastrophic loss of all wireless and wireline services, was caused by human error and prolonged by management deficiencies.

rolex.what: A Geneva watchmaker founded in London in 1905 by Hans Wilsdorf and Alfred Davis, owned since 1960 by the Hans Wilsdorf Foundation.
rolex.money: Sales of Rolex and Tudor wristwatches by a company wholly owned by the Hans Wilsdorf Foundation, a private Swiss foundation.
rolex.arts: Its Rolex Mentor and Protégé Arts Initiative, set up in 2002, pairs emerging artists with established ones and gives each protégé about $41,000.

rolfhoff.what: Norwegian art collectors who acquired the KaviarFactory building in Henningsvær, Lofoten, after the cannery closed in 2006 and turned it into a contemporary art space.
rolfhoff.money: Rolf Hoff's business, which makes signage and produces works for artists.
rolfhoff.arts: They have lent works to Tate Britain, Garage in Moscow and most Norwegian contemporary art museums, and support artist-run galleries in Oslo.

romacapitale.what: The local government of Rome, set up in 2010 under the Italian constitution in place of the comune di Roma, with its seat on the Campidoglio.
romacapitale.money: The municipal budget of Roma Capitale.

romanabramovich.what: A Russian businessman, governor of Chukotka from 2000 to 2008 and former owner of Chelsea football club, sanctioned after the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine.
romanabramovich.money: His Sibneft oil stake, sold to the Russian state for $13 billion in 2005, and his Millhouse holdings, which bought 41% of Evraz in 2006.
romanabramovich.arts: He co-founded the Garage Museum of Contemporary Art in Moscow with Dasha Zhukova in 2008.

romanianministryofculture|Romania.what: The ministry of the Government of Romania for cultural policy and heritage, first set up on 22 January 1862 and named Ministry of Culture since 2019, seated in Bucharest.

romantrotsenko.what: A Russian businessman born in 1970, owner of the investment company Aeon Corporation and president of United Shipbuilding Corporation from 2009 to 2012.
romantrotsenko.money: 70 percent of Russkaya Energia, which agreed in 2021 to buy the coal miner Vorkutaugol; Forbes put his fortune at USD 1.6 billion in 2019.

rosatommashinostroenie.what: The machine building division of Rosatom, the Russian state nuclear corporation, whose factories make reactor equipment for power plants and nuclear icebreakers.
rosatommashinostroenie.money: Sales of equipment for nuclear and thermal power plants, made in Moscow, St Petersburg, Karelia and the Moscow, Rostov, Nizhny Novgorod and Yekaterinburg regions.

rosenthalfamily.what: A private family foundation in Cincinnati, set up in 1986 by Lois and Richard Rosenthal, owners of the publisher F&W Publications.
rosenthalfamily.money: The Rosenthals' money from F&W Publications, sold in December 1999, with net assets of $27,719,722 at the end of 2024.
rosenthalfamily.arts: In 1999 it gave $6 million toward the Contemporary Arts Center building in Cincinnati, which carries the Rosenthals' name.

rosneft.what: A Russian integrated oil and gas company in Moscow, founded as a state enterprise in 1993 and controlled by state-owned Rosneftegaz, with Igor Sechin as chief executive.
rosneft.money: Oil and gas production, refining and fuel sales: revenue of ₽8.16 trillion (USD 95.75 billion) in 2025.

facts.t: On 22 October 2025 the US Treasury designated Rosneft and Lukoil, Russia’s two largest oil companies, with a number of their Russian subsidiaries.

rotasa.what: A private family foundation in Redwood City, California, with Rose Webb Roven as president and Susan Cummins as secretary, whose last listed tax return covers the year to June 2017.
rotasa.money: Contributions received each year: $557,162 of its $760,672 revenue in the year to June 2016.

rothschild.money: The Rothschild money comes from banking: Rothschild & Co, the Paris and London advisory, wealth management and merchant banking group, and for the English branch's Rothschild Foundation and Eranda Rothschild Foundation, the family fortunes built from it. The facts below are about Rothschild & Co, the bank tied to the National Gallery.

facts.t: Rothschild & Co reported 2025 revenue of €2,986 million and net income, group share, of €413 million.
Rothschild & Co SCA declared EU lobbying costs of €10,000 to €24,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

royalairmaroc.what: Morocco's national airline, founded in July 1953 and headquartered at Casablanca-Anfa Airport, with the Moroccan state holding about 98% of its capital.
royalairmaroc.money: Passenger and cargo flights, with revenue of 19.7 billion Moroccan dirhams in 2023.

royalinn.money: Royal Inn (老爺會館) is one of the hotels of the Hotel Royal group (老爺酒店集團), so its money comes from running hotels in Taiwan.

royalinstituteofbritisharchitects.what: The professional membership body for architects in the United Kingdom, formed in 1834, incorporated by Royal Charter and registered as a charity, with headquarters in London.
royalinstituteofbritisharchitects.money: Charitable activities (£17.61 million), investments (£9.37 million) and trading (£4.68 million) made up most of its £32,357,000 income in 2025.

royalnorwegianembassy|Tanzania.what: Norway's embassy in Tanzania, a mission of the Norwegian Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Dar es Salaam that also represents Norway in Burundi, Comoros, Rwanda and Uganda.
royalnorwegianembassy|Tanzania.money: The Norwegian government through its foreign ministry, and the embassy signed a NOK 19 million grant to the Legal and Human Rights Centre in 2025.

rtx.what: A US aerospace and defence group formed in 2020 by merging Raytheon with the aerospace businesses of United Technologies; its units are Collins Aerospace, Pratt & Whitney and Raytheon.
rtx.money: Aircraft engines, avionics, guided missiles and air defence systems: revenue of USD 88.6 billion in 2025, 38 percent of it from the US government.

rubelli.what: A Venetian silk and furnishing textile company dating to Lorenzo Rubelli's purchase of the G.B. Trapolin weaving mill in 1889; Alessandro Favaretto Rubelli is its president.
rubelli.money: Sales of silk fabrics and furnishing textiles worldwide.
rubelli.arts: It set up the Rubelli Foundation in 2018 to safeguard its textile heritage, and has given to the Fondazione Giorgio Cini, Venetian Heritage and Save Venice.

rubismcnat.what: The endowment fund of the French energy group Rubis, running artistic and social projects since 2011.
rubismcnat.money: The Rubis group, founded in 1990 by Gilles Gobin in Paris, which stores and distributes petroleum products and LPG.
rubismcnat.arts: It funds the Prix Rubis Mécénat with the Beaux-Arts de Paris and youth programmes in South Africa, Madagascar and Jamaica.

rundirectlybyrgionoccitanie.what: The regional council of Occitanie in France, created on 1 January 2016 by merging the Languedoc-Roussillon and Midi-Pyrénées councils, with 158 councillors and its seat in Toulouse.
rundirectlybyrgionoccitanie.money: The regional budget voted by its councillors, 3.54 billion euros for 2026.

russianfederalstate|Russia.what: The Russian federal ministry for culture policy, formed on 2 May 2008 and led by Olga Lyubimova since 21 January 2020; the Hermitage is in its charge.
russianfederalstate|Russia.money: The federal budget of Russia, which pays federal museums such as the Hermitage subsidies for their state assignments.

russianstate|Russia.what: The Russian federal ministry for culture policy, formed on 2 May 2008 and led by Olga Lyubimova since 21 January 2020; the Hermitage is in its charge.
russianstate|Russia.money: The federal budget of Russia, which pays federal museums such as the Hermitage subsidies for their state assignments.

russiasmajornaturalgasproducer.what: A Russian businessman, born in 1955, who is chairman, chief executive and major shareholder of the gas company Novatek; he set up the V-A-C Foundation in 2009.
russiasmajornaturalgasproducer.money: His stake in Novatek, Russia's second-largest natural gas producer after Gazprom, which had revenue of $17 billion in 2025.

ruth.what: A private arts foundation in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, that launched in 2022 and gives grants to artists and arts organisations across the United States.
ruth.money: A US$440 million bequest from Ruth DeYoung Kohler II (died 2020), of the family that founded the Kohler bathroom-fixture company.
ruth.arts: It planned to give US$17 million to US$20 million a year; in 2024 it gave US$950,000 to 10 Wisconsin arts groups.

rweag.what: An electricity company in Essen, founded in 1898 as Rheinisch-Westfälisches Elektrizitätswerk, that generates and trades power in Europe, the United States and Asia-Pacific.
rweag.money: Sales of power from wind, solar, hydro, biomass, gas and coal plants, and energy trading: EUR 17.63 billion revenue in 2025.

saastamoinen.what: A private foundation in Helsinki, established in 1968 by Liisa Karttunen, born Saastamoinen, and her husband Osmo P. Karttunen.
saastamoinen.money: The assets of the family company Saastamoinen Ltd of Kuopio, which closed in 1996, now held as an investment portfolio.
saastamoinen.arts: It owns nearly 3,000 works of modern and contemporary art and supports artists with grants and residencies.

sabanci.money: The Sabancı family’s money comes from Sabancı Holding, a Turkish group in banking (Akbank), energy, building materials, mobility and digital businesses.

facts.t: Sabancı Holding reported combined revenue of TL 1,243,518,569 thousand for 2024 and a consolidated net loss of TL 15,474,560 thousand.
In 2018 Turkey’s competition authority fined units of Enerjisa, jointly owned by Sabancı Holding and E.ON, 143 million lira ($26.1 million) for abusing a dominant market position.

sabo.what: An Italian chemical company founded in 1937, with its registered office at Levate in the province of Bergamo.
sabo.money: Sales of polymer additives, feed additives, industrial surfactants and performance intermediates.

sacklerfamily.what: An American family: the brothers Arthur, Mortimer and Raymond Sackler bought Purdue-Frederick in 1952, and Mortimer and Raymond later turned it into Purdue Pharma.
sacklerfamily.money: Profits of Purdue Pharma, the Stamford, Connecticut maker of OxyContin that the family owned until its 2026 shutdown, and of Mundipharma, which it founded.
sacklerfamily.arts: It gave to the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the American Museum of Natural History and the Guggenheim; in 2019 all three stopped taking gifts from Sacklers tied to Purdue.

facts.t: A 2019 audit in Purdue’s bankruptcy found the Sackler family withdrew nearly $11 billion from Purdue.
In 2020 Purdue agreed to plead guilty to three felonies and pay $8.3 billion; five Sacklers agreed to pay $225 million in a civil settlement.
A federal bankruptcy judge approved the $7.4 billion Purdue and Sackler opioid settlement on 14 November 2025.
In March 2019, after Tate and the Guggenheim said they would refuse its money, the UK Sackler Trust paused all new philanthropic giving.
Purdue Pharma, the Sackler family’s company, reported $400,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

sacklertrust.what: A UK charity (no. 1132097) and company incorporated in 2009, chaired in 2019 by Theresa Sackler, that has given to research, education and arts charities since 2010.
sacklertrust.money: The Sackler family, whose fortune derives in part from sales of the opioid OxyContin by Purdue Pharma.
sacklertrust.arts: It has committed over £60 million across science, education, arts and heritage; in March 2019 it paused all new giving.

safraeach.what: A private foundation set up by the banker Edmond J. Safra, who died in 1999, and led by his widow Lily Safra for more than twenty years; registered in Geneva.
safraeach.money: An endowment from Edmond J. Safra's banking fortune; he founded Republic National Bank of New York and sold his holdings to HSBC in 1999.
safraeach.arts: Its arts grants have gone to the Courtauld Institute of Art, the National Gallery of Art in Washington, the Israel Philharmonic Orchestra and the Grand Théâtre de Genève.

sainsbury.money: The Sainsbury family's money, and that of its charitable trusts (Linbury, Monument, Gatsby, Glass-House and others), comes from J Sainsbury plc, the supermarket group the family founded.

facts.t: J Sainsbury plc reported retail sales (including VAT, excluding fuel) of £29,992m and underlying profit before tax of £718m for the 52 weeks to 28 February 2026.

saintgobain.money: Saint-Gobain's money comes from making and selling building materials: glass, insulation, plaster and construction chemicals.

facts.t: Compagnie de Saint-Gobain declared EU lobbying costs of €400,000 to €499,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register, with 3.85 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.
Saint-Gobain Corporation paid the outside firm Cozen O'Connor Public Strategies $80,000 for US federal lobbying in 2025 (four quarterly reports of $20,000).

saintgobain20.what: A French building materials multinational, founded in Paris in 1665 as the royal mirror manufactory, listed on Euronext Paris and headquartered at La Défense in Courbevoie.
saintgobain20.money: Production and sale of construction materials, glass, ceramics, plastics, abrasives and plasterboard, with revenue of 47.94 billion euros in 2023.

salonedelmobilemilano.what: The Milan furniture fair, launched in 1961 and organised by Federlegno Arredo Eventi S.p.A., a company wholly owned by FederlegnoArredo, the Italian wood and furniture trade federation.
salonedelmobilemilano.money: The annual fair at Fiera Milano in Rho, which sells stands to exhibitors and tickets to visitors.

samsung.money: Samsung’s money comes from the Samsung group’s businesses, above all Samsung Electronics’ chips, phones and displays, and from the Lee family that controls it.

facts.t: Samsung Electronics reported 2025 revenue of KRW 333.6 trillion and operating profit of KRW 43.6 trillion.
In July 2008 a Seoul court found Samsung chairman Lee Kun-hee guilty of tax evasion and gave him a suspended three-year prison sentence.
Lee Kun-hee was pardoned by President Lee Myung-bak in December 2009.
Lee Jae-yong, convicted of bribery and embezzlement in January 2021 and paroled in August 2021 after 18 months in prison, received a presidential pardon in August 2022.

sanfranciscoartscommission|United States.what: The arts agency of the City of San Francisco, established in 1932 as the San Francisco Art Commission, with fifteen commissioners appointed by the Mayor.
sanfranciscoartscommission|United States.money: The city's hotel tax under Proposition E, $13.09 million of its $23.02 million operating budget in fiscal 2026, and the General Fund.
sanfranciscoartscommission|United States.arts: Hotel-tax money pays for its Community Investments grant programmes, budgeted at $13.79 million in fiscal 2026.

sansebastincity|Spain.what: The city council of San Sebastián in the Basque Country, seated since 1945 in the former casino by La Concha bay and led by mayor Jon Insausti of the PNV.
sansebastincity|Spain.money: The municipal budget, about €517 million for 2025 and the first above €500 million, approved in December 2024.

santander.money: Banco Santander's money comes from retail and commercial banking in Europe and the Americas; the Botín family's Fundación Botín, which runs Centro Botín, draws its budget from the dividends on its Santander shares.

facts.t: Banco Santander reported record attributable profit of €14.101 billion for 2025, up 12%.

In December 2022 the UK Financial Conduct Authority fined Santander UK £107,793,300 for serious and persistent gaps in its anti-money laundering controls over its business banking customers between 2012 and 2017.
Banking on Climate Chaos 2026 reports that Santander almost doubled its fossil debt commitments in 2025 compared with 2021, while diluting its 2030 emissions targets and exclusion policies.
Banco Santander, S.A. declared EU lobbying costs of €800,000 to €899,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.
Santander Holdings USA reported $700,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

sanyoshimbun.what: The publisher of the Sanyo Shimbun, a Japanese daily newspaper based in Okayama and founded on 4 January 1879.
sanyoshimbun.money: Newspaper sales across Okayama prefecture, eastern Hiroshima and parts of Kagawa, with a morning circulation of 438,200, plus a shareholding in TV Setouchi.

sarahshawanschutz.what: A private grantmaking foundation in Denver, tax exempt since April 2022, whose president Sarah S. Anschutz has chaired the Denver Art Museum board since March 2023.
sarahshawanschutz.money: Contributions received each year and paid out in full as grants: $290,000 in the year to November 2024.

sarofim.what: A private foundation in Houston, Texas, tax-exempt since 1971; in 2023 its assets moved to a successor of the same name, with Christopher B. Sarofim a director.
sarofim.money: Gifts, with the investor Fayez Sarofim its named substantial contributor: USD 360.5 million in the year to June 2025; net assets USD 3.14 billion.

sasktel.what: A telecommunications Crown corporation owned by the Government of Saskatchewan, founded in 1908 and based in Regina.
sasktel.money: Phone, wireless and internet services, with almost C$1.4 billion of annual revenue and C$104.7 million net income for 2025-26.

sber.what: A Russian bank branded Sber since 2020, seated in Moscow, under US and EU sanctions since 2014; the National Wealth Fund holds 50 percent plus one share.
sber.money: Banking profits: net income of RUB 1.71 trillion in 2025.

sberbank.money: Sberbank’s money comes from banking: it is Russia’s largest bank and majority-owned by the Russian government.

facts.t: On 24 February 2022 the US Treasury made Sberbank, Russia’s largest financial institution, subject to its correspondent and payable-through account directive.

On 6 April 2022 the US Treasury imposed full blocking sanctions on Sberbank and 42 subsidiaries, describing it as majority-owned by the Russian government and holding about a third of all bank assets in Russia.

scfdsalestax.what: A special tax district of the State of Colorado covering seven counties in the Denver area, created by voters in 1988 to fund scientific and cultural organisations.
scfdsalestax.money: A 0.1% sales and use tax, one penny on every $10 spent in the district.
scfdsalestax.arts: It distributes more than $80 million a year to nearly 300 organisations.

schering.what: An independent non-profit foundation in Berlin, established in 2002 by Schering AG, a Berlin company since absorbed into Bayer AG.
schering.money: An endowment of 35 million euros from Schering AG, and the foundation is financed almost entirely by income from these assets.
schering.arts: It runs its own project space for contemporary art and gives the Art Awards of the Schering Stiftung.

schlumberger.money: The de Menil money comes from the Schlumberger family's oilfield services company, now SLB, founded by Conrad and Marcel Schlumberger; SLB also gives as a company.

facts.t: SLB reported full-year 2025 revenue of $35.71 billion, down 2% year on year.

In March 2015 Schlumberger Oilfield Holdings agreed to plead guilty and pay more than $232.7 million for conspiring to violate US sanctions by facilitating illegal transactions and trade with Iran and Sudan.

schoolofartsghent.what: The school of arts of HOGENT, a university college in Ghent; its Royal Academy of Fine Arts dates from 1748 and joined Hogeschool Gent in the 1995 merger.
schoolofartsghent.money: The budget of HOGENT, an autonomous university college with about 19,500 students in 2025-2026.

schroders.what: A British asset manager founded in London in 1804 by Johann Heinrich Schröder, once listed on the London Stock Exchange and owned since October 2026 by the American firm Nuveen.
schroders.money: Asset management for clients worldwide, with revenue of £3,250.7 million and £823.7 billion under management in 2025.

schwartzmedia.what: A Melbourne news publisher, part of the Schwartz publishing group founded by the property developer Morry Schwartz, which publishes The Saturday Paper and The Monthly.
schwartzmedia.money: Subscriptions and advertising for its weekly newspaper, monthly magazine and foreign affairs journal.

scotiabank.money: Scotiabank’s money comes from banking in Canada and Latin America, wealth management and capital markets.

facts.t: Scotiabank reported net income of $7,758 million for fiscal 2025, against $7,892 million; adjusted net income was $9,510 million.

In August 2020 the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission ordered The Bank of Nova Scotia to pay $127.4 million for spoofing, false statements, and compliance and supervision violations in precious metals futures.

scottishgovernmentenvironmentdirectorate.what: A directorate of the Scottish Government in Edinburgh, responsible for environment and forestry policy, that sponsors the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, a non-departmental public body.
scottishgovernmentenvironmentdirectorate.money: The Scottish Government's budget, paid to the garden as grant-in-aid.

scottishgovernmentgrantinaid|UK.what: The devolved government of Scotland, established in 1999 and based at St Andrew's House in Edinburgh.
scottishgovernmentgrantinaid|UK.money: The Scottish budget, £67.9 billion for 2026-27, funded mainly by the Scottish block grant and devolved taxes.
scottishgovernmentgrantinaid|UK.arts: Its culture and heritage budget for 2025 to 2026 is £348.2 million.

sdworx.what: A Belgian payroll and human resources services company headquartered in Antwerp, active since 1945, which began as the social secretariat of the Flemish employers' federation VEV.
sdworx.money: Payroll and HR software and services for employers, with consolidated revenue of 1.307 billion euros in 2025.

secretaradeculturadelanacin.what: Argentina's national secretariat of culture, which reports to the Presidency and took the place of the Ministry of Culture in 2023, based in Buenos Aires.
secretaradeculturadelanacin.arts: It oversees national bodies such as the Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes.

segerstromrealestatefamily.what: A California family descended from Carl Segerstrom, a Swedish immigrant who bought a lima bean farm in 1900; its Costa Mesa firm is C. J. Segerstrom & Sons.
segerstromrealestatefamily.money: The family's real estate firm C. J. Segerstrom & Sons, developer of South Coast Plaza.

selasarsunaryo.what: The foundation that directs and supports Selasar Sunaryo Art Space, a non-profit art space in Bandung founded in 1998 by the artist Sunaryo.

senatedepartmentforculture|Germany.what: The culture ministry of the State of Berlin, one of ten departments of the Berlin Senate, headed by Senator Stefan Evers.
senatedepartmentforculture|Germany.money: The budget of the State of Berlin.
senatedepartmentforculture|Germany.arts: It funds culture with about 850 million euros a year (2026), about 90% of it for some 100 permanently funded institutions.

seplat.money: Seplat’s money comes from oil and gas production in Nigeria, onshore and offshore.

facts.t: Seplat Energy’s revenue rose 144.2% to $2,726 million in 2025, reflecting a full year of offshore assets.

serbiasministryofculture|Serbia.what: Serbia's government ministry for culture and media regulation, established in 1991 and based in Belgrade; Nikola Selaković has been minister since 2 May 2024.

servicionacionaldelpatrimoniocultural.what: The Chilean public service for libraries, archives, museums and heritage under the Ministry of Cultures, Arts and Heritage, which replaced DIBAM (founded 1929) under Law 21.045 in 2018.
servicionacionaldelpatrimoniocultural.money: The Chilean state budget, through the Ministry of Cultures, Arts and Heritage.

sesolicitors.what: A law firm in Banbury, Oxfordshire, that trades as SE-Solicitors and was registered as a private limited company in 2012.
sesolicitors.money: Fees for legal advice to businesses and individuals.

sevenwestmedia.what: A Western Australian television and newspaper company, owner of the Seven Network and The West Australian, merged with Southern Cross Media Group in January 2026 to form Seven Media Group.
sevenwestmedia.money: Broadcast television, newspaper publishing and digital media, with revenue of $1.4 billion in 2024/25.

sheffieldcitycouncil|United Kingdom.what: The local authority for the City of Sheffield, a metropolitan borough in South Yorkshire, with 84 councillors elected in 28 wards.
sheffieldcitycouncil|United Kingdom.money: Council Tax (£301.3 million), business rates and related grants (£205.2 million) and Revenue Support Grant (£47.6 million) financed its £563.8 million budget for 2025/26.
sheffieldcitycouncil|United Kingdom.arts: Its Economy, Culture and Skills service had a net budget of £8.754 million in 2025/26.

shell.money: Shell’s money comes from producing, processing and selling oil and gas, including liquefied natural gas.

facts.t: Shell posted adjusted earnings of $23.72 billion for 2024, against $28.25 billion a year earlier.
Shell declared EU lobbying costs of €4,500,000 to €4,999,999 for 2025, with 13 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.
InfluenceMap gives Shell a C- grade for its climate policy engagement.
Shell agreed a £55 million settlement with the Bodo community in Nigeria over two oil spills in 2008.
Shell USA reported $6,030,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

shellsqgcbusiness.what: A Queensland natural gas producer based in Brisbane, formerly Queensland Gas Company, bought by BG Group in November 2008 and part of Shell since February 2016.
shellsqgcbusiness.money: Coal seam gas from the Surat and Bowen Basins, liquefied at its plant on Curtis Island.

shikokuelectricpower.what: The electric utility for the four prefectures of Shikoku island in Japan, established on 1 May 1951, listed in Tokyo and headquartered in Takamatsu.
shikokuelectricpower.money: Electricity sales from hydro, thermal and nuclear plants, with operating revenue of 761,862 million yen in the year to March 2026.

shiseido.money: Shiseido’s money comes from cosmetics and skincare.

shivnadar.what: A foundation set up in 1994 by Shiv Nadar, founder of the HCL technology group, that runs universities, schools and the Kiran Nadar Museum of Art.
shivnadar.money: Shiv Nadar's fortune from HCL, a US$14.7 billion technology group by the foundation's account; the foundation has invested over US$1.85 billion.

shyllon.money: Yemisi Shyllon gives his own money and collection, through his art foundation; the records do not say how the money was made.

siae.what: Italy's authors' and publishers' collecting society, a non-profit public economic body with a membership base, founded in Milan on 23 April 1882 and based in Rome.
siae.money: Commissions, averaging 13.7 percent in 2025, on the copyright royalties it collects for more than 125,000 member authors and publishers.

siampiwat.what: A privately held retail and property developer in Bangkok, established on 10 January 1959 as Bangkok InterContinental Hotels Company by General Chalermchai Charuwat.
siampiwat.money: Shopping malls in Bangkok, among them Siam Center, Siam Discovery, Siam Paragon and Iconsiam.

sida.what: Sweden's government agency for development cooperation, formed in 1995, which answers to the Ministry for Foreign Affairs and has its headquarters in Sundbyberg.
sida.money: Swedish tax revenue, with an annual budget of 26.5 billion Swedish kronor in 2024.

sidafunded.what: Sweden's government agency for development cooperation, formed in 1995, which answers to the Ministry for Foreign Affairs and has its headquarters in Sundbyberg.
sidafunded.money: Swedish tax revenue, with an annual budget of 26.5 billion Swedish kronor in 2024.

siddharthaarts.what: A non-profit arts foundation in Kathmandu, set up in 2011 by Sangeeta Thapa, founder of Siddhartha Art Gallery, which organises the Kathmandu Triennale.
siddharthaarts.arts: It was co-commissioner of Nepal's first pavilion at the Venice Biennale in 2022.

sidneymyer.what: A perpetual charitable fund created under the will of Melbourne retailer Sidney Myer, who died in 1934, and run by the same team as The Myer Foundation.
sidneymyer.money: The invested share of Sidney Myer's estate, made in the Myer department store business; the income is distributed each year.

siemens.money: Siemens' money comes from industrial automation, software, rail and building technology and, through Siemens Healthineers, medical technology.

facts.t: Siemens reported revenue of €78.9 billion and record net income of €10.4 billion for fiscal 2025, which ended on 30 September 2025.
In December 2008 Siemens AG and three subsidiaries pleaded guilty to Foreign Corrupt Practices Act violations in the US; with the SEC and German authorities, the penalties came to $1.6 billion.
Siemens AG declared EU lobbying costs of €3,500,000 to €3,999,999 for its financial year October 2024 to September 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.

Siemens Corporation, its US arm, reported $3,760,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act; Siemens Healthineers and Siemens Energy file separately and are not counted.

siga.what: A non-profit casino operator owned by Saskatchewan's 74 First Nations, created in June 1995 and incorporated in January 1996, with its office in Saskatoon.
siga.money: Seven casinos and the PlayNow online casino in Saskatchewan, which brought in $378 million in gross revenue in fiscal year 2024-25.

sigridrausingtrust.what: A London grant-making trust for human rights, open societies and the environment, established in 1995 by Sigrid Rausing.
sigridrausingtrust.money: Funds that Sigrid Rausing, granddaughter of Tetra Pak co-founder Ruben Rausing, moved into it from her Sea Foundation in 1996.

simpsongrierson.money: A New Zealand law firm; its money is its partners' fees from legal work.

singaporeairlines.what: The flag carrier of Singapore, founded in 1947 as Malayan Airways, listed in Singapore and 53% owned by Temasek Holdings.
singaporeairlines.money: Passenger and cargo flights, with revenue of SGD 19.01 billion in the year to March 2024.

singaporetourismboard.what: A statutory board under Singapore's Ministry of Trade and Industry, founded in 1964 as the Singapore Tourist Promotion Board and renamed in 1997.
singaporetourismboard.money: Singapore government grants, with operating grants of SGD 268.4 million in the year to March 2025.

sintmartenslatem.what: The municipality of Sint-Martens-Latem in East Flanders, Belgium, made up of Sint-Martens-Latem and Deurle, with about 8,000 inhabitants and a history as a painters' village on the Leie.
sintmartenslatem.money: Local taxes and Flemish government transfers, including the Flemish Gemeentefonds, which gives Belgian municipalities about 20% of their operating resources.
sintmartenslatem.arts: It runs the Gemeentelijk Museum Gust De Smet in Deurle and invited Museum Dhondt-Dhaenens to show its collection there in 2022.

skgroup.money: SK Group’s money comes from energy and refining, telecoms (SK Telecom) and memory chips (SK hynix), under the Chey family.

facts.t: In February 2014 South Korea’s Supreme Court upheld SK Group chairman Chey Tae-won’s four-year prison term for embezzling tens of billions of won from group affiliates.
President Park Geun-hye pardoned Chey Tae-won in August 2015.

sligocountycouncil|Ireland.what: County Sligo's local authority in Ireland: 18 councillors elected for five-year terms by single transferable vote, and a chief executive, Martin Lydon.
sligocountycouncil|Ireland.money: Its 2025 budget of EUR 80.8 million: EUR 52.6 million grants and other income, EUR 15.8 million rates, EUR 12.4 million property tax.

sloan.what: A private grant-making foundation in New York, established in 1934 by Alfred P. Sloan Jr., then president and chief executive of General Motors.
sloan.money: An endowment from Alfred P. Sloan Jr.’s fortune; its assets totalled $2.2 billion in 2024.
sloan.arts: Its Film programme, launched in 1996, has given grants to over 750 film projects on science and technology themes.

sloveniasministryofculture|Slovenia.what: The Slovenian government ministry for culture, based in Ljubljana.
sloveniasministryofculture|Slovenia.arts: It funds artist residencies in Berlin, London, New York and Vienna; its call for 2027 offers up to €100,000.

smiparliamentdirectgrant|Norway.what: The elected assembly of the Sámi people in Norway, with 39 representatives chosen from seven constituencies every four years, opened in Karasjok on 9 October 1989.
smiparliamentdirectgrant|Norway.money: Grants from several lines of the Norwegian state budget, led by the Ministry of Local Government, which the parliament distributes by its own priorities.
smiparliamentdirectgrant|Norway.arts: It has taken over administrative responsibility and policy instruments from the state in language, culture and education.

smithreynolds.what: A private family foundation in Winston-Salem, established in 1936 by the children of R.J. and Katharine Smith Reynolds as a memorial to their brother Zachary Smith Reynolds.
smithreynolds.money: The siblings' shares of Zachary Smith Reynolds's estate, which came from his father R. J. Reynolds, founder of the R. J. Reynolds Tobacco Company.

sobey.what: A Nova Scotia business family whose business, begun in Stellarton in 1907, grew into Sobeys, Canada's second-largest food retailer, under Frank H. Sobey and his sons.
sobey.money: Their holdings in Empire Company, the parent company of Sobeys, where the family's wealth is mainly concentrated.
sobey.arts: Their foundations include the Sobey Art Foundation, set up in 1981, which manages the family art collection and created the Sobey Art Award in 2002, and the D.R. Sobey Foundation.

socgen.money: Société Générale's money comes from retail and investment banking in France and abroad, including BRD in Romania.

facts.t: Société Générale reported record 2025 revenues of EUR 27.3bn and Group net income of EUR 6.0bn, up 43% on 2024.
Banking on Climate Chaos 2026 ranks Société Générale 29th among the world's banks for fossil fuel financing in 2025, a change of +$807 million (+7.7%) from 2024.
Société Générale declared EU lobbying costs of €1,500,000 to €1,749,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register, with 1.85 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.

socitgnrale.what: A French bank founded in 1864, registered in Paris with its headquarters at La Défense.
socitgnrale.money: Universal banking and financial services, with revenue of EUR 27.3 billion in 2025.
socitgnrale.arts: Its corporate foundation, formed in 2021 from its music patronage association and its solidarity foundation, funds classical music and youth education.

sococimcement.money: Sococim’s money comes from making cement in Senegal; it is owned by the French group Vicat.

sofiamunicipalityyearlyacquisitions.what: The municipality of Bulgaria's capital, covering Sofia and 37 other settlements, with 1,232,905 inhabitants projected for 2025.
sofiamunicipalityyearlyacquisitions.money: The municipal budget, EUR 1.54 billion for 2026, approved by Sofia's Municipal Council on 24 September 2026.

softwareag.what: An independent charitable foundation in Darmstadt set up by Peter Schnell, who founded the software company Software AG in 1969.
softwareag.money: Returns on assets of EUR 1.3 billion, which began with the Software AG shares Schnell transferred to it in 1992.

soichirofukutakes.what: A Japanese foundation that runs Benesse Art Site Naoshima with Benesse Corporation, grown from a foundation Soichiro Fukutake set up in 2004.
soichirofukutakes.money: A personal endowment from Soichiro Fukutake, former head of Benesse, the Okayama correspondence education and publishing company.
soichirofukutakes.arts: It has been a founding patron of CIMAM, the international committee for modern art museums, since 2000.

solidarsuiza.what: A Swiss development organisation in Zurich, an association that grew out of Schweizerisches Arbeiterhilfswerk, founded in 1936 by the trade union federation and the Social Democratic Party.
solidarsuiza.money: Of CHF 25.3 million income in 2025, Glückskette gave 25.8%, the Swiss federal government 19.3%, foreign states 17.1% and donors 16.8%.

solomonr.what: A nonprofit foundation in New York founded in 1937 by Solomon R. Guggenheim and the artist Hilla von Rebay, which runs the Guggenheim museums.
solomonr.money: Revenue of USD 82.6 million in 2023, including USD 34.2 million of programme revenue and USD 27.1 million in contributions.

sony.what: A Japanese conglomerate founded in 1946 as Tokyo Tsushin Kogyo by Masaru Ibuka and Akio Morita, with headquarters in Minato, Tokyo.
sony.money: Video games, music, film, electronics, semiconductors and financial services, with revenue of JPY 12.48 trillion in the year to March 2026.

sonypictures.money: Sony Pictures Entertainment’s money comes from making and selling films and television; it is owned by Sony Group of Japan.

facts.t: Sony Pictures Entertainment reported $735,042 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.
One outside firm, the Smith-Free Group, reported $320,000 in 2025 fees from Sony Pictures Entertainment for US federal lobbying, under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.
Sony Pictures Entertainment’s PAC gave $27,000 to federal candidates in the 2023 to 2024 cycle, 39% to Republicans and 61% to Democrats, in its reports to the Federal Election Commission.

soudal.what: A Belgian family company in Turnhout that makes sealants, polyurethane foam and adhesives, founded by Vic Swerts in 1966.
soudal.money: Sales of sealants, foams and adhesives in more than 140 countries, with turnover of EUR 1.46 billion in 2024.

south32.money: South32 is a Perth miner of aluminium, alumina, manganese, zinc, silver and other metals.

facts.t: South32 reported underlying revenue of US$7,610 million and underlying earnings of US$666 million for the year to 30 June 2025.

southaustraliangovernment|Australia.what: South Australia's state government, led by Premier Peter Malinauskas from the State Administration Centre in Adelaide, set up as a responsible colonial government on 22 April 1857.
southaustraliangovernment|Australia.money: The state budget of South Australia: AUD 27.5 billion in 2023-24.
southaustraliangovernment|Australia.arts: In July 2024 it committed AUD 780,000 to repair the Tandanya building in Adelaide, home of the National Aboriginal Cultural Institute.

southbankcentretrust.what: A registered charity that runs the Southbank Centre arts complex in London, with the Royal Festival Hall, Queen Elizabeth Hall, Purcell Room and Hayward Gallery.
southbankcentretrust.money: Income of GBP 58.3 million in the year to March 2025, of which GBP 22.6 million was trading and GBP 18.3 million government grants.

southlakelandcouncilpersite|UK.what: The unitary local authority for Westmorland and Furness in Cumbria, England, created on 1 April 2023 from the former districts of Barrow-in-Furness, Eden and South Lakeland.
southlakelandcouncilpersite|UK.money: Council Tax, £194.072 million of its £301.124 million net budget for 2026 to 2027, with government revenue support grant and retained business rates.

southwarkcouncil|UK.what: The local authority for the London Borough of Southwark, based at 160 Tooley Street.
southwarkcouncil|UK.money: Its net budget for services is GBP 432.4 million for 2026 to 2027, of which council tax funds GBP 162.4 million.
southwarkcouncil|UK.arts: Its Culture Together Grants Fund offers up to GBP 144,000 per round to arts and culture organisations based in the borough.

spanishministryofculture|Spain.what: The Government of Spain's department for heritage, national museums, archives, libraries, books and film, headed by Minister Ernest Urtasun and based in Madrid.
spanishministryofculture|Spain.money: The Spanish state budget; its annual budget is €1.15 billion for 2026.

sparebank1nordnorge.what: A savings bank with its head office in Tromsø whose oldest forerunner, Tromsø Sparebank, was founded in 1836.
sparebank1nordnorge.money: Banking in northern Norway, where the 53.6% of the bank owned by the community pays its dividend into the Samfunnsløftet fund.
sparebank1nordnorge.arts: Samfunnsløftet allocated NOK 276 million in 2024 from the NOK 813 million community dividend for 2023.

sparebank1nordnorgessamfunnslftet.what: A savings bank with its head office in Tromsø whose oldest forerunner, Tromsø Sparebank, was founded in 1836.
sparebank1nordnorgessamfunnslftet.money: Banking in northern Norway, where the 53.6% of the bank owned by the community pays its dividend into the Samfunnsløftet fund.
sparebank1nordnorgessamfunnslftet.arts: Samfunnsløftet allocated NOK 276 million in 2024 from the NOK 813 million community dividend for 2023.

sparebankenvest.what: A Norwegian savings bank group created on 2 May 2025 by the merger of Sparebanken Vest and Sparebanken Sør, with head offices in Bergen and Kristiansand.
sparebankenvest.money: Its banking business; the two merged banks had 517 billion kroner in assets under management in 2024.
sparebankenvest.arts: It shares its profit with customers and local communities, with NOK 1.5 billion set for public-benefit causes in 2026.

sparebankstiftelsendnb.what: A Norwegian foundation set up in 2002 when Sparebanken NOR became a share company, tracing to Christiania Sparebank of 1822, based in Oslo.
sparebankstiftelsendnb.money: Dividends on its stake of about 8.9% in DNB.
sparebankstiftelsendnb.arts: It buys art shown in Norwegian museums and lends instruments to musicians from a collection begun in 2006.

sparkassebielefeld.what: A public savings bank in Bielefeld owned by the city, whose first forerunner was founded in 1825.
sparkassebielefeld.money: Banking in Bielefeld and the neighbouring districts, with total assets of EUR 7.816 billion in 2025.

sparkassebremen.what: An independent savings bank founded by Bremen citizens in 1825, run as a stock corporation owned by the Finanzholding der Sparkasse in Bremen, whose about 750 members represent Bremen's citizens.
sparkassebremen.money: Banking income from private and business customers, with total assets of more than 15 billion euros.

sparkasseessen.what: A public-law savings bank (Anstalt des öffentlichen Rechts) founded in 1841, whose business area is the city of Essen.
sparkasseessen.money: Lending, deposits and banking fees; its balance sheet total was EUR 10.339 billion in 2025.
sparkasseessen.arts: Among its five foundations is a Philharmonie-Stiftung, set up in 2004.

sparknz.money: Spark, formerly Telecom New Zealand, sells mobile, broadband and IT services; the Spark Foundation is its charity.

facts.t: Spark reported net profit of $260 million on revenue of $3.771 billion for the 12 months to June 2025.
Spark New Zealand Trading was fined $675,000 for false or misleading representations to consumers.

srp.what: A not-for-profit Arizona utility run by the Salt River Valley Water Users' Association, formed in 1903, and the Salt River Project Agricultural Improvement and Power District.
srp.money: Electricity and water bills from more than 2 million people, including more than 1.2 million electric customers in central Arizona.

stadsdeeloost.what: One of Amsterdam's city districts, covering areas such as Oud-Oost and the Indische Buurt, run by a three-member district board acting for the city's executive.
stadsdeeloost.money: Budgets set in the Amsterdam municipal budget, which the district board allocates to its tasks.

stadtwerkedsseldorfaspermanentpartner.what: A Düsseldorf utility company owned 54.95 percent by EnBW, 25.05 percent by the city's holding company and 20 percent by GEW Köln.
stadtwerkedsseldorfaspermanentpartner.money: Supply of electricity, natural gas, heat and drinking water: revenue of 2,516 million euros in 2025, net of electricity and energy tax.

stadtwerkeessen.what: Essen's municipal utility, formed in 1867 from the city's gas and water works; the city holding EVV owns 51 percent, Westenergie 29 percent and Thüga 20 percent.
stadtwerkeessen.money: Sales of gas, heat, power, drinking water and wastewater services in Essen: EUR 553.94 million revenue in 2023.

stadtwien|Austria.what: The city government of Vienna, run through the Magistrat under Mayor Michael Ludwig, in office since 2018; its culture department is MA 7.
stadtwien|Austria.money: The city budget: the 2026 estimate has revenue of €19.51 billion and spending of €22.14 billion.
stadtwien|Austria.arts: Its 2026 culture budget is €353.7 million, up from €348.8 million only because adult education centres were added; without them it is €322.3 million, a 7.6 percent cut.

standardbank.money: Standard Bank’s money comes from banking and insurance, in South Africa and across the rest of Africa.

facts.t: Standard Bank Group reported headline earnings of R44 503 million for 2024, up 4%.

In November 2015 Standard Bank Plc entered the UK’s first deferred prosecution agreement, paying $25.2 million and $7 million in compensation to Tanzania, over a $6 million payment in 2013 by its former sister company Stanbic Bank Tanzania.
In March 2025 Standard Bank and Uganda’s Stanbic Bank were named among the lenders of the first external financing for the East African Crude Oil Pipeline, majority-controlled by TotalEnergies.

standardbankhasbeencollection.what: A South African banking group founded in 1862, listed in Johannesburg, where it has its headquarters.
standardbankhasbeencollection.money: Banking in 21 sub-Saharan African countries, as Africa's largest lender by assets with ZAR 3.8 trillion in 2026.
standardbankhasbeencollection.arts: It sponsors the National Arts Festival, the Standard Bank Young Artist Awards and the Joy of Jazz festival, and runs its own art gallery.

stanleythomasjohnson.what: A Bern foundation set up in 1969 under the will of June Mary Johnson, who left it the whole estate of her late husband, the British industrialist Stanley Thomas Johnson.
stanleythomasjohnson.money: Its endowment, invested in shares, Swiss property and bonds: CHF 192.1 million in 2025.
stanleythomasjohnson.arts: It funds performing and visual arts, humanitarian aid, medical research and education in the canton of Bern; grants totalled CHF 4.38 million in 2025.

statenskunstfond.what: Denmark's state arts foundation, set up by law on 27 May 1964 and merged with the Danish Arts Council in 2014, administered by a Ministry of Culture agency.
statenskunstfond.money: Danish state funds allocated by the culture ministry.
statenskunstfond.arts: Its 16 expert committees award grants to more than 6,400 artists and art projects a year from about 15,700 applications.

stateofbadenwrttembergministryofscience|.what: The Baden-Württemberg state ministry for universities, research and the arts, set up in 1978 in Stuttgart; Petra Olschowski has been minister since 28 September 2022.
stateofbadenwrttembergministryofscience|.money: The budget of the State of Baden-Württemberg; the ministry's budget was about €5.74 billion in 2021.
stateofbadenwrttembergministryofscience|.arts: It is responsible for the state's universities, university hospitals and many research bodies, and for arts institutions of Baden-Württemberg.

stateofbadenwrttemberg|Germany.what: The government of the German federal state of Baden-Württemberg, founded on 25 April 1952, with its Staatsministerium (state chancellery) in Stuttgart.
stateofbadenwrttemberg|Germany.money: The state budget set by the Landtag; the draft for 2025 and 2026 planned just over EUR 136 billion of spending in total.
stateofbadenwrttemberg|Germany.arts: Its arts funding runs through the Ministry of Science, Research and the Arts (Ministerium für Wissenschaft, Forschung und Kunst).

stateofflorida|USA.what: The government of the US state of Florida, seated in Tallahassee, the capital since 1823, with Governor Ron DeSantis at the head of the executive.

stateoflowersaxony|Germany.what: The science and culture ministry of the German state of Lower Saxony in Hanover, led since 8 November 2022 by Minister Falko Mohrs.
stateoflowersaxony|Germany.money: The state budget of Lower Saxony.

stateofsopaulo|Brazil.what: The executive government of the Brazilian state of São Paulo, headed by governor Tarcísio Gomes de Freitas and seated at the Palácio dos Bandeirantes since 1964.
stateofsopaulo|Brazil.money: The state budget: the Legislative Assembly approved total revenue of R$ 382.3 billion for 2026 on 16 December 2025.
stateofsopaulo|Brazil.arts: Its culture arm is the Secretaria da Cultura, Economia e Indústria Criativas.

stavangerkommune|Norway.what: The municipality of Stavanger, Norway's fourth most populous and the administrative centre of Rogaland county, which counts 1125 as its founding year.

stavrosniarchos.what: A philanthropic foundation set up in 1996 after the death of Greek shipping magnate Stavros Niarchos, with offices in Athens, New York and Monaco.
stavrosniarchos.money: An endowment from Stavros Niarchos's shipping fortune; for many years he owned the world's largest private fleet, over 80 tankers and other vessels.
stavrosniarchos.arts: Arts and culture is one of its four grant priorities; since 1996 it has committed nearly $4 billion to grantees in 138 countries.

steeltube.money: Steel & Tube, listed on the NZX, makes and distributes steel products in New Zealand.

facts.t: Steel & Tube reported a net loss of $24.4 million on revenue of $385.4 million for the 12 months to June 2025.

stevetisch.what: An American film producer born in 1949, partner in the production company Escape Artists and chairman of the New York Giants, which he co-owned from 2005 to March 2026.
stevetisch.money: His film production work and the Tisch family's co-ownership of the New York Giants football team.

stichtingdoen.what: A Dutch foundation set up in 1991 by the Postcode Loterij that funds pioneers in the Netherlands and abroad.
stichtingdoen.money: Lottery proceeds: 24,303,520 euros from the Postcode Loterij and 7,200,000 euros from the VriendenLoterij in 2025.
stichtingdoen.arts: Its VriendenLoterij Fonds funded 70 art and culture projects in 2025.

stichtingjohanmauritsvannassau.what: A foundation set up in 1957 to support the Mauritshuis in The Hague; it has bought paintings and lent them to the museum long term.
stichtingjohanmauritsvannassau.money: It merged in 1986 with the Stichting Vrienden van het Mauritshuis, a fundraising foundation set up in 1982.

stillwater.what: A private family foundation in Austin, Texas, established in 1982 by Julia "Jill" Matthews Wilkinson, a granddaughter of Dodge Jones Foundation founder Ruth Jones.
stillwater.money: Money from the Jones and Matthews family behind the Dodge Jones Foundation, with assets of USD 151.3 million at the end of 2023.
stillwater.arts: In 2020 it gave USD 5 million to the Blanton Museum of Art and USD 5 million to Landmarks, the University of Texas at Austin's public art programme.

stockland.money: Stockland is a Sydney property developer and owner of shopping centres, housing estates and logistics property.

stockmann.what: A Finnish department store chain founded in Helsinki in 1862, now a division of Lindex Group plc, the listed company called Stockmann plc until March 2024.
stockmann.money: Department store sales in Finland, Estonia and Latvia, inside a group with revenue of EUR 952.3 million in 2025.

stonehagefleming.what: A family office firm based in Jersey, formed in 2014 when Stonehage merged with Fleming Family & Partners, and owned by the wealth manager Corient since June 2026.
stonehagefleming.money: Fees for advisory, fiduciary and investment management services to wealthy families.

storenorske.money: Store Norske’s money came from coal mining on Svalbard; the Norwegian state has owned all of it since 2015.

stouttrust.money: A trust set up after the death in 1982 of the Wellington scientist Dr John Stout to promote New Zealand's cultural and environmental heritage, later enlarged from the estate of his sister Vida Stout; Perpetual Guardian manages it.

stpetersburgcommitteeforculture.what: The executive body of the St Petersburg city government for cultural policy, covering art, cinema and art and music education, chaired by Fyodor Boltin since December 2021.
stpetersburgcommitteeforculture.money: The budget of the city of St Petersburg.

stpetersburgcommitteeforsocialpolicy.what: The executive body of the St Petersburg city government for social support and social services; in 2021 it served 3 million residents in 85 categories.
stpetersburgcommitteeforsocialpolicy.money: The budget of the city of St Petersburg.

strabagmainsponsorofneststage.what: An Austrian construction group listed on the Vienna stock exchange, with headquarters in Vienna and roots in a firm founded in 1835.
strabagmainsponsorofneststage.money: Construction work in Austria, Germany and central and eastern Europe, with revenue of EUR 17,422 million in 2024.

suffolkcounty|USA.what: The county government of Suffolk County, New York, the eastern two-thirds of Long Island, with its seat in Riverhead, main offices in Hauppauge and Edward P. Romaine as County Executive.

sulger.what: A charitable foundation in Basel, entered in the commercial register in 2015, that supports charitable, cultural and educational causes in Basel and neighbouring parts of Switzerland.

suna.what: A private foundation in Istanbul established on 27 October 2003 by Suna Kıraç, İnan Kıraç and İpek Kıraç for education, health, culture and art.
suna.money: The wealth of the Kıraç family, whose co-founder Suna Kıraç was a daughter of Vehbi Koç and vice president of Koç Holding.
suna.arts: It founded the Pera Museum in 2005 and runs the Istanbul Research Institute.

suncor.money: Suncor’s money comes from Alberta oil sands mining and upgrading, refining and its Petro-Canada fuel stations.

facts.t: Suncor reported fourth-quarter 2025 net earnings of $1.476 billion, and $12.8 billion of adjusted funds from operations for the year.
Suncor was fined $495,000 after pleading guilty to one count under Alberta’s Occupational Health and Safety Code over a 2022 worker’s death at its Base Mine.
InfluenceMap gives Suncor Energy a D- grade for its climate policy engagement.
Suncor Energy (U.S.A.) filed no 2025 federal lobbying reports of its own; its outside firm reported $60,000 in fees under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

suntory.money: Suntory’s money comes from beer, spirits (Beam Suntory, now Suntory Global Spirits) and soft drinks.

sura.money: Grupo SURA’s money comes from insurance, pensions and asset management in Latin America, and from its holdings in other companies.

facts.t: Grupo SURA’s profit grew 294.5% in 2024 to COP 6.1 trillion (6,1 billones), on revenues of COP 37.2 trillion.

svyturys.what: A Lithuanian brewing company formed in 2001 from the Švyturys brewery in Klaipėda, founded in 1784, and the Utenos brewery, founded in 1977, and owned by the Carlsberg Group.
svyturys.money: Sales of beer and other drinks in Lithuania, where Carlsberg puts its share of the beer market at 41%.

swarovski.money: Swarovski's money comes from cut crystal, jewellery and accessories, a family-owned business based in Wattens, Austria.

facts.t: Swarovski reported revenue of 1.97 billion euros for 2025, with 6 percent organic growth.

swedishartscouncil|Sweden.what: A Swedish government agency under the Ministry of Culture that distributes state cultural grants, based at Filmhuset in Stockholm.
swedishartscouncil|Sweden.money: Appropriations from the Swedish state budget, set each year in the government's regleringsbrev.

swedishstate|Sweden.what: The national cabinet of Sweden, made up of the prime minister and cabinet ministers, responsible to the Riksdag, with its seat at Rosenbad in Stockholm.

swire.money: The Swire Charitable Trust's money comes from John Swire & Sons, the Swire family's trading group.

facts.t: John Swire & Sons gave the Swire Charitable Trust £5,000,000 without conditions in 2023 and paid £948,639 of its expenses; the trust gave £5,958,442 in grants that year.
Ballard Partners reported $80,000 in 2025 fees from Swire Properties, Inc. for US federal lobbying, under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

swissagencyfordevelopment|Tanzania.what: The Swiss government's agency for development cooperation and humanitarian aid, part of the Federal Department of Foreign Affairs, based in Bern.
swissagencyfordevelopment|Tanzania.money: The Swiss federal budget, with a total aid budget of CHF 2.16 billion in 2024.
swissagencyfordevelopment|Tanzania.arts: Its offices abroad can spend up to 1% of their aid budget on local culture, and it gave Swiss cultural partners CHF 3.7 million in 2024.

swisslife.what: Switzerland's largest life insurance group, founded in Zurich in 1857 as the Schweizerische Lebensversicherungs und Rentenanstalt and named Swiss Life since 2002.
swisslife.money: Life insurance, pensions and asset management, with CHF 356.3 billion under management; net profit of CHF 1.26 billion in 2025.

swisssdc.what: The Swiss government's agency for development cooperation and humanitarian aid, part of the Federal Department of Foreign Affairs, based in Bern.
swisssdc.money: The Swiss federal budget, with a total aid budget of CHF 2.16 billion in 2024.
swisssdc.arts: Its offices abroad can spend up to 1% of their aid budget on local culture, and it gave Swiss cultural partners CHF 3.7 million in 2024.

szerencsejtkzrt.what: Hungary's national lottery and betting company, based in Budapest, wholly owned by the Hungarian state and operating since 1 January 1991, with the Finance Ministry exercising the owner's rights.
szerencsejtkzrt.money: Sales of lottery draws, scratch cards and sports bets at about 7,000 outlets, with revenue of 978 billion forints in 2023.
szerencsejtkzrt.arts: It returns about two thirds of its net gaming revenue to the state budget in taxes, fees and dividends, and names culture among the fields it supports.

taike.what: Finland's arts promotion agency under the Ministry of Education and Culture, which started work in 2013 and merged with KAVI into the Finnish Arts and Culture Agency in January 2026.
taike.arts: It awarded grants to professional artists and subsidies to arts communities of about EUR 40 million a year (2022), work the new agency continues.

tainancitysubsidynt|Taiwan.what: The municipal government of Tainan, Taiwan, formed on 25 December 2010 when Tainan City and Tainan County merged, and led by a directly elected mayor.
tainancitysubsidynt|Taiwan.money: The municipal budget of Tainan City.

taishin.money: Taishin's money comes from banking and insurance, through Taishin Financial Holding.

facts.t: Taishin Shin Kong Financial Holding (stock code 2887, Taishin's holding company) reported a 2025 after-tax net profit of NT$37.4 billion, up 86% and a record.

taiwanfordemocracy.what: A non-profit foundation in Taipei set up in June 2003 on the initiative of Taiwan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs to promote democracy around the world.
taiwanfordemocracy.money: Funding from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of China (Taiwan).

takasagothermalengineering.what: A Tokyo company that builds air conditioning systems, established on 16 November 1923 as Takasago Heating Works and listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Prime section.
takasagothermalengineering.money: Construction of air conditioning equipment, its main business, with consolidated net sales of 423,923 million yen in the year to 31 March 2026.

takenaka.money: Takenaka’s money comes from building construction, as a privately held general contractor.

talanx.what: A German insurance group based in Hannover, headed since 1996 by the holding company Talanx AG, whose majority shareholder is the mutual insurer HDI V.a.G.
talanx.money: Insurance and reinsurance premiums under brands including HDI and Hannover Re, with insurance revenue of EUR 48,994 million in 2025.

tamayo.what: A Mexican civil association formalised on 31 October 1989 by the painter Rufino Tamayo and his wife Olga to study and show international contemporary art.
tamayo.money: Contributions from its members; with the Board of Trustees and the Círculo Contemporáneo it is one of the benefactor circles that support the Museo Tamayo.

tanmiacharity.what: A Kuwaiti charity licensed by ministerial decision 125/A of 2016 that funds relief and community development projects in poor communities in Kuwait and abroad.
tanmiacharity.money: Waqf endowments, zakat funds and public fundraising campaigns.

tanotofamily.what: The family of Sukanto Tanoto, an Indonesian businessman born in 1949 who owns the Royal Golden Eagle group; he settled in Singapore in 1997 and based the group there.
tanotofamily.money: Royal Golden Eagle, a resources group in paper, palm oil, viscose and energy with assets above US$40 billion.

tata.money: Tata’s money comes from the Tata companies, among them TCS, Tata Steel and Tata Motors; 66% of the holding company Tata Sons is owned by the Tata Trusts.

facts.t: In 2024-25 the aggregate revenue of Tata companies was more than $180 billion.
In November 2023 the US Supreme Court declined to hear Tata Consultancy Services’ appeal against $140 million in punitive damages owed to Epic Systems in a trade secrets case.
Tata America International Corporation, TCS’s US arm, reported $540,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025 in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.
Tata Steel Nederland declared EU lobbying costs of €200,000 to €299,999 for the financial year April 2025 to March 2026, with 1.6 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.

tavairports.what: A Turkish airport operator founded in 1997 and listed on the Istanbul stock exchange, running 15 airports in eight countries, with Groupe ADP of France holding 46 percent.
tavairports.money: Airport operation plus duty free, food and drink, ground handling, IT and security services, with 113 million passengers at its airports in 2025.

tavitian.what: A private foundation set up in 1995 by the entrepreneur and art collector Aso O. Tavitian, who died in 2020, with its office on Fifth Avenue in New York.
tavitian.money: His fortune from Syncsort, the software company he co-founded in 1969 and led as majority shareholder, with assets of $40.6 million in 2023.
tavitian.arts: It funds education and peace work, particularly in Armenia, and the arts.

tdbank.money: TD Bank Group’s money comes from retail and commercial banking in Canada and the eastern United States, wealth management, insurance and capital markets.

facts.t: TD Bank Group reported net income of $20,538 million for fiscal 2025, against $8,842 million the year before; adjusted net income was $15,025 million.

On 10 October 2024 TD Bank N.A. pleaded guilty to conspiring to fail to maintain an anti-money laundering programme, fail to file accurate currency transaction reports and launder monetary instruments; TD Bank agreed to pay a combined $1.8 billion in penalties to the Department of Justice and retain an independent monitor.
TD Bank N.A. reported $1,750,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

teck.money: Teck’s money comes from mining copper and zinc; it sold its steelmaking coal business in 2024.

facts.t: Teck reported fourth-quarter 2025 revenue of $3,058 million and profit from continuing operations attributable to shareholders of $544 million.
In March 2021 Teck Coal was fined $60 million for releases of selenium and calcite from its Elk Valley coal mines, the largest penalty ever handed down under the federal Fisheries Act.
Teck filed no 2025 federal lobbying reports of its own; outside firms reported $330,000 in fees from Teck Resources and Teck American under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

teiger.what: A private foundation in New York, founded in 2008 by the contemporary art collector David Teiger (1929 to 2014), that funds curators' projects.
teiger.money: An endowment from the auction of most of David Teiger's art collection, which he left to the foundation at his death in 2014.
teiger.arts: It gave US$8.0 million in the year to June 2025, holding US$159.5 million in assets, and plans at least US$5 million a year for curatorial work.

teijin.what: A Japanese company established on 17 June 1918 that began with Japan's first rayon production technology, with head offices in Tokyo and Osaka.
teijin.money: Sales of aramid and carbon fibres, resins, composites and healthcare products, with revenue of ¥873.2 billion in the year to March 2026.

telefonica.money: Telefónica's money comes from telecoms: mobile, broadband and pay-TV services in Spain, Germany, the UK and Latin America.

facts.t: In July 2007 the European Commission fined Telefónica €151,875,000 for abusing its dominant position in the Spanish broadband market through a margin squeeze on competitors.
Telefónica, S.A. declared EU lobbying costs of €2,000,000 to €2,249,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register, with 5.5 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.

telstra.what: Australia's largest telecommunications company by market share, which began in the Postmaster-General's Department at federation in 1901 and was privatised in stages between 1997 and 2006, based in Melbourne.
telstra.money: Fixed-line, mobile, internet and data services: revenue of A$23.25 billion in the year to June 2023.
telstra.arts: It sponsors the National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Art Award, known as the Telstra Award.

facts.t: Telstra reported total income, excluding finance income, of $23,610 million and profit of $2,343 million for the year to 30 June 2025.

In its 2024-25 donor return to the Australian Electoral Commission, Telstra Corporation disclosed $35,450 in political donations: $18,150 to Labor branches and $17,300 to Liberal and National branches.

tepco.money: TEPCO’s money comes from generating and selling electricity in the Tokyo region; it operated the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear plant.

facts.t: TEPCO Holdings reported operating revenue of 6,810.3 billion yen for the year to March 2025 and net income of 161.2 billion yen.
In December 2023 Japan’s government raised its estimate of the costs of the Fukushima Daiichi disaster to 23.4 trillion yen, including about 8 trillion yen to decommission the damaged reactors.
In June 2025 the Tokyo High Court overturned a 2022 ruling that had ordered four former TEPCO executives to pay the company 13 trillion yen over the Fukushima disaster.

terra.money: The Terra Foundation for American Art was founded by the businessman and collector Daniel J. Terra and lives on its endowment.

facts.t: The Terra Foundation for American Art reported total assets of $583,846,758 at the end of its tax year to June 2023 and $9,907,025 in grants paid, in its Form 990-PF.

terraforamericanart.what: A private foundation for American art set up in 1978 by Daniel J. Terra, founder of Lawter Chemicals, with offices in Chicago and Paris.
terraforamericanart.money: An endowment that pays for its grants; its assets were US$582 million in 2020.
terraforamericanart.arts: It closed its Chicago museum in 2004 to give grants and lend its collection; in 2012 it gave US$7.6 million.

tesonet.what: The giving arm of Tesonet, a Vilnius venture builder founded in 2008 by Tomas Okmanas and Eimantas Sabaliauskas.
tesonet.money: Tesonet, whose ventures include Nord Security, Hostinger, Oxylabs and Surfshark.

texaf.money: Texaf’s money comes mainly from renting property in its Kinshasa concession, with a sandstone quarry and a digital business; it began in 1925 as a textile company in the Belgian Congo.

facts.t: Texaf reported 2025 revenue of €37.7 million, up 10%, and consolidated net profit of €8.9 million.

texascommissiononarts|United States.what: The State of Texas arts agency, established in 1965 as the Texas Fine Arts Commission and renamed in 1979, governed by nine commissioners whom the governor appoints.
texascommissiononarts|United States.money: State general revenue and federal funds: $18,288,573 and $1,514,538 of an estimated $20,309,111 budget in fiscal 2026.
texascommissiononarts|United States.arts: It spends 93 percent of its budget on grants to arts and cultural organisations across Texas.
