thaibev.money: ThaiBev’s money comes from spirits, beer, soft drinks and food in Thailand and Southeast Asia; the Sirivadhanabhakdi family controls it.

facts.t: ThaiBev reported sales revenue of Baht 333,286 million for fiscal 2025, down 2.1%, and net profit of Baht 31,153 million, down 11.7%.

thanetdistrictcouncil|UK.what: The district council for Thanet in Kent, England, created on 1 April 1974, with 56 councillors and offices on Cecil Street in Margate.
thanetdistrictcouncil|UK.money: A net budget of GBP 26.343 million for 2025/26, about half from the government’s settlement funding and half from council tax.

thief.what: A 119-room hotel at Landgangen 1 on Tjuvholmen in Oslo, opened on 9 January 2013 and part of Petter Stordalen's Nordic Hotels & Resorts chain.
thief.arts: It shows contemporary art in the hotel through a collaboration with the Astrup Fearnley Museet and has its own art curator, Sune Nordgren.

thomasfearnley.what: A Norwegian foundation in Oslo formed in 1995 from the Thomas Fearnley Foundation, set up in 1939 by the shipowner Thomas Fearnley, and the Heddy and Nils Astrup Foundation.
thomasfearnley.money: Endowments from descendants of the Fearnley shipping family.
thomasfearnley.arts: Its registered purpose covers social, humanitarian and cultural causes and names the running of the Astrup Fearnley Museet.

thompson.what: A Thai foundation set up in 1976 by the court-appointed administrator of Jim Thompson's property, under the royal patronage of Princess Maha Chakri Sirindhorn.
thompson.money: Jim Thompson's Bangkok house and art collection, turned over to it in 1976.
thompson.arts: It runs the Jim Thompson Art Center, artist residencies and grants for preserving Thai art and culture.

thompsonfamily.what: A New York private foundation, tax-exempt since 1988, of the family of the late businessman Wade F.B. Thompson.
thompsonfamily.money: Wade Thompson's fortune from Thor Industries, the recreational vehicle maker he founded with Peter Orthwein in 1980, with assets of $461 million in 2023.

thomson.money: The Thomson family’s money comes from Thomson Reuters, the information company it controls through the Woodbridge Company; Thomson Reuters also gives in its own name.

facts.t: Thomson Reuters filed no 2025 federal lobbying reports of its own; outside firms reported $760,000 in fees from Thomson Reuters and its West Publishing unit under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

thuringia.what: A German federal state re-established on 3 October 1990 from the GDR districts of Erfurt, Gera and Suhl, with its capital in Erfurt and Mario Voigt (CDU) as minister-president.

thyssenbornemiszaartcontemporary.what: A private non-profit art foundation set up in Vienna in 2002 by the collector Francesca Thyssen-Bornemisza, its chair, now registered in Spain with headquarters in Madrid.
thyssenbornemiszaartcontemporary.arts: It holds a collection of more than 1,000 contemporary works, commissions new art, and runs a research academy and Ocean Space in Venice.

timchenko.money: Gennady Timchenko’s money comes from energy trading, as a founder of Gunvor, and from investments through his Volga Group.

facts.t: On 20 March 2014 the US Treasury designated Timchenko as a member of the Russian leadership’s inner circle, saying his activities in the energy sector, as a founder of Gunvor, have been directly linked to Putin.

timeschina.money: Times China is a Guangzhou property developer.

facts.t: In April 2024 Hang Seng Bank filed a winding-up petition against Times China, a defaulted developer, at Hong Kong's High Court over about US$173.2 million and HK$731.4 million.

timfairfax.money: The Tim Fairfax Family Foundation is funded by Tim Fairfax, a pastoralist and member of the Fairfax family, descended from John Fairfax of the newspaper publisher.

tisch.money: The Tisch family's money comes from Loews Corporation, the holding company of the insurer CNA Financial, Boardwalk Pipelines and Loews Hotels.

facts.t: Loews Corporation reported net income of $1,667 million for 2025.
One outside firm, OGR, reported $80,000 in 2025 fees from Loews Hotels Holding Corporation for US federal lobbying; Loews Corporation itself filed no 2025 report.

tischfamily.what: The New York family of Laurence Tisch, co-founder of Loews Corporation, and his brother Preston Robert Tisch; Laurence’s son James Tisch chairs Loews.
tischfamily.money: Loews Corporation, a New York conglomerate that holds CNA Financial, Boardwalk Pipelines, Loews Hotels and Altium Packaging; revenue was US$18.5 billion in 2025.

todd.money: The Todd family's Todd Corporation, whose Todd Energy produces natural gas, oil and LPG from onshore fields in Taranaki.

facts.t: Todd Energy produces around one-third of New Zealand's natural gas from its onshore natural gas fields.
The Todd Corporation gave $50,000 each to the National and Labour parties; the Greens turned down its smaller offer for ethical reasons.

tohogas.what: A Japanese gas utility based in Atsuta-ku, Nagoya, founded on 26 June 1922, that supplies gas to the Tōkai region.
tohogas.money: Gas sales in the Chūkyō metropolitan area, with consolidated revenue of 461,199 million yen in fiscal 2018.

tokyodevelopermoribuildingcompany.what: A Tokyo property developer founded on 2 June 1959, grown out of Mori Fudosan, which Taikichiro Mori set up in 1955.
tokyodevelopermoribuildingcompany.money: Developing, leasing and managing offices, homes, shops and hotels; the Mori family owns 95.94%.
tokyodevelopermoribuildingcompany.arts: It opened the Mori Arts Center, with an art museum, on the upper floors of Roppongi Hills Mori Tower in 2003.

tommeetippee.what: A baby products company in Newcastle upon Tyne, incorporated in 1946, that owns the Tommee Tippee brand; 3i agreed in 2016 to sell it to China's Shanghai Jahwa United.
tommeetippee.money: Sales of Tommee Tippee baby feeding products; 2015 sales were £130 million, about 60 percent from international markets.

torontoartscouncil|Canada.what: Toronto's city-wide public funding body for the arts, created in 1974; a charitable organization working under an arm's-length funding agreement with the City of Toronto.
torontoartscouncil|Canada.money: An annual appropriation from the City of Toronto of about C$25 million.

totalenergies.money: TotalEnergies’ money comes mainly from producing, refining and selling oil and gas, including liquefied natural gas.

facts.t: TotalEnergies reported adjusted net income of 18,264 million dollars for 2024, down from 23,176 million in 2023.
TotalEnergies declared EU lobbying costs of €3,000,000 to €3,499,999 for 2024 and recorded 149 high-level Commission meetings.
InfluenceMap gives TotalEnergies a D+ grade for its climate policy engagement.
On 23 October 2025 a Paris court ruled that TotalEnergies’ carbon neutrality advertising misled consumers.
TotalEnergies’ Washington office reported $1,090,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

totalsngal.what: The corporate foundation of TotalEnergies Sénégal, the French energy group’s company in Dakar, set up in 2013 and run by a six-member board.
totalsngal.money: TotalEnergies Marketing Sénégal, which sells fuel and gas through its service stations in Senegal.
totalsngal.arts: Culture is one of its priority fields, beside vocational training and road safety for children.

totaltunisie.what: The Tunisian fuel distribution arm of the energy company TotalEnergies, active in the country since 1948, with its head office at Les Berges du Lac in Tunis.
totaltunisie.money: Sales of fuels and related products and services through about 160 service stations in Tunisia.
totaltunisie.arts: It renewed its long-running partnership with the Festival International de Carthage for the 60th edition, held from 16 July to 19 August 2026.

towadagas.what: A city gas company in Towada, Aomori Prefecture, founded in October 1959 with capital of ¥100 million; it began supplying gas in April 1960.
towadagas.money: City gas supply to Towada and nearby areas, sales of gas appliances and liquefied petroleum gas, and gas installation work.

toyota.money: The ties name Toyota Tsusho, the Toyota group’s trading company, and Toyota-Fonden, a Danish foundation bearing the Toyota name.

facts.t: Toyota Tsusho reported revenue of about 10.31 trillion yen for the year to March 2025, and profit attributable to owners of 362.5 billion yen.

transeuropehalles.what: A member-run network of more than 180 independent cultural centres in repurposed buildings across over 40 countries, begun in Brussels in March 1983, with its coordination office in Lund, Sweden.
transeuropehalles.money: Yearly membership fees of €360 to €2,100, set by each member centre's annual turnover.

travelers.what: A US property and casualty insurer incorporated in Minnesota, with headquarters in New York and its largest office in Hartford, Connecticut, formed in 2004 from St. Paul and Travelers.
travelers.money: Premiums on business, personal and specialty insurance, with revenue of US$48.83 billion in 2025.

trianglenetwork.what: A UK registered charity and international network of artists and arts organisations, set up in 1982 by the British businessman Robert Loder and the sculptor Anthony Caro.
trianglenetwork.money: Donations and legacies, which made up £939.47k of its £999,591 income in the year to 31 March 2026.
trianglenetwork.arts: It organises artist-led workshops and residencies through independent centres in over 30 countries.

trianglepublications.what: A privately held American media group, based in Philadelphia and later Radnor, Pennsylvania, majority owned by Walter Annenberg and his sisters and folded into News Corporation in 1988.
trianglepublications.money: Its newspapers, magazines and broadcast stations, among them TV Guide, Seventeen and the Daily Racing Form; Rupert Murdoch paid $3 billion for it.
trianglepublications.arts: After the sale Walter Annenberg set up the Annenberg Foundation in 1989 and gave over $2 billion to educational establishments and art galleries.

tromscounty|Norway.what: The regional administration of Troms county in northern Norway, run from Tromsø with a 37-member county council; it was merged into Troms og Finnmark from 2020 to 2023.
tromscounty|Norway.money: The county budget of Troms fylkeskommune.

trustformutualunderstanding.what: A private grant-making foundation in New York set up in 1985 by Sandra Ferry Rockefeller to build ties between the United States, the Soviet Union and Central and Eastern Europe.
trustformutualunderstanding.money: Investment returns, chiefly from asset sales and dividends, on net assets of USD 25.7 million at the end of 2024.
trustformutualunderstanding.arts: It funds arts and environmental collaboration between the US and 29 countries; charitable disbursements came to USD 3.95 million in 2024.

tsbnz.money: TSB Bank, wholly owned by the Toi Foundation (the TSB Community Trust until it was renamed), whose income from the bank's dividends, and from Fisher Funds, pays its grants in Taranaki.

facts.t: TSB delivered a net profit before tax of $57.6 million in the year to 31 March 2025 and paid $10 million in dividends to its shareholder Toi Foundation Holdings Limited.

tsugarukaikyoferry.what: A ferry company based in Hakodate, Hokkaido, set up on 23 February 1972, that runs routes across the Tsugaru Strait between Hokkaido and Aomori Prefecture.
tsugarukaikyoferry.money: Passenger and vehicle ferry services: sales of JPY 13.2 billion in the year to December 2025.

tube.what: A steel distributor listed on the New Zealand stock exchange, formed in 1953 by a merger of three firms, with its head office in East Tamaki, Auckland.
tube.money: Supplying, distributing and processing steel products in New Zealand.

tucker.what: A Melbourne charitable trust set up under the will of Barbara Tucker, who died in May 2015, to realise a plan she shared with her husband, the painter Albert Tucker.
tucker.money: The estate of Albert and Barbara Tucker; grants of up to A$25,000 a year go to registered charities.
tucker.arts: Its first listed aim is the support and development of public art galleries and museums; it also administers the Tucker gift of art to Heide, formalised in 2005.

tunisair.what: Tunisia's national airline, formed by the government in 1948 and based near Tunis-Carthage International Airport.
tunisair.money: Ticket sales, with turnover of TND 1,627 million in 2025; the state holds 64.86% and three state funds 9.56%.

turing.what: A Dutch charitable foundation in Amsterdam, founded in July 2006 by Pieter and Françoise Geelen and named after the computer scientist Alan Turing.
turing.money: Proceeds of the stock exchange listing of TomTom, which Pieter Geelen co-founded in 1991 as the Turing Machine Company.
turing.arts: It pays for international loans to Dutch museum exhibitions and for music education, within a budget of roughly €3,500,000 a year for all its causes.

ubs.money: UBS’s money comes from wealth management, investment banking and asset management.

facts.t: UBS Group declared EU lobbying costs of €1,000,000 to €1,249,999 for 2025, with 0.8 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.
UBS reported $520,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.
UBS Americas’ PAC gave $1,707,000 to federal candidates in the 2023 to 2024 cycle, 50% to Republicans and 49% to Democrats, in its reports to the Federal Election Commission.

uccsubvention.what: A public university in Cork, Ireland, founded in 1845 as one of three Queen's Colleges and now a constituent university of the National University of Ireland.
uccsubvention.money: Revenue of €572.4 million in 2024/25: academic fees €181.96 million, research grants and contracts €131.87 million, State grants €100.12 million.

udoundanettebrandhorst.what: A Munich foundation set up in 1993 by the collectors Udo and Anette Brandhorst; its 1999 agreement with the Free State of Bavaria led to the Museum Brandhorst.
udoundanettebrandhorst.money: An endowment of €120 million in 2009; Anette Brandhorst was a great-granddaughter of the founder of Henkel.
udoundanettebrandhorst.arts: Interest on the endowment gave an acquisition budget of more than €2 million a year in 2009, and the collection grew from about 700 works to 1,200.

ukgovernment|UK.what: The central executive of the United Kingdom, led by Prime Minister Andy Burnham since 20 July 2026, whose ministers answer to Parliament.

ukresearch.what: A non-departmental public body of the UK government, launched in April 2018 under the Higher Education and Research Act 2017, joining seven research councils, Research England and Innovate UK.
ukresearch.money: The science budget of its sponsor, the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade.

ulsteruniversity.what: A public university in Northern Ireland, legally the University of Ulster, formed in 1984 by merging the New University of Ulster and Ulster Polytechnic; its legal address is in Coleraine.
ulsteruniversity.money: Its budget was £304.4 million in 2024/25; in June 2023 the Government of Ireland announced about €45 million in funding for it.

umicore.what: A Belgian materials technology company headquartered in Brussels, formed in 1989 by a merger of four mining and smelting companies and known as Union Minière before 2001.
umicore.money: Recycling and refining of precious metals, automotive catalysts and battery materials; revenue was €3.6 billion in 2025.

unam.what: Mexico's national public research university, founded in its modern form on 22 September 1910 by Justo Sierra, with its main campus at Ciudad Universitaria in Mexico City.
unam.money: Federal subsidy: MXN 53,749 million of its MXN 59,878 million budget for 2026, with own income making up the rest.
unam.arts: It runs 26 museums and 18 historic sites.

undernonprofitmill6.what: A non-profit arts and cultural organisation founded in 2015 that manages and operates CHAT (Centre for Heritage, Arts and Textile) at The Mills in Tsuen Wan, Hong Kong.
undernonprofitmill6.money: The D. H. Chen Foundation is its Founding Donor and Nan Fung Group, whose former cotton-spinning factory houses CHAT, is its Main Donor.

undp.what: The United Nations agency for development aid, founded on 22 November 1965 and based at UN headquarters in New York, with offices in 177 countries.
undp.money: Voluntary contributions from UN member states; its budget for 2026 was US$6,482.63 million as of August 2026.

unesco.what: A specialised agency of the United Nations founded in 1945, with 194 member states and headquarters in Paris.
unesco.money: Assessed contributions that member states must pay, plus voluntary contributions from governments, international bodies, companies and other donors.

unicredit.what: An Italian banking group formed in 1998 by the merger of Credito Italiano and Unicredito, with its headquarters in the UniCredit Tower in Milan.
unicredit.money: Its banking business: revenue of EUR 24.844 billion in 2024.

facts.t: UniCredit reported stated net profit of €9.7 billion for 2024, up 2% on 2023.
Banking on Climate Chaos 2026 ranks UniCredit 42nd among the world's banks for fossil fuel financing in 2025, a change of -$1.0 billion (-18.5%) from 2024.
UniCredit declared EU lobbying costs of €700,000 to €799,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register, with 2.35 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.

unicreditbank.what: A Romanian bank in the UniCredit Group, formed when Ion Țiriac Bank, founded in 1991, merged with HVB Bank Romania in June 2005; named UniCredit Bank since August 2015.
unicreditbank.money: Banking for individuals, small firms and companies through 208 branches; total assets were RON 34.6 billion at the end of 2015.

unipar.what: A Brazilian chemical company founded in 1969 as a petrochemical holding, seated in São Paulo, whose controlling shareholder is Frank Geyer Abubakir.
unipar.money: Sales of chlorine, caustic soda and PVC from plants in Cubatão and Santo André in Brazil and Bahía Blanca in Argentina.

unipol.what: An Italian insurance and banking group headquartered in the Unipol Tower in Bologna, founded there in 1962 as a cooperative provider of non-life insurance.
unipol.money: Insurance sold under brands such as UniSalute and Linear; its largest shareholder was Coop Alleanza 3.0 with 23.48% in June 2025.

uniqa.what: An Austrian insurance group set up in 1999, listed on the Vienna Stock Exchange, with about 40 companies in 14 countries and its head office in Vienna.
uniqa.money: Insurance premiums: €8,354.7 million written in 2025, with earnings before taxes of €516.4 million.
uniqa.arts: It supports Austrian museums including the Albertina, the Kunsthistorisches Museum and the Vienna Technical Museum.

uniqlo.what: A Japanese retail holding company incorporated in 1963 by Hitoshi Yanai, owner of Uniqlo and GU, with its head office in Yamaguchi and an office in Tokyo.
uniqlo.money: Clothing sales, chiefly Uniqlo: revenue of 3.9633 trillion yen in the year to August 2026.

unitedperformingarts.what: A Milwaukee nonprofit that has raised money since 1967 for the region’s performing arts groups, with 14 member organisations and further affiliates chosen each year.
unitedperformingarts.money: Gifts from individuals, companies and foundations, with no government funding: contributions were 96.4 percent of its $8.25 million revenue in the year to August 2025.

universitymuseumofumeuniversity.what: A public university in Umeå, northern Sweden, inaugurated on 17 September 1965, with over 43,700 students; the Swedish government appoints eight members of its board.
universitymuseumofumeuniversity.money: Its annual balance sheet was SEK 5.7 billion in 2025.

universityofchile.what: A public university in Santiago, founded by the Chilean state on 19 November 1842 under the government of Manuel Bulnes, with 40,494 students.
universityofchile.money: State grants, student fees and its own sales of goods and services.

universityofmanchester.what: A public research university created by Royal Charter on 1 October 2004 by merging the Victoria University of Manchester and UMIST, on Oxford Road, Manchester.
universityofmanchester.money: Income of £1.365 billion in the year to July 2024: £714.3 million tuition fees, £287.9 million research grants, £151.0 million funding body grants.

universityofmelbourne.what: A public research university established by an act of the Parliament of Victoria on 22 January 1853, with its main campus in Parkville, Melbourne.
universityofmelbourne.money: Research income of A$900 million in 2025, an endowment of AU$1.445 billion in 2024 and fees from its overseas students.
universityofmelbourne.arts: The Ian Potter Museum of Art, founded in 1972 on the Parkville campus, is its main art museum.

universityofpennsylvaniaculturalpartners.what: A private Ivy League research university in Philadelphia, founded by Benjamin Franklin and dating its history to 1740.
universityofpennsylvaniaculturalpartners.money: A total budget of $17.7 billion in fiscal 2026, an endowment of $24.81 billion in fiscal 2025 and $1.34 billion in sponsored research awards.

universityofsouthampton.what: A public research university that began as the Hartley Institution in 1862 and gained university status by royal charter on 29 April 1952.
universityofsouthampton.money: Income of £737.6 million in 2024/25, of which £141.4 million came from research grants and contracts.

universityofwitwatersrand.what: A public university in Johannesburg with 41,702 students in 2025, grown from the South African School of Mines founded in Kimberley in 1896 and a full university since 1922.

uruguaysministryofeducation|Uruguay.what: Uruguay's government ministry for education policy, cultural development, heritage, science and human rights, in Montevideo.

usbank.what: An American bank holding company headquartered in Minneapolis, parent of U.S. Bank National Association, which operates under a national bank charter signed in 1863.
usbank.money: Banking, investment, mortgage, trust and payment services; revenue was US$28.7 billion in 2025.
usbank.arts: The U.S. Bank Foundation handles its grants, nonprofit donations and employee giving.

uscharityfriendsofixchelmuseum.what: A US charity established in 1984 to promote the Maya textile tradition of Guatemala and the Ixchel Museum in Guatemala City; registered in Princeton, New Jersey.
uscharityfriendsofixchelmuseum.money: Contributions from members and donors: $45,631 of its $45,638 revenue in 2025.
uscharityfriendsofixchelmuseum.arts: It funds renovations, field research and publications for the Ixchel Museum.

usembassy|Mongolia.what: The embassy of the United States government in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, whose Public Diplomacy Section runs its grants.
usembassy|Mongolia.money: United States federal funds under the Department of State's Public Diplomacy Programs.
usembassy|Mongolia.arts: Its 2026 Local Grants Program offers up to 5 awards of $1,000 to $15,000 for educational, cultural and civil society projects.

usfincaviga.what: A US nonprofit in Boston founded in 2002 by Jenny and Frank Phillips to restore Ernest Hemingway's house and papers at Finca Vigía, Cuba.
usfincaviga.money: Donations: contributions made up all $368,460 of its revenue in 2024.
usfincaviga.arts: It has conserved and digitized more than 10,000 Hemingway documents and built a conservation centre with archival storage at the Finca.

usmanov.money: Alisher Usmanov’s money comes from metals and mining, telecommunications and technology, held through USM, which owns Metalloinvest and of which he owns about 49 percent.

facts.t: On 3 March 2022 the US Treasury designated Usmanov, calling him close to Putin and Dmitry Medvedev, and identified his superyacht Dilbar and his Airbus A340 as blocked property.

uwebristol.what: A public university in Bristol with roots in the Bristol Trade and Mining School of 1856; Bristol Polytechnic from 1970 and a university since 1992.
uwebristol.arts: Its City Campus for creative and cultural courses is made up of Bower Ashton Studios, Arnolfini, Spike Island and Watershed.

vac.what: A private non-profit art foundation established in Moscow in 2009 by Leonid Mikhelson; it opened GES-2 House of Culture, a former Moscow power station, on 4 December 2021.
vac.money: The fortune of its founder Leonid Mikhelson, chairman, chief executive and 25% shareholder of the Russian gas company Novatek.
vac.arts: In 2017 it opened a venue in a palazzo on the Zattere in Venice for exhibitions, events and residencies.

vale.money: Vale’s money comes from mining, mainly iron ore, and nickel and copper.

facts.t: Vale reported net profit of US$6.166 billion for 2024, down 23% from US$7.983 billion in 2023.
In 2021 Vale signed a settlement of about $7 billion with Minas Gerais over the Brumadinho dam collapse, which killed more than 270 people.
In October 2024 Vale, BHP and Samarco reached a 170 billion reais settlement with Brazilian authorities over the 2015 Fundão dam collapse.
Vale declared EU lobbying costs of €100,000 to €199,999 for 2025, with 1.35 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.
Two outside firms reported $100,000 in 2025 fees from Vale USA for US federal lobbying, under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

valeculturalinstitute.what: The cultural institute of Vale, the Brazilian mining company, created in 2020 and based in Rio de Janeiro.
valeculturalinstitute.money: Money from Vale, a global mining company headquartered in Rio de Janeiro, which reported revenue of US$38.4 billion in 2025.
valeculturalinstitute.arts: It runs the Memorial Minas Gerais Vale, Museu Vale, Centro Cultural Vale Maranhão and Casa da Cultura de Canaã dos Carajás, and the Vale Música programme.

vancleef.what: A Paris jewellery house founded in 1896 by Alfred Van Cleef and Salomon Arpels, now part of the Swiss luxury group Richemont.
vancleef.money: Jewellery and watch sales for its owner Richemont, the luxury holding company Johann Rupert founded in 1988.
vancleef.arts: Dance Reflections by Van Cleef & Arpels, launched in 2020, supports the creation and promotion of dance works and dance education.

vandenende.what: A Dutch private foundation set up on 18 January 2001 by the theatre and television producer Joop van den Ende and his wife Janine.
vandenende.money: The sale of Joop van den Ende's shares in the television producer Endemol, which Telefónica bought in 2000 for €5.5 billion.
vandenende.arts: It gives grants to non-profit cultural institutions and study grants to performing arts students, and rebuilt the DeLaMar Theatre complex in Amsterdam.

veinisober.what: A wine shop and online wine store in Tallinn, owned by the company AbeStock AS.

velmakimbell.what: Velma Fuller Kimbell (1887 to 1982), wife of the Fort Worth businessman Kay Kimbell, with whom she set up the Kimbell Art Foundation; she co-chaired its board.
velmakimbell.money: Her share of the Kimbells' community property, built on Kay Kimbell's milling, grocery and oil firms, given to the foundation after his death in 1964.

venetoregion|Italy.what: An Italian ordinary-statute region, set up in 1948 and working since 1970, governed from Palazzo Balbi in Venice by president Alberto Stefani since 5 December 2025.

verbundhydro.what: Austria's largest electricity company, founded in 1947 under the second nationalisation act, listed on the Vienna Stock Exchange and 51% owned by the Republic of Austria.
verbundhydro.money: Electricity from hydropower, wind and solar, and the power grid, with revenue of 8,013.6 million euros in 2025.
verbundhydro.arts: Since 2004 it has kept its own collection of contemporary international art, the Sammlung Verbund.

verenigingehbk.what: The users’ association of OT301, a self-managed cultural centre at Overtoom 301 in Amsterdam; its members squatted the former film academy in 1999 and bought it in 2006.
verenigingehbk.money: Its members, who use housing and work spaces in the building and give voluntary hours to run it.

vestlandcounty|Norway.what: The elected regional government of Vestland county in Norway, with a county council of 65 members and administrative centres in Bergen, Leikanger and Førde.
vestlandcounty|Norway.money: The county budget set by its elected county council.
vestlandcounty|Norway.arts: Culture and cultural heritage are among its main responsibilities, handled by a Standing Committee for Culture, Sport and Inclusion.

vgc.what: The body that represents the Flemish authorities in the Brussels-Capital Region, created by the special law of 12 January 1989 and answerable to the Flemish Parliament.
vgc.money: A dotation from the Flemish government's budget, EUR 30,588,000 in 2025, plus EUR 1,116,000 a year for community infrastructure.
vgc.arts: It runs more than 20 Dutch-language public libraries, including Muntpunt, and 22 community centres in Brussels.

victorpinchuk.what: The private philanthropic foundation of the Ukrainian businessman Victor Pinchuk, who consolidated his giving under it in 2006.
victorpinchuk.money: The fortune of Victor Pinchuk, founder of the pipe, railway wheel and steel producer Interpipe and of the investment firm EastOne Group.
victorpinchuk.arts: Through PinchukArtCentre it awards the Future Generation Art Prize, $100,000 every two years for artists under 35, announced in December 2009.

vikingcruises.what: A cruise company founded by Torstein Hagen in 1997 as Viking River Cruises, headquartered in Hamilton, Bermuda, run from Basel, and listed in New York since May 2024.
vikingcruises.money: River, ocean and expedition cruises: USD 5.3 billion revenue in 2024.

villasandi.what: A Prosecco wine company in Crocetta del Montello, Treviso, owned by the Moretti Polegato family and run by Giancarlo Moretti Polegato with his children Diva and Leonardo.
villasandi.money: Sales of Prosecco DOCG and DOC wines: group turnover of over EUR 131 million in 2023.

villedebordeaux|France.what: The municipal government of Bordeaux, France's ninth most populous commune with 267,991 inhabitants in 2023 and the seat of Bordeaux Métropole.
villedebordeaux|France.money: The city budget: €636 million in 2025, with €440 million to run public services and €160.5 million of investment.

villedejoliette|Canada.what: The municipal government of Joliette, Quebec, a city incorporated in 1863 with 21,384 residents at the 2021 census, led by Mayor Pierre-Luc Bellerose.
villedejoliette|Canada.money: A 2026 budget of C$98.8 million, announced on 15 December 2025, with property tax set at $0.549 per $100 of assessed value.

villedelyon|France.what: The commune of Lyon, France's third-largest city with 519,127 residents in 2023, led by mayor Grégory Doucet since 4 July 2020.
villedelyon|France.money: The municipal budget of the city of Lyon.

villedemarseille|France.what: The municipal government of Marseille, France's second most populous commune with 886,040 inhabitants in 2023, divided into 16 arrondissements grouped in eight sectors.
villedemarseille|France.money: The city budget voted by its municipal council, whose members are elected in the eight sectors.

villedestrasbourg|France.what: The municipal government of Strasbourg, the largest commune of the Grand Est with 293,771 inhabitants on 1 January 2023 and the seat of the Eurométropole de Strasbourg.
villedestrasbourg|France.money: The city budget voted by the municipal council, drawn mainly from direct local taxes and the State's operating grant (DGF).
villedestrasbourg|France.arts: The City and the Eurométropole together allocate 120 million euros a year to culture.

villum.what: A Danish non-profit foundation set up in 1971 by the civil engineer Villum Kann Rasmussen, founder of the window maker Velux; it is the main shareholder of VKR Holding A/S.
villum.money: Revenues of the VKR Group, which owns Velux, and income from the foundation's other assets.
villum.arts: With its sister foundation Velux Fonden it gave DKK 2.3 billion across 734 grants in 2025, for scientific, cultural, artistic and social projects.

vinci.money: Vinci's money comes from building and civil engineering (Vinci Construction) and from running motorways, airports and other concessions.

vingroup.what: A Vietnamese conglomerate headquartered in Long Bien district, Hanoi, founded in Ukraine in 1993 as the food company Technocom by Phạm Nhật Vượng, its largest shareholder.
vingroup.money: Real estate, retail, industry and services from healthcare to hospitality; revenue was VND101.8 trillion in 2022.

visa.what: An American payment card services corporation headquartered in San Francisco, founded by Bank of America in 1958 as the BankAmericard programme and renamed Visa in 1976.
visa.money: Payment products it supplies to financial institutions; its network processed 257.5 billion transactions in 2025 and net revenue was US$40 billion in fiscal 2025.

visualartcollectivetrustadministersit.what: A not-for-profit trust in Bengaluru that administers 1Shanthiroad Studio/Gallery, the art space founded by Suresh Jayaram in 2002.
visualartcollectivetrustadministersit.money: Project grants, among them India Foundation for the Arts funding for its Urban Fabric and Namma Ooru, Namma Jana projects.
visualartcollectivetrustadministersit.arts: It hosts artist residencies, monthly talks and film screenings, and holds art workshops for rural and underprivileged children in Bangalore and Karnataka.

vitra.money: The Fehlbaum family's money comes from Vitra, the Swiss furniture company it owns, which makes and sells designer furniture.

vivaenergyaustralia.what: An Australian fuel company set up in August 2014 when Vitol bought Shell's Australian downstream business, seated in Melbourne and listed on the ASX since 2018.
vivaenergyaustralia.money: Refining at its Geelong refinery and fuel sales: AUD 26.7 billion revenue in 2023; Vitol keeps 29.9 percent.

vivo.what: A Brazilian telecommunications group trading as Vivo, a subsidiary of Spain's Telefónica, formed from the 1998 break-up and privatisation of the state monopoly Telebrás.
vivo.money: Mobile, broadband, fixed-line and pay-TV services sold under the Vivo brand to more than 90 million customers in Brazil.

vlaamseoverheid.what: The executive of the Flemish Community and Flemish Region of Belgium, led by a Minister-President and answerable to the Flemish Parliament.
vlaamseoverheid.money: The Flemish public budget, which its Department of Culture, Youth and Media spends on arts subsidies under the Arts Decree (Kunstendecreet).

vladimirpotanin.money: Vladimir Potanin’s money comes from metals, through Interros and his stake in Norilsk Nickel, which he heads.

facts.t: On 15 December 2022 the US State Department designated Potanin, one of Russia’s richest men, and the Treasury designated Rosbank, a bank he had acquired that year.

vladimirpotanincharitable.what: A non-profit grant-making foundation created in 1999 and named after its founder Vladimir Potanin, president of Interros and Norilsk Nickel; its office is on Tverskaya Street in Moscow.
vladimirpotanincharitable.money: Income from its endowments, which held net assets of 124.2 billion rubles at the end of 2025; Potanin added 10 billion rubles in 2022.
vladimirpotanincharitable.arts: It runs grant programmes in culture, higher education and social sports and has awarded more than 40 thousand grants and fellowships.

vodafone.what: A British telecommunications group founded on 17 July 1984 as a subsidiary of Racal Electronics, demerged in 1991, with its registered office in Newbury, Berkshire.
vodafone.money: Telecommunications services: revenue of EUR 40,461 million in the year to 31 March 2026.

volkart.what: A foundation set up in Winterthur on 1 February 1951 by Georg, Peter and Balthasar Reinhart, partners of the trading company Gebrüder Volkart, for the firm's centenary.
volkart.money: Part of the profits of Gebrüder Volkart, the Reinhart family's Winterthur merchant house that traded cotton and colonial goods until 1989.
volkart.arts: Since 2022 it funds ecology, the social sector, media and documentary film; its separate culture funding area ended in 2021.

volksbank.what: A cooperative bank seated in Mainz, formed on 1 January 2023 by the merger of Mainzer Volksbank, founded in 1862, and Volksbank Darmstadt-Südhessen.
volksbank.money: Its banking business in Mainz, Rheinhessen and the Darmstadt area, as a registered cooperative within Germany's cooperative financial group.

volkswagen.money: Volkswagen's money comes from making and selling cars and vans under brands including Volkswagen, Audi and Porsche, and from car finance; Porsche Holding Salzburg, its car importer and dealer, belongs to Volkswagen AG.

facts.t: The Volkswagen Group reported 2025 sales revenue of 321.9 billion euros and an operating result of 8.9 billion euros, 53% below 2024.

In the US diesel emissions case over defeat devices that cheated federal emissions tests, Volkswagen paid a $1.45 billion civil penalty under the Clean Air Act and funded a $2.7 billion mitigation trust; Audi AG and Porsche AG were among the defendants.
Volkswagen AG declared EU lobbying costs of €2,750,000 to €2,999,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register.
Volkswagen Group of America reported $1,150,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.
InfluenceMap gives Volkswagen a C grade for its climate policy engagement.

vriendenloterij.what: A Dutch charity lottery company, started in 1989 as the Sponsor Bingo Loterij and renamed in 2011; part of the Holding Nationale Goede Doelen Loterijen.
vriendenloterij.money: Ticket sales to its 1.3 million players; at least 40% of each ticket goes to culture, welfare and sport in the Netherlands.
vriendenloterij.arts: It gave 160 million euros to culture, sport and welfare in 2025.

vriendenloterij450.what: A Dutch charity lottery company, started in 1989 as the Sponsor Bingo Loterij and renamed in 2011; part of the Holding Nationale Goede Doelen Loterijen.
vriendenloterij450.money: Ticket sales to its 1.3 million players; at least 40% of each ticket goes to culture, welfare and sport in the Netherlands.
vriendenloterij450.arts: It gave 160 million euros to culture, sport and welfare in 2025.

vriendenloterijeur.what: A Dutch charity lottery company, started in 1989 as the Sponsor Bingo Loterij and renamed in 2011; part of the Holding Nationale Goede Doelen Loterijen.
vriendenloterijeur.money: Ticket sales to its 1.3 million players; at least 40% of each ticket goes to culture, welfare and sport in the Netherlands.
vriendenloterijeur.arts: It gave 160 million euros to culture, sport and welfare in 2025.

vriendenvannw.what: A friends' fund for NW, the Aalst art centre and cinema, set up in December 2021 at the King Baudouin Foundation on the initiative of three local figures.
vriendenvannw.money: Gifts and memberships from local art lovers, business owners and supporters, paid through the King Baudouin Foundation.

vsbfonds.what: A Dutch fund in Utrecht named after the Verenigde Spaarbank (VSB), formed in 1983 from 19th-century Nutsspaarbanken savings banks.
vsbfonds.money: Returns on capital held by Stichting VSB Vermogensfonds, built from the VSB shares the fund owned after the bank merged into Fortis in 1990.

vtb.what: A majority state-owned Russian bank founded as Vneshtorgbank in 1990, with its legal address in St Petersburg; it has been under US, EU and UK sanctions since 2014.
vtb.money: Corporate and retail banking; three state bodies held over 90 percent of its capital in 2022, and it reported 2025 net income of US$5.89 billion.

facts.t: On 24 February 2022 the US Treasury imposed full blocking sanctions on VTB Bank, which it described as Russia’s second-largest financial institution, holding nearly 20 percent of banking assets in Russia.

vtbbank.what: A majority state-owned Russian bank founded as Vneshtorgbank in 1990, with its legal address in St Petersburg; it has been under US, EU and UK sanctions since 2014.
vtbbank.money: Corporate and retail banking; three state bodies held over 90 percent of its capital in 2022, and it reported 2025 net income of US$5.89 billion.

vyksacityadministration|Russia.what: The administration of the Vyksa urban district in Nizhny Novgorod Oblast, Russia, formed from the Vyksunsky district in 2011, with 72,351 residents in 2025.
vyksacityadministration|Russia.money: The budget of the Vyksa urban district, where OMK's Vyksa Metallurgical Plant is the town's main taxpayer.

wacom.what: A Japanese maker of graphics tablets and related products, founded on 12 July 1983, listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange and headquartered in Kazo, Saitama.
wacom.money: Sales of graphics tablets and related products, with net sales of 112.7 billion yen in the year to March 2023.

wakefieldcouncil|UK.what: The local authority for the City of Wakefield metropolitan district in West Yorkshire, created on 1 April 1974 and meeting at County Hall; Reform UK has held control since 2026.

walmart.what: A US retailer founded in 1962 by the brothers Sam and Bud Walton, running Walmart stores and Sam's Club, headquartered in Bentonville, Arkansas.
walmart.money: Retail sales; total revenue was US$713.2 billion in fiscal 2026.

waltonfamily.money: The Walton family's money comes from Walmart, the retailer Sam Walton founded; the family's gifts go through the Walton Family Foundation and Alice Walton, the company's through Walmart Inc. and the Walmart Foundation.

facts.t: Walmart reported total revenues of $713,163 million for the fiscal year to January 2026.
In November 2022 state attorneys general announced a proposed $3.1 billion multistate settlement with Walmart over its role in the opioid epidemic.
Walmart reported $7,840,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

wangwei.what: A Chinese collector and businesswoman born in Shanghai in 1963, co-founder and director of the Long Museum and wife of the investor Liu Yiqian.
wangwei.money: The fortune the couple made from share trading and other businesses after marrying in 1988.
wangwei.arts: She has collected oil painting since 2003 and opened the Long Museum Pudong in 2012 and its West Bund branch in 2014.

warholfdn.what: A New York foundation set up in 1987 under Andy Warhol's will, which acts as the artist's estate and makes grants to the visual arts.
warholfdn.money: An endowment built from Warhol's estate, sales of his works through Christie's and fees for licensing his images.
warholfdn.arts: It has given over $300 million in cash grants to more than 1,000 arts organisations and donated 52,786 works to 322 institutions.

warnermusic.what: A US record and music publishing company founded in 1958, 72 percent owned by Len Blavatnik's Access Industries, which holds 98 percent of the votes.
warnermusic.money: Recorded music and publishing through Warner Chappell Music: USD 6.71 billion revenue in 2025.

wates.what: An independent grant-making family trust founded in 1966 by the brothers Allan, Norman and Ronald Wates of the Wates building firm, based in Leatherhead, Surrey.
wates.money: An endowment from the three brothers, who built up the family construction company Wates, founded in 1897, with investment income of £552,293 in 2023.

wdr3mediapartner.what: The public broadcaster for North Rhine-Westphalia, a public-law institution based in Cologne, created in 1955 from the split of NWDR and on air since 1 January 1956.
wdr3mediapartner.money: Mainly the household broadcasting fee, €18.36 a month in 2023, collected by a joint agency of ARD, ZDF and Deutschlandradio, plus limited on-air advertising.
wdr3mediapartner.arts: WDR 3 is its cultural radio channel, carrying mostly classical, jazz and world music.

weenergies.what: The corporate foundation of We Energies, the Wisconsin electricity and gas utility of WEC Energy Group in Milwaukee, tax-exempt since May 1983.
weenergies.money: The stockholders of WEC Energy Group fund it; the group sells electricity and natural gas to 4.4 million customers in four states.

weilfamilyofficeproventus.what: A family-owned investment company in Stockholm, founded in 1969 and owned by Robert Weil and family, organised since 2017 as a family office.
weilfamilyofficeproventus.money: Returns on the Weil family's assets, invested in equities, fixed income, currencies and alternatives.
weilfamilyofficeproventus.arts: It manages the assets of the Robert Weil Family Foundation, which continues the culture work Robert Weil earlier ran through the company.

weimar.what: An independent city (kreisfreie Stadt) in Thuringia with 65,566 residents at the end of 2025, led by the non-partisan mayor Peter Kleine.

weitzerhotels.what: A family-owned hotel and restaurant group trading as Florian Weitzer Hotels & Restaurants, whose Hotel Weitzer in Graz has belonged to the Weitzer family since 1910.
weitzerhotels.money: Income from its hotels and restaurants in Graz, Vienna, Salzburg and Semmering, among them Hotel Daniel, Grand Hôtel Wiesler and Grand Ferdinand.

wellcometrustendowment.what: A charitable foundation for health research based in London, founded in 1936 under the will of the pharmaceutical entrepreneur Sir Henry Wellcome.
wellcometrustendowment.money: Returns on an investment portfolio of £39.9 billion, built from Henry Wellcome's fortune in the drug company Burroughs Wellcome.
wellcometrustendowment.arts: The Wellcome Building at 183 Euston Road houses Wellcome Collection; the Trust spent £1.1 billion on charitable activities in 2023/24.

wellingtoncitycouncil|New Zealand.what: The territorial authority for Wellington, New Zealand's capital, established on 1 November 1989 in place of a city council first formed in 1870.
wellingtoncitycouncil|New Zealand.money: Rates collected from Wellington property owners, which rose by an average of 12 percent in its 2025/26 budget.
wellingtoncitycouncil|New Zealand.arts: Its Arts and Culture Multi-Year Funding pays organisations a yearly amount, generally in three-year cycles, under its Aho Tini arts policy.

wellsfargo.money: Wells Fargo's money comes from consumer and commercial banking, lending and wealth management.

facts.t: Wells Fargo reported net income of $21,338 million for 2025.
In December 2022 the CFPB ordered Wells Fargo to pay more than $2 billion in consumer redress and a $1.7 billion penalty over the mismanagement of auto loans, mortgages and deposit accounts.
Wells Fargo reported $2,700,000 of its own US federal lobbying spending for 2025, in its four quarterly reports under the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

welshgovernment|UK.what: The devolved government of Wales, set up on 12 May 1999 as the National Assembly's executive and led since May 2026 by First Minister Rhun ap Iorwerth of Plaid Cymru.
welshgovernment|UK.money: About 80 percent from a UK block grant set by the Barnett formula and 20 percent from devolved Welsh taxes; £26 billion in 2025/26.

wesfarmers.what: An Australian conglomerate headquartered in Perth, with retail, chemicals, fertiliser, industrial and safety businesses, mainly in Australia and New Zealand.
wesfarmers.money: Sales of its businesses, with revenue of A$45.7 billion in the 2025 financial year.
wesfarmers.arts: Wesfarmers Arts funds arts groups in Western Australia and nationally and manages the Wesfarmers Collection of Australian Art.

facts.t: Wesfarmers reported revenue of $45.7 billion and a statutory net profit after tax of $2,926 million for the year to 30 June 2025.

In its 2024-25 donor return to the Australian Electoral Commission, Wesfarmers Limited disclosed $61,800 in political donations: $34,300 to Labor branches and $27,500 to Liberal and National branches.

wesfarmersarts.what: An Australian conglomerate headquartered in Perth, with retail, chemicals, fertiliser, industrial and safety businesses, mainly in Australia and New Zealand.
wesfarmersarts.money: Sales of its businesses, with revenue of A$45.7 billion in the 2025 financial year.
wesfarmersarts.arts: Wesfarmers Arts funds arts groups in Western Australia and nationally and manages the Wesfarmers Collection of Australian Art.

westernfrontat.what: A society of artists and long-term patrons affiliated with the Vancouver artist-run centre Western Front, which set up the Western Front Endowment Fund in 2003.
westernfrontat.money: Gifts and bequests from artists and patrons to its endowment, whose yearly payout goes to Western Front, with matching funds from Canadian Heritage's Endowment Incentives.

westernpennsylvaniaconservancy.what: A private nonprofit conservation organisation founded in 1932 and headquartered in Pittsburgh, which Edgar Kaufmann Jr. entrusted with Fallingwater in 1963.
westernpennsylvaniaconservancy.money: Gifts from its members and other income, with total revenue of $32,834,272 and total assets of $139,538,974 in 2024.

westpac.money: Westpac is one of Australia’s four major banks.

facts.t: Westpac reported a net profit after tax of $6.9 billion for the year to 30 September 2025.

In 2020 the Federal Court ordered Westpac to pay a $1.3 billion penalty for breaches of anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing law, including failing to report international funds transfer instructions.

In its 2024-25 donor return to the Australian Electoral Commission, Westpac Banking Corporation disclosed $193,049 in political donations: $94,811 to Labor branches and $98,238 to Liberal and National branches.

wexner.money: Les Wexner's money comes from L Brands (The Limited), the retail group behind Victoria's Secret and Bath & Body Works, since split into two companies.

facts.t: In August 2019 Wexner wrote to the Wexner Foundation community that his former friend and personal money manager Jeffrey Epstein had misappropriated 'vast sums of money from me and my family' more than ten years earlier.
In February 2026 Wexner testified about his relationship with Epstein in a closed-door deposition before the House Oversight Committee, at his home in Ohio.

wexnercenter.what: A nonprofit in Columbus, Ohio, tax-exempt since 1990, that supports Ohio State University's Wexner Center for the Arts; Leslie H. Wexner, founder of Limited Brands, chairs its trustees.
wexnercenter.money: Donations: all of its USD 1.32 million revenue in the year to June 2025 came from contributions; net assets were USD 14.0 million.

whanki.what: A foundation that Kim Hyang-an, the painter Kim Whanki's widow, founded in New York in 1979 and moved to Seoul in 1989; it opened the Whanki Museum in 1992.
whanki.money: It owns the works, papers and belongings of Kim Whanki and Kim Hyang-an and manages the copyright and trademark rights to his art.
whanki.arts: It researches, shows and publishes Kim Whanki's work and supports Korean and foreign artists.

whitecube.what: A contemporary art gallery established in London in 1993 by the art dealer Jay Jopling, who owns it, with galleries in London, Hong Kong, New York, Paris and Seoul.
whitecube.money: Sales of work by the more than 70 artists and artist estates it represents.

wienerberger.what: An Austrian building materials group founded in Vienna in 1819, the world's largest producer of bricks, listed on the Vienna Stock Exchange with all shares in free float.
wienerberger.money: Sales of bricks, roof tiles, pavers and pipe systems from more than 200 plants in 28 countries, with revenue of €4,566 million in 2025.
wienerberger.arts: It runs the Brick Award for clay and brick architecture.

wienerstdtische.what: An Austrian insurer founded in Vienna in 1824, the largest single company in the Vienna Insurance Group.
wienerstdtische.money: Insurance premiums, about EUR 3,196.2 million gross; the Wiener Städtische Versicherungsverein is the group's main shareholder.

wihurifoundation.money: The foundation was set up in 1942 by the industrialist Antti Wihuri and his wife Jenny Wihuri.

williamgrant.what: The charitable foundation of William Grant & Sons, the family-owned Scotch whisky distiller founded in 1887 and based at the Glenfiddich distillery in Dufftown.
williamgrant.money: One percent of William Grant & Sons' pre-tax profits, set aside each year; it awarded £4,715,781 in 92 grants in 2023.
williamgrant.arts: The arts and Scotland's culture and heritage are among its grant themes.

williampenn.what: A private grant-making foundation in Philadelphia, founded in 1945 as the Phoebe Waterman Foundation by Otto Haas, co-founder of the chemical company Rohm and Haas, and his wife Phoebe.
williampenn.money: Much of the estate of Otto Haas, who ran Rohm and Haas until his death in 1960, with net assets of $3.3 billion in 2024.
williampenn.arts: Arts and Culture is one of its five grant programmes, and its charitable disbursements across all five were $159,969,971 in 2024.

winnipegartscouncil|Canada.what: A not-for-profit charity that the City of Winnipeg charges with distributing its arts funding and managing its Public Art Policy.
winnipegartscouncil|Canada.money: City arts funding of C$4.65 million in 2025, plus C$258,570 for five city-designated museums.

wipro.money: Wipro's money comes from IT services; Azim Premji, its founder chairman, gives through the Azim Premji Foundation, and the Wipro Foundation is the company's own.

facts.t: Wipro's IT Services revenues for FY25 amounted to USD 10.51 billion, a year-on-year degrowth of 2.3%.

wirth.what: A commercial gallery for modern and contemporary art, founded in Zurich in 1992 by Iwan Wirth, Manuela Wirth and Ursula Hauser, with galleries in Europe, Asia and North America.
wirth.money: Its gallery business for more than 80 artists and estates, among them the estates of Louise Bourgeois and Philip Guston.
wirth.arts: It runs art centres in Somerset, opened in 2014, and on Menorca's Illa del Rei, opened in 2021.

wissam.what: Chief executive of Webcor Group, a food importer and distributor that is one of the largest companies in Angola, and co-founder with his wife Hiba of the Nesr Art Foundation.
wissam.money: The Nesr family's Webcor Group, a family-owned food production and distribution business active in African markets since 1978.

wolfson.what: A UK grant-making charity set up in 1955 by Isaac Wolfson, chairman of Great Universal Stores, with his wife and son Leonard; based in London.
wolfson.money: Its endowment, just under £1 billion in 2024, when it spent £44 million on charitable activities.

workerspartyofkorea.what: The ruling party of North Korea, founded in 1949 from a merger of the Workers' Parties of North and South Korea, led by General Secretary Kim Jong Un.
workerspartyofkorea.money: Its Central Committee Bureau 39 (Room 39) keeps a foreign currency fund for North Korea's leaders.

wrth.what: A family-owned German group selling fastening and assembly materials, founded by Adolf Würth in Künzelsau in 1945 and led by his son Reinhold Würth from 1954.
wrth.money: Sales through more than 400 companies in 80 countries, EUR 20.7 billion in 2025.
wrth.arts: Its Kunsthalle Würth reopened in October 2026 for its 25th anniversary.

wstenrot.what: A charitable association run as a foundation in Ludwigsburg, formed from the Gemeinschaft der Freunde founded in Stuttgart in 1921 and active in its present form since 1990.
wstenrot.money: Two holding companies that own 40% and 26% of Wüstenrot & Württembergische AG, the listed building society and insurance group in Kornwestheim.
wstenrot.arts: Its monuments programme repairs and researches listed buildings such as the Einstein Tower in Potsdam and the Chancellor's Bungalow in Bonn, with a focus on heritage built after 1945.

wstenrotjoinedrestoration.what: A charitable association run as a foundation in Ludwigsburg, formed from the Gemeinschaft der Freunde founded in Stuttgart in 1921 and active in its present form since 1990.
wstenrotjoinedrestoration.money: Two holding companies that own 40% and 26% of Wüstenrot & Württembergische AG, the listed building society and insurance group in Kornwestheim.
wstenrotjoinedrestoration.arts: Its monuments programme repairs and researches listed buildings such as the Einstein Tower in Potsdam and the Chancellor's Bungalow in Bonn, with a focus on heritage built after 1945.

wurth.money: The Würth family's money comes from the Würth Group, a maker and seller of assembly and fastening materials built up by Reinhold Würth.

facts.t: The Würth Group reported preliminary 2025 sales of EUR 20.7 billion and an operating result of EUR 940 million.

In May 2008 Reinhold Würth accepted a penalty order of 700 daily fines from the Heilbronn District Court in his tax affair, which the Heilbronner Stimme put at €3.5 million assuming net income of at least €1.8 million.
Adolf Würth GmbH & Co. KG declared EU lobbying costs of €100,000 to €199,999 for 2025 to the EU Transparency Register, with 0.25 full-time-equivalent lobbyists.

wynn.money: Wynn Resorts runs casino resorts in Las Vegas, Macau and Boston; its founder Steve Wynn resigned as chief executive in 2018.

facts.t: Wynn Resorts posted full-year 2025 revenue of $7.1 billion, flat on 2024.

In April 2019 the Massachusetts Gaming Commission fined Wynn Resorts $35 million after executives failed to disclose years of sexual misconduct allegations against founder Steve Wynn, and fined CEO Matthew Maddox $500,000.

Outside firms reported $460,000 in 2025 fees for US federal lobbying for Wynn Resorts and Wynn Resorts Development (Brownstein Hyatt Farber Schreck $190,000, Dentons $150,000, Empire Consulting Group $120,000); the company filed no in-house report.

xacbank.what: A Mongolian bank headquartered in Ulaanbaatar, founded in 2001 through the merger of Goviin Ekhlel LLC and X.A.C. LLC, the country's two largest non-bank financial institutions.
xacbank.money: Retail, business and corporate banking for 700,000 customers in Mongolia.

xcelenergy.what: A listed electricity and natural gas utility based in Minneapolis, built on Northern States Power, Public Service Company of Colorado and Southwestern Public Service, with origins in 1909.
xcelenergy.money: Electricity sold to about 3.9 million customers and natural gas to 2.2 million across eight states, with revenue of $13.44 billion in 2024.
xcelenergy.arts: The Xcel Energy Foundation gave $4.6 million in grants to 390 nonprofit organisations in 2024, in STEM career pathways, community vitality and environmental sustainability.

yandex.money: Yandex’s money comes from internet services in Russia and nearby countries: search, ride hailing (Yandex Go), food delivery (Yandex Eda) and advertising.

yandexeda.what: The food delivery service of the Russian technology group Yandex, launched in 2018 after Yandex.Taxi bought the Moscow service Foodfox in December 2017.
yandexeda.money: Food delivery: RUB 144.6 billion revenue in 2025, within the Yandex group, owned since July 2024 by investors including Lukoil.

yanshijie.money: Yan Shijie is a collector and entrepreneur; the sources read do not name the business his money comes from.

yarur.money: The Yarur family’s money comes from Banco de Crédito e Inversiones (BCI), the Chilean bank it controls.

facts.t: BCI reported net profit of 996,212 million Chilean pesos for 2025.

yayasanilham.what: A non-profit foundation established on 22 October 2018 for charity work including arts, culture and education in Malaysia, which has run ILHAM Gallery in Kuala Lumpur since 2019.
yayasanilham.money: It took the gallery over from IB Tower Sdn Bhd, developer of Ilham Tower, whose owner the family of former finance minister Daim Zainuddin controls.

yokohamacitymanagementfee|Japan.what: The municipal government of Yokohama, the capital of Kanagawa Prefecture, a city since 1 April 1889 and a designated city since 1 September 1956.

yokonagaeceschina.money: Yoko Nagae Ceschina’s money was the $190 million fortune she inherited from her husband, Count Renzo Ceschina.

yoosungyeon.what: The late Korean businessman, born in 1917, who co-founded the Samchully coal briquette business in 1955 and the coal miner Samcheok Tanjwa Gaebal, now ST International, in 1962.
yoosungyeon.money: His family's coal business; the Yoo family's SongEun foundation holds 6.86 percent of ST International.

zabludowiczarttrust.what: The trust that principally owns the Zabludowicz Collection, the contemporary art collection Anita and Poju Zabludowicz began in 1994; the collection's UK charity is Zabludowicz Art Projects (no. 1120067).
zabludowiczarttrust.money: Poju Zabludowicz's fortune through Tamares Group, the family holding company he chairs, built by his father Shlomo around the Israeli defence contractor Soltam.

zain.what: A Kuwaiti mobile telecommunications company founded on 22 June 1983 as MTC and rebranded as Zain in 2007, publicly traded and present in eight Middle Eastern countries.
zain.money: Mobile phone services for 50.9 million active customers, with Omantel holding 21.9% and the Kuwait Investment Authority 15.9% of its shares in 2024.

zanotta.what: An Italian furniture maker founded in 1954 in Nova Milanese by Aurelio Zanotta, part of the Haworth Lifestyle group since Cassina acquired it in 2023.
zanotta.money: Sales of furniture: revenue of EUR 18.57 million in 2023.

zapopancitycouncil|Mexico.what: Zapopan's city council, which governs Jalisco's second most populous city, part of metropolitan Guadalajara; Juan José Frangie Saade is municipal president.
zapopancitycouncil|Mexico.money: The municipal budget: MXN 13,147.9 million approved for 2026 on 16 December 2025.

zeitzmocaa.what: A public not-for-profit museum of contemporary art from Africa and its diaspora in Cape Town, opened on 22 September 2017 through a partnership between the V&A Waterfront and Jochen Zeitz.
zeitzmocaa.money: The V&A Waterfront put more than R500 million into the building, and the businessman Jochen Zeitz lent his art collection for his lifetime.

zellfamily.what: The Chicago family foundation of real estate investor Sam Zell, founder of Equity Group Investments, who died in May 2023; his widow Helen Zell is its president.
zellfamily.money: Sam Zell's real estate and investment fortune; the foundation held USD 119.6 million in assets and paid USD 63.5 million in grants in 2024.

zentrumpaulkleemauricee.what: The foundation responsible for operating the Zentrum Paul Klee in Bern, a museum opened on 20 June 2005 after gifts from the Klee family and the surgeon Maurice E. Müller.
zentrumpaulkleemauricee.money: Land and most of the fortune of Maurice E. and Martha Müller, offered in 1998, plus development money from the City and Canton of Bern.

zhenghao.money: Zheng Hao's money comes from hotels, among them the Onehome Art Hotel in the park the museum shares.

zinsou.money: The Zinsou family finances the foundation; its Circle of Major Patrons lists Lionel Zinsou, Marie-Cécile Zinsou’s father, and Marie-Christine Zinsou.

zionsbank.what: Zions Bank is a division of Zions Bancorporation, N.A., a listed national bank in Salt Lake City founded in 1873 by the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.
zionsbank.money: Banking for over 1 million customers, mostly in the western United States, with revenue of US$2.705 billion in 2022.

zumtobel.what: An Austrian lighting company headquartered in Dornbirn and listed in Vienna, which grew from the firm Walter Zumtobel founded there on 1 January 1950.
zumtobel.money: Sales of luminaires, lighting management and lighting components, with revenue of 1,209.2 million euros in 2022/23 and the Zumtobel family holding approximately 36 percent.

zwirner.what: A commercial contemporary art gallery founded in New York in 1993 by the German-born dealer David Zwirner, with galleries in New York, Los Angeles, London, Paris and Hong Kong.
zwirner.money: Sales of works by the more than seventy artists and estates it represents, in the primary and secondary art markets.
